meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners - Work Session for Oct. 7, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Nida Allam presided over the October 7, 2024 Board of County Commissioners work session, which opened with reflections on the one-year anniversary of October 7th and an initial closed session on personnel. In open session, the board reviewed consent agenda items—including a $472,500 detention facility food pass door contract that prompted policy questions from Commissioner Wendy Jacobs—and suspended the rules to approve a contract amendment for uniform security services with Nighthawk Security and Consulting LLC. Commissioners then received major work session updates on the Public Art Program, the Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) prioritization and debt modeling, the USDA-funded Farm Campus community engagement report, revisions to the Business Recruitment and Expansion incentive policy, and ARPA obligation deadlines ahead of the December 31 federal cutoff before entering a second closed session and adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, Land Acknowledgment, and October 7th Anniversary Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Nida Allam opened the work session with the public charge and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs read the land acknowledgment. Chair Allam and Commissioner Jacobs both offered remarks marking the one-year anniversary of the October 7, 2023 attacks, grieving the loss of Israeli and Palestinian lives, remembering a Durham community member held hostage, and calling for a ceasefire, return of hostages, and a political two-state solution.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Personnel) and Report Out
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board recessed into closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) to consider a personnel matter. Upon returning to open session at 01:36:00, Chair Nida Allam reported that no action was taken and that the board unanimously voted to seal the closed session minutes.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Claudia Hager reviewed twelve items proposed for the upcoming regular session consent agenda, including a $472,500 contract with CML Security LLC to install 238 food pass doors at the Detention Facility, EMS SAMHSA opioid grant funding ($307,251), Central Pines Regional Council MOA, HIPAA risk assessment, Public Health grants, utility sanitary sewer extension contracts, Queen Street garage lighting, and a DHHS charge-master rate letter. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs questioned whether the 238 food pass doors would increase cell confinement times; Sheriff's Office staff clarified it was a phased safety upgrade from a 2001 assessment that would not change confinement hours. Jacobs also requested EMS overdose reduction data, and staff confirmed opioid overdoses dropped from 90 per month during COVID to 56 in July.

agenda_items.title: Other Business: Suspension of Rules and Contract Amendment with Nighthawk Security and Consulting LLC
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board was requested to suspend its rules to take immediate action authorizing the County Manager to execute a contract amendment for uniform security services with Nighthawk Security and Consulting LLC. Commissioners voted 5-0 to suspend the rules and 5-0 to approve the contract amendment.

agenda_items.title: Update Presentation on the Durham County Public Art Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy Director Perry Mans, Project Manager Brenda Hayes-Bright, and Public Art Coordinator Sarah Martin presented completed and upcoming public art installations funded under the 2019 up-to-1% public art policy, noting 75% MWBE participation and 11 of 12 selected artists residing in North Carolina. Highlights included murals at the Youth Home, Innovation Lab, 300 East Main parking deck, Stanford L. Warren Library, 500 East Main, and DecO on the Go mobile outreach panels. Commissioners Wendy Jacobs and Nimasheena Burns praised the community engagement and discussed converting Martin's contract position to permanent, supporting local artist studio space, and exploring private-sector art partnerships.

agenda_items.title: Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) Update and Prioritization
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Claudia Hager, Budget Director Keith Lane, and Deputy Director Perry Mans reviewed Phase 2 of the 10-year CIP update, detailing revised cost estimates, affordability constraints, and major projects including the Animal Shelter, Sheriff's Training Facility, Project Build at Hope Valley, Fire/EMS Station 19, Parkwood Fleet Maintenance, an $18 million homeless services center placeholder, and Admin II. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs urged coordinated city-county-DPS infrastructure planning, rethinking the Boys and Girls Club property, and evaluating surplus county/school parcels and Museum of Durham History options. Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns requested an objective infrastructure prioritization list driven by urgent building conditions rather than commissioner preferences.

agenda_items.title: USDA-Funded Farm Campus Feasibility Study: Community Engagement Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Cooperative Extension Director Donna Rewalt presented the interim community engagement report prepared with Co-Inspire Consulting for the proposed Farm Campus on Orange Factory Road, centering BIPOC, immigrant, women, and young farmers. Key insights emphasized inclusive community governance, addressing historical distrust, transit access barriers, shared commercial kitchen and cold-storage needs, and phased cohort incubator programming. Commissioners discussed agritourism opportunities and ensuring presentation of the final HR&A feasibility study to advisory boards like DOST.

agenda_items.title: Discussion of Updated Business Recruitment and Expansion Policy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic Development Director Andy Miracle and Manager Matt Filter presented proposed revisions to the 2019 business incentive policy ahead of an October 28 vote. Changes include adding a special lane for corporate headquarters projects, allowing hybrid work schedules, tying job wage verification to Durham County's living wage standard, removing the unused $1,000-per-job option, organizing Community Partnerships and Benefits into six buckets as a living attachment, shortening default 10-year terms where appropriate, and streamlining clawbacks and MWBE reporting. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs praised the living-document benefits approach and requested adding support for hiring justice-involved individuals via Justice Services, emphasizing job pathways across education levels, and formalizing annual public compliance reporting.

agenda_items.title: ARPA Update: Obligation Deadlines, DPS ILAs, and Reallocation Options
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Claudia Hager and staff reported that all 49 ARPA projects are on track to meet the December 31, 2024 federal obligation deadline, highlighted the October 23 groundbreaking of the first joint City-County ARPA affordable housing project ($2.7M ARPA gap funding out of $13.5M total), and reviewed draft capital and Pre-K/Title I ILAs with Durham Public Schools. Staff outlined Treasury flexibility to amend contracts or shift unspent balances after December 31 into priority areas like Slater Road sewer infrastructure, childcare subsidies/Pre-K, and food security. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs asked about planning for the 2026 fiscal cliff when $10.8 million in ARPA community grants expires.

agenda_items.title: Second Closed Session (Personnel, Opioid Litigation, Attorney-Client Privilege) and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) and (a)(3) for two personnel/attorney-client matters and national opioid litigation. Upon returning at 06:35:44, the board reported no action was taken, direction was given to staff, closed session minutes were sealed unanimously, and the work session adjourned.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (Personnel - N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6))
votes.notes: Entered first closed session at start of work session.
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately following the public charge, land acknowledgment, and October 7th anniversary remarks by Chair Nida Allam and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs, Chair Allam read the statutory citation under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) to consider the qualifications, competence, performance, character, fitness, or conditions of appointment/employment of a public officer or employee. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs moved to enter closed session and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton seconded. The motion passed unanimously 5-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Motion to Seal Closed Session Minutes (First Closed Session)
votes.notes: Reported by Chair Allam upon returning from closed session; no action taken during closed session.
votes.discussion_detail: Upon reconvening in open session at 01:36:00 after the personnel closed session, Chair Nida Allam reported to the public that the board had met in closed session and taken no formal action. She stated for the clerk's record that a motion to seal the closed session minutes had been made by Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns and seconded by Commissioner Heidi Carter, passing unanimously 5-0.

votes.item_title: Motion to Suspend the Rules for Immediate Action on Nighthawk Security and Consulting LLC Contract Amendment
votes.notes: Rules suspension required to take binding contract action during a work session.
votes.discussion_detail: Following the review of regular session consent agenda items, Chair Nida Allam introduced an urgent item under Other Business requesting that the board suspend its rules to authorize a contract amendment for uniform security services with Nighthawk Security and Consulting LLC. Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns moved to suspend the rules, and Commissioner Heidi Carter seconded. Chair Allam clarified the procedural vote was solely to suspend the rules, and the motion passed unanimously 5-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Authorize County Manager to Execute Contract Amendment for Uniform Security Services with Nighthawk Security and Consulting LLC
votes.notes: Approved immediately following suspension of the rules.
votes.discussion_detail: After the board unanimously suspended its rules to act during the work session, Chair Nida Allam entertained a motion to authorize the County Manager to execute the contract amendment with Nighthawk Security and Consulting LLC for uniform security services. Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns moved to authorize the contract amendment, and Commissioner Heidi Carter seconded. No commissioners raised questions or objections, and the motion passed unanimously 5-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (Personnel, National Opioid Litigation, and Attorney-Client Privilege)
votes.notes: Entered under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) and (a)(3).
votes.discussion_detail: At the conclusion of the ARPA update and regular work session agenda, Chair Nida Allam read three statutory grounds for entering closed session: a personnel matter under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6), consultation with the attorney regarding the national opioid litigation under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3), and a second attorney-client privileged item under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3). Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns moved to enter closed session for the three stated reasons and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton seconded. The motion passed unanimously 5-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Motion to Seal Closed Session Minutes (Second Closed Session)
votes.notes: Reported upon returning to open session; no action taken, direction given to staff.
votes.discussion_detail: Returning to open session at 06:35:44 after an hour-long closed session, Chair Nida Allam announced that the board had met in closed session, taken no formal action, and given direction to staff. She reported that a motion to seal the closed session minutes had been made by Commissioner Heidi Carter, seconded by Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns, and passed unanimously 5-0.

votes.item_title: Motion to Adjourn
votes.notes: Final adjournment of the October 7, 2024 work session.
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately after reporting out from the second closed session and sealing the minutes, Chair Nida Allam called for a motion to adjourn the work session. Commissioner Heidi Carter moved to adjourn and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs seconded. All five commissioners voted aye by voice vote, ending the meeting.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners - Work Session for Oct. 7, 2024
disagreements.issue: Policy Concerns Over $472,500 Detention Facility Food Pass Doors Contract (Item 24-0424)
disagreements.summary: During consent agenda review, Commissioner Wendy Jacobs questioned a surprise $472,500 contract to install 238 food pass doors at the Detention Facility, asking whether it would increase detainee cell confinement time.
disagreements.side_a_position: Questioned why the $472,500 food pass door installation appeared on consent without prior board briefing and sought assurance it would not lengthen cell confinement.
side_a_arguments: The board had not previously heard about this issue before seeing the $472,500 contract on the consent agenda.
Needed policy clarity on whether installing food pass doors for meals, documents, and tablets would increase the amount of time detainees remain confined in cells.
disagreements.side_b_position: Staff and Sheriff's Office defended the project as a phased safety/security upgrade identified in a 2001 facility assessment that does not alter detainee out-of-cell time.
side_b_arguments: About 100 doors were already installed in earlier phases over five to six years.
Food pass doors limit staff exposure when passing food, documents, or swapping tablets without changing how long detainees spend in their cells.
disagreements.resolution: Staff committed to providing additional background information to commissioners prior to the regular session consent vote; no vote was taken at the work session.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners - Work Session for Oct. 7, 2024
disagreements.issue: Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) Prioritization Criteria and Surplus Property Strategy
disagreements.summary: Commissioners challenged staff to establish objective prioritization criteria for the $2B+ CIP pipeline and to reconsider major property commitments like the Boys and Girls Club and old DSS building.
disagreements.side_a_position: Urged an objective, facility-condition-driven priority list, coordinated city-county-DPS infrastructure planning, and re-evaluating Boys and Girls Club and surplus parcels.
side_a_arguments: Urgent aging-infrastructure repairs (mold, leaks) should rank ahead of individual commissioner pet projects.
Land use rezonings drive EMS, sewer, and school capital demands and must be coordinated via a tripartite infrastructure committee.
Selling or repurposing former school sites, surplus downtown lots, and rethinking the Boys and Girls Club site could relieve CIP debt pressures.
disagreements.side_b_position: Staff noted that many CIP projects have been queued for decades and emphasized balancing capital construction with ongoing operating costs and staff capacity.
side_b_arguments: Staff capacity and Durham's AAA bond rating constrain how quickly projects can be delivered.
Worst-case placeholders (like $15M for the old DSS building and $18M for homeless infrastructure) are needed while public-private options are explored.
disagreements.resolution: Staff agreed to send a prioritization feedback template and return in November with refined sequencing, Gant timelines, and affordability scenarios.

meetings.title: BOCC Regular Meeting October 7, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: Resuming in open session on October 7, 2024, the Board of County Commissioners reviewed consent agenda items covering Detention Center food-pass doors, EMS SAMHSA opioid grants, public health grants, and sanitary sewer extensions, and voted unanimously 5-0 to suspend the rules and authorize a security contract amendment with Nighthawk Security & Consulting LLC. Commissioners received comprehensive updates on the Public Art Program, the County's $2.2 billion requested 10-year Capital Improvement Plan (CIP), the USDA-funded Farm Campus feasibility community engagement study, revisions to the Business Recruitment and Expansion incentive policy, and ARPA project obligations ahead of the December 31, 2024 deadline. The meeting concluded with a 5-0 vote to enter closed session for personnel, opioid litigation, and attorney-client matters.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Report-Out, Citizen Comments, and Consent Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Nida Allam reported a unanimous closed-session motion made by Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns and seconded by Commissioner Heidi Carter, noted no citizens had signed up for comment, and turned to Acting County Manager Claudia Hager to review consent agenda items. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs questioned item 24-0424 ($472,300 with CML Security LLC for 238 Detention Facility food-pass doors) to confirm it would not increase cell confinement time, and sought outcome data on item 24-0589 ($370,261 SAMHSA EMS opioid grant), where staff reported 3,000+ Narcan kits distributed and monthly overdoses dropping from ~90 during COVID to 56 in July. Hager also walked through solid waste planning (24-0596), HIPAA risk assessment (24-0597), Public Health grants (24-0600, 24-0601), electrical and chemical contracts (24-0612, 24-0613), Detention Center fire pump assessment (24-0616), sanitary sewer extension contracts generating net county consumption revenue (24-0617), Queen Street garage lighting (24-0621), and DHHS chargemaster rates (24-0624).

agenda_items.title: Suspension of Rules and Nighthawk Security & Consulting LLC Contract Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Under Other Business, the Board was asked to suspend its rules to authorize the County Manager to execute a contract amendment for uniform security services with Nighthawk Security & Consulting LLC. Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns moved to suspend the rules and Commissioner Heidi Carter seconded, passing 5-0. Burns then moved and Carter seconded the authorization for the County Manager to execute the contract amendment, which passed unanimously 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Durham County Public Art Program Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy Engineering Director Perry Mans, Project Manager Brenda Hayes-Bright, and Public Art Coordinator Sarah Martin presented progress under the County's up-to-1% public art policy, noting 164 RFQ applicants, 75% MWBE participation among the top 12 selected artists, and 11 of 12 artists from North Carolina. They showcased completed installations—including murals at the Youth Home, Innovation Lab, and 300 East Main parking deck daycare—alongside upcoming projects at Stanford L. Warren Library, 500 East Main parking deck, Board of Elections, Sheriff's Training Facility, and Emergency Operations Center. Commissioners praised the community-engaged murals, asked about making Martin's contract position permanent amid the hiring freeze, and inquired about maintenance plans and private-sector art funding.

agenda_items.title: Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Acting County Manager Claudia Hager, Budget Director Keith Lane, and Deputy Engineering Director Perry Mans presented the ~$2.2 billion requested 10-year CIP, including major Durham Public Schools and Durham Tech needs (such as a potential $680 million 2026 GO bond referendum), Animal Shelter architect selection, Sheriff's Training Facility GMP, Parkwood EMS/fleet maintenance, Emergency Operations Center, Durham-to-Roxboro Rail Trail corridor acquisition, and the loss of over $5 million annually in occupancy tax diverted to Discover Durham over three years. Commissioners Jacobs, Burns, and Carter pressed for objective infrastructure-driven prioritization rankings, affordable housing and homeless shelter placeholders, and an inventory of surplus county and school properties (such as the former DSS building, Boys & Girls Club site, and closed schools) ahead of the incoming board.

agenda_items.title: Farm Campus Feasibility Study Community Engagement Results
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a brief lunch recess called at 02:07:33, Cooperative Extension Director Donna Rewalt presented the interim community engagement report for the USDA-funded Farm Campus feasibility study on the Orange Factory Road property, conducted with Co-Spare Consulting and an advisory team ahead of HR&A Advisors' full feasibility report. Survey and focus group findings highlighted the need for inclusive community governance, addressing BIPOC farmer distrust and lack of bus transit access, shared commercial kitchen and cold/dry storage facilities, mentorship, and cohort learning models. Commissioners discussed scheduling a site visit, combatting rapid farmland loss, building education pipelines with Durham Tech, and exploring agritourism.

agenda_items.title: Updated Business Recruitment and Expansion Policy Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic Development Director Andy Miracle and Manager Matt Filter presented a revised Business Recruitment and Expansion Policy ahead of a planned October 28 adoption vote, separating the board resolution, six-section policy, and living Community Partnerships & Benefits document. Key updates include a special lane for headquarters projects unable to meet the $50 million CapEx or 200-job thresholds, replacing MSA title matching with Durham County's living wage standard, allowing PEOs for pooled benefits, permitting an 80% combined CapEx/job compliance average, simplifying clawbacks, and codifying a 25% MWBE target. Commissioners praised the program's nearly $3 billion private investment impact and urged stronger tracking of Durham-resident hiring (noting 32% of Corning staff live in Durham County), workforce diversity, and employer childcare support.

agenda_items.title: American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) Funding Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Acting County Manager Claudia Hager and staff updated the Board on Durham County's 49 ARPA projects ahead of the December 31, 2024 federal obligation deadline, announcing an October 23 groundbreaking for the first joint City-County ARPA affordable housing project ($2.7 million ARPA out of a $13.5 million total joint housing allocation) and near-final DPS school capital and $1.4 million Title I/Pre-K ILAs. Staff outlined U.S. Treasury flexibility to amend contracts or shift funds among existing contracts (such as Slater Road water/sewer, childcare subsidies, and food security) after December 31. Commissioner Jacobs praised the grantee outcome snapshots and asked when the County would plan for the 2026 'fiscal cliff' when $10.8 million in ARPA nonprofit grants expire.

meetings.title: BOCC Regular Meeting September 23, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: At its September 23, 2024 regular meeting, the Board of County Commissioners amended its agenda to add a closing personnel session, approved prior meeting minutes, and issued ceremonial proclamations for Minority Enterprise Development Week, Rooted in Wellness Day, and a framed resolution honoring Governor Roy Cooper's public education legacy. Commissioners approved the consent agenda 5-0 after pulling item 24-0602, discussed 2025 federal legislative priorities for NCACC—adding affordable housing, Earned Income Tax Credit expansion, HBCU support, and caregiver tax credits—and announced eight board and commission appointments. Following public comment by Amanda Wallace questioning transparency around County Manager Kimberly Sowell's leave and the designation of Acting County Manager Claudia Hager, the Board declined comment on the personnel matter and unanimously approved item 24-0602 5-0 before entering closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Adjustments, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Nida Allam convened the meeting with the public charge, Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns read the land acknowledgement, and Commissioner Heidi Carter led the Pledge of Allegiance. At a commissioner's request, the Board added a closed session for a personnel matter at the end of the meeting and approved the amended agenda 5-0. Clerk Monica Wallace and Vice Chair Burns shared announcements covering MedWeek 2024, Duke Forest deer reduction, Extension Master Food Volunteers, Engage Durham UDO sessions, Welcome Baby's sock drive, the DCoVotes app, Diabetes Prevention classes, National Night Out, RTI's Black-owned business fair, and the Student U commercial kitchen ribbon cutting.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (September 3, 2024 Work Session and September 9, 2024 Regular Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Allam presented the minutes of the September 3, 2024 work session and September 9, 2024 regular session for approval. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs moved approval and Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns seconded, passing 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations and Resolution Honoring Governor Roy Cooper
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter read the Minority Enterprise Development Week 2024 proclamation, and Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns read the third annual NC Black Alliance Rooted in Wellness Day 2024 proclamation, received by Curida Giddings. Chair Allam, Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton, and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs then read the Board's resolution honoring Governor Roy Cooper's service since 2017. Commissioners praised Cooper's support for public education and criticized his vetoed House Bill 10 for diverting over $250 million to unaccountable private school vouchers and mandating sheriff cooperation with ICE.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Item 24-0602)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Allam noted item 24-0602 was pulled due to a citizen comment request and commissioners briefly highlighted a $750,000 digital equity item on the consent agenda. The Board voted unanimously 5-0 to approve the remaining consent agenda items.

agenda_items.title: 2025 Federal Legislative Goals for NCACC
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deborah Craig-Ray led a discussion of 2025 federal legislative goals due to the North Carolina Association of County Commissioners by October 4, reviewing unfinished 2022 priorities including the Black Maternal Health Momnibus Act, Head Start/Child Care for Working Families, free school meals, SNAP for formerly incarcerated people, and Older Americans Act nutrition funding. Commissioners directed staff to carry forward applicable 2022 items and research adding federal housing legislation (the HOMES Act, $25,000 down payment assistance, and LIHTC expansion/flexibility), HBCU funding and AI/drone initiatives, the $6,000 Earned Income/Child Tax Credit expansion, the Domestic Workers Bill of Rights, and family caregiver tax credits.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Ballot Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Curtis Massey announced the Board's written ballot appointments: Nick Galvez (Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee), Nicole McCoy (Audit Oversight Committee), Rachel Seawon and Makisha Markham (Durham County Women's Commission), Latasha Best-Gaddy and Christian Rebusie (Durham Workforce Development Board), Kenneth Webb (Historic Preservation Commission), and Jay Meven (Homeless Services Advisory Committee).

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 24-0602: County Manager Leave and Acting County Manager Appointment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Amanda Wallace, founder of Operation Stop CPS, spoke against item 24-0602, questioning the lack of public transparency after County Manager Kimberly Sowell commenced leave on the evening of September 9 following a 4:30 p.m. closed session and Deputy County Manager Claudia Hager was appointed Acting County Manager, asking whether Sowell was suspended or placed on leave for wrongdoing while still paid. Chair Allam stated the Board would make no comments on a personnel item, and the Board approved item 24-0602 unanimously 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following action on item 24-0602, Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton moved and Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns seconded entering closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) to consider personnel matters. The motion passed unanimously 5-0.

votes.item_title: Approval of Amended September 23, 2024 Regular Session Agenda
votes.notes: No objections voiced.
votes.discussion_detail: After adding a closed session for a personnel matter to the end of the meeting, Commissioner Heidi Carter moved to approve the agenda as amended and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton seconded. The motion passed 5-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of Minutes (September 3, 2024 Work Session and September 9, 2024 Regular Session)
votes.notes: No corrections requested.
votes.discussion_detail: Commissioner Wendy Jacobs moved to approve the September 3, 2024 work session and September 9, 2024 regular session minutes, seconded by Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns. The motion passed unanimously 5-0.

votes.notes: Mover and seconder were not verbally named ('So moved. Second.').
votes.discussion_detail: After citizen speaker Amanda Wallace questioned the transparency of County Manager Kimberly Sowell's leave and Deputy County Manager Claudia Hager's appointment as Acting County Manager, Chair Allam stated the Board would not comment on a personnel matter and called for a motion on item 24-0602. The motion passed unanimously 5-0.

votes.notes: No objections voiced.

meetings.title: BOCC Regular Meeting September 9, 2024 (Pt. 2)
meetings.executive_summary: Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns presided over the opening portion of the September 9, 2024 regular session (with four commissioners present) before Chair Nida Allam returned at 00:49:05 to preside over the remainder of the meeting. The board approved the agenda and minutes 4-0, presented five ceremonial recognitions and proclamations (including a $1.5 million DOE grant check for the EBERP residential energy efficiency program, World Alzheimer's Awareness Day, Recovery Month, and Welcoming Week), and unanimously adopted its consent agenda 5-0 featuring $3 million for Durham Tech expansion and $2 million for homeless services. Commissioners also held a public hearing—with no public speakers and no vote required—on the $20 million Chin Page Road Lift Station engineering report and State Revolving Fund loan before adjourning into closed session.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Adjustments and Approval of Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns opened Part 2 of the regular session, asked for any agenda adjustments, and entertained a motion to approve the agenda. With Chair Nida Allam absent at the start, the four commissioners present approved the agenda 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk Monica Wallace announced the Board of Elections move to Shops at Hope Valley, launch of the DCoVotes app, CenterFest, and updated COVID-19 vaccines. Commissioners offered remarks honoring 9/11 first responders, a deceased county employee, and the Pauli Murray Center grand opening, while Vice Chair Burns criticized state lawmakers for private school vouchers and ICE mandates and urged residents to join DPS's paid CDL bus-driver training program, and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs promoted upcoming UDO rewrite engagement sessions.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Recognition: $1.5M Energy Burden and Emissions Reduction Program (EBERP) Grant
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Sustainability Manager Tobin Freid and Sustainability Specialist Megan Pendall presented a $1.5 million Inflation Reduction Act / DOE EECBG grant—the largest competitive award in the nation—partnering with Orange and Granville Counties to retrofit at least 200 income-qualified owner- or renter-occupied homes at no cost, focusing on Justice40 census tracts. Commissioners praised the program's racial, economic, and environmental equity impact and protections preventing landlords from raising rents post-retrofit.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns paused the transition to ceremonial items to secure approval of the prior meeting minutes. Commissioner Heidi Carter moved and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs seconded approval, which carried 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations: World Alzheimer's Awareness Day, Recovery Month, and Welcoming Week
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners read proclamations for World Alzheimer's Awareness Day (Sept 21) with Dementia Inclusive Inc., Durham Celebrates Recovery (Sept 2024) with Recovery Community of Durham, Welcoming Week (Sept 13–22) with Immigrant & Refugee Affairs Coordinator Nao and Equitable Well-Being Director Dr. Brent Lewis (who announced a new language access coordinator position), and National Recovery Month with Justice Services Director Roshanna Parker and counselor George O'Bryant. Chair Nida Allam returned at 00:49:05 and resumed presiding.

agenda_items.title: Adoption of Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: No items were pulled from the consent agenda, though Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns briefly celebrated $3 million in funding for Durham Technical Community College campus expansion and $2 million for homeless services. The board unanimously approved the consent agenda 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Utilities Division Engineering Report for Chin Page Road Lift Station, Force Main, and Gravity Main Project
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Utilities staff presented the engineering report and environmental information document for a new 10.2 MGD Chin Page Road lift station outside the 500-year floodplain to relieve Stirrup Iron Creek capacity near RTP, funded in part by a $19.3 million NCDEQ Clean Water State Revolving Fund loan (1.16% interest over 20 years) and $1.875 million from the sewer enterprise fund balance. Commissioners questioned the two-and-a-half-year timeline, capacity for RTP 3.0 and the comprehensive plan, and Vice Chair Burns proposed setting aside corporate tax incentive revenues into an infrastructure fund so businesses help finance future sewer expansions. No members of the public commented, and Chair Allam closed the public hearing after confirming no board vote was required.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Public Hearing Only / No vote required

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Personnel and Economic Development Incentives)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) for a personnel matter and N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) to discuss economic development incentives for business location or expansion.

votes.item_title: Approval of the September 9, 2024 Regular Session Agenda
votes.notes: Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns presided; Chair Nida Allam had not yet returned until 00:49:05.
votes.discussion_detail: Opening the second portion of the September 9, 2024 regular session, Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns presided in Chair Nida Allam's temporary absence and asked if there were any adjustments to the published agenda. Hearing none, she called for a motion to approve the agenda. A motion and second were made from the board, and the four commissioners present voted unanimously 4-0 by voice vote to adopt the agenda.

votes.item_title: Approval of Prior Meeting Minutes
votes.notes: Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns presided while Chair Nida Allam was absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Just before beginning the $1.5 million EBERP sustainability grant recognition, Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns paused proceedings to complete the formal approval of minutes. Commissioner Heidi Carter moved to approve the minutes and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs seconded. With no objections or corrections, the four present commissioners approved the minutes 4-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (Personnel and Economic Development Incentives)
votes.notes: Entered under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) and (a)(4); economic development item discussed first.
votes.discussion_detail: After closing the Chin Page Road lift station public hearing with no action required, Chair Nida Allam noted that no items had been pulled from consent and read two statutory bases for closed session: a personnel evaluation/employment matter under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) and economic development incentive negotiations under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4). Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton moved to adjourn into closed session and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs seconded. All five commissioners voted aye by voice vote.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Session for Monday, September 9, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: The Board of County Commissioners began its September 9, 2024 regular session with a 4-0 vote to hold a two-and-a-half-hour closed session on personnel matters before returning for the 7:00 p.m. public meeting. Commissioners approved the agenda and minutes, celebrated a $1.5 million U.S. Department of Energy Energy Burden and Emissions Reduction Program (E-BERP) grant for Justice40 home retrofits, and issued five ceremonial proclamations covering World Alzheimer's Awareness Day, Recovery Month, Welcoming Week, and National Hispanic Heritage Month. The Board unanimously approved the consent agenda 5-0, held a public hearing with no speakers on the ~$20 million Chin Page Road sewer lift station project, and concluded with a 5-0 vote to enter closed session on personnel and economic development incentives, taking no action afterward.

agenda_items.title: Early Closed Session Pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Opening the meeting early for a closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) on personnel/public officer matters, the Board voted 4-0 on a motion by Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns and second by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs. Upon returning to open session at 02:36:00, Chair Nida Allam reported that direction was given to staff.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Approval, and Commissioner Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Allam read the public charge, Vice Chair Burns read the land acknowledgement, and Allam briefly stepped away while Burns presided over agenda approval (4-0) and announcements. Clerk Monica Wallace announced the Board of Elections' new facility at the Shops at Hope Valley, CenterFest, and Tri-County Pasture Field Day. Vice Chair Burns criticized the state legislature for delaying the state budget while passing $250 million+ in private school vouchers ($12.85 million affecting 2,756 Durham applicants) and $1.1 billion for ICE-sheriff mandates, and Commissioner Jacobs promoted upcoming Engage Durham UDO rewrite sessions.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Prior Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presiding Vice Chair Burns called for a motion to approve the minutes. Commissioner Heidi Carter moved approval and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs seconded, passing unanimously among members present.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Check Presentation: $1.5 Million DOE Energy Burden and Emissions Reduction Program (E-BERP)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Sustainability Manager Tobin Freed presented the $1.5 million U.S. Department of Energy grant awarded regionally with Orange and Granville Counties to retrofit approximately 200 owner- and renter-occupied homes in Justice40 disadvantaged census tracts (23–26 blocks in Durham County) over three years, with landlord agreements barring rent hikes or flipping. Commissioners Burns, Carter, and Howerton thanked staff and the Biden administration for advancing environmental, racial, and housing affordability equity.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations (Alzheimer's, Recovery Month, Welcoming Week, and Hispanic Heritage Month)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners issued five proclamations: World Alzheimer's Awareness Day 2024 (read by Commissioner Howerton; Susan Sewell of Dementia Inclusive Inc. highlighted the Sept. 20 forum), Durham Celebrates Recovery 2024 (read by Commissioner Carter; Recovery Community of Durham members invited residents to Sept. 27 festivities), Welcoming Week 2024 (with Immigrant & Refugee Coordinator Nayo, Maria Padilla, and Dr. Brett Lewis announcing the Sept. 14 international soccer tournament and resource fair), National Hispanic Heritage Month 2024 (read by Commissioner Jacobs), and Durham Recovery Month 2024 (read by Vice Chair Burns; Justice Services Director Roshana Parker and counselor George O'Brien spoke on substance use recovery).

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: No items were pulled from the consent agenda, though commissioners briefly praised $3 million and $2 million allocations in the package. Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton moved approval and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs seconded, passing unanimously 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Chin Page Road Lift Station, Force Main, and Gravity Main Engineering Report / EID
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Utilities staff presented the engineering report and Environmental Information Document for the ~$20 million Chin Page Road lift station project in the Northeast Creek basin near RTP and Highway 70, funded through a 20-year Clean Water State Revolving Fund loan (maximum 1.16% interest) plus $1,875,250 in enterprise fund balance for pre-construction, without anticipated sewer rate increases ahead of a Q2 2025 rate study. Commissioners Carter and Jacobs asked why no written comments had been received and confirmed the hearing was required for the state loan. After opening and closing the public hearing with zero speakers, Chair Allam confirmed no board vote was required.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) and (a)(4)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At the close of the regular agenda, Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton moved and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs seconded entering closed session for personnel matters (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6)) and economic development incentives/business location (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4)), passing 5-0. Returning at 05:14:27, Chair Allam reported no action was taken and direction was given to staff before adjourning.

votes.notes: Chair announced 'We are closed session 4-0' (transcribed as '40'); three members are named in the segment while the fourth present commissioner was not verbally identified.
votes.discussion_detail: Convening early prior to the 7:00 p.m. regular session, Chair Nida Allam sought a motion to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) for personnel matters. Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns moved and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs seconded, passing 4-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of September 9, 2024 Regular Session Agenda
votes.notes: Mover and seconder were not verbally named; Chair Allam had stepped away at 02:38:07.
votes.discussion_detail: After Chair Nida Allam stepped away briefly following the land acknowledgement, Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns presided and called for approval of the evening's agenda with no adjustments. The remaining four commissioners approved the agenda by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of Prior Meeting Minutes
votes.notes: Chair Allam returned to the dais later at 03:27:20.
votes.discussion_detail: With Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns still presiding during Chair Allam's temporary absence, Commissioner Heidi Carter moved to approve the minutes and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs seconded. The motion passed unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session Pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) and (a)(4)
votes.notes: Upon returning at 05:14:27, the Board reported no action taken and direction given to staff (on unanimous motion by Howerton, seconded by Jacobs).
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Allam called for a motion to enter closed session on two items: personnel matters under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) and economic development negotiations/location of industries under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4). Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton moved and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs seconded, passing unanimously 5-0.

meetings.title: BOCC Work Session September 3, 2024 (part 3)
meetings.executive_summary: In Part 3 of its September 3, 2024 work session, the Board of County Commissioners heard a GoDurham Access update showing improved on-time performance, a 40% reduction in no-shows, and the upcoming October launch of an East/North Durham microtransit pilot. Commissioners then engaged in a sharp debate over the City-County Planning Department's proposal to limit BOCC review of municipal annexations to cases outside the Urban Growth Boundary on an informational-only basis, with Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton objecting to the loss of citizen hearing opportunities while a majority favored structured work-session reviews paired with JCCPC tracking of inconsistent rezonings. The Board also provided initial feedback on updating the 2019/2020 Business Recruitment and Expansion incentive policy and received a 2025 Property Tax Reappraisal briefing showing Durham County's sales-to-assessment ratio at 61%.

agenda_items.title: GoDurham Access and Microtransit Consolidated Service Delivery Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transit staff reported early gains from GoDurham Access's new Spare scheduling software in August, reducing average trip duration from 32 to 26 minutes and cutting no-shows by 40%, and announced GoDurham Access will resume the fare-free East and North Durham microtransit pilot in October (forecasted at 61,000+ FY25 trips within a $705,000 Transit Plan budget). The consolidated model will also enable integration with Uber, Lyft, and private providers, plus on-demand trips to the Museum of Life and Science. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs welcomed the revival of the Transit Advisory Committee and asked about employer coordination in Treyburn, where Economic Development Director Andy Miracle confirmed ~32–33% of Corning's 450 workers reside in Durham County.

agenda_items.title: County Review Process for Municipal Annexation Cases (JCCPC Proposal)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Sara Young outlined the Joint City-County Planning Committee's three-part recommendation to stop JCCPC summary case lists and periodic staff comment emails on routine inside-UGB annexations, instead bringing annexations outside the Urban Growth Boundary to the BOCC as informational work-session items after Planning Commission review. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs pushed to keep JCCPC summary reports for inconsistent rezonings inside the UGB, while Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton objected that barring item-specific public hearings strips unincorporated county residents of representation. Chair Nida Allam, Commissioner Heidi Carter, and Jacobs endorsed formalizing out-of-UGB work-session reviews using written commissioner comment sheets to pass to City Council.

agenda_items.title: Business Recruitment and Expansion Policy Update (Initial Review)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic Development Director Andy Miracle and Manager Matt Filter reviewed the incentive program's track record (~$3 billion in projected private investment, $72 million in MWBE spending, $633 in taxable investment per county dollar) and sought high-level guidance on six updates ahead of October: codifying 25% MWBE goals and moving Community Benefits to a living appendix, simplifying policy language, legal review, evaluating award tiers, removing barriers (allowing PEOs, replacing MSA wage matching with Durham County's living wage, and weighting CapEx overperformance against job shortfalls), and adding a lane for headquarters projects. Commissioners voiced broad support while pressing for data on Durham-resident hiring, workforce diversity, family-friendly leave policies, and employer childcare partnerships.

agenda_items.title: 2025 Property Tax Reappraisal Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Tax Administration leadership and Commercial Supervisor James Roberts presented preliminary 2025 reappraisal market trends, noting Durham County's assessment-to-sales ratio dropped to 61% since 2019 as residential prices surged from ~$240,000 in 2019 to over $440,000 in 2024 (with sample homes rising 63% to 110%). Commercial data showed tight retail demand, a record 11.6% multifamily vacancy rate with slight rent declines, and office values projected to bottom in early 2025. Staff outlined the October Schedule of Values schedule, public inspection, and appointment-based taxpayer outreach, and commissioners requested posting the schedule online and presenting to City Council.

agenda_items.title: Board Directives Tracking Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff noted the live Board Directives spreadsheet link had been emailed to commissioners for review and questions. Commissioners raised no questions or edits before moving to adjourn.

disagreements.issue: County Input Process and Citizen Hearing Rights on Municipal Annexations
disagreements.summary: Following public comment opposing reduced county oversight of city annexations, commissioners disagreed on whether shifting to informational-only work-session reviews for out-of-UGB annexations adequately protected unincorporated county residents.
disagreements.side_a_position: Formalize BOCC work-session informational reviews for annexations outside the Urban Growth Boundary and forward written commissioner comments to City Council, while keeping JCCPC summary reports for inconsistent in-UGB rezonings.
side_a_arguments: The County lacks legal jurisdiction over municipal annexations, so holding a formal public hearing at the BOCC risks creating the legal illusion of county decision-making authority.

Replacing ad-hoc staff emails with structured work-session presentations and written commissioner comment sheets will actually increase commissioner preparation and formal record input to City Council.
disagreements.side_b_position: Reject limiting BOCC annexation reviews to informational work-session items where residents cannot speak during an item-specific public hearing.
side_b_arguments: Unincorporated county residents cannot vote for City Council and rely on the BOCC as their only elected voice when adjacent city annexations cause flooding or blasting damage.
Discontinuing formal public hearings on annexation cases effectively removes residents' opportunity to speak directly to the Board on specific projects.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote taken at the work session; Planning Director Sara Young agreed to retain JCCPC summary reports highlighting inconsistent rezonings inside the UGB, drop the periodic comment emails, and prepare written commissioner comment sheets for future out-of-UGB work-session items ahead of the next JCCPC meeting.

meetings.title: BOCC Work Session September 3, 2024 (part 2)
meetings.executive_summary: In Part 2 of the September 3, 2024 work session, county residents strongly opposed a Planning Department proposal to end BOCC review of municipal annexations inside the Urban Growth Boundary, urging commissioners to preserve their voice on adjacent city development impacts. Acting County Manager Claudia Hager walked commissioners through a comprehensive consent agenda—featuring the 500 East Main affordable housing 40-year HUD mortgage alignment, Justice Services Transition House renovations, election printing contracts, Durham Tech GO bond land and utility projects, and farmland conservation easements—without taking formal votes. The Board also received a detailed briefing from NC DIT Broadband Infrastructure Office's Jeffrey Brooks on a $1.42 million CAB broadband expansion requiring zero county match and heard the inaugural presentation from Durham County's new Office of Equitable Well-Being.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments on Municipal Annexation Review Proposals
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Four county residents—including Wanda Allen (citing 35 Junction Road residents on a polluted well), Heidi Grable of Northern Durham/Bahama, an in-person presenter citing flooding on Savannah Kilman's property, and virtual speaker Paige Polk of Southeast Durham (speaking at 00:18:39 after technical delays)—urged the BOCC to reject the Planning Department's memo discontinuing county review of annexations inside the Urban Growth Boundary (~70% of the county). Speakers argued unincorporated residents cannot vote for Durham's Mayor or City Council and suffer from blasting, deforestation, and stormwater runoff from city-annexed developments, demanding item-specific comment opportunities rather than general public comment only.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review for September Regular Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Acting County Manager Claudia Hager and staff reviewed upcoming consent items, including the DOE E-BERP sustainability grant (24-0328), 500 East Main affordable housing documents aligning the county mortgage to HUD's 40-year term while retaining year-40 right of first refusal (24-0452), a $246,000 DOJ Sheriff's opioid jail-transition grant (24-0453), and $422,428 for Justice Services Transition House design evaluation (24-0456), where Commissioner Wendy Jacobs questioned the cost of renovating versus replacing the facility before the Dec. 31 ARPA deadline. Staff also covered Board of Elections ballot/mailing amendments (24-0519, 24-0520), Public Health grants and blood pressure cuffs (24-0521–0523, 24-0558–0559), Durham Tech GO bond land/police/utility/roof items (24-0539, 24-0540, 24-0542), RDU FAA pass-through grants (24-0541, 24-0548), 15-501/Garrett Rd DOT easements (24-0546), two farmland conservation easements (24-0552), Mirla restaurant lease extension (24-0564), and pre-construction funding for Project BUILD and the Sheriff's Training Facility (24-0573, 24-0574).

agenda_items.title: 24-0555: Broadband Infrastructure Funds Update (NC DIT CAB & BEAD Programs)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jeffrey Brooks of the NC DIT Broadband Infrastructure Office, alongside Acting Manager Hager and CIO Greg Marrow, updated commissioners on broadband expansion, noting 1,700 Durham County locations funded via GREAT grants with Lumos and Frontier and presenting GIS address-level maps of remaining unserved households. Brooks unveiled a CAB 2.0 opportunity allocating $500,000 in state-held match toward up to a $1.42 million fiber buildout in Durham County with a September 9 application deadline and zero county funding required, ahead of $1.57 billion in federal BEAD and Digital Equity funds in 2025–2026. Commissioners Carter, Jacobs, and Burns discussed utility pole make-ready fees, shared conduit/dig-once hurdles, and rural broadband health and education equity.

agenda_items.title: Office of Equitable Well-Being Inaugural Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief of Staff Shannon Trapp, Equitable Well-Being Director Dr. Brent Lewis, Manager Cassandra Kiger, and Racial Equity Analyst Robert Espinoza introduced the new office's mission, values, and internal/external initiatives. Staff highlighted training over 320 county employees in DEIB 101, launching a 201 LMS course and 25-hour departmental expert track, assigning each staff member to consult with seven county departments, hosting 22 heritage/cultural programs, launching five Employee Resource Groups (ERGs), developing a GARE racial equity action plan and decision-making checklist for the Board, and hosting a Spanish language access simulation. Commissioners praised the breadth of work and urged incorporating the GARE checklist into future Board policy and budget decisions.

meetings.title: BOCC Regular Meeting August 26, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Nida Allam presided over the brief August 26, 2024 Board of County Commissioners regular session, reporting out of an earlier closed session with no action taken and a 5-0 vote to seal those minutes. After approving the August 5 and August 12 minutes 5-0 and presenting a proclamation for Leaders in Equitable Economic Development Month, the board voted 5-0 to add four opioid/recovery-related and high school dropout-age legislative goals for NCACC submission to the consent agenda before adopting the consent agenda unanimously. Commissioners then made appointments to five advisory boards and adjourned into a second closed session on personnel and national opioid litigation.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Report, Public Charge, Land Acknowledgment, Pledge, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Nida Allam opened the meeting and reported that the board met in closed session prior to regular session, took no action, and voted unanimously to seal the minutes. Following the land acknowledgment and Pledge of Allegiance, Clerk Monica Wallace read announcements on the RISE Assessment Center forum, public health nutrition workshops, MED Week sponsorships, COVID-19 vaccines, and Labor Day closures, and Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns recognized Women's Equality Day.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (August 5, 2024 Work Session and August 12, 2024 Regular Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Wendy Jacobs moved and Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns seconded approval of the August 5, 2024 work session and August 12, 2024 regular session minutes. The motion passed unanimously 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamation: Leaders in Equitable Economic Development Month 2024
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter read a proclamation honoring Black-owned and historically underutilized businesses in Durham, referencing Black Wall Street and Hayti. Chief of Staff Shannon Trapp highlighted a recent HUB meet-and-greet with over 140 registrants, upcoming October MED Week events, and the MWBE Evolution cohort, while commissioners praised General Services Director Motiryo Keambiroiro for achieving roughly 40% MWBE participation against the county's 25% goal.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Adjustment and Adoption of Consent Agenda (Including NCACC Legislative Goals)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Wendy Jacobs apologized for skipping agenda adjustments earlier and requested adding NCACC legislative goals to the consent agenda so they could meet the association's submission deadline: expanding Good Samaritan drug-overdose immunity, promoting opioid harm reduction/treatment, requiring NARR certification and prohibiting medication barriers in recovery housing, and requiring jails to assess and treat opioid use disorder with post-release care coordination. Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns added a previously supported goal to raise North Carolina's high school dropout age from 16 to 18. The board voted 5-0 to add the legislative goals and 5-0 to adopt the consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Curtis Massey tallied the board's ballots and announced appointments to the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission (John Lawler), Criminal Justice Advisory Committee (Tanya Dixon), Dangerous Dog Appeal Board (Elizabeth Wier and Brian Mulligan), Environmental Affairs Board (Larry Hall and Stone Yan), and Library Board of Trustees (Ivanhoe Francis and Leah Josephson). Commissioners praised the high caliber of applicants and Clerk Wallace confirmed unappointed applications stay on file for one year.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Personnel and National Opioid Litigation)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) for a personnel matter and N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with legal counsel regarding the national opioid litigation.

She reported for the clerk's record that Commissioner Wendy Jacobs moved to seal the closed session minutes, Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns seconded, and the motion passed unanimously 5-0.

meetings.title: BOCC Regular meeting August 12, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: At its August 12, 2024 regular meeting, the Board of County Commissioners reported out from an earlier closed session with no action taken, approved the July 8 minutes 5-0, and presented four ceremonial recognitions for Purple Heart Month, Child Support Awareness Month, Breastfeeding Family-Friendly Community Month, and the Bull City Express Track Club's Junior Olympic All-Americans alongside NACo achievement awards. Commissioners passed the consent agenda 5-0 after pulling two contracts, approved item 24-0475 ($139,700 for the Museum of Durham History) 4-0 with Chair Nida Allam abstaining, and tabled item 24-0473 (Alliance Health) until the September work session. Following a public hearing with no speakers, the Board unanimously adopted UDO Text Amendment TC2400001 (Omnibus 19) and its consistency statement 5-0 and announced an appointment to the Durham Workforce Development Board.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Report-Out, Call to Order, Agenda Adjustments, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Nida Allam reported the Board had met in closed session and given direction to staff with no action taken, delivered the public charge and land acknowledgement, and had Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns lead the Pledge of Allegiance. Commissioner Heidi Carter requested pulling consent item 24-0473 (Alliance Health). Clerk Monica Wallace and commissioners shared announcements including Purple Heart Month, Low Income Homeowners Relief Program, Kids Voting, Dr. Rod Jenkins completing his UNC PhD, the new DPS Superintendent's swearing-in, Miami Blvd/Page Rd rezoning meetings, and Renegade Durham affordable housing applications opening with an 86-child onsite daycare.

agenda_items.title: Approval of July 8, 2024 Regular Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Allam called for approval of the July 8, 2024 regular session minutes. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs moved approval and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton seconded, passing unanimously 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations, Track Club Resolution, and NACo Awards
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners issued proclamations for Purple Heart Month 2024 (read by Commissioner Howerton, noting a DoD Vietnam War commemoration award for Veterans Services), Child Support Awareness Month 2024 (read by Commissioner Jacobs, highlighting $15.3 million collected across 7,576 cases and eCourts integration), and Breastfeeding Family-Friendly Community Month 2024 (read by Chair Allam, where Breastfeed Durham noted an 8% drop in Durham's infant mortality rate and Duke Regional's Baby-Friendly designation, prompting discussion of Black maternal/infant disparities and Family Connects). Vice Chair Burns read a resolution honoring Bull City Express Track Club athletes and coaches Omar Beasley and James Carter for their USATF Junior Olympic All-American honors, and staff were recognized for national NACo awards.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Items 24-0473 and 24-0475)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Allam noted four consent items added since the work session (24-048*, 24-050*, 24-0514, and 24-0525), pulled item 24-0475 for her abstention, and confirmed item 24-0473 was pulled. Commissioner Heidi Carter moved and Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns seconded approval of the remainder of the consent agenda, passing 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 24-0475: FY 2025 Contract with Museum of Durham History ($139,700)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered pulled consent item 24-0475 approving the FY 2025 contract with the Museum of Durham History in the amount of $139,700. Four commissioners voted aye while Chair Nida Allam abstained, passing the item 4-0 with one abstention.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 24-0473: Contract with Alliance Health
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Curtis Massey asked the Board to table item 24-0473 until the next regular session. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs noted the Board had already directed at its work session to hold the contract until Alliance Health returned with a budget at the September work session, and the Board deferred the item accordingly without objection.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Tabled / Deferred to September work session without objection

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment TC2400001 (Omnibus 19)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Robin Schultz presented Omnibus 19 (TC2400001), a staff-initiated technical amendment to 11 UDO articles bringing the ordinance into compliance with state law (street renaming notices, triplexes/quadplexes under the NC Residential Building Code, NCDEQ purview), correcting post-SCAD incongruities (removing required parking mentions, clarifying 2+ ADU site plan requirements, height calculations, CN density, and preserving boundary buffers during mass grading), and fixing minor inconsistencies. After a public hearing with no speakers, the Board unanimously adopted both the UDO amendment ordinance and the N.C.G.S. 160D-605 consistency statement 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Curtis Massey announced the Board's appointment to the Durham Workforce Development Board (first name Sebastian, surname partially inaudible in transcript) before the Board voted to adjourn.

meetings.title: BOCC Work Session August 5, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: In the afternoon portion of the August 5, 2024 work session presided over by Chair Nida Allam, the Board heard a presentation from Aging Well Durham on its newly redesigned 2024 comprehensive nine-domain Age-Friendly Durham plan and acknowledged an oversight in omitting its funding from the adopted budget. County staff provided capital project and ARPA compliance updates covering rising construction costs, a $3.7 million transitional housing estimate, the $53 million joint City-County backup 911/EOC project, a $750,000 digital equity grant, and forthcoming Durham Public Schools capital and Pre-K interlocal agreements. The Board suspended its rules and voted 4-0 to appoint Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns as the NCACC conference voting delegate and Commissioner Heidi Carter as alternate. Commissioners also reviewed consent agenda contracts—calling for stronger performance metrics on Hayti Reborn and deferring the Alliance Health contract pending detailed budget data—before discussing non-congregate housing under the Familiar Faces Initiative and adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Aging Well Durham Comprehensive Aging Plan Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Representatives from Aging Well Durham (the County's Home and Community Care Block Grant advisory committee and backbone organization) presented the 2024 Comprehensive Aging Plan covering nine age-friendly domains for adults 50+ and adults 18+ with disabilities. Commissioners discussed pedestrian crossing and traffic signal safety for seniors, pledged to involve Aging Well Durham in transit planning, and apologized for omitting the organization's funding from the adopted FY24-25 budget with plans to address it at the next meeting.

agenda_items.title: County Capital Projects and Transitional Housing Cost Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff updated commissioners on post-COVID construction cost escalation across county capital projects, including the animal shelter, Sheriff's Training Facility, Junction Road Fleet Maintenance Facility, and the joint City-County backup 911 call center/EOC ($53 million total project budget, allocated $28 million City and $24 million County under current ILAs). Staff highlighted a new $3.7 million cost estimate for transitional wraparound housing and noted they were exploring purchasing an existing home with ARPA funds to move quickly.

agenda_items.title: ARPA Compliance, Digital Equity, DPS ILAs, and Land Trust RFP Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County compliance staff reported on ARPA oversight across major investments, including a $750,000 City digital equity partnership running through September 30, 2026 with over 75% directed to internet service provision. Staff noted they completed compliance due diligence on ARPA-funded Durham Public Schools capital and Pre-K projects to bring ILAs back this month, and received two qualified proposals in response to the Land Trust investment program RFPs.

agenda_items.title: NCACC Conference Voting Delegate Appointment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Nida Allam introduced the item to designate Durham County's voting delegate and alternate for the upcoming North Carolina Association of County Commissioners (NCACC) conference. The Board first voted 4-0 to suspend its rules and then voted 4-0 to appoint Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns as voting delegate and Commissioner Heidi Carter as alternate.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review: Hayti Reborn KPIs and Alliance Health Contract Deferral
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed upcoming consent agenda items including 24-0392, 24-0420, 24-0423, 24-0427, and 24-0428. Commissioner Heidi Carter sought reassurance on periodic reporting for the Hayti Reborn contract amendment, while Chair Nida Allam reiterated her unpaid request for a detailed personnel expense breakdown and concrete numeric service targets modeled on the digital equity contract. On the Alliance Health contract, commissioners agreed to hold approval for three weeks until Alliance supplies a detailed budget, provided ongoing services are not interrupted.

agenda_items.title: Familiar Faces Initiative, Non-Congregate Housing, and Urban Ministries Outreach
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A commissioner highlighted discussions from the Familiar Faces Initiative regarding the urgent need for non-congregate pallet housing for individuals with severe, complex needs, and noted ongoing meetings with Urban Ministries of Durham (UMD) to stay ahead of budget needs. Chair Nida Allam added that formal appointments to the joint working committee—with Commissioner Heidi Carter serving as County liaison alongside Council Member Javiera Caballero—would be voted on at the next meeting before adjourning.

votes.item_title: Suspend the Rules to Consider NCACC Voting Delegate Appointment
votes.notes: Passed 4-0 by voice vote; Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns is not recorded speaking during this session.
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Nida Allam noted the Board needed to suspend the rules during the work session in order to take action on appointing the NCACC conference voting delegate and alternate. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs moved to suspend the rules, Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton seconded, and the motion passed 4-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Appoint Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns as NCACC Voting Delegate and Commissioner Heidi Carter as Alternate
votes.notes: Both motions confirmed as passing 4-0 at 01:54:33.
votes.discussion_detail: Following suspension of the rules, Chair Nida Allam entertained a motion to appoint Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns as the County's voting delegate and Commissioner Heidi Carter as alternate for the NCACC conference. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs moved approval, Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton seconded, and the motion passed 4-0 by voice vote.

meetings.title: BOCC Regular Meeting July 08, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Nida Allam presided over the July 8, 2024 Board of County Commissioners regular meeting, the Board's sole meeting for July prior to its summer recess. After commissioner updates on the Triangle Mobility Hub RAISE grant, MWBE certification, and economic development ROI ($633 returned per tax incentive dollar) and citizen comments regarding unpaid subcontractor invoices owed by prime consultant HDR to Kitech, the Board approved prior minutes 5-0 and recognized 4-H Youth Voice delegate Amanda Davis. Following public hearings, the Board voted 5-0 to approve two economic development performance-based incentive agreements: $170,000 for Iona's Project High Power headquarters (203 jobs, $10 million investment) and $930,000 for Science Corporation's Project Foundry expansion ($65 million investment, 54 jobs). The meeting concluded with board and commission appointment announcements and a unanimous vote to enter closed session regarding national opioid litigation.

agenda_items.title: Opening Ceremonies, Announcements, and Commissioner Reports
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Nida Allam read the public charge and land acknowledgement, Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns led the Pledge of Allegiance, and Clerk Monica Wallace shared community announcements (DSS fan/AC distribution, Disability Pride Month events, and a Stagville descendants panel). Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton highlighted GoTriangle's Triangle Mobility Hub RAISE grant award for regional transit, Commissioner Wendy Jacobs discussed MWBE certification efforts, and Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns noted that County economic development incentives return $633 for every $1 invested.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments: Unpaid Subcontractor Invoices (Kitech / HDR)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A representative of Kitech addressed the Board regarding two overdue invoices totaling nearly $50,000 ($33,478 outstanding 138 days and $15,152.35 outstanding 160 days) owed by prime consultant HDR on a County project despite timely billing. Chair Nida Allam apologized for the inconvenience and stated the County Manager would follow up with HDR to determine why payment had been delayed.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Nida Allam presented one work session and two regular session sets of meeting minutes for approval. Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton moved approval, Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns seconded, and the Board approved the minutes 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Item: Introduction of 2024 4-H Youth Voice Delegate Amanda Davis
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham County Cooperative Extension introduced rising 10th grader Amanda Davis as Durham County's 2024 NCACC Youth Voice 4-H delegate, noting her leadership in 4-H and Kids Voting. Davis addressed the Board and posed for a group photo with commissioners.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Nida Allam opened the lengthy pre-recess consent agenda for questions without pulling items unless needed. Commissioner Heidi Carter asked a question on item 24-0388 (lease approval), and commissioners also discussed the County strategic plan and food security grants administered by Communities in Partnership.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Project High Power (Iona) Performance-Based Incentive Award
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic Development Manager Matt Gladdek presented a $170,000 performance-based incentive for Iona's new office headquarters (Project High Power), projecting 203 jobs and $10 million in investment over five years, with Iona CFO Derek Rush and Greater Durham Chamber of Commerce remarks during the public hearing. Following the hearing, the Board voted 5-0 to approve the $170,000 award and authorize the County Manager to negotiate and execute the performance agreement.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Project Foundry (Science Corporation) Performance-Based Incentive Award
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented a $930,000 performance-based incentive award for Science Corporation's $65 million Foundry expansion in Durham County (brain-computer interface medical technology creating 54 jobs), with Operations Manager John Beck noting a CHIPS and Science Act pre-application and Durham Chamber representatives speaking in support. After closing the public hearing, the Board voted 5-0 to approve the $930,000 award and authorize the County Manager to negotiate and execute the agreement.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments and Closed Session (National Opioid Litigation)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Attorney Massey read board and commission appointment results (including Derek McGee to the Memorial Stadium Authority), and Chair Nida Allam thanked all applicants. The Board then voted unanimously by voice vote to adjourn into closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to discuss the national opioid litigation.

votes.item_title: Approval of Work Session and Regular Session Meeting Minutes
votes.notes: Transcript records mover as 'commissioner hardin' (Brenda A. Howerton).
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Nida Allam requested approval of one set of work session minutes and two sets of regular session minutes. Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton moved approval, Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns seconded, and the motion passed 5-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approve $170,000 Performance-Based Incentive Award for Project High Power (Iona) and Authorize Agreement Execution
votes.notes: Incentive tied to annual verification of 203 jobs, ~$10M investment, and property tax payments at least twice the scheduled payout.
votes.discussion_detail: After closing the public hearing for Project High Power, Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton moved and Commissioner Heidi Carter seconded approval of the $170,000 performance-based award to Iona, amended to explicitly authorize the County Manager to negotiate and execute the agreement. Both mover and seconder accepted the amendment, and the motion passed 5-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approve $930,000 Performance-Based Incentive Award for Project Foundry (Science Corporation) and Authorize Agreement Execution
votes.notes: Incentive covers 54 new jobs (67% requiring a two-year degree or less) and $65M capital investment.
votes.discussion_detail: Following the public hearing on Science Corporation's $65 million Project Foundry expansion, Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns moved and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs seconded approval of the $930,000 award and authorization for the County Manager to negotiate and execute the performance agreement. The motion passed 5-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Enter Closed Session Pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) (National Opioid Litigation)
votes.notes: All five commissioners were seated and voted 5-0 on prior items in the meeting.
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Nida Allam read the statutory citation (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3)) to enter closed session regarding the national opioid litigation. Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton moved, Commissioner Wendy Jacobs seconded, and the motion carried unanimously by voice vote.
