meetings.title: BOCC Regular Session for Monday, June 24, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns presided over the June 24, 2024 Board of County Commissioners regular session alongside only Commissioner Heidi Carter, as the remaining three commissioners were absent and the board lacked a quorum. Consequently, all formal action items—including minute approvals, the consent agenda, excused absences, a public hearing, and closed session—were deferred to the July 8, 2024 meeting. During the informational and ceremonial portion of the evening, Vice Chair Burns and Commissioner Carter recognized the Office of Emergency Services Community Paramedicine Program for winning a CPI Security/WRAL Community Impact Award and issued a proclamation honoring Durham Refugee Day 2024.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, Land Acknowledgment, Pledge, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns opened the meeting noting the absence of a quorum and skipped agenda adjustments. Clerk Monica Wallace read announcements including applications for the new RISE Assessment Center advisory board, Durham Refugee Day, Welcome Baby's School is Cool celebration, library cooling centers, the county tax bill calculator, and Durham Pre-K enrollment. Vice Chair Burns highlighted that the RISE Assessment Center is now open—countering earlier critics who claimed it was a jail—with a diversion specialist helping divert over 3,000 youth annually, and promoted Durham Success Summit applications in light of recent youth gun violence.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Recognition: OES Community Paramedicine Program Community Impact Award
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant County Manager Dwayne Brinson, OES Director Lockheart, Captain Helen Tripp, and Community Paramedic Lisa Smith recognized Durham County EMS for receiving the CPI Security/WRAL Community Impact Award—and donating its $1,000 prize to the Vic Pearson Memorial Fund—for their field-based Medication for Opioid Use Disorder (buprenorphine) induction and Narcan outreach program, which has completed 26 inductions since May 2023. Commissioner Heidi Carter and Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns praised the life-saving harm reduction initiative and EMS's proactive equipment planning.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamation: Durham Refugee Day 2024
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter read a proclamation declaring June 29, 2024 as Durham Refugee Day. Immigrant and Refugee Affairs Coordinator Nao introduced refugee leader and new U.S. citizen Osman Abdullahi, who thanked Durham County for welcoming newcomers, and both Vice Chair Burns and Commissioner Carter reaffirmed Durham's commitment to supporting immigrant and refugee families.

agenda_items.title: Lack of Quorum Determination and Deferral of Action Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After completing all ceremonial recognitions, Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns announced on advice of the clerk that the board had gone as far as legally possible without a quorum (only Burns and Carter present). All voting items—including minutes, consent agenda, excused absences, public hearing, and closed session—were deferred to the July 8, 2024 meeting, and the gathering ended.

meetings.title: BOCC Regular Meeting June 10, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Nida Allam presided over the June 10, 2024 regular meeting, which opened with a closed-session report (no action taken), public charge, land acknowledgement, and clerk announcements before the Board approved its May 28, 2024 minutes 5-0. Commissioners honored winners of the DECO On the Go bus-design art contest and heard Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton read a resolution signed by all commissioners supporting the 2029 World University Games across Durham venues. In remarks celebrating adoption of the historic $966 million FY 2024-25 budget, commissioners highlighted over $208 million in total Durham Public Schools funding (including $74.36 million in new investments, classified/certified raises, master's pay restoration, and half of the hard-to-fill EC teacher supplement), expanded Durham Pre-K funding exceeding $9 million, eviction diversion raised from $180,000 to $780,000, $112 million for social services, and nearly $100 million for public safety. With no consent agenda items pulled, the Board voted 5-0 to enter closed session regarding economic development incentives.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Report, Opening Ceremonies, and Community Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Nida Allam reported no action was taken in closed session, read the public charge and land acknowledgement, asked Commissioner Wendy Jacobs to lead the Pledge of Allegiance, and invited attendees to sign appreciation cards and enjoy cupcakes for County budget staff. Clerk Wallace read announcements regarding Renegade downtown housing, 2024 Innovate Durham Demo Day, and the City-County Planning interactive map on engagedurham.com.

agenda_items.title: Approval of May 28, 2024 Regular Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Nida Allam presented the May 28, 2024 regular session minutes for approval with no requested adjustments. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs moved approval, Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns seconded, and the motion passed 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Item: DECO On the Go Design Contest Winners
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff recognized youth and adult art contest winners for the DECO On the Go mobile engagement vehicle, including youth winners Dalia Lewis (third place) and Jenny (first place) and adult winners Aaron (third place), Brandon Hampton (second place), and the first-place two-sided bus design winner.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Supporting the 2029 World University Games
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Kimberly Sowell and Hill Carrow presented a resolution expressing full County support for hosting the 2029 World University Games (July 11-22, 2029) across North Carolina venues including Duke University, NCCU, and Durham Bulls Athletic Park. Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton read the resolution—signed by all commissioners—citing 10,000 participants from 150 countries, up to 600,000 spectators, and $150-$350 million in projected regional economic impact.

agenda_items.title: FY 2024-25 Budget Adoption Remarks and Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners delivered celebratory yet sober remarks on adopting the $966 million FY 2024-25 budget, emphasizing historic school investments (> $208 million for DPS, full certified/classified raises, master's pay, half of the EC/hard-to-fill supplement, and >$9 million for Durham Pre-K including Murray-Massenburg), eviction diversion rising from $180,000 to $780,000, $750,000 for low-income homeowner tax relief, $112 million for social services, and nearly $100 million for public safety. Speakers thanked County Manager Kimberly Sowell, Deputy Manager Claudia Hager, budget staff, department heads, and advocates (DAE, People's Alliance) while warning that future fiscal sustainability requires stronger North Carolina General Assembly school funding; Chair Allam also noted no consent agenda items were pulled.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / Vote occurred prior to remark timestamps in truncated segment

agenda_items.title: Closed Session: Economic Development Incentives
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Nida Allam read the statutory authority under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) to enter closed session to discuss matters relating to the location or expansion of businesses and tentative economic development incentives. Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns moved approval, Commissioner Wendy Jacobs seconded, and the Board voted 5-0 to enter closed session.

votes.item_title: Approval of May 28, 2024 Regular Session Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Nida Allam asked for adjustments or a motion to approve the May 28, 2024 regular session minutes. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs moved approval, Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns seconded, and the motion passed 5-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Enter Closed Session Pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) (Economic Development Incentives)
votes.discussion_detail: Following Manager Sowell's closing remarks, Chair Nida Allam read the closed-session citation under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) regarding potential business location/expansion incentives. Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns moved to enter closed session, Commissioner Wendy Jacobs seconded, and the motion passed 5-0 by voice vote.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners - FY 2024-25 Budget Work Session #4 - Wednesday, June 4, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns presided over FY 2024-25 Budget Work Session #4 on June 4, 2024, opening with youth violence prevention and Project Build program reviews where Director Harris reported third-party evaluations and limited non-JCPC funding ($19,000) for ages 18-21, drawing sharp criticism from Burns over missing budget details and City Council funding gaps. Budget Director Keith Lane and County Manager Dr. Kimberly Sowell then presented a creative financing package for Durham Public Schools—combining a $19.8 million general fund increase, $6 million in ARPA funds, and $4 million shifted from current capital to current expense—funding nearly all of DPS's $27.4 million request aside from a late $1.39 million addition for hard-to-fill positions. Final deliberations revealed sharp divisions on the dais: Commissioner Wendy Jacobs supported extraordinary action for public schools, Vice Chair Burns pledged to vote yes while demanding accountability from DPS on student safety, and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton expressed deep sadness over the tax burden on low-to-middle-income residents and skepticism over school outcomes. The session ended after a brief procedural clash over Howerton's request to schedule a September presentation on a Zafiqo Temple land deal.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Public Charge, and Land Acknowledgement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns opened FY 2024-25 Budget Work Session #4, clarifying it was a work session rather than a special meeting, and read the Board's public charge and land acknowledgement.

agenda_items.title: Youth Violence Prevention and Project Build Budget & Evaluation Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Director Harris presented third-party program evaluation updates and data on gun violence in target areas (Cornwallis and Fayetteville Street) and Project Build / My Brother's Keeper initiatives, noting Project Build relies on $130,000 in JCPC funds restricted to ages 14-17 and only $19,000 for ages 18-21. Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns criticized the lack of a line-item budget presentation, called for stronger outreach and data transparency, and sharply faulted City Council for rejecting summer camp funding requests while staff promised to send requested budget figures and explore internal reallocations.

agenda_items.title: FY 2024-25 Budget Balancing and Durham Public Schools Financing Package
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Dr. Kimberly Sowell and Budget Director Keith Lane presented revised budget-balancing options ahead of the June 10 adoption vote to support Durham Public Schools while limiting property tax increases. The proposed package combined a $19.8 million general fund increase, $6 million in ARPA funds, and $4 million shifted from current capital (dropping from $6 million to $2 million) to current expense, covering DPS's $27.4 million request except for the Board of Education's late $1.39 million addition for hard-to-fill positions.

agenda_items.title: Commissioner Final Budget Deliberations and Agenda Scheduling Dispute
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners offered candid closing perspectives on the compromise budget: Commissioner Wendy Jacobs supported extraordinary crisis action to strengthen schools, Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns announced she would vote yes while holding DPS accountable for unaddressed student safety emails, and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton voiced deep sadness over the tax impact on low- and middle-income residents and doubted student outcomes would improve. At 01:57:25, Howerton's request to place a September presentation on a Zafiqo Temple land deal on a future agenda drew pushback over introducing non-budget matters, and Vice Chair Burns referred the request to board leadership and adjourned the meeting.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners - FY 2024-25 Budget Work Session #4 - Wednesday, June 4, 2024
disagreements.issue: FY 2024-25 Property Tax Burden and Durham Public Schools Funding Accountability
disagreements.summary: Commissioners split sharply in tone and assessment over the proposed FY 2024-25 budget compromise, weighing tax impacts on lower-income residents and DPS governance concerns against urgent school funding needs.
disagreements.side_a_position: Express deep dissatisfaction with the tax burden on low-to-middle-income residents and skepticism over DPS outcomes despite record funding
side_a_arguments: The resulting property tax increase burdens low- and middle-income households while higher-income residents are insulated.
DPS has not demonstrated a strategy to improve student outcomes next year or avoid returning with a $25M+ gap in 2025.
disagreements.side_b_position: Support the compromise school funding package as necessary crisis action while pushing for DPS accountability
side_b_arguments: Thriving public schools are essential to Durham's economy, safety, and families, requiring extraordinary action during a crisis.
Supporting the budget can coexist with demanding accountability from the School Board on child safety and financial management.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote taken at Work Session #4; County Manager Dr. Kimberly Sowell noted the compromise left everyone partly unsatisfied while minimizing the property tax rate increase ahead of the June 10 vote.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners - FY 2024-25 Budget Work Session #4 - Wednesday, June 4, 2024
disagreements.issue: Scheduling Non-Budget Zafiqo Temple Presentation During Budget Work Session
disagreements.summary: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton sought to schedule a future September presentation on a Zafiqo Temple land deal at the close of the final budget work session, prompting pushback that non-budget items were inappropriate in the current financial climate and budget session.
disagreements.side_a_position: Place the Zafiqo Temple land deal community presentation on a September agenda
side_a_arguments: Community members undertaking the land deal between Raleigh and Durham requested an opportunity to present to the Board.
disagreements.side_b_position: Defer non-budget presentation requests out of the budget work session to board leadership
side_b_arguments: A presentation involving a land deal is unrelated to the FY 2024-25 budget and inappropriate given the tight financial climate.
disagreements.resolution: Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns noted the request would be discussed in leadership/agenda planning and adjourned the budget work session.

meetings.title: BOCC Work Session June 3, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns presided over the June 3, 2024 BOCC work session in Chair Nida Allam's absence, opening with public comments on Charles Hamilton Houston Foundation funding, retiree health insurance premiums, Southeast Durham blasting and Falls Lake sediment pollution, and full funding for Durham Public Schools. During consent agenda review, commissioners debated the proposed $5 million Emergency Operations Center and backup 911 call center prior to resolving primary 911 unification, and suspended the rules to approve a $1,696,670 ARPA capital amendment for the Slater Road Lift Station (updated to 4-0). The board also received presentations on the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) rewrite—where commissioners challenged assumptions that higher density lowers rents and questioned whether rural Durham residents are heard—Project Access of Durham County's 15-year safety-net impact, and the draft Durham County Forward 2025–2029 Strategic Plan.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, Land Acknowledgment, and Public Comment Period
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns opened the work session and heard public comments from six speakers: DeWarren Langley requesting $25,000 for the Charles Hamilton Houston Foundation; retired EMS Chief Brandon Mitchell urging the board to hold under-65 retirees harmless from rising healthcare premiums; Preserve Rural Durham members Pamela Andrews, Wanda Allen, and Donna Stainback raising alarms over Virgil Road annexation, blasting damage to homes, red sediment runoff into Lick Creek and Falls Lake, and exclusion from UDO outreach; and parent/researcher Valerie Lewis urging full funding of the Durham Public Schools budget request.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review (Transit Work Program, Historical Marker Easement, EOC/911 Center, and Debt Capacity)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Claudia Hager walked through consent items including the FY25 Durham Annual Transit Work Program (with performance tracker and Museum of Life and Science shuttle/microtransit), election software maintenance, utility and Hayti historical marker easements at Stanford L. Warren Library, year-end personnel transfers, the Durham REPAIR rail-crossing grant, a $241,500 Duke Endowment fatherhood grant, Granicus maintenance, and NACo voting delegate selection. Under item 24-0319 ($5M LOBs for a new Emergency Operations Center and shared City-County backup 911 center), Commissioner Wendy Jacobs and Vice Chair Burns pressed staff on why the county had not yet merged primary 911 centers or consulted Sheriff Birkhead and state DIT; staff explained Duke University's December 2026 termination of the city's backup lease and COVID EOC inadequacies drove the schedule. Budget Director Keith Lane also explained LOBs asset limits and AAA bond rating constraints.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / Work session review (except Slater Road below)

agenda_items.title: Suspension of Rules and Approval of Capital Project Amendment 24CPA00028 (Slater Road Lift Station)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Because of time-sensitive ARPA deadlines, the board voted 3-0 to suspend its rules and approved Capital Project Amendment 24CPA00028 appropriating $1,696,670 in ARPA fund balance for the Slater Road Lift Station, Force Main, and Outfall project and authorizing a $1,615,187 preconstruction contract with Crowder Construction Company. Upon Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton returning to the dais seconds later, Vice Chair Burns updated the final approval vote to 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) Rewrite: Code Audit, Economic Modeling, and Equitable Engagement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant Planning Director Bo Dobrzenski, Code Studio principal Colin Scarff, and Equitable Engagement Consultant Dr. ToNola Allen presented the UDO rewrite framework, proposing to streamline 17 articles into 10, consolidate zoning districts aligned with the Comprehensive Plan's Place Type map, focus on built form rather than units-per-acre density caps, and recruit community engagement ambassadors. Economic pro formas suggested allowing multiplexes with reduced square footage and parking could lower modeled rents from $3,500 to $2,000/month. However, Commissioner Heidi Carter sought clarity on Preserve Rural Durham's concerns and density regulation, while Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns strongly disputed that increased density lowers housing costs in booming tech hubs like Durham and warned that rural and Southeast Durham residents feel ignored despite engagement efforts.

agenda_items.title: Presentation: Project Access of Durham County (15+ Years of Donated Specialty Care)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Executive Director Sally Wilson and Board Chair Dr. John Paat presented Project Access of Durham County's 15-year safety-net impact, noting over 25,000 referrals from Lincoln Community Health Center, ~43,000 episodes of donated specialty care worth nearly $100 million, 77,000 prescriptions filled, and a 37% reduction in avoidable emergency department utilization. Commissioners Wendy Jacobs, Heidi Carter, Brenda A. Howerton, and Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns commended the program's high appointment attendance rate and asked about Medicaid expansion impacts, Duke Health savings data, homeless medical respite permanent housing, and County funding trends ($408,400 base plus respite support).

agenda_items.title: Strategic Plan Update: Durham County Forward 2025–2029
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Strategy and Performance Director Josh Edwards and Chief of Staff Shannon Trapp presented the final draft of the homegrown 2025–2029 Strategic Plan, featuring seven focus areas, 23 objectives, 74 initiatives, and ~70 streamlined performance metrics (replacing ~700 legacy ClearPoint measures), scheduled for formal adoption on June 24. Commissioners praised the internal staff-led process, clearer visual design, and enhanced environmental focus, while requesting strong integration into agenda action forms and the budget book and expressing concern over removing 'Commitment' from core values.

agenda_items.title: Introduction of Summer Interns, Commissioner Directives, Agenda Prep, and Lunch Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant to the County Manager Danielle Bryant introduced five summer interns (two county-funded and three Duke-funded) from Duke, UNC, and Penn. Chief of Staff Shannon Trapp briefly reviewed the 2024 commissioner directives tracker with Commissioner Wendy Jacobs noting outstanding 2023 items, before Vice Chair Burns adjourned the morning work session for lunch ahead of the 1:30 PM budget session.

votes.item_title: Motion to Suspend the Rules for Immediate Action on Capital Project Amendment 24CPA00028 (Slater Road Lift Station)
votes.notes: Chair Nida Allam was absent; Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton was temporarily away from the dais during the rules-suspension vote and returned immediately after the main motion.
votes.discussion_detail: At the close of consent agenda review, County Manager Claudia Hager reminded the board that item 24-0285 (Slater Road Lift Station ARPA capital project amendment) was time-sensitive and required immediate action at the work session. After a brief lighthearted exchange with the County Attorney, Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns called for a motion to suspend the rules. A motion and second were made by the three commissioners present on the dais (Burns, Jacobs, and Carter), passing 3-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of Capital Project Amendment No. 24CPA00028 ($1,696,670 ARPA Fund Balance) and Crowder Construction Co. Contract ($1,615,187) for Slater Road Lift Station
votes.notes: Initially passed 3-0 at 01:06:56; at 01:07:25 Vice Chair Burns updated the official vote count to 4-0 for the clerk's record as Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton returned to the dais. Chair Nida Allam was absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Following suspension of the rules, Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns read the motion to approve Capital Project Amendment No. 24CPA00028 appropriating $1,696,670 of ARPA fund balance to create the Slater Road Lift Station, Force Main, and Outfall capital project (SC066) and authorizing a $1,615,187 preconstruction design-build contract with Crowder Construction Company (with related amendments up to $1,696,670). The motion was seconded and passed 3-0 by voice vote with no objections. Moments later at 01:07:25, as Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton returned to the dais, Vice Chair Burns instructed the clerk to record the vote as 4-0.

disagreements.issue: EOC and Backup 911 Call Center Investment vs. Primary City-County 911 Unification
disagreements.summary: During consent review of a $5 million LOBs appropriation and design contract for a new Emergency Operations Center and shared backup 911 center, commissioners questioned moving forward before resolving primary 911 consolidation and consulting the Sheriff and state regulators.
disagreements.side_a_position: Expressed frustration that emergency lease deadlines are forcing a major 911 backup investment before resolving the long-stalled policy issue of consolidating City and County 911 call centers, and questioned whether Sheriff Birkhead and state DIT were consulted.
side_a_arguments: The County is being forced into the investment because Duke is ending the City's backup 911 lease rather than resolving primary 911 unification first.
Sheriff Clarence Birkhead publicly stated no one has spoken directly with him about consolidation.
State DIT regulates 911 VoIP compliance and has not been consulted on a merger.
disagreements.side_b_position: Staff maintained the EOC/backup 911 facility is an urgent, jointly funded (53%/47% City/County) necessity that leaves primary consolidation open for future discussion.
side_b_arguments: Duke University requires the City to vacate its leased backup 911 space by December 2026.
The existing EOC on Broad Street was inadequate for social distancing during COVID-19.
The new facility provides a shared City-County backup 911 center while keeping separate primary centers for outage redundancy as requested by the Sheriff.
disagreements.resolution: Item remained on the consent agenda for future regular-session action; staff committed to convening stakeholders around primary 911 coordination separately.

disagreements.issue: UDO Rewrite: Relaxing Density Caps for Affordability vs. High-Growth Market Reality and Rural Community Voices
disagreements.summary: Commissioners questioned Code Studio's recommendation to shift away from units-per-acre density limits toward form-based rules, disputing whether higher density reduces rents in Durham and raising concerns about Preserve Rural Durham residents not being heard.
disagreements.side_a_position: Challenged the premise that increasing residential density lowers apartment rents in booming tech markets like Durham and warned that rural and Southeast Durham residents' environmental and blasting complaints are being ignored.
side_a_arguments: In fast-growing tech hubs receiving thousands of high-paying jobs ($170k average salaries near RTP/Davis Drive), adding dense apartments has not lowered rents in Austin, Boston, Atlanta, or Silicon Valley.
Despite hiring engagement consultants, residents who bring engineers, dirty water, and blasting permit documentation are still not being heard.
Both Carter and Burns misread JCCPC's density bullet and expressed continuing concern even after staff clarification.
disagreements.side_b_position: Supported form-based design and higher density near transit as the primary strategy to improve affordability, equity, and climate outcomes.
side_b_arguments: Economic modeling showed removing units-per-acre limits and lowering parking minimums could drop modeled multiplex rents from $3,500 to $2,000/month.
Joint MPO modeling shows higher-density land use around transit reduces congestion and greenhouse gas emissions.
Prior UDO text amendments already incorporated several Preserve Rural Durham environmental proposals.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken; Vice Chair Burns requested Colin Scarff email empirical examples of high-growth tech cities where increased density lowered rents, and staff committed to updating the misleading slide text.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners - FY 2024-25 Budget Work Session #3 - June 3, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Nida Allam opened FY 2024-25 Budget Work Session #3 on June 3, 2024 before handing presiding duties to Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns due to a family emergency. Interim Superintendent Catty Moore presented Durham Public Schools' budget request and new fiscal controls implemented following the classified salary study shortfall, including eliminating over-formula school positions, freezing allotment conversions, tightening emergency-license payroll rules, curbing travel, and requiring cabinet review for local spending. In afternoon add/delete deliberations, Budget Director Keith Lane and staff walked commissioners through competing requests—$107,000 for Cooperative Extension early childhood support, $504,000 for Durham Tech, Pre-K expansions, $8.8 million for DPS's classified study, $1.39 million in late BOE hard-to-fill supplements, $1.7 million for employee health benefit relief, and $1.45 million for Hayti Reborn—warning the full list would require roughly a 4.83-cent tax increase. Commissioners debated whether to trim the late $1.39 million DPS add-on and disagreed over funding Hayti Reborn while cutting County employee health benefits.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Public Charge, Land Acknowledgement, and Presiding Handover
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Nida Allam opened FY 2024-25 Budget Work Session #3 with the public charge and land acknowledgement. She announced an ongoing family emergency and turned over presiding duties to Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns.

agenda_items.title: Durham Public Schools FY 2024-25 Budget Request and Fiscal Controls Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim Superintendent Catty Moore highlighted 2022-23 academic growth (88.2% of schools meeting or exceeding growth, 20 in the top 20% statewide), a $29.5 million grant with Duke Health and Durham Tech for a healthcare early college, and Principal Asia Cunningham's Milken Educator Award. Addressing the classified salary study shortfall, Moore detailed strict new fiscal controls—eliminating over-formula positions beyond the base budget, freezing allotment conversions, enforcing certification timelines on emergency/permit-to-teach staff, ending out-of-state travel, and requiring cabinet approval for local funds—before reviewing mandated state raises, teacher supplements, and master's pay in the Board of Education's request.

agenda_items.title: Budget Add/Delete Deliberations and Tax Rate Tradeoffs
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget staff reviewed pending additions outside the Manager's recommended budget, including $107,000 from reserves for Cooperative Extension early childhood support, $504,000 for Durham Tech upfit/rental space, $1.015 million for two Durham Pre-K classrooms, $716,000 for DPS Pre-K at Murray-Massenburg, $8.8 million (plus $1.776 million charter surcharge) for DPS classified pay, $1.39 million (plus $278,000 surcharge) for late-added hard-to-fill teacher supplements, $1.7 million for employee health benefit relief, and $1.45 million for Hayti Reborn. Staff cautioned that funding the package pushed the tax increase to 4.83 cents alongside the City's 3.85 cents; commissioners debated cutting the late $1.39 million DPS add-on and clashed over funding Hayti Reborn.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners - FY 2024-25 Budget Work Session #3 - June 3, 2024
disagreements.issue: Funding Board of Education's Late $1.39 Million Hard-to-Fill / EC Teacher Supplement Request
disagreements.summary: Commissioners differed over whether to include the Board of Education's late $1.39 million addition (carrying a $278,000 charter school surcharge, ~$1.67 million total) for hard-to-fill positions in the county budget.
disagreements.side_a_position: Remove or deprioritize the late $1.39 million addition to reduce the tax-rate burden and prioritize core County/school obligations
side_a_arguments: The $1.39 million addition was added late at the quarterly retreat and was not in the original budget request.
Removing it saves roughly $1.67 million including the 20% charter surcharge before the Board has even addressed County staff compensation.
disagreements.side_b_position: Emphasize the critical need for competitive Exceptional Children (EC) teacher supplements
side_b_arguments: Exceptional Children teaching positions are very difficult work and highly competitive to fill, causing DPS to lose staff.
disagreements.resolution: Deferred to June 4 budget work session; staff noted it could be reconsidered later if not included in the initial adopted budget.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners - FY 2024-25 Budget Work Session #3 - June 3, 2024
disagreements.issue: County Funding for Hayti Reborn Justice Movement ($1.45 Million) Amid Employee Benefit Cuts
disagreements.summary: Commissioners disagreed on whether Durham County should fund Hayti Reborn's $1.45 million reduced budget request in a year requiring property tax hikes and County employee health benefit reductions.
disagreements.side_a_position: Oppose $1.45 million in County funding for Hayti Reborn
side_a_arguments: Hayti Reborn is already slated to receive $1 million from the City (half of its prior $2 million budget) and was originally understood as one-time funding.
Most of the $1.4 million request goes to salaries while Durham County is cutting health benefits for its own staff.
disagreements.side_b_position: Maintain County financial support for Hayti Reborn for at least two years
side_b_arguments: The County helped launch Hayti Reborn and it makes no sense to undercut a young organization serving youth connected to Durham Tech before the City's contribution is even certain.
disagreements.resolution: Remained unresolved on the add/delete list pending further budget balancing on June 4.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners - FY 2024-25 Budget Work Session #2 - Thursday, May 30, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns presided over FY 2024-25 Budget Work Session #2 on May 30, 2024. Durham Technical Community College President J.B. Buxton presented DTCC's budget request, explaining that DTCC cut or shifted nearly $600,000 onto Article 46 sales tax funds to relieve the County's general fund, leaving $770,000 in fixed cost increases—driven by 3% state employee raises ($203,000) and full-year living-wage janitorial pay ($171,000)—and an unfunded $500,000 gap under the Manager's budget alongside design updates on its $35 million Life Sciences facility. In the late-afternoon wrap-up, commissioners and staff reviewed capital facility timelines (including the animal shelter and DSS main building) and tallied over 6.6 cents in potential add/delete tax impacts across DTCC, Hayti Reborn, employee benefits, and Durham Public Schools. Commissioners Brenda A. Howerton, Nimasheena Burns, and Wendy Jacobs united in demanding stronger fiscal guardrails, multi-year strategy, and reporting transparency from DPS on both operating and bond funds before finalizing numbers on June 4.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Public Charge, and Land Acknowledgement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns established a quorum and opened FY 2024-25 Budget Work Session #2, reading the Board's public charge and land acknowledgement.

agenda_items.title: Durham Technical Community College FY 2024-25 Budget Request and Capital Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DTCC President J.B. Buxton reported sustained enrollment and completion gains and noted DTCC identified nearly $300,000 in reductions and shifted $311,000 in positions to Article 46 funds (~$2.3 million total) to ease County general fund pressure. Fixed cost increases still totaled $770,000—led by 3% state salary/benefit hikes ($203,000), a full-year living-wage janitorial contract ($171,000), utilities, and accredited space rent—leaving roughly a $500,000 shortfall under the Manager's recommended budget, while Buxton also noted the $35 million, 35,000-square-foot Life Sciences facility entered design with Skanska selected as construction manager.

agenda_items.title: Capital Next Steps, Add/Delete List Review, and DPS Accountability Guardrails
agenda_items.discussion_summary: In the afternoon wrap-up, staff outlined formalized next steps for capital projects including the animal shelter and DSS main building and reviewed the pending add/delete list ($504,000 for DTCC, Hayti Reborn, up to $1.7 million for employee health benefits, and over $10 million for DPS classified wages and master's pay), warning the combined requests could add 6.66 cents or more to the tax rate. Commissioners Brenda A. Howerton, Nimasheena Burns, and Wendy Jacobs pressed staff to establish strict reporting mechanisms, multi-year accountability, and guardrails over both DPS operating and bond funds ahead of the June 4 and June 10 sessions.

meetings.title: BOCC Regular Meeting May 28, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Nida Allam presided over the May 28, 2024 Board of County Commissioners regular session, noting she was two weeks postpartum and would step out briefly as needed while Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns assisted. The board unanimously approved prior meeting minutes, issued ceremonial resolutions recognizing Asian American and Pacific Islander Heritage Month and Jewish American Heritage Month, and adopted its five-item consent agenda 5-0. Commissioners then conducted an extended public hearing on the FY 2024–25 County Manager's Recommended Budget featuring roughly 58 speakers—primarily Durham Public Schools parents, teachers, Durham Association of Educators members urging full funding of the $27.4 million school board request, Durham for DSA advocates opposing the $250M+ relocation of Durham School of the Arts, county retirees defending under-65 healthcare benefits, and maternal health and youth advocates—before making four board appointments and adjourning into closed session on the national opioid litigation.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, Land Acknowledgment, Pledge, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Nida Allam called the packed regular session to order, noted a point of personal privilege that she was two weeks postpartum and might briefly step out, and asked Commissioner Heidi Carter to lead the Pledge of Allegiance. Clerk Monica Wallace read announcements covering the Aging Well Durham website, Partnership for a Healthy Durham listening sessions, electronic recycling, the Juneteenth flag raising, Durham Neighborhood College, NC Cash unclaimed property, and the 'My Durham' kids guide.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (May 6, 2024 Work Session and May 13, 2024 Regular Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton moved and Commissioner Heidi Carter seconded approval of the May 6, 2024 work session and May 13, 2024 regular session minutes. The motion passed unanimously 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Resolutions: Asian American and Pacific Islander Heritage Month & Jewish American Heritage Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Nida Allam read the resolution proclaiming May 2024 as Asian American and Pacific Islander Heritage Month, and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs read the resolution proclaiming May 2024 as Jewish American Heritage Month. Office of Equitable Well-Being Director Dr. Brent Lewis accepted both resolutions and noted the profound staff and community impact of the cultural programming ahead of his one-year anniversary with the county.

agenda_items.title: Adoption of Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: No items were pulled from the five-item consent agenda. Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns moved and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs seconded adoption, which carried unanimously 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: FY 2024–25 County Manager's Recommended Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board held a nearly two-hour public hearing on the FY 2024–25 recommended budget with approximately 58 speakers limited to 1.5 minutes each, after Vice Chair Burns affirmed that the board welcomes public applause and expression. Speakers divided primarily around several major themes: teachers, parents, and Durham Association of Educators (DAE) supporters demanding full approval of the Board of Education's $27.4 million request (including $8.9M for classified staff pay, EC/ESL supplements, and master's pay) even if it required raising property taxes or tapping fund balance; Durham for DSA parents urging commissioners to demand accountability so DPS renovates the downtown DSA campus rather than spending $250M+ to relocate it at the expense of Title I elementary school renovations; retired EMS Chief Brandon Mitchell warning against doubling under-65 retiree healthcare premiums; and advocates seeking $25,000 for the Charles Hamilton Houston Foundation, $500,000 for Black maternal/doula care, and protected funding for General Services and Durham County Stadium.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following ballot counting by County Attorney Curtis Massey, the board announced appointments to the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission (Anthony Reevy), Community Child Protection and Child Fatality Prevention Team (Elizabeth Conrat), Dangerous Dog Appeal Board (Nicodemus Monts), and Memorial Stadium Authority (Charles Epps).

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (National Opioid Litigation)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with legal counsel regarding the national opioid litigation.

votes.item_title: Approval of Minutes for May 6, 2024 Work Session and May 13, 2024 Regular Session
votes.notes: Unanimous approval of May 6 and May 13, 2024 minutes.
votes.discussion_detail: After Clerk Monica Wallace read the evening's published county announcements and Chair Nida Allam invited the standing crowd to fill available seats, Chair Allam presented the minutes from the May 6, 2024 work session and May 13, 2024 regular session for approval. Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton moved to approve the minutes and Commissioner Heidi Carter seconded. With no corrections offered, the board approved the minutes unanimously 5-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Board and Commission Appointments (BPAC, Child Protection/Fatality Prevention Team, Dangerous Dog Appeal Board, Memorial Stadium Authority)
votes.notes: Written ballots counted and announced by County Attorney Curtis Massey: Anthony Reevy (BPAC), Elizabeth Conrat (Community Child Protection & Child Fatality Prevention Team), Nicodemus Monts (Dangerous Dog Appeal Board), Charles Epps (Memorial Stadium Authority).
votes.discussion_detail: After closing the lengthy FY 2024–25 budget public hearing and congratulating the Durham Association of Educators on reaching majority membership, Chair Nida Allam called on County Attorney Curtis Massey to count the board's appointment ballots. Attorney Massey announced the board's selections: Anthony Reevy to the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission, Elizabeth Conrat to the Community Child Protection and Child Fatality Prevention Team, Nicodemus Monts to the Dangerous Dog Appeal Board, and Charles Epps to the Memorial Stadium Authority. Chair Allam congratulated the appointees and encouraged residents to apply for remaining board vacancies.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (National Opioid Litigation - N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3))
votes.notes: Entered under attorney-client privilege pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3).
votes.discussion_detail: As the final item on the May 28 regular session agenda, Chair Nida Allam read the statutory citation under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to adjourn into closed session to consult with an attorney employed or retained by the County in order to preserve attorney-client privilege regarding the national opioid litigation. Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns moved to enter closed session and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs seconded. All five commissioners voted aye by voice vote.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners - FY 2024-25 Budget Work Session #1 - Thursday, May 23, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns presided over the May 23, 2024 FY 2024-25 Budget Work Session #1, where Budget Director Keith Lane and Deputy County Manager Claudia Hager warned that slowing sales tax and natural revenue growth left the County starting $14 million in the hole ($33 million in base expenditure needs versus ~$19 million in revenue) before considering school or departmental expansions. Staff outlined the County Manager's proposed 3.25-cent property tax increase, ~$13 million DPS increase, 3% employee COLA, limit of 10 new FTEs, reduced fund balance reliance after rigorous rating agency and LGC reviews, and future zero-based budgeting exercises. Commissioners also questioned prior-year debt service tax allocations for 2022 GO bonds and occupancy tax rules. At the close of the session, commissioners added follow-up items for the June 3-4 work sessions covering Alliance Health and Threshold funding, the sustainability plan, the Homeless Services Advisory Committee's ~$2.3 million request, opioid settlement funds for drug testing, economic development tax incentive ROI, and joint City-County rental assistance and 911 operations.

agenda_items.title: FY 2024-25 Revenue Slowdown, Tax Rate Proposal, and Capital Financing Overview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Keith Lane and Deputy County Manager Claudia Hager opened Work Session #1 by noting that expenditure growth was outpacing slowing post-pandemic sales tax collections, leaving a $33 million-to-$19 million structural gap even before school expansion requests and motivating the Manager's 3.25-cent property tax increase alongside a 3% COLA, 10 new FTEs, and paused departmental expansions. Staff highlighted rigorous credit rating agency and LGC reviews of long-term debt, upcoming ground-up departmental budget reviews, and answered questions regarding the prior year's 3-cent tax increase (1.5 cents general fund and 1.5 cents capital financing for 2022 GO bonds) and Board policy dedicating occupancy tax revenues to debt service.

agenda_items.title: Commissioner Agenda Requests for Subsequent Budget Work Sessions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners compiled follow-up topics requiring addition to the June 3 and June 4 budget work sessions, including an Alliance Health budget breakdown and Threshold funding review, sustainability plan budget alignment, and the Homeless Services Advisory Committee's ~$2.3 million request and shelter space needs. Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns requested $25,000 (potentially via opioid settlement funds) for a safety and wellness task force drug-testing initiative, a 20-minute briefing on economic development tax incentive ROI ($613 returned per $1 spent), and reiterated her $100,000 Black Boys Roundtable request, while Chair Nida Allam sought updates on overlapping City-County rental assistance and 911 call center costs.

meetings.title: Durham County Manager's FY 2024-25 Recommended Budget Presentation
meetings.executive_summary: County Manager Dr. Kimberly Sowell presented her FY 2024-25 recommended budget and DCo Forward 2029 plan to the Board of County Commissioners on May 15, 2024, presided over by Chair Nida Allam. Facing slowing post-pandemic sales tax growth, Sowell proposed freezing non-critical vacant positions, cutting ~$1 million in departmental operating budgets, funding a 3% employee COLA ($7.1 million) alongside a dual-premium health insurance model to contain >$3 million in benefits growth, and raising the general fund property tax rate by 3.25 cents to generate $17 million. Key investments included over $220 million across Durham Public Schools, Durham Tech ($500,000 for Bulls and Back to Work scholarships), and Durham Pre-K (adding $965,000+ for Murray-Massenburg Elementary), plus $845,000 and 27 replacement vehicles for the Sheriff's Office, 8 new positions for the 36-bed Youth Home, $1.4 million for joint eviction diversion, a 13% sewer rate increase, and $2.6 million for transit and rail crossing feasibility. Sowell outlined the May 28 public hearing, work sessions, and June 10 adoption date before Chair Allam thanked staff and noted she would attend work sessions virtually.

agenda_items.title: FY 2024-25 Recommended Budget Overview, Revenue Slowdown, and Tax Rate Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Dr. Kimberly Sowell introduced her FY 2024-25 recommended budget and DCo Forward 2029 strategic framework, noting that sales tax growth had slowed to pre-pandemic levels (~1 cent property-tax equivalent compared to over 4 cents in prior years). To balance slower revenues with growing obligations, she recommended freezing non-critical vacancies, trimming ~$1 million from departmental budgets, providing a 3% employee COLA ($7.1 million), introducing a dual-premium health plan to offset >$3 million in benefits increases, and raising the general fund property tax rate by 3.25 cents ($17 million) alongside fire district adjustments (0.5-cent increase in Redwood, 1.5-cent decrease in Durham County Fire & Rescue).

agenda_items.title: Departmental and Community Priorities: Education, Public Safety, Housing, and Transit
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Sowell detailed major investments across focus areas: over $220 million for education (DPS, Durham Tech scholarships, and >$965,000 for new Durham Pre-K seats at Murray-Massenburg Elementary), two bilingual nutrition educators, $845,000 and 27 replacement vehicles for the Sheriff's Office, 10 replacement vehicles (5 ambulances) for OES, and 8 new positions including a diversion coordinator for the 36-bed Youth Home. Additional allocations included $1.4 million for City-County eviction diversion, Orange Factory Road Farm management and stream stabilization, a 13% sewer consumption rate increase ($1.6 million), $2.6 million in economic development incentives, and $2.6 million for the Durham County Transit Plan and an East Durham federal railroad crossing feasibility grant.

agenda_items.title: FY 2024-25 Budget Calendar and Chair Closing Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Sowell reviewed key dates for the budget process: a May 28 public hearing, budget work sessions on May 23, May 30, June 3, and June 4, and planned adoption on June 10, 2024. Chair Nida Allam thanked Deputy Managers Claudia Hager and Maurice Jones, the budget team, and county departments, and noted she would participate in the upcoming work sessions via Zoom.

meetings.title: BOCC Regular Meeting May 13, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Nida Allam presided over the May 13, 2024 regular session of the Durham County Board of Commissioners, opening with a moment of silence led by Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns for victims of nearly a dozen recent shootings and an announcement that Chair Allam would be going on leave and joining upcoming budget work sessions virtually. The board approved five ceremonial proclamations recognizing EMS Week (50th anniversary), Memorial Day, Mental Health Awareness Month, Durham County Treatment Court Month (celebrating its 1,000th Drug Treatment Court graduate), and National Foster Care Month. County Manager Dr. Sowell then presented the FY 2024-25 Recommended Budget totaling $954 million (+7.3%, with a $641 million general fund), proposing a 3.25-cent property tax rate increase, $201 million for Durham Public Schools (+$13.2 million), a 3% employee COLA, a tiered health insurance plan, non-critical vacancy freezes, and utility fee increases. The board unanimously approved the April 29, 2024 minutes and the consent agenda 5-0 before adjourning into closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) regarding economic development incentives.

agenda_items.title: Opening Remarks, Moment of Silence, Announcements, and Approval of April 29, 2024 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Nida Allam opened the meeting with the public charge and land acknowledgment, and Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns led a moment of silence following nearly a dozen shootings in Durham over the preceding week. Clerk Wallace read community announcements including the FY 2024-25 citizen budget survey, May 28 budget public hearing, Sun Bucks summer meal cards, voter photo ID outreach, RTP South zoning open house, Memorial Day ceremony, Fair Chance Employment Resource Fair, and Local Government Career Expo. Chair Allam announced this was her last regular session before going on leave, and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs clarified that the detention center lobby naloxone vending machine is accessible 24/7 without security screening before the board approved the April 29, 2024 minutes.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: Emergency Medical Services Week 2024
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Nida Allam read a proclamation designating May 19-25, 2024 as Emergency Medical Services Week on the 50th anniversary of EMS Week nationwide. Office of Emergency Services Director Stuart Lockhart and Interim Chief Paramedic Gordon Smith accepted the proclamation and highlighted Durham County's community paramedic program, post-overdose response team, MOUD training for all paramedics and EMTs, and fleet modernization efforts.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: Memorial Day 2024
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter read a proclamation designating May 27, 2024 as Memorial Day in Durham County and honoring the 375 known Durham County service members who died in service. Veterans Services Director Lois Harvin-Ravin and staff member Lindsey Atkins thanked the board for supporting a seven-person Veterans Services department and invited residents to the May 27 remembrance ceremony.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: Mental Health Awareness Month 2024
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton read a proclamation designating May 2024 as Mental Health Awareness Month. Justice Services Director Rashana Parker and Clinical Services Manager Mark Strange accepted the proclamation, noting that over half of individuals entering the detention center are referred to mental health services and discussing the therapeutic housing unit, mental health court, and the forthcoming forensic community support team with Alliance Behavioral Health.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: Durham County Treatment Court Month 2024
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns read a proclamation declaring May 2024 as Treatment Court Month in Durham County. Justice Services Director Rashana Parker, Drug Treatment Court Coordinator Rogers-Duncan, and Judge Hall celebrated the Adult Drug Treatment Court's 1,000th graduate and credited the county for funding the court after state defunding.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: National Foster Care Month 2024
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Wendy Jacobs read a proclamation declaring May 2024 as National Foster Care Month, citing 243 children and youth in foster care and 30 young adults ages 18-21 in extended foster care in Durham County as of April 30, 2024. Department of Social Services leadership and program managers Susan Lee and Carol Trimble thanked foster and kinship caregivers and highlighted youth transition supports.

agenda_items.title: Presentation of County Manager's Recommended FY 2024-25 Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Dr. Sowell presented a $954 million total FY 2024-25 recommended budget (+7.3%, including a $641 million general fund, +6.8%) amid slowing sales tax growth ($3.3M projected growth vs. $22M prior year) and declining Medicaid hold harmless and Register of Deeds revenues. Key recommendations included a 3.25-cent general fund property tax rate increase ($17M), $201 million for Durham Public Schools (+$13.2M or 7%, short of the district's full request), over $965,000 for new Pre-K seats at Murray-Massenberg Elementary, a 3% employee COLA ($7.1M), a dual-option tiered health insurance plan, a freeze on non-critical vacancies with only 10 new FTEs, $1.4M for eviction diversion, 8 new positions for the 36-bed Youth Home, 27 Sheriff and 10 EMS replacement vehicles, a 13% sewer consumption rate increase, and a stormwater fee increase from $64 to $80 per ERU. Work sessions were scheduled for May 23 through June 4, with a public hearing on May 28 and adoption planned for June 10.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Nida Allam asked whether any commissioner wished to pull any item from the consent agenda for separate discussion. Seeing none, the board moved, seconded, and approved the consent agenda without discussion.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session: Economic Development Incentives (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted to adjourn into closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) to discuss matters relating to the location or expansion of industries or businesses and tentative economic development incentives.

meetings.title: BOCC Work Session May 6, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 6, 2024 work session, the Board of County Commissioners reviewed consent agenda items for the upcoming regular session, including human services grants, sewer infrastructure, transit work program amendments, and the Durham-to-Roxboro Rail Trail feasibility study. Commissioners held substantive policy discussions on the City-County Planning Department's FY25 Work Program—raising concerns about county infrastructure and school costs generated by city annexations and rezonings—and reviewed a comprehensive $62.4 million ARPA funding status update. No formal votes were taken during the work session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Citizen Comments, and Consent Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Nida Allam called the meeting to order and opened virtual citizen comments, during which DeWarren Langley urged FY25 budget investments for boys and young men of color. Commissioners then reviewed upcoming regular-session consent items covering Library, DSS, and Public Health grants (including DINE nutrition funding in item 24-0229), Chin Page Road sewer lift station improvements (24-0237), FY24 Q4 Durham Transit Work Program reallocations (24-0240), ERP consulting (24-0250), RDU FAA grant (24-0260), the Durham-to-Roxboro Rail Trail feasibility ILA (24-0262), and Board of Elections facility architectural and furniture contracts (24-0263, 24-0264). Commissioner Wendy Jacobs requested follow-up on schools served by DINE and architectural plans for item 24-0263, while Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns questioned a $976,000 reduction in North Durham transit funding that staff explained was shifted to night and weekend service.

agenda_items.title: City-County Planning Department FY25 Work Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Sara Young presented the FY25 Work Program, detailing ongoing development review, the Unified Development Ordinance rewrite, the RTP South Design District, water/sewer extension amendments without annexation, Comprehensive Plan report card tracking, small area planning for Walltown/Northgate, landscape manual updates, and a 55% Urban Growth Boundary tree canopy analysis. Vice Chair Burns asked about community open houses for RTP South, while Chair Allam, Commissioner Jacobs, and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton raised concerns about the 50/50 City-County funding split and uncompensated county service burdens—particularly schools and EMS—resulting from city rezonings and annexations.

agenda_items.title: American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) Funding Update and Treasury Obligation Rules
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy County Manager Claudia Hager and staff presented an update on the County's $62.4 million ARPA allocation across 53 projects, reporting 89% committed and 88% under contract, with $4.5 million remaining outside pending Land Trust and Homeless Day Center RFPs. Staff outlined U.S. Treasury Final Rule flexibility for meeting the December 31, 2024 obligation deadline, including revenue replacement, contract amendments, and covering personnel through 2026. Commissioners debated managing the upcoming fiscal cliff for community partners, affordability commitments at the 300 E. Main St. childcare center, and whether to fund an Urban Ministries shelter/day center feasibility study immediately or route it through the joint City-County-DPS housing task force.

agenda_items.title: Board Directives Tracking Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief of Staff Shannon Trap briefly walked commissioners through the April 2024 tab of the live shared Board Directives tracker to confirm item statuses and upcoming follow-ups before concluding the work session.

disagreements.issue: County Service Impacts and 50/50 Funding Equity in City-County Planning Work Program (24-0232)
disagreements.summary: Commissioners challenged how city-initiated rezonings, annexations, and water/sewer extensions generate countywide infrastructure, school, and EMS demands while Durham County pays half of the joint Planning Department's budget.
disagreements.side_a_position: The joint planning model and 50/50 cost split disproportionately burden Durham County taxpayers with downstream school and public safety costs from city growth approvals.
side_a_arguments: City rezonings and annexations add students and emergency calls without matching county operational funding or direct county approval over municipal land-use cases.
Staff capacity under the 50/50 split is heavily consumed by city development cases and annexations.
disagreements.side_b_position: The FY25 work program reflects mutually adopted Comprehensive Plan priorities and balanced city-county staffing commitments under the existing interlocal framework.
side_b_arguments: The work program advances shared goals such as the UDO rewrite, Urban Growth Boundary tree canopy protection, and small area planning.
Joint planning coordinates regional standards across both jurisdictions.
disagreements.resolution: Informational work session review; commissioners signaled interest in scrutinizing county fiscal impacts and joint governance during the budget process.

disagreements.issue: Urban Ministries Expanded Shelter and Day Center Feasibility Study Timing vs. Joint Housing Task Force
disagreements.summary: During the ARPA update, commissioners and county leadership differed on whether to move forward rapidly with a local shelter/day center feasibility study or wait for alignment at the joint City-County-DPS housing table.
disagreements.side_a_position: Advance funding for an Urban Ministries expanded shelter and day center feasibility study promptly rather than delaying for broader multi-body coordination.
side_a_arguments: Local homelessness and shelter capacity needs are urgent and would benefit from accelerating site and feasibility analysis now.
Remaining unallocated ARPA funds or local dollars could be positioned sooner if planning begins immediately.
disagreements.side_b_position: Coordinate shelter and day center planning through the Combined City-County-DPS Housing Initiative before committing additional study resources.
side_b_arguments: The joint City-County-DPS table is actively aligning intergovernmental homelessness and housing priorities to avoid duplicated efforts.
The Homeless Day Center RFP closing June 5 will provide direct provider proposals to evaluate alongside joint plans.
disagreements.resolution: No formal action taken; County Manager Kimberly Sowell and Deputy Manager Claudia Hager noted staff would coordinate around the pending RFP and joint housing discussions.

meetings.title: BOCC Regular Meeting Apr. 29, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 29, 2024 regular meeting, the Board of County Commissioners approved minutes, recognized four ceremonial proclamations and resolutions, announced board and commission ballot appointments, and adopted the consent agenda. Sharp debate erupted over pulled item 24-0245, a $750,000 ARPA award to Knox Street Studios, after Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton moved to delay the contract for further review while Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns and Commissioner Heidi Carter objected to holding a Black-led organization to higher scrutiny than previously approved Forward Cities ($1.5M). Howerton's continuance motion died for lack of a second, and the Board approved the contract 4-1 with both organizations invited to present on May 6.

agenda_items.title: Announcements, Minutes Approval, and Ceremonial Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk Monica Wallace and commissioners shared community announcements covering FAFSA outreach, Durham Center for Senior Life's 75th anniversary, SunBucks food aid, FRA S-Line rail funding, rural transit, and aging/childcare advocacy days. Following unanimous approval of minutes, the Board presented resolutions and proclamations for Arab American Heritage Month, Year of the Aerial Insectivore, Lights Out Durham, and Alcohol Awareness Month, during which Vice Chair Burns critiqued school suspensions and police referrals for youth substance incidents.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Items 24-0241 and 24-0245)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Before voting on the consent agenda, Chair Allam noted item 24-0241 (Arts Council ARPA interlocal agreement) was pulled for Commissioner Carter's recusal, and Commissioner Howerton requested pulling item 24-0245 ($750,000 ARPA award to Knox Street Studios) to gather more contract information at the May 6 work session. Commissioners approved the remaining consent agenda unanimously while reserving both pulled items for separate votes.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Ballot Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Curtis Massey announced the Board's written ballot appointments: Joycelyn Horne to the Citizens Advisory Committee; Denise Barnes, Pat Ashley, Valerie Jarvis, and Jane Brown as community representatives and Dr. Marba Cole as physician representative to the Durham County Hospital Corporation Board of Trustees; and Taylor Blouser to the Durham Open Space and Trails Commission.

agenda_items.title: City-County Arts Council $1,000,000 ARPA Interlocal Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered pulled item 24-0241, an interlocal agreement allocating $1 million in ARPA funds for the Durham Arts Council, which was separated so Commissioner Heidi Carter could recuse herself due to her liaison role with the Arts Council.

agenda_items.title: Knox Street Studios $750,000 ARPA Economic Development Award
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners debated item 24-0245 after Commissioner Howerton moved to continue the $750,000 Knox Street Studios ARPA contract to the May 6 work session, stating she lacked clarity on nonprofit deliverables and staffing split. Vice Chair Burns strongly opposed delay, arguing that Forward Cities received $1.5 million without a comparable hold and that Economic Development Director Andy Miracle had vetted the timeline since December 2023. After Howerton's continuance motion died without a second, the Board approved the award 4-1 with a compromise directing both Forward Cities and Knox Street Studios to present at the May 6 work session.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Continuance failed (no second); main motion approved 4-1 (Howerton nay)

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following final action on pulled consent items, the Board voted unanimously to enter closed session under North Carolina General Statute 143-318.11(a)(6) to consider personnel matters.

votes.item_title: Approval of Minutes (April 1, 2024 Work Session and April 8, 2024 Regular Session)
votes.notes: No corrections noted to the draft minutes.
votes.discussion_detail: Following community and commissioner announcements, Chair Nida Allam called for approval of the April 1, 2024 work session and April 8, 2024 regular session minutes. Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton moved to approve the minutes as submitted, and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs seconded the motion. No revisions or discussion were offered by any member. The Board adopted the minutes unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Items 24-0241 and 24-0245)
votes.notes: Items 24-0241 and 24-0245 were pulled for separate discussion and votes.
votes.discussion_detail: Before adopting the consent agenda, Chair Allam noted that item 24-0241 (Arts Council ARPA ILA) was pulled to allow Commissioner Heidi Carter to abstain, and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton requested pulling item 24-0245 (Knox Street Studios ARPA contract) to discuss continuing it to the May 6 work session. Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns questioned delaying 24-0245 during agenda setting, prompting Howerton to clarify that she had insufficient information prior to voting. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs then moved to approve the remainder of the consent agenda, seconded by Vice Chair Burns. The motion passed unanimously 5-0.

votes.item_title: Item 24-0241: Arts Council $1,000,000 ARPA Interlocal Agreement
votes.notes: Chair announced tally as 4-0 with 1 abstention (Commissioner Heidi Carter recused as Arts Council liaison).
votes.discussion_detail: Pulled item 24-0241 authorized the interlocal agreement governing $1 million in ARPA funding for the Durham Arts Council. The item was separated from the consent agenda specifically so Commissioner Heidi Carter could abstain due to her liaison role with the organization. Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns moved approval and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs seconded the motion. The remaining four seated commissioners voted aye, passing the item 4-0 with Carter's abstention recorded.

votes.item_title: Motion to Continue Item 24-0245 (Knox Street Studios $750,000 ARPA Award) to May 6, 2024 Work Session
votes.notes: Motion died for lack of a second following extended debate.
votes.discussion_detail: During debate on item 24-0245, Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton argued that the Board had not sufficiently reviewed the $750,000 ARPA contract with Knox Street Studios, including the 50/50 split between staffing and pass-through funding, and moved to continue the item to the May 6 work session. Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns objected strongly, noting that Forward Cities had already been approved for $1.5 million without delay and accusing the Board of holding a Black-led local organization to an inequitable standard despite months of staff review by Economic Development Director Andy Miracle. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs suggested approving the contract immediately while inviting both Knox Street Studios and Forward Cities to present at the May 6 work session. No commissioner seconded Howerton's continuance motion, so it failed on the floor.

votes.item_title: Item 24-0245: Approve Knox Street Studios $750,000 ARPA Contract with May 6 Presentations
votes.notes: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton stated her opposition prior to the vote and audibly voted nay.
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately after the continuance motion failed for lack of a second, Commissioner Heidi Carter moved to approve item 24-0245—the $750,000 ARPA economic development award to Knox Street Studios—incorporating Commissioner Wendy Jacobs's proposal that both Forward Cities and Knox Street Studios present at the May 6 work session. Jacobs seconded the motion. Prior to the vote, Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton reiterated that she did not vote on contracts without adequate briefing and stated she would vote no. The motion passed 4-1 with Howerton casting the sole nay vote.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session Pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6)
votes.notes: Closed session to consider personnel matters.
votes.discussion_detail: At the conclusion of open-session business, Chair Allam read the statutory citation to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) regarding personnel matters. Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns moved to go into closed session, and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton seconded. The Board approved the motion unanimously 5-0.

disagreements.issue: Approval vs. Continuance of $750,000 ARPA Award to Knox Street Studios (Item 24-0245)
disagreements.summary: The Board split 4-1 over whether to approve a $750,000 ARPA contract for Knox Street Studios immediately or defer it to the May 6 work session for further review, raising sharp tensions over equity and contract vetting standards.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the $750,000 Knox Street Studios contract immediately without further delay, while scheduling both Forward Cities and Knox Street Studios to present at the May 6 work session.
side_a_arguments: Staff under Economic Development Director Andy Miracle had vetted the allocation timeline since December 2023 and March 2024.
Forward Cities received $1.5 million in ARPA funds without being pulled or delayed, making additional holds on Black-led Knox Street Studios inequitable.
Scheduling both organizations for May 6 provides transparency without stalling contract execution ahead of federal ARPA deadlines.
disagreements.side_b_position: Continue item 24-0245 to the May 6 work session before voting so commissioners can examine contract terms and the 50/50 split between administrative staff and pass-through funding.
side_b_arguments: Commissioners should not vote on a $750,000 nonprofit contract without sufficient work-session briefing and clarity on deliverables.
Requests for review were driven by fiduciary diligence regarding contract structure rather than the race of the recipient.
disagreements.resolution: Howerton's continuance motion failed for lack of a second, and the main motion to approve item 24-0245 with May 6 presentations from both recipients passed 4-1.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2024-04-09 9:00 AM - Joint City of Durham and Board of County Commissioners Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 9, 2024 Joint City of Durham and Board of County Commissioners meeting presided over by Chair Nida Allam, the two boards held policy briefings on unified housing planning, property tax relief, rental assistance shortfalls, and youth summer programming, taking only one formal vote to unanimously approve the February 28, 2024 minutes once quorum was confirmed. Council Member Javiera Caballero updated officials on appointments and private-funding plans for an independent Housing Needs Assessment under the City-County-DPS Housing Task Force, while Tax Administrator Keyar Doyle reported rapid growth in the jointly funded $1.25 million Low-Income Homeowners Relief (LIHR) program ahead of the 2025 property reappraisal. During a detailed discussion of depleted emergency rental assistance funds, City and County officials surfaced an intergovernmental cost-sharing tension over whether the City should split immediate emergency rent aid (roughly $48,000) given its existing funding for Legal Aid eviction diversion attorneys and competing City budget pressures, ultimately asking County Manager Dr. Kimberly Sowell and City Manager Wanda Page to prepare three short-term funding options before April 22. The meeting concluded with a review of the City-County Office on Youth's comprehensive summer opportunities directory.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and City-County-DPS Housing Task Force Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Nida Allam opened the meeting at 9:07 a.m., deferred minutes approval pending quorum, and called on Council Member Javiera Caballero for a briefing on the unified City-County-DPS housing initiative. Caballero outlined board chair/mayor appointee reviews, staff and community brainstorming partners, and efforts to secure private funding for an independent Housing Needs Assessment without waiting one to two budget cycles; Commissioner Wendy Jacobs added that local realtors and Durham Tech are eager to partner on workforce housing.

agenda_items.title: Low-Income Homeowners Relief (LIHR) Program Briefing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Tax Administrator Keyar Doyle reviewed the DSS-administered Low-Income Homeowners Relief program, funded by $750,000 from the County and $500,000 from the City across three AMI tiers (including up to 100% tax-bill relief for seniors 60+ at or below 30% AMI). Doyle reported growth from 200 approved Year 1 applications to 539 applications through March 31 of Year 3, prompting discussion of senior home-repair coordination, documentation streamlining, and outreach ahead of the 2025 reappraisal.

agenda_items.title: Eviction Diversion and Emergency Rental Assistance Shortfall Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion, City and County officials debated how to cover an immediate emergency rental assistance shortfall while structuring next year's program. A City speaker noted the City already commits its share to Legal Aid eviction diversion attorneys and asked whether the County would reciprocally cost-share attorneys, while Mayor Leonardo Williams noted competing urgent City needs requiring full Council work-session review; Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns and County officials asked Managers Dr. Kimberly Sowell and Wanda Page to prepare three options ahead of the County's April 22 meeting.

agenda_items.title: Approval of February 28, 2024 Joint Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With quorum present, the presiding chair returned to the first item and called for a motion on the February 28, 2024 joint meeting minutes. Moved by Mayor Leonardo Williams and seconded by Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns, the minutes passed unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: City-County Office on Youth Summer Programming Briefing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Officials reviewed an emailed memo from Ms. Khalil of the City-County Office on Youth and its updated March 28 online directory listing summer opportunities across the City, County, and Durham Public Schools. City Manager Wanda Page noted she would highlight youth mentoring at that evening's State of the City address, and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs urged broad community outreach beyond web access before adjournment.

votes.item_title: Approval of February 28, 2024 Joint City/County Meeting Minutes
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote ('minutes are approved unanimously'). Individual member roll call was not taken in this joint City-County session; BOCC members Nida Allam, Nimasheena Burns, and Wendy Jacobs were confirmed present in the digest.
votes.discussion_detail: Deferred from 00:00:07 until quorum was established; passed after Mayor Leonardo Williams moved and Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns seconded, with a commissioner praising the quality of the minutes.
