meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2024-04-08 7:00 PM - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 8, 2024 regular session, with Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton excused while attending a conference in Washington, D.C., the four present commissioners excused her absence and approved the March 25 minutes. The Board introduced new Office of Emergency Services Director Mark Lockhart, adopted five ceremonial proclamations (Second Chance Month, Fair Housing Month, Child Abuse Prevention Month, Omega Psi Phi's 50th anniversary at Duke, and Black Maternal Health Week), and approved the consent agenda 4-0. Pulled item 24-0193, a $1 million Arts Council ARPA interlocal agreement, passed 3-0 with Commissioner Heidi Carter abstaining.

agenda_items.title: Announcements, Excused Absence of Commissioner Howerton, and Minutes Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners and clerk staff shared announcements including the Register of Deeds 'Hacking into History' racially restrictive covenants project, the NC Heirs Property Symposium, and an April 15 MWBE outreach event at Durham Station. The four present board members voted 4-0 to excuse Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton's absence due to travel in Washington, D.C., and approved the March 25, 2024 regular session minutes 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Introduction of Emergency Services Director Mark Lockhart and Ceremonial Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant County Manager Dwayne Brinson introduced Mark Lockhart as Durham County's new Office of Emergency Services Director. The Board then presented proclamations for Second Chance Month (Justice Services Department), Fair Housing Month (Durham Regional Association of Realtors), Child Abuse Prevention Month (DSS), Omega Psi Phi Fraternity's Omega Zeta Chapter 50th anniversary at Duke (accepted by former NC Supreme Court Justice Mike Morgan), and Black Maternal Health Week (Women's Commission and Equity Before Birth).

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Item 24-0193)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Item 24-0193 (Arts Council $1 million ARPA interlocal agreement) was pulled for Commissioner Carter's recusal, and Commissioner Jacobs highlighted item 24-0196, a $750,000 ARPA home repair contract with Central Pines Regional Council, asking staff how seniors are referred. Following clarification on DSS/Aging coordination, the Board adopted the remainder of the consent agenda 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item: City-County Arts Council $1,000,000 ARPA Interlocal Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following adoption of the main consent agenda, the Board considered item 24-0193 separately so Commissioner Heidi Carter could abstain under general statutes due to her conflict/liaison affiliation. The three remaining voting members approved the item 3-0.

votes.item_title: Excuse Absence of Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton
votes.notes: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton was absent attending a conference in Washington, D.C.
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Nida Allam announced that Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton was absent while attending a conference in Washington, D.C., and called for a motion to excuse her absence. A board member moved and another seconded the motion by voice without naming speakers on the record. All four present commissioners—Allam, Burns, Jacobs, and Carter—voted aye, formally excusing Howerton's absence 4-0.

votes.item_title: Approval of March 25, 2024 Regular Session Minutes
votes.notes: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Allam presented the draft minutes from the March 25, 2024 regular session for board approval. Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns moved to approve the minutes, and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs seconded the motion. With no amendments or discussion requested, the four present commissioners voted aye unanimously 4-0.

votes.item_title: Item 24-0193: City-County Arts Council $1,000,000 ARPA Interlocal Agreement
votes.notes: Commissioner Heidi Carter abstained pursuant to statutory conflict rules; Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Pulled item 24-0193 covered the $1 million ARPA interlocal agreement for the Durham Arts Council, separated from the consent agenda so Commissioner Heidi Carter could recuse herself. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs moved to approve the item, seconded by Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns. With Carter abstaining and Commissioner Howerton absent, the three remaining commissioners voted aye to pass the item 3-0.

meetings.title: BOCC - April 01, 2024 - Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: In the second portion of the April 1, 2024 work session, commissioners completed Q&A on the Community Safety & Wellness Task Force recommendations—including opioid settlement funding for drug checking and HEART expansion—and reviewed leasing and childcare operator plans at 115 N. Queen St. / 300 E. Main St. The Board also received presentations on the FY25 Durham Transit Work Program, GoDurham's FY23 annual report, GoTriangle regional projects, and the County's MWBE program with consultant C2 Contractors. Major policy debates centered on childcare rent subsidies versus low-income seat mandates at 300 E. Main St. and transparency in C2 Contractors' MWBE scope and tracking.

agenda_items.title: Community Safety and Wellness Task Force Q&A, Opioid Settlement, and HEART Expansion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Continuing from the morning session, commissioners questioned task force representatives and Assistant County Manager Dwayne Brinson regarding opioid settlement Wave 2 funding ($22.5M total), FTIR drug checking equipment costs, and countywide HEART expansion estimates ranging from $35,000 for call diversion to $1.6 million for full deployment. Vice Chair Burns raised concerns about bypassing RFPs on proposed ethnodramas, Youth Home opposition, 911 legal constraints, and Sheriff consultation.

agenda_items.title: Retail Space Occupancy Process for 115 N. Queen St. (300 E. Main St. Complex)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Real estate staff presented leasing options for three ground-floor retail spaces at 115 N. Queen St., noting one was leased through December 2024 to contractor Progress Carolinas while two roughly 1,000-square-foot cold-shell spaces remained vacant. Because buildout costs deterred nonprofits, staff asked whether to entertain a letter of interest from a local for-profit personal services business; commissioners expressed openness to reviewing an LOI while Commissioner Jacobs preferred holding pending the Homeless Day Center RFP.

agenda_items.title: Childcare / Pre-K Operator Selection Update for 300 E. Main St.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Child Care Services Association (CCSA) Senior VP Linda Chappelle and staff updated the Board on selecting an operator for the 10,000+ square foot childcare facility (capacity 86 children plus a Durham Pre-K class), having narrowed 14 applicants to four finalists (one nonprofit and three for-profit). Commissioners and County Attorney Curtis Massey debated below-market rent legality, opposing open-ended rent subsidies while demanding enforceable sliding-scale and voucher seat commitments despite $300,000–$500,000+ upfit costs.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / Staff to return with options

agenda_items.title: FY25 Durham Transit Work Program Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation Director Ellen Beckman and staff presented the FY25 Durham Transit Work Program projecting $45.5 million in revenue, driven by $43 million from the half-cent transit sales tax. Major capital allocations included boosting GoDurham and paratransit maintenance facility funding from $5M to $30M, Durham Station improvements from $2.7M to $9.9M, an East Durham railroad crossing study supported by a Rep. Valerie Foushee grant, and 50 bus stop upgrades annually, though commissioners noted a remaining $30M City maintenance facility funding gap.

agenda_items.title: GoDurham FY23 Annual Report and GoTriangle Regional Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Transportation Director Sean Egan reported a 19% GoDurham ridership increase (over 6 million annual trips, second highest in NC), full restoration of 2020 service levels, starting driver pay rising above $20/hour, and an upcoming FY26 fiscal cliff as COVID relief expires. GoTriangle CEO Charles Lattuca then reviewed 1.5 million regional trips, the July 1 return to fares with low-income fare programs, 381 ADA bus stop upgrades in Durham, RUS Bus construction, and the 19-acre Triangle Mobility Hub in RTP.

agenda_items.title: Minority and Women-Owned Business Enterprise (MWBE) Program and C2 Contractors Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief of Staff Shannon Trap, staff member Nicodemus Munoz, and C2 Contractors leaders Cornelius 'CC' Lambert and Richard Fuquay presented MWBE outreach metrics, HUB database utilization, and development consulting across projects such as 220 E. Main, 3825 S. Roxboro, 826 E. Pettigrew, and the Durham School of the Arts site. Vice Chair Burns sharply questioned C2's exact scope, NAICS commodity tracking, and board reporting gaps, while County Manager Kimberly Sowell and Commissioners Carter and Jacobs defended C2's capital tracking and outlined plans for new goods-and-services procurement software.

disagreements.issue: Rent Subsidies vs. Binding Affordability Mandates for 300 E. Main St. Childcare Operator
disagreements.summary: Commissioners clashed over how to balance nonprofit/for-profit operator selection, below-market lease terms, and guaranteed affordable childcare slots at the 300 E. Main St. county complex.
disagreements.side_a_position: Oppose ongoing county rent subsidies given $2M+ already committed to the lease/buildout, and enforce strict sliding-scale and voucher seat percentages directly in the lease.
side_a_arguments: Durham County is already paying roughly $176,000/year plus 2% annual escalations over 15 years, making nominal rent an inappropriate precedent.
County Attorney Curtis Massey advised that nominal or below-market rent legally requires binding public-purpose restrictions such as sliding-scale or voucher quotas rather than mere 501(c)(3) status.
Commissioners Carter and Allam stressed that guaranteeing affordable seats for low-income families must remain central despite $300k–$500k+ upfit costs above the developer allowance.
disagreements.side_b_position: Avoid changing procurement expectations retroactively after inviting for-profit applicants and evaluate concrete subsidy-to-seat tradeoffs before locking in requirements.
side_b_arguments: If nonprofit-only operation was a mandatory condition, the County and CCSA should have restricted the RFP upfront rather than shortlisting three for-profit finalists.
Upfit costs of $300k–$500k+ affect whether any operator can sustain high affordable-seat quotas without lease or capital assistance.
disagreements.resolution: Staff and CCSA were directed to return to the Board with structured lease, upfit, and sliding-scale/voucher seat scenarios.

disagreements.issue: MWBE Program Accountability, C2 Contractors Scope, and Goods/Services Tracking
disagreements.summary: Vice Chair Burns questioned the transparency, scope, and board oversight of C2 Contractors' MWBE consulting work, prompting defense from County Manager Sowell and Commissioners Carter and Jacobs.
disagreements.side_a_position: C2 Contractors' exact scope of work, NAICS/commodity code tracking, and regular performance reports to the Board have been unclear and insufficient given historical disparity findings.
side_a_arguments: Commissioners have not received granular, recurring reports detailing C2's scope and measurable impact across non-construction goods and services.
Without commodity-level tracking and clear accountability benchmarks, prior disparity gaps risk persisting.
disagreements.side_b_position: C2 Contractors has delivered tangible capital-project outreach and preliminary RFQ development while the County simultaneously modernizes its internal goods-and-services tracking software.
side_b_arguments: County Manager Kimberly Sowell explained C2 supported preliminary RFQ work on 220 E. Main and outreach events, while the County is launching dedicated procurement tracking software to capture goods/services data.
Commissioners Carter and Jacobs praised the bond and capital MWBE metrics and outreach progress presented.
disagreements.resolution: Informational discussion; staff noted ongoing procurement software implementation and reporting follow-up.

meetings.title: BOCC - April 01, 2024 - Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: In the opening portion of the April 1, 2024 work session, the Board reviewed consent agenda items—sparking criticism over bringing standalone preconstruction capital items outside the comprehensive Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) review—and paused two projects (`24-0179` Sheriff's Training Facility and `24-0183` Project BUILD renovations). Commissioners then received an update on the $3 million ARPA-funded BullS Academy / Made in Durham youth workforce initiative and heard seven policy requests from the Community Safety & Wellness Task Force's final report. No formal votes occurred in this work session segment.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review and Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) Sequencing Concerns
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed upcoming consent agenda items including Stanford L. Warren Library upgrades and furnishings (24-0113, 24-0146), Public Health refugee screening (24-0126), Detention Center fire alarm work (24-0134), Emery Cemetery grave relocation (24-0136), utility and sewer contracts (24-0159, 24-0167, 24-0178), Hayti Reborn Justice Movement funding (24-0186), and 826 E. Pettigrew St. planning for Bull City United. Expressing concern about approving off-cycle capital items ahead of comprehensive CIP prioritization—while long-delayed facilities like the animal shelter waited—commissioners asked to pause item 24-0179 ($350k Sheriff's Training Facility preconstruction) and item 24-0183 ($200k Project BUILD renovations).

agenda_items.title: BullS Academy and Made in Durham Workforce Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic Development Director Andy Miracle and Made in Durham leadership (Casey Steinbaker, Rasheed Bellamy, Joseph Featherstone) presented outcomes for the $3 million ARPA-funded BullS Academy serving young adults ages 18–25 (96% Black and brown). Cohort 6 achieved a 90% graduation rate (18 of 20) with 25 confirmed placements and Salesforce CRM tracking, though presenters and commissioners warned about post-ARPA sustainability, housing affordability barriers, and tying corporate incentives to local workforce commitments.

agenda_items.title: Community Safety and Wellness Task Force Final Report Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Task force representatives (Xavier Cason, Dr. Jennifer Carroll, Manju Rajendran, Marcia Owen, Muffin Hudson, and colleague Mike) presented 17 total recommendations distilled into seven BOCC budget and policy requests: opioid harm reduction (FTIR drug checking and syringes), countywide/DPS 24/7 HEART expansion with a non-911 line, Justice Services pre- and post-arrest diversion courts, Detention Center 3:1 staffing and solitary confinement limits (<15 days), DSS and Abuse/Neglect/Dependency court reforms, gun/domestic violence ethnodramas and DVPO service, and DPS restorative wellness workshops. Commissioners Howerton and Burns pressed the task force to rank top priorities for a tight FY25 budget, and Burns criticized the panel for not allowing Muffin Hudson to speak earlier.

disagreements.issue: Off-Cycle Preconstruction Capital Requests vs. Comprehensive CIP Review (Items 24-0179 and 24-0183)
disagreements.summary: Commissioners pushed back against placing ad-hoc facility and preconstruction items on the consent agenda outside the formal annual Capital Improvement Plan prioritization process.
disagreements.side_a_position: Pause standalone preconstruction and renovation items (24-0179 Sheriff's Training Facility $350k and 24-0183 Project BUILD $200k) until the Board conducts full CIP and budget deliberations.
side_a_arguments: Approving individual capital preconstruction requests piecemeal bypasses Board ranking against long-waiting priorities such as the animal shelter (delayed 12 years).
Deferring items to budget/CIP work sessions allows commissioners to weigh total capital capacity and site readiness together.
disagreements.side_b_position: Bring forward time-sensitive departmental facility and partner space needs for early preconstruction authorization as they arise.
side_b_arguments: Advancing design and preconstruction prevents delays on active public safety and youth-intervention programs.
disagreements.resolution: Staff agreed to pause item 24-0179 until CIP/budget review and hold item 24-0183 for May work session discussion.

disagreements.issue: Prioritizing Community Safety & Wellness Task Force Budget Requests and Presentation Inclusion
disagreements.summary: During the Community Safety & Wellness Task Force presentation, commissioners pressed for fiscal prioritization among seven costly requests and criticized internal exclusion of task force member Muffin Hudson.
disagreements.side_a_position: The task force must narrow its seven broad funding requests to a realistic top-three priority list for FY25 and ensure all members—especially community representative Muffin Hudson—are permitted to speak fully.
side_a_arguments: The County faces tight FY25 revenue constraints and cannot fund all seven multi-million-dollar requests simultaneously.
Vice Chair Burns objected that task force leadership failed to allow Muffin Hudson to present her sections earlier in the briefing.
disagreements.side_b_position: Present the full seven-part interconnected safety and wellness package as adopted by the task force rather than pre-cutting community recommendations.
side_b_arguments: Harm reduction, diversion, detention reform, DSS family support, and HEART expansion address mutually reinforcing root causes of justice involvement.
disagreements.resolution: Discussion continued into the afternoon session (Part 2) with staff directed to price options such as FTIR drug checking and countywide HEART tiers.

meetings.title: BOCC - March 25, 2024 - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: The available recording for the March 25, 2024 regular session begins mid-discussion on pulled consent items 24-0174 and 24-0128, a roughly $280,000 mid-year renewal for Sheriff's Office Microsoft Office 365 licenses, which the Board unanimously approved 5-0 while criticizing the last-minute recurring oversight. CFO Tiffany Murray and external auditors then presented the FY23 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR), reporting an unmodified clean audit opinion with only one non-material DSS compliance finding. The Board concluded by announcing Amanda Gordon Redmond's appointment to the Durham County Women's Commission and voting unanimously to enter closed session.

agenda_items.title: Sheriff's Office Microsoft Office 365 License Mid-Year Renewal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: In the opening segment captured on the recording, Attorney Lovelace and Assistant County Manager Dwayne Brinson explained that a ~$280,000 mid-year renewal for Sheriff's Office email licenses had been missed during budget transition following Finance Director Mr. Hinton's passing, requiring a one-time general fund balance appropriation and incorporation into the FY25 base budget. Vice Chair Burns and Chair Allam voiced frustration over late recurring requests before the Board voted 5-0 to approve.

agenda_items.title: FY23 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR) and Audit Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Tiffany Murray, Crystal Lee, and external auditor Scott presented the FY23 audit, awarding unmodified opinions on both the financial statements and single audit, with one non-material noncompliance finding in a DSS monthly cross-cutting report and a $2.5 million fair-market-value investment adjustment not rising to a significant deficiency. Auditors reviewed GASB 96 subscription-based IT asset implementation and upcoming GASB compensated-absences rules, answered Commissioner Jacobs's questions on negative net position from pension/OPEB and GO bonds, and heard Vice Chair Burns praise the County's clean audit relative to Durham Public Schools' payroll issues.

agenda_items.title: Board Appointment Announcement and Closed Session Motion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Curtis Massey announced the Board's appointment of Amanda Gordon Redmond to the Durham County Women's Commission. The Board then voted unanimously to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) for economic development incentives and attorney-client privilege.

votes.item_title: Items 24-0174 and 24-0128: Sheriff's Office Microsoft Office 365 Email License Renewal
votes.notes: Recording begins mid-discussion of these items; funded one-time from general fund balance and slated for FY25 base budget.
votes.discussion_detail: Staff explained that an approximately $280,000 mid-year renewal for Sheriff's Office Microsoft Office 365 licenses had fallen through the cracks during leadership transitions after Finance Director Mr. Hinton's death, and Assistant County Manager Dwayne Brinson confirmed no surplus existed in the public safety budget to absorb it. Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns and Chair Nida Allam expressed frustration that recurring software licenses were brought forward at the last minute, urging staff to embed the cost permanently into the FY25 base budget. Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton moved approval of items 24-0174 and 24-0128, seconded by Vice Chair Burns. The Board approved both items unanimously 5-0.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session Pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) and Attorney-Client Privilege
votes.notes: Closed session regarding economic development incentives and attorney-client privileged matters.
votes.discussion_detail: After the ACFR audit presentation and the Women's Commission appointment announcement, Chair Nida Allam called at 00:38:56 for a motion to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) to discuss economic development incentives and consult with the County Attorney on privileged matters. Unidentified commissioners moved and seconded the motion on the floor. All five commissioners voted aye unanimously by voice vote at 00:40:00.

meetings.title: BOCC - March 11, 2024 - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 11, 2024 regular session, Chair Nida Allam delivered Durham County's first-ever Land Acknowledgement, Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns announced the Edna Spaulding Leadership Awards honoring the historic all-women board, and Interim County Attorney Curtis Massey was ceremonially sworn in. After presenting proclamations for Women's History Month, the 50th Annual CROP Hunger Walk, and Ramadan, the Board approved the consent agenda 5-0 excluding pulled item 24-0076. Following public testimony from Preserve Rural Durham residents demanding a development moratorium over Falls Lake and Little Lick Creek pollution, the Board voted 5-0 to approve item 24-0076, a $91,900 City-County interlocal agreement to develop the Southeast Durham Watershed Improvement Plan, before entering closed session.

agenda_items.title: First Land Acknowledgement, Announcements, and Ceremonial Swearing-In of Interim County Attorney Curtis Massey
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Nida Allam opened the meeting with Durham County's inaugural Land Acknowledgement, followed by announcements including Vice Chair Burns launching the Edna Spaulding Leadership Awards to mark the final month of the all-women Board and Allam announcing a March 27 community Ramadan Iftar. The Board then held a ceremonial swearing-in for Interim County Attorney Curtis Massey, with all five commissioners praising his leadership on COVID-19 orders, the CROWN Act, and the Non-Discrimination Ordinance.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations (Women's History Month, CROP Hunger Walk, Ramadan)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners read and presented proclamations recognizing Women's History Month (accepted by Cassandra Cooper of Equitable Well-Being), the 50th Annual Durham CROP Hunger Walk (accepted by event organizers), and the Governor's Ramadan 2024 Proclamation (read by Chair Allam).

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Item 24-0076)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With item 24-0076 pulled for public comment on Southeast Durham watershed planning, Commissioner Heidi Carter moved and Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns seconded approval of the remainder of the consent agenda, passing 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item: Southeast Durham Watershed Improvement Plan Interlocal Agreement ($91,900)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: During public comment on item 24-0076, Preserve Rural Durham speakers Pam Andrews, Tammy Sawyer, and Tom Freeman cited NC State and UNC Collaboratory studies documenting stream sediment and chlorophyll-a degradation in Little Lick Creek and Falls Lake, urged an immediate moratorium on high-density development for ~37,000 projected new residents, and sought monthly public RFP transparency. Vice Chair Burns questioned passing the item without direct relief for residents and pressed for stronger community outreach, while Commissioner Jacobs and staff clarified the $91,900 contract initiates the watershed plan and community engagement before passing 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following adoption of item 24-0076, the Board voted unanimously 5-0 to enter closed session to consult with the County Attorney regarding two attorney-client privileged matters, including Wood/Edmonds et al.

votes.item_title: Item 24-0076: Interlocal Agreement with City of Durham for Southeast Durham Watershed Improvement Plan ($91,900)
votes.notes: Authorizes $91,900 County contribution under City-County ILA to procure and execute the watershed study and community outreach.
votes.discussion_detail: Three Southeast Durham residents—Pam Andrews, Tammy Sawyer, and Tom Freeman—spoke against rapid high-density growth in the Little Lick Creek and Falls Lake watersheds, citing NC State and UNC Collaboratory water-quality studies and urging a development moratorium plus monthly public reporting on the plan's RFP. Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns questioned voting on the ILA without immediate regulatory relief for impacted residents and joined Commissioner Wendy Jacobs in seeking assurance of direct resident outreach. County staff clarified that the vote authorizes the interlocal contract specifically to hire consultants, conduct the watershed analysis, and carry out community engagement. Commissioner Jacobs moved approval, seconded by Commissioner Heidi Carter, and the Board passed the item unanimously 5-0.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session Pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3)
votes.notes: Closed session for attorney-client privilege on two matters including Wood/Edmonds et al.
votes.discussion_detail: At 00:56:30, Chair Allam stated the Board needed to convene in closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with legal counsel regarding two matters, including Wood/Edmonds et al. Unidentified board members moved and seconded the motion. The Board approved entering closed session unanimously 5-0 by voice vote at 00:57:25.

disagreements.issue: Southeast Durham Watershed Improvement Plan Scope vs. Resident Demands for Development Moratorium (Item 24-0076)
disagreements.summary: Public commenters and Vice Chair Burns questioned whether approving a $91,900 watershed planning agreement addressed urgent stormwater pollution without halting high-density construction in Southeast Durham.
disagreements.side_a_position: Residents need immediate regulatory relief—including a moratorium on high-density development—and guaranteed community participation rather than merely commissioning another planning study.
side_a_arguments: Speakers cited elevated sediment and chlorophyll-a levels in Little Lick Creek and Falls Lake alongside roughly 37,000 incoming residents.
Vice Chair Burns questioned moving forward without direct resident relief and demanded verifiable outreach to impacted neighborhoods.
disagreements.side_b_position: Approve the $91,900 City-County interlocal agreement now so technical watershed analysis and formal community outreach can proceed.
side_b_arguments: Staff and Commissioner Jacobs clarified the contract itself funds the watershed improvement plan and structured stakeholder engagement.
Completing the joint study equips the City and County with actionable engineering and policy recommendations.
disagreements.resolution: Following clarifications on community engagement scope, the Board voted unanimously 5-0 to approve item 24-0076.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2024-03-04 9:00 AM - Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its March 4, 2024 Work Session presided over by Chair Nida Allam, the Durham Board of County Commissioners heard public comments on Department of Social Services (DSS) custody cases, Health and Human Services (HHS) building air quality, housing/labor issues, and youth mentorship funding, and unanimously appointed Curtis Massey as Interim County Attorney in its only formal action (with no split or contested votes). Responding to air-quality concerns, the County Manager reported that the NC Department of Labor closed the HHS carbon monoxide complaint on February 6 and an external contractor's preliminary readings showed 1.5–3 ppm, well below the 9 ppm EPA threshold. During consent review, Commissioner Wendy Jacobs and staff discussed Item 24-076, an interlocal agreement with the City of Durham for the $3 million Southeast Durham Watershed Improvement Plan (including ~$910,895.51 from County enterprise funds) to guide Falls Lake stormwater retrofits and the UDO rewrite. Following a truncated middle segment, staff briefed the Board on the newly closed 129-acre Northern Durham farm/agricultural campus (~$2 million acquisition), detailing immediate code/dam repairs alongside plans for precision agriculture, 0.25-to-2-acre training plots for beginning and BIPOC farmers, and grant leveraging before the Board suspended its rules and appointed Massey as Interim County Attorney.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Citizen Comments, and HHS Building Carbon Monoxide Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Nida Allam opened the work session and heard four public speakers: Cheryl Smith (requesting an open-court DSS hearing and visitation), Rafik Sadiq (requesting FOIA status on HHS building carbon monoxide testing), Amanda Wallace (criticizing rent, school/union pay, and DSS oversight), and a Charles Hamilton Youth Foundation representative seeking FY budget mentorship funding. County Manager then reported a February 6 NC Department of Labor closure letter finding no hazardous CO conditions and preliminary external testing at 1.5–3 ppm (below the 9 ppm EPA 8-hour limit) with 4x/day staff monitoring.

agenda_items.title: Consent Review: Item 24-076 Southeast Durham Watershed Improvement Plan ILA
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented Item 24-076, authorizing an interlocal agreement with the City of Durham for the $3 million Southeast Durham Watershed Improvement Plan, including a County enterprise-fund contribution of $910,895.51 and work by Wildlands Engineering over 18–24 months. Responding to Commissioner Wendy Jacobs (Chair of the Upper Neuse River Basin Association), staff confirmed the study will identify Falls Lake stormwater retrofits and nutrient-management projects while informing the Comprehensive Plan and UDO rewrite.

agenda_items.title: Northern Durham 129-Acre Farm / Agricultural Campus Planning Briefing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion of the transcript, staff briefed commissioners on the recently closed 129-acre Northern Durham property (~$2 million acquisition approved in November), outlining immediate building-code and dam/pond stabilization needs alongside public engagement and grant-leveraging plans. Presenters highlighted opportunities for northern county meeting space, recreation, controlled-environment agriculture, and 0.25-to-2-acre training plots for beginning, veteran, immigrant, and BIPOC farmers, winning strong praise from Commissioner Wendy Jacobs and colleagues.

agenda_items.title: Suspension of Rules and Appointment of Interim County Attorney Curtis Massey
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At the close of the work session, the Board unanimously voted to suspend the rules (moved by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs) and then unanimously voted to appoint Curtis Massey as Interim County Attorney until a permanent County Attorney is named (moved by Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns, seconded by Commissioner Heidi Carter). Before adjourning, Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton requested placing school aftercare on a future work session agenda.

votes.item_title: Motion to Suspend Rules for Interim County Attorney Appointment
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote ('All in favor... Any opposed? No. Okay. Rules are suspended'). Named mover is Commissioner Wendy Jacobs; full attendance count across the truncated 4.5-hour work session is not explicitly read on the record.
votes.discussion_detail: Procedural motion suspending the rules to allow formal action at the work session to appoint an Interim County Attorney.

votes.item_title: Appointment of Curtis Massey as Interim County Attorney
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote ('Move by vice chair. Seconded by commissioner Carter. All in favor say aye. Any opposed? Congratulations. Interim county attorney').
votes.discussion_detail: Appoints Curtis Massey to serve as Interim County Attorney until a permanent County Attorney appointment is made.

meetings.executive_summary: At the February 26, 2024 regular session, the Board of County Commissioners approved prior meeting minutes 5-0 and recognized Black History Month, Piedmont Farm Family of the Year (Bull City Farm), Soil & Water Conservation Technical District of the Year, and Conservation Education Teachers of the Year. Commissioners adopted the consent agenda 5-0 excluding three Sheriff's Office items (24-0034, 24-0042, and 24-0045) pulled for public comment, and subsequently approved those three items 5-0 after hearing speakers question carceral spending and urge greater prevention investments. agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, Minutes Approval, and Ceremonial Recognitions

The Board approved three sets of minutes 5-0 and presented recognitions for Black History Month, Bull City Farm as Piedmont Farm Family of the Year, the Soil & Water Conservation District Technical District of the Year, and Conservation Education Teachers of the Year; Chair Allam also declined an off-agenda public comment request under existing meeting rules.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Items 24-0034, 24-0042, and 24-0045)

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners - Work Session for February 5, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Nida Allam presided over a five-hour February 5, 2024 BOCC work session covering urgent detention center/youth home contracts, capital project updates, ARPA affordable housing strategy, strategic planning, and the draft FY25 Transit Work Program. During citizen comments, Durham Public Schools classified employees pleaded for commissioner intervention and funding after salary schedule changes dropped experienced workers down the pay scale. Under Other Business, the board suspended the rules and unanimously voted 5-0 to approve three urgent contracts and budget amendments totaling $609,963.33 for detention center boilers and Wellpath medical staffing. Lengthy work session discussions included Santee Road Park planning, Durham Tech's $112M bond-funded Life and Health Sciences buildings, the Durham Affordable Housing Loan Fund with Self-Help Credit Union, DCo Forward 2029 strategic plan feedback, the $45M draft FY25 Transit Work Program, and the Museum of Life and Science capital update.

agenda_items.title: Public Charge, Agenda Adjustments, and Citizen Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Nida Allam announced the cancellation of the February 12-13 meeting due to the NACo conference and moved Item 24-0055 (ARPA Update) before lunch. Four citizens spoke: Durham Public Schools classified employees (including physical therapist Heidi Jo Hetland) described being dropped from step 33 to step 1 on the new salary schedule and pleaded for commissioner intervention and funding to prevent mass resignations, while another speaker criticized Durham County's child welfare system.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review for Next Regular Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Dr. Sowell reviewed upcoming consent items, including a sidewalk and bus shelter easement at 300 E. Main Street (23-0665), a $104,197 LeChase Construction contingency increase for the 300 E. Main Street parking deck due to a 10-week podium delay (24-0027), $280,241.07 in Microsoft licenses for the Sheriff's Office (24-0034), a $24,000 City-County Bike and Pedestrian Plan ILA (24-0058), the FY23 Transit Progress Report (24-0059) and $126,254 Q3 Transit Work Program amendment (24-0061), $105,300 JCPC reallocation (24-0064), and $100,000 in Open Space matching grants to the Eno River Association and El Futuro (24-0067).

agenda_items.title: Other Business (24-0038): Detention Center Reheat Boilers Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff explained that two detention center reheat boilers installed in 2011 had experienced recurring heat-exchanger failures over the last five years and requested approval of a $213,971 CIP-funded contract with Envirotrol LLC for more efficient replacements. The board suspended the rules and approved the contract.

agenda_items.title: Other Business (24-0006): Youth Home Wellpath Enhanced Staffing (BOA 24BCC0077)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board considered Budget Ordinance Amendment 24BCC0077 appropriating $283,192 from general fund balance to fund enhanced staffing under the Wellpath contract for the Durham County Youth Home. With no questions, the board suspended the rules and unanimously approved the amendment.

agenda_items.title: Other Business (24-0047): Detention Center & Youth Home Wellpath Medical Contract CPI Increase (BOA 24BCC0078)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health Director Rod Jenkins explained that Budget Ordinance Amendment 24BCC0078 appropriating $112,800.33 from general fund balance represented a negotiated 3% Consumer Price Index increase on the existing Wellpath inmate and youth home comprehensive medical contract, distinct from the staffing addition in 24-0006. The board suspended the rules and approved the item.

agenda_items.title: Santee Road Park Project Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Open Space Manager Celeste Burns presented plans for the 268-acre Santee Road property in East Durham acquired with City of Raleigh watershed protection funds, leaving 36 acres eligible for trails, camping, and nature-based outdoor education. Staff proposed issuing an RFQ for community engagement and preliminary design funded by roughly $300,000 held in trust by the Durham Parks Foundation without requiring new county appropriations.

agenda_items.title: Item 24-0069: Durham Technical Community College Capital Projects Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham Tech President J.B. Buxton and Dr. Susan Bowen updated commissioners on the $35M Life Sciences Building (Andre Johnson Architects, 36% MWBE) and $77M Health Sciences Building (Lord Aeck Sargent, 17% MWBE), noting a minimum 25% MWBE commitment for construction managers at risk and expected completions in late 2027 and January 2028. They also discussed renovating Building 9 for the Health Sciences Early College starting Fall 2025 via a ~$30M Bloomberg Philanthropies grant (with Duke Health waiving under-18 clinical rotation restrictions) and awaiting 4% LIHTC approval on the South Briggs affordable housing project.

agenda_items.title: Item 24-0055: ARPA Update and Durham Affordable Housing Loan Fund Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy County Manager Claudia Hager and Self-Help Credit Union's John Frolick reported on the $10M Durham Affordable Housing Loan Fund (fully deployed across 243 preserved units) and outlined how $500,000 to $2 million in county top-loss capital could leverage up to $8 million in total new lending capacity (expanding the fund to $18M). Commissioners questioned staff and Frolick on preserving existing affordable housing versus new construction, deed restriction lengths (10-20 years vs. 30 years and right of first refusal), senior home repair braiding, and whether to contribute directly to the existing City fund or issue a county RFP.

agenda_items.title: Item 24-0066: Strategic Plan Update (DCo Forward 2029)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief of Staff Shannon Trapp, Director of Strategy and Performance Josh Edwards, and staff presented resident and employee survey findings (505 resident responses, 25% staff response), DEIB-revised mission/vision/core values statements, and seven proposed strategic focus areas ahead of a June 2024 final approval target. Commissioners Heidi Carter, Nimasheena Burns, and Wendy Jacobs urged simpler, measurable language and called for explicitly elevating environmental sustainability and MWBE contracting goals.

agenda_items.title: Item 24-0065: Draft FY25 Durham Annual Transit Work Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation Director Ellen Beckman and GoTriangle's Steve Schlossberg presented the ~$45 million draft FY25 Durham Annual Transit Work Program (excluding the vehicle rental tax retained by GoTriangle), highlighting GoDurham service restoration, increased transit share ($30M) for GoDurham bus and paratransit maintenance facilities, $9.98M for Durham Station upgrades, $600K local match alongside a $1.2M federal grant for the East Durham railroad crossing study, and two new fare-equity proposals ($374K City reprogramming plus $1.9M City ask for fare-free GoDurham; $78K Durham share for GoTriangle's regional low-income pass). Commissioners discussed minimum fund balance policies, raising the $5 vehicle fee at the General Assembly, and fare-free versus sliding-scale fare structures ahead of April adoption.

agenda_items.title: Item 24-0056: Museum of Life and Science Capital Projects Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Museum of Life and Science leadership reported completing all 2016 bond projects (Earth Moves, Play to Learn, parking deck, animal quarantine), launching 2022 bond projects including a Living Building Challenge café and climate/biotech exhibits, and reaching 580,000 annual visitors (+80,000) and 14,000 Ignite $5-membership visits. Commissioners discussed improving public transit access to the campus, expanding Ignite outreach through DSS/early childhood networks, and positioning the museum at the General Assembly relative to Kidzu's state children's museum designation effort.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session: Attorney-Client Privilege (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session on two attorney-client privilege items under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3). Upon returning at 05:20:24, the board reported giving direction to staff and adjourned.

votes.item_title: Motion to Suspend Rules for Item 24-0038 (Detention Center Boilers)
votes.notes: Moved by Vice Chair Burns, seconded by Commissioner Howerton; unanimous Aye.
votes.discussion_detail: Because work sessions do not normally include formal votes, the board voted to suspend the rules to take immediate action on the urgent detention center reheat boiler replacement contract.

votes.notes: Includes authority to execute change orders/amendments within available CIP funds.
votes.discussion_detail: Commissioner Wendy Jacobs asked why the existing boilers purchased earlier were failing; staff clarified they were installed in 2011 and had repeated heat-exchanger failures over the past five years, and a different, more efficient boiler type was selected. Approved unanimously after suspension of rules.

votes.item_title: Motion to Suspend Rules for Item 24-0006 (Youth Home Wellpath Staffing)
votes.notes: Moved by Vice Chair Burns, seconded by Commissioner Jacobs.
votes.discussion_detail: The board voted to suspend the rules at the work session to act immediately on Budget Ordinance Amendment 24BCC0077 for Youth Home enhanced staffing.

votes.item_title: Approval of Item 24-0006: BOA 24BCC0077 ($283,192) for Wellpath Youth Home Enhanced Staffing
votes.notes: Chair Allam announced '24-006 is approved unanimously.'
votes.discussion_detail: Appropriates $283,192 of general fund balance to cover enhanced staffing in the Wellpath contract for the Durham County Youth Home. Passed unanimously without further questions.

votes.item_title: Motion to Suspend Rules for Item 24-0047 (Wellpath Medical Contract CPI Increase)
votes.notes: Chair announced motion by Commissioner Howerton, second by Vice Chair Burns; unanimous Aye.
votes.discussion_detail: Following Public Health Director Rod Jenkins's clarification that Item 24-0047 covered a negotiated 3% CPI increase distinct from Item 24-0006, the board voted to suspend the rules for immediate action.

votes.item_title: Approval of Item 24-0047: BOA 24BCC0078 ($112,800.33) for Wellpath Comprehensive Medical Services
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote with no opposed.
votes.discussion_detail: Appropriates $112,800.33 of general fund balance to cover a 3% CPI increase to the Wellpath medical services contract for inmates at the Durham County Detention Center and residents at the Youth Home.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners - Work Session for February 5, 2024
disagreements.issue: Durham Affordable Housing Loan Fund: Affordability Deed-Restriction Terms and County Fund Structure
disagreements.summary: Commissioners differed during the ARPA/Self-Help Credit Union presentation over whether public dollars in the loan fund should require strict 30-year affordability and right-of-first-refusal terms versus more flexible 10-to-20-year restrictions to attract developers, and whether Durham County should invest directly in the existing City/Self-Help loan fund or launch a separate county RFP and fund.
disagreements.side_a_position: Require long-term (30-year) affordability restrictions and public right of first refusal, and contribute non-ARPA county dollars directly to the existing City/Self-Help fund rather than creating a separate fund.
side_a_arguments: 10-year affordability periods on public investments are insufficient and risk losing affordable units back to market rate.
Contributing directly to the existing City/Self-Help fund avoids duplicating administrative infrastructure.
disagreements.side_b_position: Maintain flexibility on developer restrictions to avoid deterring deals, and establish a distinct county revolving housing fund/RFP targeting $20 million.
side_b_arguments: Overly rigid restrictions can leave developers unwilling to participate, yielding zero units instead of flexible affordable units.
A dedicated county RFP/fund similar to Wake County's model can target county-specific needs and scale toward $20 million.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote taken; staff noted they would return with refined options and recommendations at a subsequent meeting.

meetings.title: BOCC - Regular Session for Monday, January 22, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Nida Allam presided over the January 22, 2024 regular session, which opened with a 4-0 vote to enter a one-hour closed session on personnel matters under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) before reconvening in open session with all five commissioners present. The board thanked county emergency management, DSS, public health, and library staff for operating warming stations during the prior week's winter power outages and approved the January 2 and January 8 minutes and the consent agenda 5-0, including Lincoln Community Health Center parking expansion and an updated Development Finance Initiative RFP scope for the DSS building expansion. Following a public hearing with no speakers, the board voted 5-0 to adopt a resolution authorizing installment financing contract amendments for up to $87 million in Limited Obligation Bonds (Series 2024A and 2024B) for Board of Elections renovations, the Snow Hill Road pump station, school facility renovations/safety improvements, and the 500 block of East Main Street parking facility. County Attorney Curtis Massey also announced three board and commission appointments.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session: Personnel (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board opened the meeting by voting 4-0 to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) to consider the qualifications, competence, performance, character, fitness, or conditions of appointment of a public officer or employee. The board reconvened in open session at 01:00:02 reporting no action taken and direction given to staff.

agenda_items.title: Opening Ceremonies, Announcements, Staff Acknowledgements, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Wendy Jacobs led the Pledge of Allegiance and Clerk Wallace read published announcements including the January 25 MLK observance, February 3 Durham Pre-K info session, Soil and Water conservation contest, Cooperative Extension grafting workshop, DCo Cares nonprofit applications, the draft FY25 Transit Work Program, Voter ID outreach, March 5 primary early voting, and public health vaccine clinics. Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns and Commissioner Jacobs praised emergency management, DSS, public health, library staff, and small businesses for shelter, food, and warming center responses during the prior week's power outages, and the board approved the January 2 and January 8, 2024 minutes.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: No items were pulled from the consent agenda, though Commissioner Wendy Jacobs highlighted two items advancing the long-awaited Lincoln Community Health Center parking lot expansion and asked about community engagement in Item 24-0032 (updating the DSS building expansion RFP with DFI). County staff explained DFI would refine financial and market information for a broad RFP first and conduct community engagement on outfitting the building after vendor selection, and the board approved the consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Resolution: Not to Exceed $87 Million Limited Obligation Bonds (Series 2024A and 2024B)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board conducted a noticed public hearing on amending an installment financing contract to issue up to $87 million in Limited Obligation Bonds for shopping center renovations housing the Board of Elections, the Snow Hill Road pump station, renovations and public safety improvements to county school facilities, and a parking facility at the 500 block of East Main Street. With no members of the public signed up to speak in person or online, the board closed the public hearing and adopted the authorizing financing resolution.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Curtis Massey announced the tallied board ballot selections: Jean Rhea for the Board of Health pharmacist position, Kirsten Bethe for the Durham County Women's Commission at-large position, and Matt Copac for the Durham Planning Commission at-large position.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6))
votes.notes: Chair Allam announced 'Motion passes. Four to zero.' Four of five seated commissioners were present at the start of the meeting (identity of the fourth voting member between Brenda A. Howerton and Wendy Jacobs is not spoken on the record; all five were present by the regular session).
votes.discussion_detail: At the start of the meeting, Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns moved and Commissioner Heidi Carter seconded entering closed session to discuss a personnel matter under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6).

votes.item_title: Approval of January 2, 2024 Work Session and January 8, 2024 Regular Session Minutes
votes.notes: Chair Allam announced 'Minutes are approved. Five to zero.'
votes.discussion_detail: Commissioner Wendy Jacobs moved and Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns seconded approval of the January 2, 2024 work session minutes and January 8, 2024 regular session minutes.

votes.item_title: Motion to Close Public Hearing on Not to Exceed $87 Million Limited Obligation Bonds
votes.notes: Mover and seconder were not named aloud by the chair; all five commissioners were present and voted Aye with none opposed.
votes.discussion_detail: After confirming no speakers signed up in person or online for the public hearing on the Limited Obligation Bonds installment financing amendment, a commissioner moved to close the public hearing and the board voted unanimously in favor.

meetings.title: BOCC - Regular Session for Monday, January 8, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Nida Allam presided over the January 8, 2024 regular session, which featured ceremonial recognitions alongside two land-use public hearings. The board introduced Durham County's new Early Childhood Coordinator, adopted proclamations and resolutions for National Mentoring Month and Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Day, congratulated Sheriff Clarence Birkhead on a 100/100 ACA jail reaccreditation audit score, and approved prior minutes and the consent agenda 5-0. Following public hearings, the board voted 5-0 to adopt UDO Text Amendment TC23003 creating the Eno River Critical District A2 (EA2) watershed overlay around the new Teer Quarry water intake and its consistency statement, and voted 5-0 to approve Street Closing SC220008 closing portions of Electra Road, Exum Road, and an unimproved 30-foot lane to expand the Sheriff's firing range buffer after clarifying to a resident that no algae scrubber was planned on the site. The board concluded with a closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6), taking no action.

agenda_items.title: Opening Ceremonies, Announcements, Sheriff Re-Accreditation Recognition, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter led the Pledge of Allegiance and Clerk Wallace read published announcements including the Justice Resources resource fair, FY24 Q3 Durham Transit Work Plan comment period, and vaccine clinics. Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns congratulated Sheriff Clarence Birkhead on achieving 100 out of 100 compliance during the detention center's American Correctional Association three-year reaccreditation audit, and the board approved the November 27, 2023 and December 4, 2023 minutes.

agenda_items.title: Introduction of New Durham County Early Childhood Coordinator
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff introduced Durham County's newly hired Early Childhood Coordinator (former Book Babies leader at Book Harvest with an M.Ed. in early intervention and family support) to lead implementation of the Early Childhood Action Plan alongside the county's $6 million-plus investment in Durham Pre-K. Commissioners welcomed her and emphasized early childhood brain development and family support.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: National Mentoring Month (January 2024)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter read a proclamation declaring January 2024 National Mentoring Month. DeWarren Langley of the Charles Hamilton Houston Foundation and representatives from El Centro Hispano, Bull City Bulldogs, Wall Street Juniors, Inspiring Minds, and MBK Durham shared updates on youth mentoring, financial literacy, and violence-prevention programs.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Celebrating and Honoring Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns read a resolution honoring the life and service of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. DeWarren Langley accepted the resolution on behalf of the MLK Steering Committee and announced upcoming observance ceremonies, $1,000 student scholarships, and Keeper of the Dream awards.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Nida Allam noted the items had been reviewed during the prior work session and asked if any commissioner wished to pull an item. Seeing none, the board unanimously approved the consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment — Teer Quarry Intake (TC23003)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff Aaron Cain and Sarah Young presented staff-initiated UDO Text Amendment TC23003 (revising Articles 4, 8, and 12) required by state watershed regulations for a new Eno River water intake at Teer Quarry, creating the Eno River Critical District A2 (EA2) overlay within a half-mile of the intake while exempting existing lots unless redeveloped. Water Management's Sid Miller noted construction and regular supplemental water withdrawal are roughly three to four years away; with no public speakers, the board adopted the ordinance and its N.C.G.S. 160D-605 consistency statement.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing (24-0002): Street Closing Request — Electra Road, Exum Road, and 30-Foot Lane (SC220008)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented County-initiated street closing SC220008 (filed by Jose Torres on behalf of Durham County) to permanently close a 1,112-foot section of Electra Road, a 694-foot unimproved portion of Exum Road, and a 1,168-foot unimproved 30-foot lane so adjacent county parcels could recombine into a 90.2-acre parcel providing a larger, safer buffer for the Sheriff's firing range. Resident Wanda Allen questioned whether the closure was linked to a $10M Falls Lake algae scrubber shown on a county map; staff and ACM Julio Delgado confirmed the site plan contained no algae scrubber and the parcels did not extend to the water, after which the board closed the hearing and approved the street closing.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session: Personnel (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) regarding an individual public officer or employee. Upon returning at 02:57:32, the board announced no action was taken and adjourned.

votes.item_title: Approval of November 27, 2023 Regular Session and December 4, 2023 Work Session Minutes
votes.notes: Chair Allam announced 'Motion to approve the minutes passes five to zero.'
votes.discussion_detail: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton moved and Commissioner Heidi Carter seconded approval of the November 27, 2023 regular session minutes and December 4, 2023 work session minutes.

votes.item_title: Adoption of UDO Text Amendment Ordinance: Teer Quarry Intake (TC23003)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously with none opposed (5-0 confirmed on adjacent consistency vote).
votes.discussion_detail: Following the public hearing with no speakers, Commissioner Wendy Jacobs moved and Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns seconded adopting the ordinance amending UDO Articles 4, 8, and 12 to establish the Eno River Critical District A2 (EA2) watershed overlay for Teer Quarry.

votes.item_title: Adoption of Consistency Statement (N.C.G.S. 160D-605) for UDO Text Amendment TC23003
votes.notes: Chair Allam announced 'The ayes have it. Five to zero to adopt the consistency statement.'
votes.discussion_detail: Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns moved and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs seconded adopting the statutory consistency statement required by N.C.G.S. 160D-605 for the Teer Quarry UDO text amendment.

Howerton seconded permanently closing the 1,112-foot portion of Electra Road, 1,168-foot portion of the 30-foot lane, and Exum Road.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6))
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote with none opposed.

meetings.title: BOCC - Work Session for Tuesday, January 2, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Nida Allam presided over the January 2, 2024 BOCC work session, opening with citizen comments from Durham County library staff opposing a proposed Sunday hours expansion without first conducting an independent staffing audit, ending 7-day work rotations, guaranteeing comp time, and recognizing workers' right to organize; County Manager Dr. Sowell replied that no decision had been made and an external consultant and internal operational assessment were underway. Commissioners reviewed upcoming consent agenda items including separating the Public Information Office into its own fund center ($175,000), expanding a Durham Center for Senior Life navigator to full time ($40,000), increasing Freese and Nichols's Snow Hill Road pump station contract (+$416,360), and switching 17 Sheriff hybrid vehicles to EcoBoost due to supply availability ($159,000 savings). Under discussion items, the board suspended the rules and voted 5-0 to approve statutory public official bonds, and reviewed an ARPA update showing 71% of $62.4 million encumbered across 57 projects alongside Affordable Housing Task Force recommendations before entering closed session on litigation (Anthony DiBrosky v. Durham County).

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments: Library Sunday Hours, Staffing, and Labor Protections
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Library workers Kyle Lampert, John Davis (whose Zoom audio dropped, prompting the clerk to invite written submission), and Larkin Coffey urged the board to perform an independent staffing audit, fill vacant positions, end 11-month terminations of substitute workers, prohibit 7-day work rotations, guarantee full comp time for Sunday shifts, and recognize workers' right to organize before opening libraries on Sundays. County Manager Dr. Sowell responded that no decision had been made, any proposed rotation would involve only 3-4 Sundays per year without 7-day stretches, and both an external consultant and the Office of Strategy and Performance were evaluating library operations and culture.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review for Next Regular Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Dr. Sowell reviewed items slated for the regular session consent agenda, including creating a dedicated PIO fund center ($175,000, Item 23-0762), renewing Accela for Durham One Call ($42,770.82, Item 23-0911), expanding a Durham Center for Senior Life food/benefits navigator to 1 FTE ($40,000, Item 23-0920), increasing Freese & Nichols engineering services for the Snow Hill Road pump station (+$416,360 to $821,360, Item 23-0924), and substituting 17 Ford EcoBoost interceptors for unavailable hybrids for the Sheriff's Office (Item 24-0015, saving $159,000). Commissioners asked about city cost-sharing and Cabin Branch failing septic systems on Snow Hill Road and thanked retiring food security coordinator Mary Oxendine.

agenda_items.title: Discussion Item: Approval of Public Official Bonds
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Andrews presented statutory performance bonds required by North Carolina General Statutes—held over from December due to new personnel in the CFO ($1M cap) and Tax Administrator roles and covering the Register of Deeds and Sheriff as well—while noting dated statutory language like 'chairman' and 'his' would be updated where permissible. The board suspended the rules and unanimously approved the bonds for all four officials.

agenda_items.title: ARPA Implementation Update and Affordable Housing Task Force Recommendations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy County Manager Claudia Hager reported that 71% of the county's $62.4 million ARPA funds were encumbered or committed across 57 projects ahead of the December 21, 2024 encumbrance deadline, with ~$500,000 remaining uncommitted alongside $3.5 million in revenue replacement flexibility and pending RFPs for youth, digital equity, arts, senior home repair, and land trusts. Hager and engineering staff presented three Affordable Housing Task Force white-paper recommendations: investing in an affordable housing loan fund, reviewing post-pandemic housing support services, and establishing an affordable housing scorecard. Commissioners debated contributing directly to the existing City/Self-Help fund versus running a county RFP for a $20M revolving fund, stressed 30-year affordability and right-of-first-refusal safeguards, and discussed transit/planning representation and homelessness shelter needs ahead of a February deep-dive.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session: Attorney-Client Privilege (Anthony DiBrosky v. Durham County, N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to adjourn into closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with counsel regarding Anthony DiBrosky v. Durham County. After returning at 02:24:38, the chair reported no action was taken and direction was given to staff, and adjourned the meeting.

votes.item_title: Motion to Suspend Rules for Approval of Public Official Bonds
votes.notes: Chair Allam announced 'Ayes have it 5 to 0.' Mover and seconder were not named aloud.
votes.discussion_detail: Because timely filing with the Clerk of Court was required for newly appointed CFO and Tax Administrator performance bonds alongside the Register of Deeds and Sheriff bonds, the board voted to suspend the rules at the work session.

votes.item_title: Approval of Public Official Bonds (CFO, Tax Administrator, Register of Deeds, and Sheriff)
votes.notes: Chair Allam announced 'Ayes have it 5 to 0.'
votes.discussion_detail: Commissioner Wendy Jacobs moved approval of the public official bonds for all four statutory officers (CFO, Tax Administrator, Register of Deeds, and Sheriff) to meet statutory requirements, and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton seconded.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3))
votes.notes: Chair Allam announced 'the ayes have it five to zero.'
votes.discussion_detail: Commissioner Heidi Carter moved and Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns seconded entering closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with the county attorney regarding Anthony DiBrosky v. Durham County.

disagreements.meeting_title: BOCC - Work Session for Tuesday, January 2, 2024
disagreements.issue: Structure of County Participation in Affordable Housing Loan Fund (Direct City Contribution vs. County-Specific RFP)
disagreements.summary: During discussion of the Affordable Housing Task Force's first recommendation, commissioners expressed differing preferences on whether to contribute non-ARPA county funds directly into the existing City of Durham loan fund or issue a separate county RFP to establish a distinct county revolving housing fund.
disagreements.side_a_position: Contribute non-ARPA county funding directly to the existing City of Durham loan fund for governmental efficiency while reserving ARPA/RFP funds for distinct models like community land trusts.
side_a_arguments: Creating a separate county fund duplicates an existing City/Self-Help mechanism.
Community land trusts are a distinct model that permanently protects against gentrification and warrants their own RFP.
disagreements.side_b_position: Launch a new county RFP and distinct revolving housing fund scaled toward $20 million rather than simply folding into the City's existing fund.
side_b_arguments: The task force white paper identified nuances in county priorities—such as supporting both builders and individuals—that justify a separate county RFP.
Wake County launched its own $61M fund via RFP, and Durham County should aim for a $20M fund rather than remaining at $500,000.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote taken; staff committed to returning in February 2024 with Self-Help Credit Union and detailed funding options.

meetings.title: BOCC - Dec 11, 2023 - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Nida Allam presided over her first regular session following her December 4 election, with Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton granted an excused absence (4-0). The board approved the November 6 work session minutes (4-0), passed the ARPA-heavy consent agenda (4-0), and heard a Department of Social Services presentation on North Carolina's Medicaid expansion rollout. Commissioners then held four Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) public hearings, unanimously approving (4-0) the annual UDO Omnibus Text Amendment, the Pedestrian Malls amendment (23-0894 / TC-2304), and the Conservation Subdivisions clarification (23-0895). On the fourth public hearing—the contentious, privately initiated Simplifying Codes for Affordable Development (SCAD, 23-0896) amendment—the board voted 3-1 to adopt the City Council-modified ordinance and consistency statement, with Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns dissenting.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Excused Absence of Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Nida Allam opened the meeting, read the public charge, and invited Commissioner Heidi Carter to lead the Pledge of Allegiance. Clerk Monica Wallace read announcements including the December 18 Board of Elections Phase One and MWBE outreach session and the DCHC MPO / CAMPO Destination 2055 transportation survey. Chair Allam announced that Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton requested an excused absence, which the board approved.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Presentation: Eno River Association 2024 Calendar
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Eno River Association Executive Director Jessica Sheffield presented the organization's 2024 calendar to the board. Commissioners thanked the association for its ongoing conservation partnership with Durham County.

agenda_items.title: Approval of November 6, 2023 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns's reminder, the board returned to the minutes item before taking up the consent agenda. Commissioners approved the November 6, 2023 work session minutes without edits.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Including ARPA Equity Framework Allocations)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Nimasheena Burns highlighted that the consent agenda included roughly 20 items advancing ARPA funding through an equity framework prioritizing rural, diverse, and urban communities, and praised County Manager Dr. Kimberly Sowell and Deputy Managers Maurice Jones and Claudia Hager. Chair Nida Allam echoed the recognition of staff's work before calling the vote.

agenda_items.title: Presentation on Medicaid Expansion Implementation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Department of Social Services Director Maggie, COO Kelly Inman, and Assistant Director Margaret Faircloth briefed the board on North Carolina's Medicaid expansion launch, explaining online applications via epass.nc.gov as well as in-person and phone intake. Staff reported keeping wait times under 30 minutes while coordinating with partner groups such as Urban Ministries and serving approximately 70,000 existing Medicaid enrollees.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing 1: UDO Omnibus Text Amendment (Comprehensive Plan & Technical Revisions)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Planning Manager Alexander Cahill presented the annual UDO Omnibus Text Amendment, combining technical updates with early Comprehensive Plan implementation measures. Proposed changes expanded mailed public hearing notice from 600 to 1,000 feet, required sign postings for multifamily properties when mailing addresses are unavailable, aligned childcare definitions with state law, allowed Durham Public Schools to seek residential-area school sites via rezoning rather than special use permits, permitted two driveways for duplexes, removed the infill tree-coverage exemption for single-family and duplex lots, and added a 0.6 opacity county-line buffer. No speakers signed up for the public hearing.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing 2 (23-0894 / TC-2304): UDO Text Amendment — Pedestrian Malls
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a privately initiated text amendment (TC-2304) modifying Article 16 Design District streetscape, right-of-way, and block/lot standards for pedestrian malls. Commissioners noted the process worked smoothly and no members of the public signed up to speak.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing 3 (23-0895): UDO Text Amendment — Conservation Subdivisions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Curtis Massey presented a UDO text amendment to Section 6.2.4 / Article 6 clarifying that the 12 general purpose statements for conservation subdivisions are not all mandatory criteria, addressing pending litigation against the county while preserving the 50% open-space requirement. Two public speakers testified during the hearing, and staff noted that recently adopted phased-development and tree-preservation rules apply to conservation subdivisions and residential districts would be prioritized in the UDO rewrite.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing 4 (23-0896): UDO Text Amendment — Simplifying Codes for Affordable Development (SCAD)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented the privately initiated SCAD text amendment as modified and adopted by Durham City Council, noting that the Planning Commission had recommended denial 6-6 in March and that Council removed provisions opposed by staff. Twenty-two speakers addressed the board, with critics raising concerns over inadequate community engagement, developer loopholes, rural/unincorporated impacts, and disability parking accessibility, while supporters urged approval to expand housing supply, ADUs, and walkability. Commissioners voted 4-0 at 04:11:30 to extend the meeting by 15 minutes until 11:00 PM; in final deliberation, Commissioners Carter, Jacobs, and Chair Allam supported adopting the revised SCAD text to maintain a single City-County UDO and expand ADUs and parking-minimum removal, while Vice Chair Burns opposed passing private text amendments prior to the UDO rewrite.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Andrews announced the results of the board's written ballots for two advisory bodies: an appointment to the City-County Appearance Commission and an appointment to the Durham Open Space and Trails Commission.

disagreements.issue: Adoption of Privately Initiated SCAD UDO Text Amendment (23-0896)
disagreements.summary: Commissioners split 3-1 over adopting the City Council-amended Simplifying Codes for Affordable Development (SCAD) UDO text amendment, debating joint City-County UDO uniformity, ADU and parking rules, and whether privately initiated text amendments should wait for the comprehensive UDO rewrite.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt the City Council-modified SCAD amendment to keep a unified City-County UDO, expand ADUs and remove parking minimums, and monitor impacts during the UDO rewrite.
side_a_arguments: Voting no would split the shared UDO into separate City and County ordinances for the first time.

City Council removed the provisions Planning staff flagged as problematic, and remaining items like larger ADUs (above 800 sq ft) and ADUs on church property help county residents and aging family members.
Removing parking minimums reduces car dependency and supports walkability and transit, while staff will monitor unintended impacts ahead of the UDO rewrite.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose adopting the privately initiated SCAD amendment prior to the comprehensive UDO rewrite.
side_b_arguments: As chair of the Joint City-County Planning Committee, Burns recalled near-unanimous agreement to limit private text amendments until the comprehensive UDO rewrite was completed.
Most provisions primarily affect the City rather than unincorporated Durham County, and ADU amendments had already been passed previously.
Rejected political pressure from external advocates and argued the amendment did not meaningfully guarantee affordable housing.
disagreements.resolution: Both the ordinance (23-0896) and its statutory consistency statement passed 3-1 (Allam, Jacobs, Carter aye; Burns nay).
