meetings.title: BOCC Work Session for December 4, 2023
meetings.executive_summary: The December 4, 2023 Work Session opened with the annual board leadership elections, in which the board elected Nida Allam as Chair (majority voice vote) and Nimasheena Burns unanimously as Vice Chair (5-0). Commissioners then reviewed consent agenda items for the December 11 regular meeting, including public health grants, a $50,000 county share for a joint City-County crisis communications plan, $600,000 in LOBs for the new Emergency Operations Center and backup 911 center, and the 2024 meeting calendar (moved to December 11 after flagging a Passover conflict on April 22). In work session presentations, Research Triangle Foundation staff presented proposals for a 100-acre Hub RTP social district and the long-range RTP 3.0 land-use and Urban Research Service District (URSD) tax-district framework. Deputy Manager Claudia Hager concluded with an ARPA update covering remaining project timelines through September 2026, school nurse funding, pre-K, cultural arts, and $2 million for homelessness planning and infrastructure.

agenda_items.title: Annual Election of Board Chair and Vice Chair
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Andrews presided over the statutory annual election of the Board Chair; Commissioner Heidi Carter nominated Nida Allam, who was elected Chair by a majority vote. Newly elected Chair Allam then presided over the Vice Chair election, where Commissioner Wendy Jacobs nominated Nimasheena Burns, who was unanimously elected Vice Chair. Both new leaders and outgoing Chair Brenda A. Howerton—who noted she would not seek reelection—offered remarks on community priorities.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Chair elected by majority; Vice Chair elected 5-0

agenda_items.title: Public Charge and Citizens' Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Allam read the public charge. DeWarren Langley, Executive Director of the Charles Hamilton Houston Foundation, spoke during public comment to urge board investment in youth programming and services.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review for December 11, 2023 Regular Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Dr. Kimberly Sowell walked commissioners through consent items including public health grants (230808 $1,200 RJCM pilot; 230809 $100,000 NACCHO COVID-19 access; 230851 $59,743 Guilford training; 230853 fee schedule), an interlocal agreement with the City of Durham for a Joint Crisis Communications Plan up to $50,000 (230832, with commissioners requesting school stakeholder inclusion), a McKim & Creed utilities contract amendment (230845), Emory Cemetery relocation (230854), tax administration software/authority (230870, 230871, 230872), $600,000 in LOBs for the new EOC and backup 911/Sheriff's Call Center (230882, where Commissioner Jacobs urged pursuing integrated City-County 911 operations), and the 2024 BOCC calendar (230901, deferred to December 11 to check a Passover conflict on April 22).

agenda_items.title: Hub RTP Social District Proposal Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy County Manager Maurice Jones and Research Triangle Foundation Senior Director of Placemaking Amanda Ronan presented a request to establish a social district across the 100-acre Hub RTP site, launching initially in Phase 1 around the retail/food-and-beverage horseshoe, stream, stage, lawn, and splash pad. Vice Chair Burns asked about Research Triangle High School across the street, >35% MWBE construction participation, private security (Cain Security), and transit capacity for future Davis Drive job growth.

agenda_items.title: RTP 3.0 Framework and Urban Research Service District (URSD) Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: RTP leadership and County staff presented the RTP 3.0 long-term vision introducing enhanced corporate campuses, missing-middle residential neighborhoods, and mixed-use density nodes, which would require covenant votes by park landowners and tenants. County staff explained the existing RTP special tax district and statutory Urban Research Service District (URSD) sub-district mechanism—capped at Durham City's 55-cent tax rate—to finance infrastructure and debt service, while commissioners stressed integrating workforce/affordable housing, transit, the Comprehensive Plan, and Durham Tech partnerships.

agenda_items.title: ARPA Funding Recap, Project Status, and Upcoming Allocations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County staff presented an update on the ARPA framework ahead of the September 2026 expenditure deadline, highlighting unspent funds held for public school health nurses (pending hiring), DCO on the Go, pre-K expansion, $735,000 in cultural arts funding led with the City, and $2 million in homelessness planning and infrastructure funds scheduled for January follow-up. Commissioner Jacobs urged prioritizing a homeless day center, reentry housing for women, and addressing rising unsheltered counts and MAT insurance/stigma barriers, while Vice Chair Burns requested a future proclamation honoring outgoing Mayor Elaine O'Neal.

In the named voice vote, Allam, Carter, and Jacobs voted aye; responses from Burns and Howerton were indistinct on the recording, and Attorney Andrews announced the vote in favor of Allam by a majority of the board.

meetings.title: BOCC - Nov 27, 2023 - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the November 27, 2023 Regular Session with Commissioner Nida Allam excused. The board approved the minutes (4-0) and adopted resolutions honoring the late former Youth Home Director Arnold Dennis (23-0863), OES Director Jim Groves for the Colonel Phillips Nichols Waters Award (23-0836), and retiring Justice Services Director Gudrun Parmer for receiving the Order of the Long Leaf Pine. Chair Howerton delivered a multi-year commission highlights report (23-0864) summarizing achievements from 2020–2023 across leadership hires, ARPA investments, affordable housing, the $550.2M 2022 GO bond, and transit. The board unanimously approved the consent agenda (4-0), including a farm campus real estate item (23-0857) and Shoppes at Southpoint management, heard a Food Security Initiatives update (23-0850), and made three advisory board appointments.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, Minutes Approval (23-0881), and Excused Absence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton called the meeting to order, read the public charge, and asked Commissioner Heidi Carter to lead the Pledge of Allegiance. Clerk Monica Wallace announced upcoming events including the Durham Holiday Parade and Navigating Grief at the Main Library. The board approved minutes item 23-0881 (4-0), and Chair Howerton noted Commissioner Nida Allam had an excused absence.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Resolution 23-0863: Honoring the Memory of Arnold Dennis
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Howerton read a resolution honoring Arnold Dennis, who served as Durham County's Youth Home Director from 1985 until his retirement in 2005 and passed away on November 1, 2023. Commissioners Wendy Jacobs and Brenda A. Howerton and Mrs. Betty Dennis reflected on his service on the gang reduction task force and dedication to Durham youth.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Recognition 23-0836: OES Director Jim Groves and Justice Services Director Gudrun Parmer
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board recognized Office of Emergency Services Director Jim Groves for receiving the 2023 Colonel Phillips Nichols Waters Award from the North Carolina Emergency Management Association, alongside retiring Fire Marshal/OES contributions praised by Vice Chair Jacobs and Commissioner Burns. The board also honored retiring Justice Services Director Gudrun Parmer on receiving the Order of the Long Leaf Pine, with remarks from US Attorney's Office representative Rob Lang, Durham Familiar Faces Initiative leaders, and commissioners highlighting drug treatment court, pretrial services, opioid settlement planning, and JCPC expansion.

agenda_items.title: Item 23-0864: Durham County Commission Multi-Year Highlights (2020–2023)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presented a comprehensive review of the board's accomplishments over her three-year tenure as chair, noting the hiring of County Manager Dr. Kimberly Sowell, County Attorney Andrews, and Tax Administrator Keyar Doyle. She highlighted COVID-19 recovery, securing the 2029 World University Summer Games, adopting the 2023 Comprehensive Plan, deploying $62M in ARPA funds, $27M in City-County affordable housing ILAs plus Carver Creek and 300/500 East Main Street, launching DCO Thrives, passing the $550.2M 2022 GO Bond, adopting the Durham County Transit Plan and winning a $1.2M FRA rail safety grant, establishing Community Intervention & Support Services, and expanding county employee benefits with Moms Rising.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Including Farm Campus Real Estate Deal 23-0857 and Shoppes at Southpoint)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Sowell asked if commissioners wished to pull any consent items; Commissioner Wendy Jacobs spotlighted item 23-0857 (farm campus real estate acquisition supporting northern Durham agriculture and commercial kitchen space) for future work-session recognition. Commissioner Burns also highlighted closing the management company agreement for the Shoppes at Southpoint on MLK before the board unanimously approved the consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: Item 23-0850: Food Security Initiatives Update and Upcoming Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Food Security Coordinator Mary Oxendine and Cooperative Extension Director Donna Rewalt presented an update on Durham County's food security continuum, community-designed farm campus planning, and systemic wealth-building strategies. Commissioners asked about sustaining programs after pandemic federal funds expire, pantry 501(c)(3) formation, aging/senior center kitchen infrastructure, and food-waste redirection initiatives.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Andrews announced ballot appointment results: Alexandra Alvarez to the Durham County Women's Commission, and Kenyan Browning and Nicole Connolly to the Farmland Protection Advisory Board.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners Work Session for November 6, 2023
meetings.executive_summary: During the six-hour November 6, 2023 Work Session, Chair Brenda A. Howerton and all five commissioners heard public comments thanking the board for $3 million to preserve Carver Creek Apartments and urging stronger Juvenile Crime Prevention Council (JCPC) data reporting. The board reviewed a slate of consent agenda grants, then suspended the rules (5-0) and approved a resolution (5-0) granting an expedited hearing for UDO conservation-subdivision amendment TC23005 (23-0828). Commissioners also received detailed presentations on the Durham Transit Plan FY24 Q2 Work Program amendments ($139,550 net for GoTriangle mobile ticketing and the FAST 2 study) and Bus Speed & Reliability / BRT study, the 2025 General Reappraisal (23-0821), public health harm reduction and opioid settlement funding, JCPC monitoring ($701,001 state allocation), and Durham County's blasting permit process (23-0827), before discussing commissioner comments and adjourning after closed session.

agenda_items.title: Citizens' Comments (Carver Creek Apartments and JCPC Data)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Housing for New Hope leader Russ Pierce thanked the board for $3 million in matching funding alongside the City of Durham to acquire and preserve 48 affordable units at Carver Creek Apartments as part of an expanding ~120-unit supportive housing campus. DeWarren Langley of the Charles Hamilton Houston Foundation urged the board to ask JCPC for actionable risk-and-needs and juvenile complaint trend recommendations rather than only an annual funding plan.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review (Public Health, Justice Grants, Utilities, and Capital Projects)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Dr. Sowell presented upcoming consent agenda items including $862,450 for public health infrastructure (230746), $1.404M for school health teams (230748), $265,113 for COVID-19 immunization (230750), $150,000 for Triple P (230751), $199,106 JAG grant (230760), Homeland Security and DOJ grants (230780, 230781), Northeast Creek sewer modeling ILA (230793), $400,000 for the Shoppes of Hope Valley pre-development study (230797), $237,000 for Stagville Memorial (230799), and a $21.3M capital project amendment (230824). Public Health Director Rod Jenkins answered Commissioner Carter's questions on recruiting environmental health specialists and school nurses.

agenda_items.title: Discussion Item 23-0828: Expedited Hearing Request for UDO Amendment TC23005 (Conservation Subdivisions)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Curtis Massey and Planning Director Sara Young requested suspending the rules to approve an expedited public hearing schedule for UDO Section 6.2.4 / Paragraph 6.4 (TC23005) due to pending litigation challenging whether general purpose statements are mandatory subdivision standards. The board voted 5-0 to suspend the rules and 5-0 to adopt the expedited-hearing resolution.

agenda_items.title: Durham Transit Plan FY24 Q2 Work Program Amendments and Bus Speed & Reliability Study
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Administrative Officer Brandy Minor, DCHC MPO Executive Director Doug Plachcinski, and GoTriangle Assistant Finance Director Steven Schlossberg presented two FY24 Q2 Transit Plan amendments totaling $139,550 net: GoTriangle's mobile ticketing open-payment upgrade ($75,550 gross, $29,550 net) ahead of July 1, 2024 fare return, and Durham County's $110,000 share of the $850,000 regional FAST 2 BRT/highway transit study. Staff also briefed the board on the countywide Bus Speed and Reliability Study, with commissioners stressing outreach after zero public comments, rider education, and coordination with the Comprehensive Plan and UDO.

agenda_items.title: Presentation 23-0821: Durham County 2025 General Reappraisal Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Introduced by Assistant County Manager Dwayne Brinson, newly appointed Tax Administrator Keyar Doyle and Deputy Assessor Starlin Beatty provided an update on the January 1, 2025 general reappraisal. They reviewed Durham County's rapid population growth past 350,000 residents, the transition to a four-year reappraisal cycle, and how comparable market sales drive tax value adjustments.

agenda_items.title: Harm Reduction and Opioid Settlement Funding Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health staff presented outcomes from syringe-services, naloxone, and xylazine test-strip distribution, noting federal grant restrictions against purchasing naloxone or sterile syringes and proposing opioid settlement funding for a dedicated harm-reduction specialist, supplies, peer outreach, and a library naloxone vending machine pilot. Commissioners asked about youth overdose prevention and naloxone availability in schools.

agenda_items.title: Juvenile Crime Prevention Council (JCPC) Annual Overview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: JCPC Chair Kevin McIver, NC DPS consultant Eddie Cruz, and Justice Services manager Mark Strange reviewed the $701,001 state allocation (with a 15% county match), monthly and annual monitoring of funded youth programs, waitlists, and unspent-fund reversions caused by staffing vacancies. Commissioners discussed school attendance ties, evening/night offense timing, and the recent state pay-raise resolution for detention workers and court counselors.

agenda_items.title: Presentation 23-0827: Durham County Blasting Permit Process
agenda_items.discussion_summary: OES Director Jim Groves, Assistant Fire Marshal Greg Bowden, and City Fire Marshal Chief Joey Morton and Deputy Chief Chris Wilcox explained statutory authority under NCGS 153A and NC Fire Code Chapter 5607, noting that 24-hour resident notification currently applies only to buildings within 500 feet—leaving rural sites with repeat blasting unnotified. meetings.title: BOCC - Oct. 23, 2023 - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton and all five commissioners convened on October 23, 2023, approving prior minutes (5-0) and voting unanimously (5-0) to appoint and swear in Keyar Doyle as Durham County Tax Administrator. Commissioners Nida Allam and Nimasheena Burns delivered a joint statement condemning rising Islamophobia and anti-Semitism while mourning victims of violence in Palestine, Israel, and Illinois, followed by ceremonial items for Breast Cancer Awareness Month and Operation Green Light for Veterans (23-0777). The board approved the 7-item consent agenda (5-0)—including 35 new DSS positions for December 1 Medicaid expansion—and then held the continued public hearing on UDO Text Amendment TC2302 (23-0783) aligning the UDO with the newly adopted Comprehensive Plan, adopting both the ordinance and consistency statement on 4-1 votes. The meeting concluded with advisory board ballot appointments and a closed session on economic development incentives under GS 143-318.11(a)(4).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton called the meeting to order and read the public charge, with Commissioner Nimasheena Burns leading the Pledge of Allegiance. Clerk Wallace read announcements including voter information and the DCO on the Go design contest, and Burns recognized Chair Howerton for receiving the Lifetime Achievement Award from the National Association of Black County Commissioners. The board approved the October 2 work session and October 9 regular session minutes with minor typographical edits.

agenda_items.title: Appointment and Swearing-In of Tax Administrator Keyar Doyle
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to appoint Keyar Doyle as Durham County Tax Administrator. Clerk Monica Wallace administered the oath of office, and commissioners praised Interim Administrator Teresa Harrison and the Tax Administration team.

agenda_items.title: Joint Statement on Violence in Palestine and Israel and Rising Islamophobia and Anti-Semitism
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners Nida Allam and Nimasheena Burns delivered a joint statement mourning the killing of six-year-old Palestinian American boy Wadea Al-Fayoume in Illinois, Israelis killed in the October 7 Hamas attacks, and Palestinian civilians killed in Gaza, while condemning rising Islamophobia and anti-Semitism.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: Breast Cancer Awareness Month and Operation Green Light (23-0777)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board recognized Breast Cancer Awareness Month and adopted Resolution 23-0777 supporting Operation Green Light for Veterans 2023 by lighting county buildings green. Veteran Services Officer Jonathan Crooms spoke on outreach events in Bahama, Halloween at South Dillard Street, and the November 9 Veterans Day program.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Including 35 New DSS Positions for Medicaid Expansion)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Burns highlighted a consent item adding 35 new DSS employees to prepare for December 1 Medicaid expansion covering an estimated 22,000 new Durham enrollees, and Chair Howerton announced an on-the-spot Saturday hiring fair at the Health and Human Services building. The board unanimously approved the 7-item consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing 23-0783 (TC2302): UDO Text Amendment Aligning with 2023 Comprehensive Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Manager Scott Whiteman presented UDO Text Amendment TC2302—continued from October 9—making minimum terminology and procedural updates to reflect the newly adopted Comprehensive Plan, including replacing Future Land Use Map references with Place Type Map, creating a biennial evaluation report, and adjusting development-tier applicability. Public speakers criticized Lick Creek and Falls Lake development impacts, Perry Farms, and urban growth boundary additions; commissioners clarified the distinction between TC2302 and the already-adopted Comprehensive Plan, praised resident activism and planning staff, and voted 4-1 to adopt the ordinance and consistency statement.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Andrews announced ballot selections for the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission (Jack Dougherty and Susan Wilinski), Discover Durham Tourism Development Authority (Barry Van Deman), Durham County Women's Commission (Kelly Lindsey), Durham Planning Commission (Edward Johnson and Kerry/Carrie Wolk), and Environmental Affairs Board (Rebecca Effler).

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (GS 143-318.11(a)(4) Economic Development Incentives)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board entered closed session pursuant to GS 143-318.11(a)(4) regarding industrial or business location/expansion and tentative economic development incentives, returning at 02:48:07 with direction to staff and no formal action before adjourning.

votes.notes: Mover and seconder not named on mic.

disagreements.issue: UDO Text Amendment TC2302 (23-0783) Aligning Ordinance with Comprehensive Plan and Urban Growth Boundary Procedures
disagreements.summary: The board split 4-1 on adopting UDO Text Amendment TC2302 following public outcry over urban growth boundary expansions, Lick Creek and Falls Lake environmental impacts, and confusion over how the Comprehensive Plan had been approved on consent.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt TC2302 as the minimum procedural alignment needed to implement the adopted Comprehensive Plan while pursuing the UDO rewrite and blasting-permit reforms.
side_a_arguments: TC2302 only updates UDO references (Future Land Use Map to Place Type Map, biennial assessment reporting, and Downtown Design District boundaries) to match the already-adopted Comprehensive Plan.
Residents were heard on both sides of the urban growth boundary, and the Comprehensive Plan guarantees utility access and affordable housing policies in new growth areas.
Deeper zoning and conservation protections will be addressed during the upcoming UDO rewrite and City-County blasting permit review.
disagreements.side_b_position: Dissent against adopting TC2302 (1 nay vote; individual dissenter unnamed in voice vote), reflecting public concerns over overdevelopment and lack of transparency.
side_b_arguments: Public speakers opposed expanding subdivisions bisecting Lick Creek and threatening Falls Lake and Perry Farms.

Commissioners acknowledged residents did not realize they could request pulling the Comprehensive Plan from the prior consent agenda and expressed concern about missing markup/maps in the earlier packet.
disagreements.resolution: Both TC2302 (23-0783) and its NCGS 160D-605 consistency statement passed 4-1 on voice votes.

meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton opened the October 9, 2023 Regular Session with a moment of silence for violence in Israel and Gaza, followed by remarks from Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs recognizing 111-year-old Durham resident Catherine Farrell and addressing civilian suffering in both Israel and Gaza. The board unanimously approved prior meeting minutes (5-0), celebrated the appointment of Rashana Parker as Justice Services Director (23-0768), and adopted a resolution honoring Indigenous Peoples' Day. After passing the consent agenda (5-0), the board opened Public Hearing 23-0754 (UDO Text Amendment TC2302 for Comprehensive Plan alignment) and voted to continue it to October 23, 2023 so staff could correct missing strikethrough/underline formatting in the draft ordinance, before recognizing Comprehensive Plan staff and entering closed session on personnel and Robin Barefoot v. Durham County litigation.

Howerton called the meeting to order, led a moment of silence regarding violence in Israel, read the public charge, and asked Commissioner Heidi Carter to lead the Pledge of Allegiance. Clerk Wallace announced the October 10 municipal primary/election, Cultural Plan survey, and local farmers' markets, and the board approved the September 5 work session and September 25 regular session minutes (5-0). agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: Justice Services Director Rashana Parker (23-0768) and Indigenous Peoples' Day Resolution

Commissioners also read a resolution honoring Indigenous Peoples' Day acknowledging the Eno, Tuscarora, Lumbee, Occaneechi, Cheraw, Shakori, Saponi, and Catawba tribes and thanking Food Security Coordinator Mary Oxendine for helping draft the resolution.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing 23-0754 (TC2302): UDO Comprehensive Plan Alignment (Continued to October 23)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff requested continuing Public Hearing 23-0754 (TC2302) because the draft ordinance omitted strikethrough and underline markup showing exact text changes. Commissioners questioned staff on state-law limits prohibiting separate Urban Growth Boundary applications outside zoning actions, differences between the University/College and University/College 2 districts, septic/stormwater impacts on carved-out homeowner tracts, and blasting permits before opening the hearing (with no public speakers signed up) and voting to continue it to October 23, 2023.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of City-County Comprehensive Plan Staff
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff member Lisa Miller and colleagues addressed the board to mark four years of work since June 2019 on the newly adopted Durham Comprehensive Plan, and commissioners thanked staff and residents for their engagement.

meetings.title: BOCC - Sept 25, 2023 - Regular Session n
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the September 25, 2023 Regular Session with Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs joining remotely via Zoom and all five commissioners participating. During announcements, commissioners celebrated North Carolina's passage of Medicaid expansion (extending coverage to an estimated 30,000–40,000 Durham residents starting December 1), reviewed state budget allocations, and highlighted early childhood programming. The board unanimously approved the September 11 minutes (5-0), issued proclamations for Minority Enterprise Development Week, Domestic Violence Awareness Month, and National Hispanic Heritage Month, unanimously passed the 9-item consent agenda (5-0)—highlighting 132 affordable housing units at <=60% AMI (23-0732) and Hollow Rock Nature Park—and made advisory board appointments including to the Library Board of Trustees.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Approval of September 11, 2023 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton opened the meeting, read the public charge, noted Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs's remote participation via Zoom, and had Commissioner Burns lead the Pledge of Allegiance. Clerk Wallace shared announcements on municipal voting, the Sheriff's Animal Services podcast, and Duke Energy's student career conference; commissioners discussed Bull City Summit, the newly passed state budget and Medicaid expansion rollout, banned-books library outreach, and community mental health. The board approved the September 11, 2023 minutes (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations: MED Week, Domestic Violence Awareness Month, and National Hispanic Heritage Month

Commissioners Heidi Carter and Wendy Jacobs underscored that more than 30% of Durham Public Schools students and over 14% of Durham County residents are of Hispanic or Latinx heritage, stressing language accessibility and equity.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Including 132-Unit Affordable Housing Development 23-0732 and Hollow Rock Nature Park)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board approved the 9-item consent agenda 5-0 without pulling items. Commissioner Burns highlighted item 23-0732 supporting 132 affordable housing units at 60% AMI and below with free internet, while Vice Chair Jacobs praised items regarding Hollow Rock Nature Park and Cooperative Extension youth programs (23-0163).

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The county attorney read ballot appointment selections for advisory boards, including selecting Tracy Chatman to the Library Board of Trustees and filling seats on the Fire/EMS-related board, before the board adjourned at 01:30:50.

meetings.title: BOCC - Sept 11, 2023 - Regular Session n
meetings.executive_summary: Opening the September 11, 2023 Regular Session after exiting closed session (5-0), Chair Brenda A. Howerton offered 9/11 remembrance remarks, and Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs highlighted an amendment expanding Durham County's 6-week paid parental leave to foster and adoptive parents of children aged five and older. Following minutes approval (5-0), ceremonial proclamations for Durham Recovery Month (23-0691), Chuck/Mika Manning, and World Alzheimer's Awareness Day (23-0716), and unanimous passage of the 28-item consent agenda (5-0), the board held a heavily debated public hearing on UDO Text Amendment 23-0687 (TC2200004) governing phased grading and tree preservation. Despite concerns from residents and Commissioner Nimasheena Burns over the 50-acre phasing cap, perceived loopholes, and enforcement capacity along Lick Creek, the board approved the ordinance and consistency statement 3-2. The board then unanimously approved naming County Agriculture Building Conference Rooms 129A and B after Carl Hodges (23-0699, 5-0) before entering closed session (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Exit Closed Session, 9/11 Remembrance, Announcements, and Paid Parental Leave Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to exit closed session, read the public charge, and observed a 9/11 commemoration led by Chair Brenda A. Howerton. Clerk Wallace announced free county blood lead testing, and commissioners shared updates on veterans resources, the September 27 Local Reentry Council fair, and an amended county paid parental leave policy expanding 6-week bonding leave to employees fostering or adopting children aged five and older.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board approved the prior regular session minutes unanimously with no edits.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: Durham Recovery Month (23-0691), Chuck Manning Resolution, and World Alzheimer's Awareness Day (23-0716)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Carter read the Durham Recovery Month proclamation (23-0691) with Interim Justice Services Director Rashana Parker highlighting treatment court and recovery events. The board also passed a resolution honoring the late Chuck Manning for his reentry and pandemic hotel support work, and Vice Chair Jacobs read Proclamation 23-0716 designating September 21, 2023 as World Alzheimer's Awareness Day.

agenda_items.title: Approval of 28-Item Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed the 28-item consent agenda without pulling any items, with Commissioner Carter requesting a future Urban Ministries report and Commissioner Allam highlighting nearly $1 million in Public Health grant funds.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing 23-0687 (TC2200004): UDO Text Amendment — Phased Development and Tree Preservation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Planner and Arborist Robin Schultz presented TC2200004 (already unanimously approved by City Council on September 5), requiring phased grading of no more than 50 acres per phase and tiered tree-preservation requirements to incentivize tree retention over replacement. Public speakers urged stronger protections against mass grading and Lick Creek sediment pollution, while Commissioner Burns questioned why Durham allowed 50-acre phases versus Cary/Wake Forest's 20–25 acre rules and pressed staff on enforcement. Planning and erosion-control staff explained that Durham's phase-based rule avoids Cary's high-density loophole and detailed ongoing Lick Creek inspections, after which the board approved the ordinance and consistency statement 3-2.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing 23-0699: Naming Request for Carl Hodges (Agriculture Building Conference Rooms 129A & B)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented a naming committee recommendation and hallway historical display honoring Carl Hodges, the first African American Extension Director in Durham County, North Carolina, and the United States. Cooperative Extension Director Donna Rewalt, community leaders, and Hodges family members testified during the public hearing, and the board unanimously approved the naming request (5-0).

agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board entered closed session under GS 143-318.11(a)(5) regarding real property acquisition and employment contract negotiations, returning at 03:43:35 with direction to staff and no public action before adjourning.

disagreements.issue: Phased Grading Acreage Limits, Tree Preservation Tiers, and Enforcement in UDO Text Amendment 23-0687 (TC2200004)
disagreements.summary: The board split 3-2 over UDO Text Amendment TC2200004, debating whether a 50-acre phase cap and tiered tree-preservation rules went far enough to curb mass grading, buffer clearing, and sediment runoff into Lick Creek.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve TC2200004 as an immediate step forward that prevents unphased clear-cutting, avoids high-density loopholes, and can be strengthened during the UDO rewrite.
side_a_arguments: Requiring tree preservation within each phase prevents developers from clear-cutting an entire 50+ acre tract at once and clustering saved trees on one edge.
Unlike Cary's three-tier rule that exempts developments above 8 dwelling units per acre from grading limits, Durham's rule applies across all applicable projects.
City Council already passed the amendment unanimously, and rejecting or delaying it would postpone environmental protections while staff prepares the UDO rewrite.
disagreements.side_b_position: Dissent against adopting TC2200004 as drafted (2 nay votes on voice vote), arguing the 50-acre phase cap and enforcement mechanisms fail to match stricter peer limits or stop developer damage.
side_b_arguments: Commissioner Burns questioned why Durham allowed 50-acre phases rather than adopting the 20–25 acre mass-grading limits used by Cary, Raleigh, or Wake Forest.
Critics and public speakers pointed to continued sediment runoff into Lick Creek, utility/buffer disturbance exceptions, and perceived delays in enforcement despite added county inspection positions.
disagreements.resolution: Both TC2200004 (23-0687) and its NCGS 160D-605 consistency statement passed 3-2 on voice votes.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners - Work Session for Sep. 5, 2023
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the September 5, 2023 Board of County Commissioners work session, with all five commissioners reviewing proposed regular-session consent items ranging from Double Bucks ARPA funding and HHS HVAC repairs to public health grants, Triangle Wastewater Treatment Plant rehabilitation, and a Durham-to-Roxboro Rail Trail grant support letter. Work session briefings covered Unified Development Ordinance text amendment TC22004 on phased development and tree preservation, Durham Open Space and Trails Commission interlocal updates, DSS eviction diversion and Low-Income Homeowners Relief (LIHR) gaps, opioid harm reduction, strategic planning, and a major $15.8 million ARPA realignment toward joint City-County affordable housing, homelessness services, and water/sewer infrastructure. Under an added action item moved from August 28, the board voted 4-0 to suspend its rules and shorten the Durham Technical Community College Board of Trustees appointment to a two-year term before appointing Dr. Tara Fikes via ballot, followed by a brief closed session on real property acquisition and employment negotiations.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, and Consent Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton called the work session to order, read the public charge, noted no speakers had signed up for Citizens' Comments, and guided the board through consent agenda review. Commissioners questioned Detention Center maintenance technical budget adjustments, EMS Operative IQ fleet software versus RTA compatibility ($46,200), Farmer Foodshare's selection over Bellwoods Residential Solutions as Double Bucks ARPA fiscal sponsor ($483,972), and GAP certification barriers for local farms selling to Durham Public Schools. Staff also reviewed HHS HVAC split-system upgrades ($421,500), five NCDHHS Public Health epidemiology/communicable-disease grants, a $1,263,635 Triangle WWTP rehabilitation package, a $400,000 Whispering Pines stream restoration grant, a $500,000 Durham-to-Roxboro Rail Trail planning grant support letter, and moved the Farmland Preservation Board presentation to the upcoming regular agenda.

agenda_items.title: 23-0658: UDO Text Amendment (TC22004) on Phased Development and Tree Preservation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Planner Robin Schultz and Planning Director Sara Young presented UDO text amendment TC22004, capping development phases at 50 acres, triggering tiered tree preservation at 35 acres (20% preservation for 35-acre suburban developments and 30% for larger sites), adding five-foot and ten-foot grading setbacks near buffers, and requiring 0.6 opacity boundary buffers across all tiers. Commissioners pressed staff on clear-cutting enforcement, monitoring loopholes on small lots, and why the affordable housing density/preservation incentive stops at 80% AMI rather than targeting deeper 30%-50% AMI need. Staff confirmed the Planning Commission and JCCPC reviewed the measure ahead of the September 11 public hearing.

agenda_items.title: 23-0638: Durham Open Space and Trails Commission (DOST) Interlocal Agreement Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff planner Karl Kaszmarek outlined proposed updates to the Durham Open Space and Trails Commission interlocal agreement to adopt gender-neutral language, substitute 'resident' for 'citizen,' reduce maximum membership from 30 to 17 by removing self-appointed and Planning Commission seats, convert Council and BOCC liaisons to non-voting ex-officio status, and authorize $50 stipend eligibility. Commissioners raised brief clarifying questions on term alignment and city-county coordination.

agenda_items.title: 23-0652: DSS Low-Income Homeowners Relief (LIHR) and Emergency Rental Assistance (ERAP) Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DSS staff reported that LIHR received 353 applications after reopening (with ~200 still pending) and recommended shifting to a year-round application window and covering 100% of tax bills for seniors 60+ at or below 30% AMI. Staff also warned that remaining NC PRO 2.0 emergency rental assistance funds ($1.6M-$1.8M of $7.1M total, spending ~$240,000/month) would be exhausted around March 2024 amid roughly 7,295 annual eviction filings. Commissioners Heidi Carter, Wendy Jacobs, and Nimasheena Burns urged immediate City-County coordination on sustainable eviction diversion funding and courtroom social worker capacity.

agenda_items.title: 23-0660: ACEs, Resilience, and Opioid Crisis / Harm Reduction Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health Director Rod Jenkins, Jess Baskett, Dr. Jeff Jenks, Lindsay Bickers-Bock, and Dennis Hamlet reviewed Durham County's trauma-informed Community Resiliency Model (CRM) training expansion, juvenile/youth policy priorities, and $400,000 in FY24 opioid settlement funding for Community Linkages to Care. Presenters detailed overdose trends, peer support outreach, naloxone distribution and vending machines, and the addition of xylazine test strips to harm reduction kits, while commissioners asked about school-based resilience coordination and detention center linkage outcomes.

agenda_items.title: Durham County Forward 2029 Strategic Planning Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Office of Strategy and Performance staff presented the roadmap for the FY2025-2029 'Durham County Forward 2029' strategic plan in partnership with consultant Dr. Monica Allen (Insight Performance Management Group). Staff outlined seven focus areas, community and employee engagement schedules, and plans to present a draft strategic framework in February 2024.

agenda_items.title: 23-0663: Naming Committee Request for Carl D. Hodges Conference Room (Ag Building)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Naming Committee representatives presented options to name the Agriculture Building conference room (Rooms 129A/B) in honor of Cooperative Extension leader Carl D. Hodges, noting Option 2 plaque placement as the preferred design ahead of the September 11 public hearing.

agenda_items.title: 23-0669: American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) Status and Realignment Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Claudia Hager and staff reported that roughly 40% ($24 million across 39 projects) of Durham County's $62.4 million ARPA award had been encumbered and proposed realigning approximately $15.8 million—largely from unallocated broadband/state-matched funds—into $3.5 million for joint City-County affordable housing (including $700,000 for McKissick Square/Geer Street and $2 million for Southside Phases 3-4), $2 million for Homeless Services Center planning, senior home repair, land trust support, $6 million in water/sewer infrastructure, and DSS Medicaid-expansion ERP upgrades. Commissioners Wendy Jacobs and Heidi Carter pressed staff to address eviction diversion gaps and capital housing needs for re-entering mothers and children.

agenda_items.title: 23-0674: Board Discussion and Vote on Durham Technical Community College Board of Trustees Appointment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following up on the August 28 deferral, County Attorney Al Andrews advised that modifying the appointment ballot required suspending board rules. Commissioner Nimasheena Burns moved to suspend the rules and then moved to convert the open Durham Tech Board of Trustees seat from a four-year to a two-year term to preserve board continuity amid state legislative changes, both passing 4-0; Attorney Andrews then announced the board's ballot selection appointing Dr. Tara Fikes to the two-year term.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 4-0 (Suspend Rules; Two-Year Term; Ballot Appointment of Dr. Tara Fikes)

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Real Property Acquisition & Employment Contracts) and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At 06:13:08, the board recessed into closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) and (a)(6) to instruct staff regarding real property acquisition terms and employment contract compensation. Reconvening at 06:26:50, Chair Howerton reported that direction was given to staff with no action taken, and the board adjourned by voice vote at 06:27:00.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (Voice vote to enter closed session and adjourn)

votes.item_title: Motion to Suspend the Rules to Amend the Ballot for the Durham Technical Community College Board of Trustees Appointment (23-0674)
votes.notes: Voice vote recorded as 4-0; fifth commissioner's vote not recorded in the tally.
votes.discussion_detail: After County Attorney Al Andrews advised at 06:09:50 that changing the structure of the ballot required a formal suspension of the rules, Commissioner Nimasheena Burns moved to suspend the rules so the board could amend the Durham Technical Community College Board of Trustees appointment ballot. Following a second, Chair Brenda A. Howerton called the voice vote and announced the motion approved 4-0.

votes.item_title: Motion to Set the Durham Technical Community College Board of Trustees Appointment (23-0674) to a Two-Year Term
votes.notes: Shortened term length from four years to two years prior to announcing ballot nominee.
votes.discussion_detail: Commissioner Nimasheena Burns cited extenuating circumstances and legislative changes affecting community college governance and moved that the Durham Technical Community College Board of Trustees appointment before the board be set for a two-year term rather than a four-year term. Following a second, the motion passed 4-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Ballot Appointment of Dr. Tara Fikes to the Durham Technical Community College Board of Trustees (Two-Year Term, 23-0674)
votes.notes: Written ballot tabulated by County Attorney Al Andrews; coincides with the 4-0 procedural votes immediately prior.
votes.discussion_detail: At Chair Howerton's request to announce the named appointee for the record, County Attorney Al Andrews confirmed that based on the board's completed written ballot and prior term-length motion, the board appointed Dr. Tara Fikes to the Durham Technical Community College Board of Trustees for a two-year term.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (Real Property Acquisition & Employment Contracts - N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) & (a)(6))
votes.notes: Exact numeric count not stated aloud; entered closed session at 06:14:11.
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Brenda A. Howerton read the statutory closed-session notice covering instructions to negotiating agents on real property acquisition terms and employment contract compensation terms under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) and (a)(6). A commissioner moved and seconded entering closed session, which passed without objection; the board later returned at 06:26:50 reporting direction given and no formal action taken.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Session for Aug. 28, 2023
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the August 28, 2023 regular session, which opened with a personnel closed session and a procedural re-vote in open session approving 5-0 a 4% salary increase for appointed/elected officials (Clerk Monica Wallace, County Attorney Al Andrews, County Manager Kimberly Sowell, Register of Deeds Sharon Davis, Sheriff Clarence Birkhead, former Tax Administrator Dwayne Brinson, and the Board of County Commissioners). During agenda adjustments, Commissioner Nida Allam moved—over Chair Howerton's pushback regarding prior precedent—to pull and defer the Durham Technical Community College Board of Trustees appointment to the September 5 work session to debate full versus unexpired terms on term-limited seats. The board then unanimously approved prior minutes, issued resolutions and proclamations for Phi Beta Sigma, National Recovery Month, Public Health's Re-Accreditation with Honors, and naming the I-40/US 15-501 interchange for Congressman David Price, adopted its 10-item consent agenda 5-0, authorized transportation staff to draft FY24 THUD rail-funding letters to the Congressional delegation, announced three advisory board appointments, and entered an economic development closed session.

agenda_items.title: Initial Closed Session (Personnel) and Open-Session Vote on 4% Salary Increases
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At 00:01:40, commissioners voted 4-0 to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) for personnel evaluations. Upon returning at 01:54:03, the board voted on 4% salary increases for Clerk Monica Wallace, County Attorney Al Andrews, County Manager Kimberly Sowell, Register of Deeds Sharon Davis, Sheriff Clarence Birkhead, former Tax Administrator Dwayne Brinson, and the BOCC before realizing it had not yet formally exited closed session; after voting to close closed session at 01:56:06, reading the public charge, and reciting the Pledge, the board re-voted in open session at 01:58:49 and approved the 4% increases 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Adjustments: Deferral of Durham Tech Board of Trustees Appointment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Nida Allam moved to pull the Durham Technical Community College Board of Trustees appointment from the evening's agenda and hold it until the September 5 work session to evaluate whether reappointments involving expired or term-limited seats constitute full or unexpired terms. Chair Brenda A. Howerton disagreed on past practice and asked staff to compile historical examples, noting prior boards had handled similar appointments differently even if not since Allam and Burns took office; the motion to move the item to September 5 passed by voice vote.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (Voice vote moving DTCC appointment to Sep. 5 work session)

agenda_items.title: Announcements, Moment of Silence, and Approval of Minutes (July 10 & August 14, 2023)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk Monica Wallace read announcements covering COVID-19 boosters, the August 31 Comprehensive Plan hearing, Exchange Youth Ambassadors, Duke meal survey incentives, Discover Durham town halls, transportation TIP priorities, stormwater outreach, and Alert Durham, followed by Chair Howerton leading a moment of silence for fatal shootings at UNC and in Jacksonville, Florida. Commissioners Burns and Allam recognized EMS/fire personnel, Public Health's #1 county health ranking, an NCACC agricultural innovation award, and veteran homelessness initiatives before unanimously approving the July 10 and August 14, 2023 regular session minutes.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: Phi Beta Sigma, Recovery Month, Public Health Accreditation, and Congressman David Price Interchange Naming
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board presented a resolution welcoming Phi Beta Sigma Fraternity's September 9 North Carolina state conference at Durham Tech, proclaimed September as National Recovery Month with remarks from recovery and CJRC partners, recognized Durham County Department of Public Health for earning North Carolina Re-Accreditation with Honors under Director Rod Jenkins, and read a resolution read by Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs supporting NCDOT naming of the I-40 / US 15-501 interchange in honor of former Congressman David Price.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 23-0567 through 23-0637)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: No items were pulled from the 10-item consent agenda, though Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs placed a formal statement on the record regarding item 23-0637 (300 East Main Street ground-floor retail/office contract), emphasizing the board's ongoing six-year priority to recruit nonprofit, community, and workforce development tenants near Urban Ministries and the Justice Services Center. Jacobs then moved adoption of the consent agenda, seconded by Commissioners Nida Allam and Heidi Carter, passing 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Added Item: Congressional Delegation Letter on FY24 THUD Rail & Transit Appropriations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs requested board authorization for Transportation Director Ellen Beckman to adapt a local advocacy letter from APTA/DCHC MPO urging North Carolina's U.S. Senators and House delegation to preserve Bipartisan Infrastructure Law rail and transit funding in the FY 2023-24 THUD appropriations bill. County Attorney Al Andrews confirmed consensus thumbs-up sufficed without a formal motion, and Commissioner Nimasheena Burns confirmed letters would go to the full NC Congressional delegation.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Approved by consensus (No formal motion required)

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments & Economic Development Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Al Andrews announced written ballot selections appointing Mary Fontana to the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission, David Zebly to the City-County Appearance Commission, and Laura Topteam to the Juvenile Crime Prevention Council, noting the Durham Tech Board of Trustees vote was deferred to September 5. Commissioners Heidi Carter and Nida Allam then moved and seconded entering closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) on business location/economic development incentives; the board returned at 03:51:44 reporting direction given to staff with no action taken and adjourned.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (Personnel - N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6))
votes.notes: Initial pre-regular-session closed session; passed 4-0 with four commissioners present at call.
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Brenda A. Howerton read the statutory authority under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) to discuss personnel evaluations. After a motion and second at 00:01:40, the board approved entering closed session 4-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Initial Procedural Voice Vote on 4% Salary Increases for Appointed and Elected Officials
votes.notes: Procedurally superseded by the formal closed-session exit vote at 01:56:06 and open-session re-vote at 01:58:49.
votes.discussion_detail: Upon emerging from the closed session conference room, Chair Howerton read a list of 4% salary increases for Clerk Monica Wallace, County Attorney Al Andrews, County Manager Kimberly Sowell, Register of Deeds Sharon Davis, Sheriff Clarence Birkhead, former Tax Administrator Dwayne Brinson, and the Board of County Commissioners, and called for a motion, which passed by voice vote before staff noted closed session had not yet been formally exited.

votes.item_title: Motion to Formally Exit Closed Session
votes.notes: Preceded reading the public charge, Pledge of Allegiance, and open-session re-vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Following procedural clarification between commissioners, Clerk Monica Wallace, and County Attorney Al Andrews regarding ensuring votes occur strictly in open session, a commissioner moved and seconded formally closing the closed session, passing by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Open-Session Re-Vote Approving 4% Salary Increases for Elected/Appointed Officials and Commissioners
votes.notes: Confirmed 5-0 vote in open session to cure procedural order from 01:54:49.
votes.discussion_detail: After reading the public charge and reciting the Pledge of Allegiance to clarify the open-session record, Chair Howerton invited a new motion on the 4% salary increases for the Clerk to the Board, County Attorney, County Manager, Register of Deeds, Sheriff, former Tax Administrator, and Board of County Commissioners. The motion was moved, seconded, and approved 5-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Motion to Pull and Defer Durham Technical Community College Board of Trustees Appointment to September 5 Work Session
votes.notes: Deferred item for discussion and potential vote at the September 5, 2023 work session.
votes.discussion_detail: Commissioner Nida Allam moved to pull the Durham Technical Community College Board of Trustees appointment from the August 28 agenda and defer it to the September 5 work session so the board could discuss whether an appointment to an expired/term-limited seat should be a full term. After debate with Chair Howerton over prior board history and bylaws, the board agreed on September 5 as the deferral date and approved the motion by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of Minutes (July 10, 2023 and August 14, 2023 Regular Sessions)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Howerton called for edits or additions to the July 10 and August 14, 2023 regular session minutes. A commissioner moved and another seconded approval as presented, passing by voice vote with all five commissioners present.

votes.item_title: Board and Commission Appointments (BPAC, City-County Appearance Commission, JCPC)
votes.notes: Written ballot appointments; JCPC noted as 'majority of the board selected.'
votes.discussion_detail: County Attorney Al Andrews reported the results of the board's written ballots: Mary Fontana to the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission, David Zebly to the City-County Appearance Commission, and majority selection of Laura Topteam to the Juvenile Crime Prevention Council, noting the Durham Tech Board of Trustees vote was deferred to September 5.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (Economic Development Incentives - N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4))
votes.notes: Final substantive business before adjournment at 03:51:55.
votes.discussion_detail: Commissioner Heidi Carter moved and Commissioner Nida Allam seconded entering closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) to discuss business location/expansion and tentative economic development incentives. The board approved the motion by voice vote, later returning at 03:51:44 reporting direction given to staff with no action taken.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Session for Aug. 28, 2023
disagreements.issue: Procedural Rules and Term-Length Precedent for Deferring the Durham Tech Board of Trustees Appointment
disagreements.summary: During agenda adjustments, Commissioner Nida Allam moved to pull and defer the Durham Technical Community College Board of Trustees appointment from August 28 to the September 5 work session to address whether reappointing a term-limited incumbent to an expired slot yields a full term or shortened term, sparking pushback from Chair Brenda A. Howerton over past board precedent.
disagreements.side_a_position: Pull the Durham Tech appointment until September 5 so the board can examine bylaws and deliberate whether the expired/term-limited seat should be filled for a full or partial term.
side_a_arguments: No other applicants were considered for the expired term-limited seat, so the full board needs time to discuss the term-length implication before voting.
Under the current board's tenure since Commissioners Allam and Burns joined, a reappointment structured this way had not previously occurred.
disagreements.side_b_position: Maintain awareness that prior Boards of Commissioners have filled similar expired/term-limited appointments under existing bylaws and require staff to document historical precedent if delaying the vote.
side_b_arguments: While not done since the two newest commissioners took office, the board had handled similar appointments under its bylaws in earlier years.
Directed staff to pull historical records of prior appointments to inform the discussion.
disagreements.resolution: The board approved pulling the Durham Tech Board of Trustees vote to the September 5, 2023 work session, where it subsequently voted 4-0 to suspend the rules, set a two-year term, and appoint Dr. Tara Fikes.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Session for Aug. 14, 2023 (Full Recording)
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the August 14, 2023 regular session (full recording spanning the 5:45 PM personnel closed session through open-session adjournment; duplicated in part by companion open-session stream TA7hC9ceLZ4). Following the closed session report with no action taken, proclamations for Child Support Awareness Month, 4-H Youth Delegate Addison O'Bryant, and national IT/Elections awards for CIO Greg Marrow and the Board of Elections, the board unanimously approved June 12 and June 26 minutes and 54 of 56 consent agenda items (including $1.6 million for Interfaith Food Shuttle food security, $3 million for workforce programs, and APS shelter support). Commissioners pulled two marquee ARPA items for dedicated highlights and separate votes: unanimously approving 5-0 the $1.69 million 'DCo Thrives' guaranteed income pilot providing $750/month stipends (plus $100 survey incentives) to families with children, and passing 4-0-1 a bundle of five ARPA youth enrichment contracts after Commissioner Nimasheena Burns recused herself due to serving on the Museum of Life and Science board; Sheriff Clarence Birkhead also introduced new Project Safe Neighborhoods leadership.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Personnel) and Call to Order of Open Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At 00:00:19, commissioners approved a motion by Commissioner Nimasheena Burns and seconded by Commissioner Heidi Carter to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6). Reconvening in open session at 01:29:47, Chair Brenda A. Howerton reported direction was given to staff with no action taken, read the public charge, and asked Commissioner Burns to lead the Pledge of Allegiance.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (Voice vote to enter closed session; no action taken)

agenda_items.title: Announcements and Approval of Minutes (June 12 & June 26, 2023)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk Monica Wallace announced upcoming community events including the August 19 Stop the Violence/Ceasefire resource fair, August 21 Disparity Study public hearing, August 23 Building a Safer Community conference, LIHR tax relief reopening, US 70 East corridor planning, childhood immunizations, voter ID cards, Overdose Awareness Day, MWBE open house, and the August 31 Comprehensive Plan public hearing. Commissioners Nida Allam and Heidi Carter then moved and seconded approval of the June 12 and June 26, 2023 regular session minutes, passing 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: Child Support Awareness Month, 4-H Delegate, Digital County/GovTech, and Clearie Award
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board proclaimed August 2023 as Child Support Awareness Month recognizing DSS Child Support Services director and staff, recognized 4-H Youth Delegate Addison O'Bryant for attending the National 4-H Congress (with Commissioner Burns encouraging youth follow-up reports), honored CIO Greg Marrow and IS&T for Top 10 Digital County and GovTech Top 25 Doers, Dreamers and Drivers recognition, and acknowledged the Board of Elections for winning a U.S. Election Assistance Commission Clearinghouse ('Clearie') Award.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (54 of 56 Items Approved; Items 23-0543 and 23-0617 Pulled for Highlight)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Reviewing the 56-item consent agenda, staff and commissioners pulled items 23-0543 (DCo Thrives guaranteed income pilot) and 23-0617 (ARPA youth enrichment contracts) for separate discussion and votes, while confirming NACO voting did not require a rule suspension. Commissioner Nida Allam highlighted APS funding included on the package before the board unanimously approved the remaining 54 consent items 5-0 (including $1.6M for Interfaith Food Shuttle food security and $3M for workforce development).

agenda_items.title: 23-0543: Approval of DCo Thrives Counties for Guaranteed Income Pilot ($1.69 Million ARPA)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Howerton and Commissioners Nida Allam, Nimasheena Burns, Heidi Carter, and Wendy Jacobs celebrated Chief of Staff Shannon Trapp and Cooperative Extension staff for launching 'DCo Thrives' ($1.69M in ARPA funding providing $750 monthly stipends for one year plus $100 survey stipends to low-income families with children), tying it to NACo Counties for Guaranteed Income, the Early Childhood Action Plan, and upstream child welfare prevention. Allam moved and Jacobs seconded approval, passing 5-0.

agenda_items.title: 23-0617: ARPA Community Grants — Youth Initiatives and Enrichment Contracts (5 Nonprofits)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Claudia Hager reviewed five contracts out of the $10.4M ARPA Community Grants portfolio supporting City of Durham Parks and Recreation, Empower Dance Foundation, Kids Note, Museum of Life and Science, and World Relief Durham. Commissioner Nimasheena Burns praised all five programs while announcing she would abstain due to serving on the Museum of Life and Science board; Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs moved approval, seconded by Commissioners Carter and Allam, passing 4-0-1.

agenda_items.title: 23-0590: Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) Leadership and Strategy Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Sheriff Clarence Birkhead introduced Project Safe Neighborhoods assistant coordinator Tamika Gilmer and lead coordinator Bishop Phillip Cousin (a former commissioner), reviewing the DOJ-backed 'carrot-and-stick' focus combining wraparound reentry/employment/addiction services with state and federal prosecution for habitual violent offenders. Birkhead noted 50+ community groups committed to the August 19 Ceasefire/Stop the Violence kickoff at Durham County Memorial Stadium and an executed crime-data analytics MOU with UNCG; commissioners praised the collaborative data-driven model with no formal action required.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (Personnel - N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6))
votes.notes: Pre-regular-session closed session; Chair Howerton reported at 01:29:52 that direction was given to staff and no action was taken.
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Brenda A. Howerton read the statutory personnel closed-session citation under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6). Commissioner Nimasheena Burns moved to enter closed session and Commissioner Heidi Carter seconded; the motion passed unanimously by voice vote prior to reconvening in open session at 01:29:47.

votes.item_title: Approval of Minutes (June 12, 2023 and June 26, 2023 Regular Sessions)
votes.notes: All five commissioners present and voting aye.
votes.discussion_detail: Following announcements, Commissioner Nida Allam moved and Commissioner Heidi Carter seconded approval of the June 12 and June 26, 2023 regular session minutes as submitted. The motion carried 5-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of Item 23-0543: DCo Thrives Counties for Guaranteed Income Pilot ($1.69M ARPA)
votes.notes: Spearheaded by Chair Howerton, Commissioner Allam, Chief of Staff Shannon Trapp, and Cooperative Extension.
votes.discussion_detail: Following remarks from all five commissioners supporting the guaranteed income pilot providing $750/month direct stipends (plus $100 survey stipends) for families with children, Commissioner Nida Allam moved approval of item 23-0543 and Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs seconded. The motion passed 5-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of Item 23-0617: ARPA Community Grants — Youth Initiatives and Enrichment Contracts
votes.notes: Commissioner Nimasheena Burns recused herself on the record because one of the five grantees is the Museum of Life and Science.
votes.discussion_detail: Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs moved approval of item 23-0617 covering five ARPA youth enrichment contracts (Durham Parks and Recreation, Empower Dance Foundation, Kids Note, Museum of Life and Science, and World Relief Durham), seconded simultaneously by Commissioners Heidi Carter and Nida Allam. Commissioner Nimasheena Burns formally abstained due to serving on the Museum of Life and Science board while expressing full support for the youth investments; the motion passed 4-0-1.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2023-08-07 9:00 AM - Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the August 7, 2023 Work Session presided over by Chair Brenda A. Howerton, the Durham Board of County Commissioners heard public comments on affordable housing near transit hubs, watershed protection, fire response times, blasting and mass-grading impacts from townhome developments, and respectful conduct under the public charge after personal attacks on the Public Health Director, then reviewed consent items including the GHSP grant, water/wastewater contracts, and accommodations and family phone-call standards in the NCDPS Durham County Youth Home agreement. Following a middle portion omitted in the transcript digest, the board suspended the rules (4-0) and unanimously (4-0) approved a $50-per-meeting stipend program for resident members of county boards and commissions to match the City of Durham's rate. The board also suspended the rules (4-0, moved by Heidi Carter and seconded by Nida Allam) and unanimously (4-0) approved Item 23-0571, an interlocal agreement with the City of Durham and Housing for New Hope alongside Budget Ordinance Amendment 24BCC00017 allocating $6,050,000 for the Carver Creek permanent supportive housing campus. After reviewing application-deadline findings for the Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC) Board vacancy, suspending the rules (4-0), and voting by ballot to retain incumbent Donald Lebkis on the ABC Board, the commissioners entered closed session (Item 23-0593) and later returned to adjourn with no further action and no split or contested votes recorded.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, and Pledge of Allegiance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton called the August 7, 2023 Work Session to order at 00:02:47 and read the board's public charge calling for respectful, courteous conduct from both board members and citizens. She then invited Commissioner Nida Allam (transcribed as 'commissioner Alom') to lead the Pledge of Allegiance.

agenda_items.title: Citizens' Comments (Affordable Housing, Watershed/Development Impacts, and Public Charge Reminder)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public speakers addressed several land-use and housing topics: Becky Winder discussed a Coalition for Affordable Housing draft position referencing the county's 2014 goal of 15% affordable housing at rail stops and bus hubs, while Wanda Allen opposed development in critical watersheds lacking fire stations, CIP funding, and adequate Durham Fire Department response times amid 17,900 projected dwellings. Other speakers urged compensation for blasting damage, requested a 10-foot no-clearing/no-grading buffer next to existing homes, and called for environmental testing and treatment. After a speaker attacked the Public Health Director, commissioners paused to reiterate that the public charge prohibits personal attacks on county staff.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review (GHSP Grant, Utilities Contracts, Rougemont Water Plan, and Youth Home MOA)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Manager presented consent items including Item 23-0480 (FY23-24 Governor's Highway Safety Program grant resolution), Item 23-0483 (Triangle Wastewater Treatment Plant chemical contracts, IFB 23-034), Item 23-0487 (Rougemont Water System Water Shortage Response Plan), Item 23-0500 (transcribed '2350', NCDPS/Durham County Youth Home MOA), Item 23-0505 (bulk diesel contract of $65,000 up to $90,000 under RFP 23-032), and Item 23-0514 (budget ordinance amendment) before a middle gap in the transcript. On the Youth Home MOA, Commissioner Nida Allam (transcribed 'Commissioner Long') questioned accommodations for gender-nonconforming, genderqueer, and transgender youth—with staff confirming individual rooms and gender-responsive room/bathroom assignments—and requested specifying minimum family phone call frequency in the agreement.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Resident Member Stipend Program ($50 per Meeting)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After a middle portion omitted from the transcript digest, the board suspended the rules 4-0 and considered a stipend program for resident members of county boards and commissions. Following a brief exchange over Robert's Rules of Order (motion, second, discussion, vote), a commissioner explained her motion to set the stipend at $50 per meeting rather than staff's $25 proposal in order to standardize with the City of Durham's $50 rate. The motion passed 4-0 by voice vote, and staff noted the program website page and notification letters were ready to distribute.

agenda_items.title: Carver Creek Supportive Housing Contract (Housing for New Hope) and Budget Amendment 24BCC00017 (Item 23-0571)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following introduction of new budget/grant staff member John (formerly a budget director at NC DPI), the board considered Item 23-0571 for Housing for New Hope and Budget Ordinance Amendment 24BCC00017 allocating $6,050,000 to purchase the Carver Creek permanent supportive housing campus (recognizing $3,000,000 from the City of Durham and appropriating general fund balance). The board suspended the rules 4-0 on a motion by Commissioner Heidi Carter seconded by Commissioner Nida Allam, and then approved the city-county interlocal agreement and budget amendment 4-0 by voice vote. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs afterward shared remarks praising the project for serving unhoused residents with severe mental illness met during the Point-in-Time count.

agenda_items.title: Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC) Board Vacancy Process Review and Ballot Appointment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented findings on applicant filing dates for the ABC Board vacancy, explaining that one applicant's name was excluded from the ballot because her application arrived after the June 30 deadline despite her possible confusion with a separate July 7 vacancy closing date. The board voted 4-0 to suspend the rules and proceeded to a ballot vote on the ABC Board appointment, selecting incumbent Donald Lebkis (Donald Lebkes) to retain his seat without requiring a follow-up voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Item 23-0593) and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The chair read Item 23-0593 to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) regarding personnel qualifications, performance, appointment conditions, or complaints/grievances, and the board approved entering closed session by voice vote at 06:04:44. Upon returning to open session at 07:20:16 (after noting at 07:10:32 that Wendy Jacobs was rejoining), the board reported it had given direction to staff with no actions to be taken and adjourned by voice vote at 07:20:31.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Session for Jul. 10, 2023
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the July 10, 2023 regular session, opening with an initial personnel closed session (entered 3-0, exited 5-0) and poignant remarks alongside Commissioner Nimasheena Burns mourning a five-year-old child killed and a fifteen-year-old injured by gun violence. Resident Jacqueline Wagstaff urged the board to reopen ABC Board applications after documenting that the County website displayed 'no vacancies' throughout June, prompting County Attorney Al Andrews to investigate mid-meeting and commissioners—after debate among Burns, Allam, and Howerton—to agree by consensus to postpone the ABC Board appointment until late August to verify fairness while proceeding with appointments to BPAC, the Convention Center Authority, Workforce Development Board, JCPC, Library Board of Trustees, and the RDU Airport Authority. The board also approved May 22 minutes 5-0, recognized 7 NACo Achievement Awards and the Senior Tar Heel Legislature's 30th anniversary, adopted 14 of 15 consent items 4-0-1, and unanimously approved 5-0 item 23-0472 retaining McGuireWoods Consulting for state lobbying.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (23-0489 Personnel), Public Charge, Announcements, and Gun Violence Condolences
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners Heidi Carter, Nida Allam, and Chair Brenda A. Howerton opened the 5:45 PM closed session 3-0 under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6), returning at 01:15:46 by a 5-0 vote to exit. Clerk Monica Wallace read announcements (including the July 14 Lowell L. Siler Lobby naming ceremony, STAR Talk podcast with Ryan Smith and Sheriff Birkhead on HEART, and library/open space events), after which Chair Howerton and Commissioner Burns spoke emotionally mourning a five-year-old killed and a fifteen-year-old injured by gun violence.

agenda_items.title: Citizens' Comments: ABC Board Vacancy Process Complaint and JCPC Thanks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jacqueline Wagstaff testified that she checked Durham County's boards and commissions portal throughout June (June 1 to July 1) and repeatedly saw 'no vacancies' for the ABC Board, requesting the application window be reopened rather than appointing tonight. County Attorney Al Andrews stated the complaint merited factual/IT review and agreed to confer with Clerk Wallace during the meeting, while JCPC Chair Dewan Langley thanked commissioners for increasing JCPC's annual allocation by $105,300.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (May 22, 2023) and Ceremonial Recognitions (Senior Tar Heel Legislature & 7 NACo Awards)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners approved the May 22, 2023 regular session minutes 5-0, issued a proclamation celebrating the 30th anniversary of the North Carolina Senior Tar Heel Legislature with remarks from delegate Kenneth Johnson, and celebrated seven 2023 National Association of Counties (NACo) Achievement Awards earned across the Board of Elections, HR, IS&T (x2), Economic Development (Andy Miracle), Register of Deeds, and Durham County Library.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (14 of 15 Items Approved) and Item 23-0472: McGuireWoods State Lobbying Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Howerton pulled item 23-0472 for public spotlight while Vice Chair Jacobs praised item 23-0482 (the County's disparity study work); Commissioner Heidi Carter moved and Commissioner Nida Allam seconded approval of the remaining 14 consent items, passing 4-0-1. Commissioners then enthusiastically highlighted item 23-0472 retaining McGuireWoods Consulting for state legislative lobbying in Raleigh—asking Assistant County Manager Deborah Craig-Ray to ensure education and environmental legislation are added to the firm's scope—before passing 23-0472 5-0 on Jacobs's motion seconded by Allam.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments and Consensus Deferral of ABC Board Vote
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Al Andrews reported that his preliminary review found no constitutional irregularity stopping the evening's ballot votes, though investigation of the website posting could continue. Following debate—with Commissioner Burns willing to wait a month out of fairness to Wagstaff, Commissioner Allam questioning waiting without reopening applications, and Chair Howerton proposing holding the vote until late August while verifying staff's process before deciding on re-advertising—the board agreed by consensus to hold the ABC Board appointment while announcing selections for BPAC (Andres Otero), Convention Center Authority (Lorente Bryant), Workforce Development Board (Andrew Miracle), JCPC (Kevin McIver, Leah Selvey, Jonathan Wilson, John Morris, LaBria Stevens, Renee Hill, Lisa Jones), Library Board (Aquarius Anderson, Tal Madeline, Jen McConnell, Carl Newman, five at-large seats), and RDU Airport Authority (David Morgan).
