disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Session for Jul. 10, 2023
disagreements.issue: Whether to Proceed With or Defer the ABC Board Appointment Pending Investigation of Website Posting Complaint
disagreements.summary: Following Jacqueline Wagstaff's citizen complaint that Durham County's website listed 'no vacancies' for the ABC Board throughout June, commissioners debated whether to hold the appointment and whether holding without immediately reopening applications accomplished fairness.
disagreements.side_a_position: Hold off on voting on the ABC Board appointment until staff investigates and verifies that the public application process was free of technical irregularities.
side_a_arguments: Deferring a single non-regulatory advisory/board appointment by one cycle preserves public trust without operational harm.
Staff needs time to verify website audit logs before finalizing an appointment rather than deciding whether to re-advertise prematurely.
disagreements.side_b_position: Questioned the utility of delaying the vote for a month unless new applications would also be accepted if warranted, while willing to defer if verification is the goal.
side_b_arguments: If applications are not reopened, holding a vote on the same applicant pool for one month may not change the substance of the complaint unless irregularities trigger re-advertising.
disagreements.resolution: Resolved by board consensus to hold the ABC Board appointment until the late August meeting pending County Attorney and Clerk verification of the online application posting, with re-advertising triggered only if irregularities were found.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Session for Jun. 26, 2023
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the June 26, 2023 regular session with four commissioners present (Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs on an approved excused absence abroad). Following severe-weather shelter briefings, adoption of the June 5 work session minutes 4-0, a Durham Refugee Day proclamation, and 4-0 passage of the 26-item consent agenda (covering $60M in capital, $6M Pre-K, $6M affordable housing, and Housing for New Hope's recovery campus), the board conducted two public hearings. Commissioners unanimously voted 4-0 to open and close the hearing and formally name the Admin II first-floor lobby the 'Lowell L. Siler Lobby' honoring Durham County's first African American County Attorney of 36 years, and voted 4-0 to hold the hearing, adopt the bond order, and adopt the issuance resolution for up to $60 million in General Obligation Refunding Bonds Series 2023; finally, the board reviewed the Durham Sports Commission's proposed multi-sport complex—with Commissioner Burns demanding written equity, MWBE, and HBCU/school-access commitments—and filled 11 advisory boards while holding JCPC and RDU Airport Authority to July 10.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Severe Weather Briefing, Announcements, and June 5 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton opened the 7:00 PM session amid severe storm warnings, reading the public charge and inviting Emergency Services Director Jim Groves to instruct attendees on tornado shelter-in-place procedures. Clerk Monica Wallace read announcements (Summer Meals, July 8 Refugee Day, Library Summer Reading, voter registration, August 31 Comprehensive Plan hearing, and Ag Economic Development grants), Commissioner Burns plugged Durham Tech's paid BioAg Pro internship, and Commissioner Allam celebrated $1.5B in federal NC broadband funding and Eid al-Adha before the board approved the June 5 work session minutes 4-0.

agenda_items.title: 23-0416: Durham Refugee Day 2023 Proclamation & 26-Item Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Howerton read the proclamation declaring July 8, 2023 as Durham Refugee Day, accepted by Cooperative Extension Director Donna Rewalt on behalf of Refugee Affairs Coordinator Nayo and partner agencies, with remarks from Commissioners Allam and Carter. With no items pulled, the board unanimously adopted the 26-item consent agenda 4-0, and Commissioner Burns delivered a 60-second summary highlighting $60M in capital projects, $6M for Pre-K, $6M for affordable housing, and $1M for agriculture; at meeting end (02:15:30), Commissioner Allam read Vice Chair Jacobs's statement praising Housing for New Hope's recovery housing partnership included on consent.

agenda_items.title: 23-0450: Public Hearing and Approval to Name Admin II Lobby the Lowell L. Siler Lobby
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief of Staff Shannon Trapp presented updated silver-framed Option 2 design concepts and Commissioner Burns's suggestion for engraved lobby lettering honoring Lowell L. Siler, Durham County's first African American County Attorney who served for over 36 years, as requested by the Durham Committee on the Affairs of Black People and Omega Psi Phi Beta Phi Chapter. Commissioners voted 4-0 to open the public hearing at 00:58:47, heard emotional tributes from Antonio Jones, Henry Pruitt, Chief District Court Judge Clayton Jones, Philip Terry, Michael Palmer, and Coach Butch Williams, voted 4-0 to close the hearing at 01:14:16, selected Option 2 placement, and formally approved naming the Admin II lobby the Lowell L. Siler Lobby 4-0 at 01:19:55.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 4-0 (Open PH, Close PH, and Formal Naming Approval)

agenda_items.title: 23-0456: Public Hearing, Bond Order, and Resolution for Not-to-Exceed $60M GO Refunding Bonds Series 2023
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Chris Wright and bond counsel Carlos Mazzano (Parker Poe) presented the $60 million General Obligation Refunding Bonds Series 2023 refinancing 2021 short-term variable-rate bonds from the 2016 school, library, museum, and community college referendum into long-term fixed-rate debt. Clerk Monica Wallace reported net debt at 1.24% of assessed valuation and $35,434,933 in estimated total interest; with no public speakers, the board voted 4-0 across four sequential motions to open the public hearing, close the hearing, adopt the bond order, and adopt the issuance resolution.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 4-0 (Open/Close PH, Bond Order, and Resolution)

agenda_items.title: 23-0326: Durham Sports Commission Major Sports Complex Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Discover Durham CEO Susan Amey and Durham Sports Commission Executive Director Marcus Manning presented early feasibility metrics on a proposed regional multi-sport complex (~250,000 sq ft indoor facility plus 37-acre outdoor fields) ahead of a formal fall funding/site recommendation. While commissioners saw regional tourism value toward the 2029 World University Games, Commissioner Nimasheena Burns strongly pushed back against vague equity plans, demanding concrete written MWBE contracting guarantees, affordable community access, colocation hotel impacts, and consultation with NCCU (noting Coach LeVelle Moton's gym facility shortages) and local high schools before advancing.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments (11 Boards Filled; JCPC & RDU Held to July 10)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Al Andrews announced the four present commissioners' ballot selections filling seats across 11 bodies: BPAC (Kai Monast, Nathan Lee, Edward Rizzotto), Board of Adjustment (Michael Tarrant), Criminal Justice Advisory Committee (B. Angelo Burch Sr.), Women's Commission (Kathleen Lockwood, Roberta Price, Ashley Marshall), DOST (Eric Faust), Planning Commission (William Chris Young), Racial Equity Commission (Shreyas Gupta), Sports Commission (Jonathan Leach), Workforce Development Board (Anthony Nelson), Environmental Affairs Board (Malcolm Gregory), Homeless Services Advisory Committee (Angela Holmes, Renee Vaughn), and Jury Commission (Jeanette Amis). At staff's recommendation due to Jacobs's absence, JCPC and RDU Airport Authority appointments were deferred to July 10.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 4-0 (11 boards); JCPC & RDU held to July 10

votes.notes: Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs absent (excused June 12).
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Howerton presented the June 5, 2023 work session minutes for approval. A commissioner moved and another seconded approval as written, passing 4-0 by voice vote with Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs absent on an excused absence.

votes.item_title: Motion to Open Public Hearing on 23-0450 (Lowell L. Siler Lobby Naming Request)
votes.notes: Four commissioners present.
votes.discussion_detail: Following Chief of Staff Shannon Trapp's design presentation and attorney guidance to take a formal vote to open the hearing, the motion to open the public hearing on naming the Admin II lobby the Lowell L. Siler Lobby was moved, seconded, and approved 4-0.

votes.item_title: Motion to Close Public Hearing on 23-0450 (Lowell L. Siler Lobby Naming Request)
votes.notes: Followed by unanimous informal support for Option 2 wall placement plus front-wall engraving.
votes.discussion_detail: After six community leaders and colleagues testified honoring former County Attorney Lowell L. Siler's 36 years of service, a commissioner moved and another seconded closing the public hearing, passing 4-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of Item 23-0450: Naming the Administrative II Lobby the Lowell L. Siler Lobby
votes.notes: Dedication ceremony scheduled for July 14, 2023 at 10:00 AM.
votes.discussion_detail: At staff's request to record a formal policy vote following the public hearing and Option 2 placement selection, a commissioner moved per county policy to name the Administrative II Building first-floor lobby the Lowell L. Siler Lobby. After a second, the motion passed 4-0.

votes.item_title: Motion to Open Public Hearing on 23-0456 ($60M General Obligation Refunding Bonds Series 2023)
votes.notes: Statement of debt reported net county indebtedness at 1.24% of assessed valuation.
votes.discussion_detail: After CFO Chris Wright, bond counsel Carlos Mazzano, and Clerk Monica Wallace read the required Local Government Bond Act filings into the record, a commissioner moved and another seconded opening the public hearing on the $60 million GO refunding bond order, passing 4-0.

votes.item_title: Motion to Close Public Hearing on 23-0456 ($60M General Obligation Refunding Bonds Series 2023)
votes.notes: Unanimous among four commissioners present.
votes.discussion_detail: With Clerk Monica Wallace confirming no members of the public signed up to speak on the refunding bond order, a commissioner moved and another seconded closing the public hearing, passing 4-0.

votes.item_title: Adoption of General Obligation Refunding Bond Order Authorizing $60M Series 2023 Bonds (23-0456)
votes.notes: Refinances 2021 short-term variable-rate bonds from the 2016 referendum into long-term fixed-rate debt.
votes.discussion_detail: A commissioner moved to adopt the bond order introduced on June 12 authorizing up to $60 million in General Obligation Refunding Bonds Series 2023 and directing the Clerk to publish notice of adoption under the Local Government Bond Act. Following a second and no further discussion, the motion passed 4-0.

votes.item_title: Adoption of Bond Resolution Providing for Issuance of $60M GO Refunding Bonds Series 2023 (23-0456)
votes.notes: Completes June 26 statutory authorization steps.
votes.discussion_detail: Following adoption of the bond order, a commissioner moved and another seconded adopting the resolution providing for the issuance of the Series 2023 General Obligation Refunding Bonds. The motion passed 4-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Board and Commission Appointments (11 Advisory Boards & Commissions)
votes.notes: Written ballot selection by the four commissioners present; two boards held for full-board participation.
votes.discussion_detail: County Attorney Al Andrews tabulated and read the four commissioners' ballot selections filling vacancies across 11 boards and commissions (BPAC, Board of Adjustment, CJAC, Women's Commission, DOST, Planning Commission, Racial Equity Commission, Sports Commission, Workforce Development Board, EAB, HSAC, and Jury Commission) while deferring JCPC and RDU Airport Authority appointments until July 10.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Session for Jun. 26, 2023
disagreements.issue: Equity Guarantees, HBCU/School Access, and MWBE Benchmarks for Proposed Regional Multi-Sport Complex
disagreements.summary: Following Discover Durham and the Durham Sports Commission's presentation on a major 250,000-sq-ft indoor and 37-acre outdoor sports complex, Commissioner Nimasheena Burns challenged staff to replace broad promises with binding equity, local access, and MWBE commitments before seeking county funds.
disagreements.side_a_position: Do not advance county support without written details on MWBE inclusion, affordable local resident/youth access, hotel coordination, and consultation with HBCU (NCCU) and high school athletic leadership.
side_a_arguments: Local programs such as NCCU basketball lack adequate practice courts and local youth are often priced out of tourism-driven facilities.
The board's equity standards require concrete written access, minority/women-owned contracting plans, and community stakeholder outreach—not general assurances.
disagreements.side_b_position: Continue feasibility scoping toward a fall funding and site recommendation centered on sports tourism economic impact and the 2029 World University Games.
side_b_arguments: Durham lacks competitive indoor/outdoor tournament capacity compared with peer communities, missing out on youth access and sports-tourism revenue.
Staff welcomed the feedback and pledged to return in the fall with expanded equity, access, and facility-sharing details.
disagreements.resolution: Informational update concluded with no vote; presenters committed to incorporating Burns's MWBE, HBCU, and local access benchmarks into the fall recommendation.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Session for Jun. 12, 2023
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the June 12, 2023 regular session with all five commissioners present, highlighted by the unanimous 5-0 adoption of Durham County's FY 2023-24 $844,940,496 Annual Budget Ordinance featuring a 3-cent property tax increase, a $19.22/hour county living wage floor, $187.95 million for Durham Public Schools (+$10.8M / $4,650 per pupil), $7.9 million for Durham Pre-K, $2.4 million for Durham Tech scholarships, and new Familiar Faces and opioid MAT investments. To comply with Session Law 2021-191 conflict-of-interest rules, the board separately passed 4-0-1 three nonprofit budget amendments for Downtown Durham Inc. ($200,000), Museum of Durham History ($76,000), and the NC Museum of Life and Science ($2,358,124). Commissioners also passed 5-0 a landmark Chapter 4 Animal Control ordinance amendment establishing a Trap-Neuter-Vaccinate-Release (TNVR) program for community cats, approved initial findings and public-hearing resolutions 5-0 for $60 million in GO Refunding Bonds Series 2023, executed two pulled ARPA youth and maternal-health contracts 5-0, and granted Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs an excused absence for June 26.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, Minutes (May 1 & May 8), and Ceremonial Resolutions (Conan Morgan & Pride Month)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton opened the regular session, led approval of the May 1 work session and May 8 regular session minutes 5-0, and joined commissioners in reading resolution 23-0415 mourning political strategist and 2022 bond consultant Conan Traval Morgan. Howerton then issued Pride Month proclamation 23-0422, accepted by LGBTQ Center of Durham interim director Natalie who noted a $25,000 matching challenge and LGBTQ training with Wake County, alongside comments from Commissioners Burns, Allam, Jacobs, and Howerton lifting up Juneteenth and anti-discrimination protections; staff also acknowledged CIO Greg Marrow's PTI and GovTech awards (23-0385/0386).

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 23-0296 through 23-0435, Excluding 23-0425, 23-0433, 23-0434)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and commissioners pulled item 23-0425 (GO Refunding Bonds) and items 23-0433 and 23-0434 (ARPA community grant contracts) for separate discussion. The remaining consent agenda items were moved, seconded, and passed 5-0 by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: 23-0414: Adoption of FY 2023-24 Annual Budget Ordinance ($844,940,496)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following public comment by Dewan Langley (requesting $250,000 for Charles Hamilton Houston Foundation and $210,330 for JCPC while thanking County Manager Kimberly Sowell for $105,300 added to JCPC), the board voted 5-0 to adopt the FY 2023-24 Annual Budget Ordinance totaling $844,940,496. Commissioners highlighted the $19.22/hour minimum wage floor, +$10.8M for DPS ($187,951,627 total / $4,650 per pupil plus classified/certified raises), $7.9M for Pre-K, $2.4M for Durham Tech Promise, Familiar Faces data integration, detention center MAT medical leadership, 17 net new positions (incl. Elections, Veterans, Stormwater outreach) alongside $2.5M in position reductions, and concern over projected $6.4M annual DPS losses to state Opportunity Scholarship vouchers.

agenda_items.title: 23-0437, 23-0438, 23-0436: SL 2021-191 Nonprofit Budget Ordinance Amendments (DDI, Museum of Durham History, Museum of Life & Science)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: To comply with Session Law 2021-191 / N.C.G.S. 14-234.3 conflict-of-interest recusal requirements where board members serve on recipient nonprofit boards, commissioners voted individually on three budget ordinance amendments: item 23-0437 (24BCC00002) appropriating $200,000 to Downtown Durham Inc. (passed 4-0-1), item 23-0438 (24BCC00003) appropriating $76,000 to the Museum of Durham History (passed 4-0-1), and item 23-0436 (24BCC00001) appropriating $2,358,124 to the NC Museum of Life and Science (passed 4-0-1, with VP Kate Center thanking the board).

agenda_items.title: 23-0425: Initial Resolutions and Bond Order Introduction for $60M GO Refunding Bonds Series 2023
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Finance staff and bond counsel Carlos Mazzano (Parker Poe) presented the initial steps to refinance $60 million in 2021 short-term variable-rate bonds from the 2016 referendum into long-term fixed-rate bonds. The board voted 5-0 to adopt the initial resolution making certain statements of fact (02:01:19), read the Bond Order introduction into the record without requiring a vote, and voted 5-0 to adopt the resolution calling the June 26 public hearing (02:03:56).

agenda_items.title: 23-0389: Chapter 4 Animal Control Ordinance Amendment Establishing Trap-Neuter-Vaccinate-Release (TNVR) Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Assistant County Attorney Curtis Massey presented the negotiated amendment to Chapter 4 of the Durham County Code removing four legal barriers flagged by the Animal Welfare Advisory Committee and APS to authorize a Trap-Neuter-Vaccinate-Release (TNVR) program for free-roaming community cats. Commissioners Jacobs, Allam, Carter, and Burns thanked Massey and advocates for years of compromise on a humane, cost-effective solution; Burns moved adoption and the amendment passed 5-0.

agenda_items.title: 23-0433 & 23-0434: ARPA Community Grants (Youth Tutoring & Maternal Health) and Excused Absence Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy County Manager Claudia Hager highlighted items 23-0433 (youth tutoring and enrichment contracts with Purpose Learning Lab and Emily K Center) and 23-0434 (maternal and infant health capacity building with Duke University's Center for Child and Family Health), noting 24-month expenditure timelines ahead of federal deadlines; the board approved both items 5-0 at 02:20:38. meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners - Budget Work Session #4 (June 5, 2023)
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over Budget Work Session #4 on June 5, 2023, as commissioners worked with County Manager Kimberly Sowell, Budget Director Keith Lane, and staff to finalize consensus items ahead of the June 12 FY 2023-24 budget adoption vote. Three major policy clashes emerged during the session: Commissioners scrutinized the Animal Protection Society (APS) of Durham's $201,958 (23%) shelter funding increase and sole-source contract longevity before reaching a 3-commissioner consensus to fund the request pending operational follow-up; Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs clashed with Commissioner Heidi Carter over threatening to withhold future school capital funding until Durham Public Schools presents reuse plans for the former Northern High School and Durham School of the Arts campuses; and Commissioners Carter, Allam, and Jacobs pushed back against Chair Howerton's push to add $80,000 for two Boys and Girls Club vans directly onto the add/delete list outside departmental nonprofit vetting. Commissioners also discussed $100,000 for advisory board stipends ($50 in-person / $25 virtual), $1.9 billion in 10-year Capital Improvement Plan cost escalations, Museum of Durham History expansion timing, RTP's 3.5-cent special tax district request, and Session Law 2021-191 recusal compliance; no formal votes were taken.

agenda_items.title: 23-0406: Animal Protection Society (APS) of Durham FY24 Budget Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: APS Director Shafonda Allen and staff presented a $201,958 (23%) contract increase to $1,080,333 for running the county animal shelter, alongside Manager Sowell's proposed flat/10% alternatives. Commissioner Nimasheena Burns questioned the 30-year sole-source relationship, capacity/intake hours, reserve balances, and audit transparency, while Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs praised APS's 33-year partnership, volunteer leverage, and modest 3% wage ask, requesting benchmarking data against peer counties. Near the end of the session (03:13:00), three commissioners gave an informal thumbs-up to incorporate the full $201,958 increase subject to follow-up reporting on shelter hours and benchmarks.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / Informal consensus (3 commissioners thumbs-up for $201,958 increase)

agenda_items.title: 23-0407: Boards and Commissions Stipend Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief of Staff Shannon Trapp and Clerk Monica Wallace outlined the $100,000 FY24 stipend program paying appointed volunteers $50 per in-person meeting and $25 per virtual meeting to offset participation barriers, leaving implementation details such as joint City-County boards to board guidance. Commissioner Heidi Carter urged matching the City of Durham's flat $50 rate regardless of format on joint boards so county appointees are not treated inequitably.

agenda_items.title: Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) Update and Surplus School Site Reuse Debate
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Keith Lane and Deputy County Manager Claudia Hager reviewed the $1.9 billion 10-year Capital Improvement Plan, highlighting severe construction escalations (Animal Shelter rising from $30M to $45M-$50M; new Durham School of the Arts nearing $200M) and plans for a 2026 GO bond referendum. Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs sparked a sharp debate by warning she would vote against future school capital projects unless DPS delivers concrete reuse plans for vacated Northern High School and DSA campuses, while Commissioner Heidi Carter urged respecting the elected Board of Education's authority.

agenda_items.title: Museum of Durham History Supplemental Funding Request ($568k Design & $108k Operations)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Museum Executive Director Patrick Mucklow requested $568,000 toward design costs at 500 West Main Street and $108,000 in annual operating/salary support as the museum outgrows the 1938 Hubbs/Admin Annex site. County Manager Kimberly Sowell and staff recommended deferring capital design commitments outside the FY24 operating budget until the Joint City-County Facilities/Capital committee evaluates space needs alongside the Main Street renovation project.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / Deferred outside FY24 operating budget

agenda_items.title: Add/Delete Budget List, Boys & Girls Club Van Request Debate, RTP Special Tax, and SL 2021-191 Recusals
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Reviewing the Add/Delete reconciliation sheet with David Ades and Keith Lane, commissioners discussed Boys & Girls Club's late $80,000 request for two student transport vans: Chair Howerton urged immediate funding for DPS youth transport, while Commissioners Carter, Allam, and Jacobs objected to bypassing staff/departmental nonprofit vetting via the add/delete list (ultimately directing staff to explore surplus vehicles or ARPA funding while adopting a formal nonprofit vetting policy). Commissioners also reviewed Research Triangle Park's 3.5-cent special tax district request (noting property-tax mechanics) and County Attorney guidance on Session Law 2021-191 separate voting for boards where commissioners serve as directors.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / Direction to staff (No formal votes)

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners - Budget Work Session #4 (June 5, 2023)
disagreements.issue: Magnitude and Oversight of APS Shelter Funding Increase (23% / $201,958 vs. Flat / 10%)
disagreements.summary: Commissioners split over whether to fully grant the Animal Protection Society of Durham's 23% ($201,958) funding increase given its 30-year non-competitive sole-source contract and capacity pauses, or honor its full operating/wage request.
disagreements.side_a_position: Support full $201,958 funding in light of APS's 33-year partnership, heavy private fundraising, 650+ volunteers, and overdue staff wage increases.
side_a_arguments: The County covers only ~34% ($841,000) of the shelter budget while APS fundraises nearly three-quarters of total costs and provides immense volunteer labor value.
APS's requested 3% wage adjustment is modest given county employees are moving to a $19.22/hr living wage floor.
disagreements.side_b_position: Question an immediate 23% increase without recent competitive RFPs, clearer reserve/profit-and-loss separation, and operational review of intake capacity pauses.
side_b_arguments: Holding a sole-source shelter contract for roughly 30 years without competitive RFPs warrants stronger financial audit review and performance transparency.
At points when the shelter hit capacity, intake stalled; requested clearer operational reporting before committing permanent increases.
disagreements.resolution: Resolved via informal work-session poll at 03:13:00 with three commissioners giving thumbs-up to add the $201,958 APS increase to the FY24 budget subject to follow-up data on shelter hours and peer benchmarks; subsequently enacted in the June 12 budget.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners - Budget Work Session #4 (June 5, 2023)
disagreements.issue: Conditioning Future School Capital Funding on DPS Reuse Plans for Surplus Campuses
disagreements.summary: During the 10-year Capital Improvement Plan briefing, Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs and Commissioner Heidi Carter disagreed over whether the board should leverage county bond/capital approvals to force DPS reuse plans for vacated Northern High School and Durham School of the Arts sites.
disagreements.side_a_position: Withhold support for new school capital allocations unless DPS produces concrete reuse plans for vacated public school facilities.
side_a_arguments: Escalating bond costs (such as DSA rising toward $200 million) require joint city-county-school discipline so aging campuses are not left vacant or underutilized.
Commissioners control capital funding and must demand coordinated multi-agency planning.
disagreements.side_b_position: Defer to the elected Board of Education's statutory governance over school facility disposition and reuse decisions rather than imposing capital vetoes.
side_b_arguments: School board members are separately elected officials accountable to voters for managing DPS property decisions.
Capital funding decisions should support joint student needs without undermining school board autonomy.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken during the CIP briefing; County staff noted ongoing multi-agency coordination ahead of the 2026 bond cycle.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners - Budget Work Session #4 (June 5, 2023)
disagreements.issue: Boys & Girls Club $80,000 Van Request and Nonprofit Vetting Integrity in the Add/Delete Process
disagreements.summary: A sharp disagreement broke out over Chair Brenda A. Howerton's push to insert $80,000 for two Boys and Girls Club transport vans into the budget add/delete list, with three commissioners warning the request bypassed departmental nonprofit vetting.
disagreements.side_a_position: Do not insert unvetted mid-budget nonprofit requests onto the add/delete list outside established departmental and subject-matter-expert review.
side_a_arguments: Bypassing competitive grants and staff vetting sets a precedent that politicizes the add/delete process and creates inequities among worthy local nonprofits.
Requests from outside organizations must run through consistent formal policy criteria and ARPA/surplus channels rather than last-minute commissioner add-ons.
disagreements.side_b_position: Act urgently to fund two vans for the Boys and Girls Club so vulnerable Durham Public Schools students have safe transportation to after-school programming.
side_b_arguments: The Boys and Girls Club's existing vans are deteriorating and urgent youth transportation needs cannot wait until another budget cycle.
With only weeks left before adoption, commissioners must find an immediate way to support children already served by DPS.
disagreements.resolution: Although Commissioner Carter briefly offered collegial compromise, commissioners reached consensus not to insert the $80,000 into the general operating add/delete list, instead directing County Manager Sowell to explore surplus county vans or ARPA options and establish a clear nonprofit budget-request policy.

meetings.title: BOCC Work Session - June 5, 2023
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the June 5, 2023 BOCC Work Session, which opened with virtual public comment urging commissioners to consider Durham Police Department gun violence data affecting Black boys and young men when finalizing budget allocations. The board unanimously approved an agenda adjustment adding a resolution honoring the late Conan Morgan to the June 12 regular session consent agenda and reviewed 17 consent items covering wastewater infrastructure, Youth Home security equipment, staffing contracts, and volunteer fire department agreements. Commissioners also heard presentations on the county's refined facility naming policy, the Durham County Transit Plan work program and GoTriangle microtransit budget adjustments, and upcoming affordable housing and ARPA RFP projects before adjourning to transition to the courthouse for afternoon budget deliberations.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment on Gun Violence Data and Budget Priorities
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Warren Langley of the Charles Hamilton Houston Foundation spoke virtually during the public comment period, referencing Durham Police Department data showing that Black boys and young men are overwhelmingly affected by gun violence. He urged the Board of County Commissioners to weigh those data calls as they allocate funding in the upcoming FY23-24 budget. No other speakers signed up in person or virtually.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Adjustment: Resolution Honoring the Late Conan Morgan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A commissioner moved to suspend the rules and add a resolution honoring the late Conan Morgan to the consent agenda so that it could be approved, sent to the family, and read in its entirety at the upcoming Monday regular session. After brief procedural clarification with the chair, the motion was seconded and approved unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review (17 Items)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Dr. Kimberly Sowell walked the board through 17 consent agenda items for the upcoming regular session, including a $900,000 sewer utility fund balance appropriation and $817,993 sole-source exemption for Triangle Wastewater Treatment Plant rotors and gearboxes (23-0296), a millimeter-wave scanner for the new Durham County Youth Home (23-0325), a charter resolution renaming Triangle J Council of Governments to Central Pines Regional Council (23-0348), and multiple staffing and aeration basin service contracts. Regarding item 23-0370 on fire protection contracts with Bahama, Lebanon, and Redwood VFDs and extensions with Eno and New Hope VFDs, a commissioner asked to receive the planned July service-change presentation earlier given budget implications, and staff also committed to emailing a requested model report before Monday.

agenda_items.title: County Facility Naming Policy and Naming Committee Recommendation

agenda_items.title: Durham County Transit Plan Work Program and GoTriangle Microtransit Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DCHC MPO Executive Director Doug Plachinski and transit staff presented the annual Transit Plan work program, project implementation staffing, equity and MWBE participation metrics, and accountability framework. Discussion addressed GoTriangle's ~$670,000 microtransit pilot exceeding its current-year budget because trips duplicated fixed-route bus corridors, requiring rule adjustments for phase two, as well as a $1.4 million funding reduction after GoTriangle removed 50% of the vehicle rental tax allocation effective July 2023. agenda_items.title: Affordable Housing Projects and ARPA/RFP Funding Recommendations

meetings.title: BOCC - Budget Work Session #3 - June 1, 2023
meetings.executive_summary: At Budget Work Session #3 on June 1, 2023, Durham Technical Community College leaders presented their FY23-24 budget priorities, including living-wage janitorial contracts, workforce scholarships funded through Article 46 sales tax, in-house facilities positions, and faculty/staff recruitment and retention funds. Later in the session, commissioners and County Manager Dr. Kimberly Sowell debated whether to add a 30-minute Museum of Durham History presentation to the June 5 work session despite the City of Durham not yet considering the joint request. The board also reviewed opioid settlement fund governance and removed a $600,000 item from the budget add/delete list because three commissioners were not ready to support it.

agenda_items.title: Item 23-0396: Durham Technical Community College and Economic Development Budget Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DTCC President J.B. Buxton, Chief Academic Officer Dr. Baddler, and Workforce Engagement Executive Director Jerry Jones presented five priorities in the County Manager's recommended budget: living wages (including a rebid housekeeping/janitorial contract meeting Durham County's living wage), key infrastructure positions such as an in-house plumber, economic and workforce development (Small Business Center and apprenticeship coordinators), faculty/staff recruitment and retention inducements, and student scholarships (Back-to-Work $700 non-credit grants, BULLS stipends, and Durham Tech Promise $500/semester grants). Buxton also noted plans to discuss repurposing Article 46 funds alongside a $50,000 private grant to cover textbooks and transportation for DPS high school students earning workforce credentials.

agenda_items.title: Museum of Durham History Budget Request and June 5 Work Session Schedule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle gap in the digest, commissioners discussed Commissioner Nida Allam's request to use an open 30-minute slot on June 5 for a presentation from the Museum of Durham History on facility expansion and staff salary increases. County Manager Dr. Kimberly Sowell and Budget Director Keith Lane noted she had moved the item to the June 13 Joint City-County meeting because the City had not yet received or processed the joint funding request. Commissioners ultimately agreed to allow a 30-minute informational presentation on June 5 while acknowledging that any joint funding decision would require coordination with the City.

agenda_items.title: Opioid Settlement Funds Process and Budget Add/Delete List Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff clarified that opioid settlement expenditures (now coordinated by Dwayne following Gudrun's departure) would be brought individually as specific strategies and initiatives are developed rather than bundled into the annual operating budget. Reviewing the add/delete list ahead of the June 5 wrap-up, commissioners confirmed that three members were not ready to proceed on a $600,000 item and agreed to remove it from the list, leaving a net general fund balance increase of $708,000.

disagreements.issue: Scheduling the Museum of Durham History Funding Presentation for the June 5 Budget Work Session
disagreements.summary: Commissioners and County Management disagreed on whether to place the Museum of Durham History's expansion and salary funding request on the June 5 final budget work session agenda before the City of Durham had acted on the joint request.
disagreements.side_a_position: Hear a 30-minute informational presentation from the Museum of Durham History at the June 5 work session so the full board can review the request before the July recess.
side_a_arguments: Not all commissioners have received the background information shared with the museum liaison, and the next regular work session after June is not until August due to the July break.
Joint City-County meetings do not include the full Board of County Commissioners, and Council Member Williams had already asked about it on the City side.
A 30-minute slot was open in the June 5 afternoon schedule.
disagreements.side_b_position: Defer joint City-County funding requests like the Museum of Durham History to the June 13 Joint City-County meeting rather than placing unvetted joint asks on the June 5 budget wrap-up session.
side_b_arguments: Budget work sessions are intended for items the County will fund wholly and decide upon for the June 12 budget adoption, whereas the City budget office received the request late and was not considering it yet.
Making a County budget commitment or add/delete decision on June 5 without knowing the City's position would be premature, and any post-June 12 funding would require August fund balance action.
disagreements.resolution: Commissioners agreed to accommodate a strictly 30-minute informational presentation on June 5 while deferring any joint funding coordination to the June 13 Joint City-County meeting.

meetings.title: BOCC - Budget Work Session #2 - May 24, 2023
meetings.executive_summary: During Budget Work Session #2 on May 24, 2023, the board received an update on Durham's Refugee and Immigrant Affairs program, highlighting partner outreach, the MyDurham civic integration cohort, planned community resource and needs assessments, and delays in finalizing a City-County interlocal agreement. Commissioners also previewed Youth Home, Sheriff's Office Medication-Assisted Treatment (MAT), and Justice Services' Familiar Faces and Stepping Up initiatives. Near the close of the session, staff outlined a late 3- to 3.5-cent tax rate increase request for the RTP Special Tax District, and commissioners debated agenda discipline for the remaining June 1 and June 5 budget work sessions as well as resident concerns regarding the Lebanon Fire District.

agenda_items.title: Item 23-0081: Refugee and Immigrant Affairs Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Refugee and Immigrant Affairs Coordinator presented an overview of Durham's immigrant and refugee population—noting 14.8% speak languages other than English at home—along with over 100 partner meetings, the MyDurham civic integration program (200+ participants), and proposed resource mapping and needs assessment work. Commissioners discussed trust-building with immigrant communities, youth outreach through Durham Public Schools and Durham Tech, language access barriers, and following up on why the City-County interlocal agreement signed in October 2021 for the joint Office of Immigrant and Refugee Affairs had stalled at the City level.

agenda_items.title: Youth Home, Sheriff's Office Opioid/MAT Program, and Justice Services Preview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County staff introduced budget presentations covering the new Durham County Youth Home, the Sheriff's Office detention center opioid treatment and Medication-Assisted Treatment (MAT) programs including a newly recommended medical director position, and Justice Services' Familiar Faces Initiative (FFI) and Stepping Up Initiative. (Subsequent middle remarks were truncated in the digest.)

agenda_items.title: RTP Special Tax District Rate Request, Lebanon Fire District, and June Budget Schedule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and the County Attorney explained that a requested 3- to 3.5-cent property tax rate increase for the Research Triangle Park (RTP) special tax district arrived after the recommended budget was published and would be placed on the add/delete list for June 12 budget ordinance adoption, with clarification needed on its impact as RTP parcels convert from commercial to residential in 2024. Commissioners also debated the June 1 and June 5 work session agendas, with Commissioner Wendy Jacobs requesting information on full-time firefighter layoffs at the Lebanon Fire District and board-first review of Low-Income Homeowner Relief policy changes, while Commissioner Nimasheena Burns objected to adding late presentations or spilling into June 6.

disagreements.issue: Adding Late Presentations (Museum of Durham History, Lebanon Fire District) and Potentially Using June 6 for Budget Work Sessions
disagreements.summary: Commissioners differed over whether to add non-tax-rate or late-submitted presentations onto the June 1 and June 5 budget work sessions or extend deliberations to the reserved June 6 date.
disagreements.side_a_position: Add timely informational updates such as the Lebanon Fire District staffing transition and Museum of Durham History to upcoming work sessions, and ensure Low-Income Homeowner Relief policy changes come to the full BOCC first.
side_a_arguments: Residents in the Lebanon Fire District are alarmed about full-time firefighters being let go and potential impacts on response and homeowners insurance ratings.
The full BOCC does not attend Joint City-County meetings, so board members need direct briefings on policies they must approve.
disagreements.side_b_position: Keep the June 1 and June 5 budget work sessions strictly focused on county budget decisions and honor the pre-scheduled calendar without spilling over to June 6.
side_b_arguments: The board already faces 7.5-hour budget work session days, and adding 30- to 45-minute late requests from external groups is unfair to budget staff and other presenters.
Budget dates have been on the calendar since the start of the year and should be honored rather than forcing staff and commissioners back on June 6.
disagreements.resolution: Staff noted Lebanon Fire District had no tax rate increase and would be placed on a regular work session after the budget, Low-Income Homeowner Relief policy updates would return to the full board without affecting the budget allocation, and the pre-set June 1 and June 5 schedule was maintained.

meetings.title: BOCC - May 22, 2023 - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the May 22, 2023 Regular Session while Chair Brenda A. Howerton participated virtually. The board unanimously approved the April 24 minutes, issued an EMS Week proclamation, and conducted a collaborative reading of a joint Day of Remembrance resolution condemning youth and gun violence alongside Durham City Council and Durham Public Schools. Following discussion of a stakeholder-negotiated Trap-Neuter-Vaccinate-Release (TNVR) cat management proposal, commissioners unanimously directed the County Attorney to draft a formal Chapter 4 ordinance amendment resolution for a June 12 vote, and after a closed session unanimously authorized up to $285,000 in additional funding and condemnation authority for the Snow Hill Road pump station and force main replacement project.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Virtual Chair Notice, and Community Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs announced that Chair Brenda A. Howerton was attending virtually and that Jacobs would preside over the meeting. Clerk Monica Wallace read agenda announcements covering World Hunger Day Durham on June 4, the Durham Black Chamber of Commerce Enrich Bookkeeping Assistance Pilot Program, and the Sheriff's Office Start Talk podcast, followed by an animal shelter adoption reminder.

agenda_items.title: Approval of April 24, 2023 Board Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Nimasheena Burns moved to approve the April 24, 2023 board minutes with no revisions noted. The motion was seconded and approved unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: EMS Week Proclamation, Military Appreciation, and Day of Remembrance Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter read a proclamation declaring May 21–27, 2023 as EMS Week in Durham County, recognizing Chief Paramedic Mark Lockhart, regional fire and hospital partners, overdose outreach, and familiar-faces check-ins. After a military appreciation and Memorial Day appeal, commissioners led by Nimasheena Burns performed a round-robin reading of a joint Day of Remembrance resolution—crafted with Mayor O'Neal and DPS Board Chair Bettina Umstead—pledging action to reduce gun violence, support responsible gun ownership, and mobilize community volunteers for Durham youth.

agenda_items.title: Chapter 4 Animal Ordinance Amendment: Trap-Neuter-Vaccinate-Release (TNVR) Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle truncation in the digest, Commissioner Heidi Carter endorsed the March 21, 2023 stakeholder-negotiated draft allowing a volunteer-supported TNVR outdoor cat management program without requiring county budget funds. County Attorney Allen Andrews advised formalizing the amendment via a clean redlined resolution under County Ordinance 1-11 rather than adopting an unformatted draft on the spot. Carter then moved, seconded by Commissioner Nida Allam, to direct the County Attorney to prepare a Chapter 4 resolution based on the March 21, 2023 working group proposal for final action at the June 12, 2023 meeting.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Attorney read the board's ballot appointment results for county boards and commissions, including William Young and Tia Rawlings (business representative on the Memorial Stadium Authority). Vice Chair Jacobs thanked the volunteers stepping forward to serve and noted no consent agenda items were pulled.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Snow Hill Road Pump Station / Force Main Replacement Authorization
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted unanimously to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) to instruct staff on real property acquisition negotiations and employment contract compensation terms. Upon returning to open session at 03:48:51, commissioners unanimously approved a motion authorizing up to $285,000 in additional funding for the Snow Hill Road pump station and force main replacement project and directing staff to exercise all powers, including condemnation, to acquire necessary parcels before adjourning.

meetings.executive_summary: At Budget Work Session #1 on May 16, 2023, budget staff reviewed the fiscal framework behind the County Manager's FY23-24 recommended budget, highlighting $35.8 million in natural revenue growth, strong sales tax and Medicaid hold harmless gains, a 3-cent total property tax rate increase (split evenly between general fund operations and 2022 GO Bond capital financing), and $15 million in MAG study and merit pay raises. Staff also noted $2.5 million in operational reductions from historical unspent departmental funds and previewed upcoming property revaluation effects and a pending Research Triangle Foundation tax rate request. In the afternoon portion, staff updated commissioners on the BULLS life sciences workforce initiative, one-time funding priorities including a homeless day center RFP and water/sewer infrastructure needs, and the Interise MWBE training program.

agenda_items.title: FY23-24 Budget Revenue Outlook, Property Tax Rate, Compensation, and Revaluation Preview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget staff presented the macroeconomic and revenue picture for the FY23-24 recommended budget, reporting $35.8 million in natural general fund revenue growth led by $21.8 million in total new sales tax revenue ($13.4M general fund, $8.4M capital financing) and $12 million in Medicaid hold harmless funds. To fund the 7% MAG study compensation increase ($10.5M), 3–4% merit increases ($4.5M), full Durham Public Schools funding, and nearly $2 million in added DTCC support ($2.4M total in Article 46 scholarships), the budget pairs $2.5 million in departmental operational reallocations with a 3-cent property tax increase (1.5 cents general fund and 1.5 cents 2022 GO Bond debt service). Staff also previewed the upcoming property revaluation—projecting a revenue-neutral rate in the high 50s or 60s—and noted a late RTP tax district request scheduled for May 24.

agenda_items.title: BULLS Workforce Initiative, One-Time Funding Proposals, and Interise MWBE Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle gap in the digest, staff and Assistant County Manager Tammy Hall briefed the board on the BULLS workforce pipeline as cohorts 4 and 5 prepared to graduate, noting an $800,000 Made in Durham grant for nonprofit success coaches, $250,000 in annual county stipends, plans for DPS teacher externships, independent program evaluation, and adding a second industry pathway alongside biopharma. Commissioners praised the program while pressing for earlier outreach to enrolled DPS high school students and stronger post-graduation job interview placement. Staff also discussed one-time funding priorities—such as a homeless day center RFP, a small business entrepreneurship fund, and nearly $100 million in water/sewer needs—and reported progress on the 13-week Interise MWBE Evolution training program.

meetings.title: County Manager's Recommended Fiscal Year 23-24 Budget Presentation
meetings.executive_summary: On May 11, 2023, County Manager Dr. Kimberly Sowell formally presented the FY23-24 Recommended Budget to the Board of County Commissioners pursuant to N.C.G.S. 159-12. Highlighting $36 million in natural revenue growth outpaced by $38 million in core priority increases, Sowell proposed a 3-cent property tax rate increase (1.5 cents general fund, 1.5 cents capital financing) to fund a 7% MAG compensation study adjustment plus 3%–4% merit raises for county employees while limiting new position growth. Education remained the largest investment at over $207 million—fully funding Durham Public Schools' request at $188 million, raising DTCC support by nearly $2 million, and adding over $1 million for Durham Pre-K—alongside new investments in detention center medical/opioid care, the Youth Home, a new Office of Engagement, and 2024 election readiness.

agenda_items.title: Manager's Strategic Vision, Organizational Restructure, and Position Restraint
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Dr. Kimberly Sowell opened her FY23-24 budget address under N.C.G.S. 159-12 by announcing a reimagining of Durham County's strategic plan as a measurable framework for all policy and budget choices. She described an internal leadership reorganization establishing deputy and assistant county manager portfolios and explained her intentional decision to limit new FTE additions while existing vacancies remain high.

agenda_items.title: Revenue Outlook, 3-Cent Tax Rate Recommendation, and Employee Compensation (MAG Study)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Sowell reported $36 million in natural revenue growth from property tax, sales tax, Medicaid hold harmless funds, occupancy tax, and fund balance, contrasted with $38 million in core priority cost increases. To retain county staff amid inflation and regional competition, the budget implements the Management Advisory Group (MAG) compensation study recommendation of a 7% across-the-board increase plus 3%–4% pay-for-performance merit raises (10%–11% maximum), supported by a recommended 3-cent property tax rate increase split between 1.5 cents for capital financing and 1.5 cents for general fund operations.

agenda_items.title: Education Funding: Durham Public Schools ($188M), DTCC (+20%), and Universal Pre-K
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Recommending over $207 million across education partners, Sowell proposed fully funding Durham Public Schools' request at $188 million (33% of the general fund, including a $10.8 million current expense increase lifting per-pupil funding by $289 to $4,650 per student, plus ~$58 million in indirect county support). The budget also increases Durham Tech funding by nearly $2 million (20%, including $520,000 more for $2.4 million total in Durham Student Scholarships and school-to-work pipeline roles) and adds over $1 million to expand Durham Pre-K by up to 100 children.

agenda_items.title: Community Safety, Veterans Services, Engagement Office, Elections, and Adoption Timeline
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Sowell detailed targeted investments including $532,000 for second-year food security grants, an additional Veteran Services Officer, a dedicated detention center medical director for the Sheriff's Office opioid/MAT program, CJRC psychiatric services and the Familiar Faces Initiative, opening the new Youth Home and assessment center, and expanded JCPC juvenile crime prevention grants. meetings.title: BOCC - May 8, 2023 - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton opened the May 8, 2023 Regular Session with a moment of silence for victims of gun violence in Texas, followed by announcements including Fidelity Investments' extended May 15 scholarship deadline for Durham students. The board unanimously (5-0) approved the April 10 regular session minutes and adopted proclamations for Resilient and Thriving Communities Week (23-0308) and Older Americans Month (23-0309). Later, the board held a public hearing with no speakers on updated water and sewer System Development Fees (to be incorporated into the upcoming budget) and received the Management Advisory Group (MAG) compensation study and proposed pay plan establishing a $19.22/hour living wage floor and 7% across-the-board pay adjustment.

agenda_items.title: Moment of Silence, Agenda Announcements, and Fidelity Scholars Extension
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton led a moment of silence for children and residents killed in Texas before Clerk Monica Wallace read announcements on free COVID-19 home test kits, the June 1 homestead property tax relief deadline, the end of pandemic SNAP/EBT emergency allotments, a library bookmark contest, and foster care recruitment. Commissioner Nimasheena Burns added an announcement that Fidelity Investments extended its May 15 application deadline for its $250 million last-dollar scholarship program for African American and Hispanic students in Durham and four other NC cities.

agenda_items.title: Approval of April 10, 2023 Regular Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no edits requested, the board moved, seconded, and unanimously voted 5-0 by voice vote to approve the April 10, 2023 regular session minutes.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations: Resilient and Thriving Communities Week (23-0308) and Older Americans Month (23-0309)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Nimasheena Burns read resolution 23-0308 proclaiming April 29–May 6, 2023 as Resilient and Thriving Communities Week, accepted by Public Health Adverse Childhood Experiences and Resilience Coordinator Jess Bosquette, with commissioners highlighting the Surgeon General's advisory on youth loneliness and upcoming joint school board mental health discussions. Commissioner Heidi Carter then read proclamation 23-0309 recognizing May 2023 as Older Americans Month in coordination with the Department of Social Services.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Updated Water and Sewer System Development Fees (SDF)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle gap in the digest, rate consultants and staff presented the five-year update to Durham County's System Development Fees, noting the county had been dramatically undercharging relative to calculated full-cost-recovery fees needed to support capital projects. Chair Howerton opened and closed the public hearing with no speakers signed up in person or on Zoom, and staff confirmed no separate vote was needed as the revised fees would be included in the upcoming budget adoption.

agenda_items.title: Other Business: Management Advisory Group (MAG) Compensation Study and Proposed Pay Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief HR Officer Kathy Everett-Perry introduced MAG consultant Russell Campbell, who presented the compensation study and pay plan affecting 1,876 county employees, recommending movement to the 75th market percentile, a 7% general salary increase, pay-for-performance adjustments, and a $19.22/hour living wage floor indexed annually to the Consumer Price Index. Commissioners welcomed the $19.22 living wage and clear compensation policies, noted existing hard-to-fill sign-on bonuses for detention officers, EMS technicians, and youth home counselors, and deferred deeper discussion to the upcoming budget work sessions.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2023-05-01 9:00 AM - Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 1, 2023 Work Session chaired by Brenda A. Howerton, the Durham Board of County Commissioners heard public comments on affordable housing funding, agricultural stormwater fee burdens, acquisition of the Carver Creek apartments (backed by the Homeless Services Advisory Committee and Community Empowerment Fund), Falls Lake cleanup costs, and widespread community opposition to the SCAD private zoning text amendment from the InterNeighborhood Council, Leesville Road Coalition, and residents, before reviewing consent items including the FY24 Planning Work Program (23-0291) and a $1,338,298.48 GO bond reallocation to Northern High School (23-0293). Following a middle portion omitted in the transcript digest, commissioners reviewed the Final Recommended Durham County Transit Plan and FY24 Transit Work Program—discussing bus-stop accessibility acceleration from 25 to 75 stops per year, North Durham route delays from driver shortages, a $1.5 million FY24 funding reduction, an $18.5 million financial model gap, fare-free transit transitions, and a May 8 public hearing—before entering closed session under Item 23-0320 to consult with County Attorney Andrews regarding Wendell Davis v. Durham County. Returning to open session after court-ordered mediation produced a tentative settlement of all claims in Wendell Davis v. Durham County, the board approved the settlement in a 3-1 split voice vote (3 Ayes, 1 Nay, 1 seated member absent or not voting); because the vote was taken by voice without a roll call, the transcript did not identify which individual commissioners on the seated board (Brenda A. Howerton, Wendy Jacobs, Nida Allam, Nimasheena Burns, and Heidi Carter) cast the three Ayes versus the single Nay.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Public Charge
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton called the May 1, 2023 Work Session to order and read the public charge calling on board members and citizens to maintain courteous, respectful conduct. She then outlined the three-minute public comment procedure and called the first signed-up speaker.

agenda_items.title: Citizens' Comments (Carver Creek Affordable Housing, Agricultural Stormwater Fees, Watershed Costs, and SCAD)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speakers including Sheldon Mitchell, Captain Helen Trip (via written Homeless Services Advisory Committee letter), and Community Empowerment Fund Executive Director Donna Carrington urged commissioners to fund the acquisition of Carver Creek for multifamily permanent supportive housing. A local farmer warned that stormwater fees without agricultural BMP credits threaten farms, and another speaker questioned county water governance while citing $17 million in 2021 stream cleanups and $2.5 million budgeted for a Falls Lake algae scrubber. Multiple speakers—including a Leesville Road Coalition co-founder citing an InterNeighborhood Council resolution and Sherry Zand-Rosenthal—urged postponing or rejecting the SCAD private text amendment until the new Comprehensive Plan is adopted.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review (FY24 Planning Work Program 23-0291 and DPS GO Bond Amendment 23-0293)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Manager began presenting consent items, starting with Item 23-0291 (City-County Planning Department FY24 Work Program), on which a commissioner followed up on a Joint City-County Planning Committee funding concern and staff committed to bringing back a plan. Item 23-0293 covered Capital Project Amendments 23CPA00023 and 23CPA00021 reducing four DPS capital projects by $1,338,298.48 in 2016 General Obligation Bond funds and increasing the Northern High School replacement project (5910SH239) by $1,338,298.48, before a middle gap in the transcript.

agenda_items.title: FY24 Transit Work Program and Final Recommended Durham County Transit Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle gap in the transcript digest, staff (including Katherine) discussed scaling bus stop upgrades from 20–25 to 75 per year, reallocating the delayed North Durham Duke Regional-to-Duke route due to bus driver shortages, expanding 15- and 30-minute route frequencies, and launching a public accountability tracker. Commissioners and staff reviewed a $1.5 million FY24 funding reduction, an $18.5 million financial model shortfall in the Final Recommended Durham County Transit Plan, higher-than-projected sales tax receipts, fare-free transit plans (City funding outside transit plan dollars and GoTriangle low-income fare options), and Village Transit Center / East Durham Crosstown connections ahead of a May 8 public hearing and June work-program adoption.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session: Wendell Davis v. Durham County (Item 23-0320)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The chair read Item 23-0320 requesting closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to preserve attorney-client privilege in the matter of Wendell Davis v. Durham County. A motion to enter closed session was moved, properly seconded, and approved by voice vote at 06:19:06.

agenda_items.title: Open Session Settlement Vote: Wendell Davis v. Durham County and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Returning to open session at 07:02:05, County Attorney Andrews announced that court-ordered mediation the prior Thursday had produced a tentative settlement of all claims in Wendell Davis v. Durham County subject to board approval. A commissioner moved to authorize settling the lawsuit and resolving all related open matters and disputes, which was seconded and approved 3-1 by voice vote at 07:05:05 (individual Aye/Nay voters were not named in the voice vote), after which the meeting adjourned.

meetings.title: BOCC - April 24, 2023 - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 24, 2023 Regular Session, Chair Brenda A. Howerton welcomed new Department of Social Services Director Maggie Cveticanin and the board approved the April 3 work session minutes (5-0) and proclaimed April 30 as National Therapy Animal Day. Commissioners unanimously approved (5-0) the consent agenda—including 24 ARPA nonprofit contracts out of the $10.3 million allocation—while briefly pulling item 23-0277 so Commissioner Heidi Carter could highlight the Community Child Protection Team's preventable safe-sleep recommendations. The board also reviewed an Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs) and trauma-informed policy presentation and announced multiple board and commission ballot appointments while deferring a Juvenile Crime Prevention Council citizen seat for additional applicants.

agenda_items.title: Community Announcements and Introduction of New DSS Director
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk Monica Wallace read community announcements including Public Health COVID-19 vaccine walk-in hours, the April 26 Local Reentry Council Resource Fair, the Durham Dementia Community Event, the Carolina Flyers home opener, and open 2023-24 Durham Pre-K applications. Chair Brenda A. Howerton also welcomed new Department of Social Services (DSS) Director Maggie Cveticanin during her second week on the job.

agenda_items.title: Approval of April 3, 2023 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no edits or corrections proposed, the board moved, seconded, and approved the April 3, 2023 work session minutes by a 5-0 voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Item: National Therapy Animal Day Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Wendy Jacobs read a proclamation declaring April 30, 2023 as National Therapy Animal Day in Durham County, accepted by a Pet Partners therapy animal volunteer, with commissioners praising therapy animals' stress-relief benefits for students and youth.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (23-0130 to 23-0300), Pulled Item 23-0277, and ARPA Nonprofit Contracts Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board approved all consent agenda items except 23-0277 on a 5-0 vote, allowing Commissioner Heidi Carter to highlight the Community Child Protection Team's report on preventable infant deaths and urge administrative review of safe-sleep campaign recommendations ahead of the budget. Later at 02:27:13, County Manager Dr. Sowell highlighted that the consent agenda included 24 nonprofit contracts from the $10.3 million ARPA allocation across seven focus areas and noted staff were updating a public county webpage tracking funded outside organizations.

agenda_items.title: Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs), Trauma-Informed Policy, and Environmental Justice Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle gap in the digest, commissioners responded to a presentation from Jess Bosquette and Rod on adverse childhood experiences, cultural and climate trauma, and racial equity. Commissioners urged translating the framework into actionable budget and policy measures—including trauma-informed and racial-equity budget screening, youth programs, universal basic income concepts, and monitoring PFAS environmental impacts—while staff noted a formal resolution would return in coming weeks.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Attorney announced ballot appointments to the Durham County Hospital Corporation Board of Trustees (Whitney Stanley and Charles Cooperberg), Duke Regional Medical Staff (Philip Bong), Lincoln Community Health Center (Federico Manion), Duke Regional Physicians (Michelle L. Al-Hegelan), and the Historic Preservation Commission (Kenneth Webb). Because no candidate received a board majority for a Juvenile Crime Prevention Council citizen seat, the board deferred that appointment to the following month to gather more applicants.

meetings.title: BOCC - April 10, 2023 - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: Opening the April 10, 2023 Regular Session after closed session, the board unanimously authorized staff to sign the Supplemental Agreement for Additional Funds (SAAF) and five National Opioid Settlement participation agreements (CVS, Walgreens, Walmart, Allergan, and Teva) and formally exited closed session. Commissioners approved the March 27 minutes (5-0), issued proclamations for Second Chance Month and National County Government Month, and honored Patrick Hannah for his 2015–2023 service and chairmanship on the Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority board. The board then unanimously approved a 43-item consent agenda and, following a public hearing with no speakers, voted 5-0 to adopt the revised County Stormwater Ordinance (Item 22-0216) incentivizing Low Impact Development to meet May 1 state watershed deadlines.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Action: National Opioid Settlement (SAAF and Five Participation Agreements)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Allen Andrews reported that in closed session the board agreed to participate in the Supplemental Agreement for Additional Funds (SAAF) and five national opioid litigation agreements with CVS, Walgreens, Walmart, Allergan, and Teva. In open session, commissioners unanimously approved a motion (seconded by Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs) authorizing staff as signatory and adopting the conforming resolution, followed by a formal motion to exit closed session.

agenda_items.title: Announcements and Approval of March 27, 2023 Regular Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff read announcements on county summer/management internships and fellowships, Welcome Babies breastfeeding support classes, and Partnership for a Healthy Durham's 2022 Community Health Assessment presentation. After Commissioner Nida Allam reminded the chair to take up the minutes, the board unanimously voted 5-0 to approve the March 27, 2023 regular session minutes.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Resolutions: Second Chance Month, Patrick Hannah (RDU), and County Government Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Nida Allam read a proclamation declaring April 2023 as Second Chance Month, accepted by Criminal Justice Resource Center Assistant Director Rashana Parker (with Director Gudrun Parmer), noting more than 400 residents returning from prison and nearly 6,600 jail entries annually alongside an April calendar of reentry events. Later, the board presented a resolution honoring Patrick Hannah for his 2015–2023 service and chairmanship on the Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority board, and Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs read a proclamation declaring April 2023 as National County Government Month.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (43 Items)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presented the 43-item consent agenda and asked if any commissioner wished to pull an item for separate discussion. Hearing no requests, the board moved, seconded (by Commissioner Nimasheena Burns), and unanimously approved all 43 consent items.

agenda_items.title: Item 22-0216: Public Hearing and Adoption of Revised County Stormwater Ordinance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Stormwater and Erosion Control Division Manager Ryan Eaves and Stormwater Manager McKenzie Bradshaw presented the revised County Stormwater Ordinance, reorganizing rules for clarity and fulfilling state Neuse/Falls/Jordan watershed management requirements ahead of a May 1 deadline. Answering Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs, Eaves explained the update incentivizes Low Impact Development (LID) and green infrastructure by exempting qualifying low-impact designs from additional stormwater control measure calculations; after a public hearing with no speakers, the board voted 5-0 to adopt the ordinance.

votes.item_title: Authorize Staff Signatory for SAAF and Five National Opioid Settlement Participation Agreements
votes.notes: Mover was not identified by name in the audio transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: County Attorney Allen Andrews summarized the closed-session agreement to participate in the Supplemental Agreement for Additional Funds (SAAF) and five related opioid settlement participation agreements with CVS, Walgreens, Walmart, Allergan, and Teva. A commissioner moved to authorize staff as signatory on behalf of the board in those five matters and adopt the conforming resolution, Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs seconded, and the motion passed unanimously.

meetings.title: BOCC - Work Session for April 3, 2023
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the April 3, 2023 Board of County Commissioners work session, which opened with public comments urging $1.875 million in ARPA funding for an extremely low-income rental assistance guaranteed income pilot and updating the Board on City Council review of the Simplifying Codes for Affordable Development (SCAD) text amendments. Commissioners reviewed 19 consent agenda items—highlighting $473,659 in ARPA water assistance for DSS, $875,000 in LOBs contingency for the 500 East Main Street parking deck, $145,520 for detention center security upgrades, and $300,800 for provider selection at the 300 East Main Street childcare center—and received a Criminal Justice Resource Center detention services presentation noting that 47% of jail bookings are referred to mental health services. The Board suspended the rules to approve two Cooperative Extension general fund balance appropriations and food-security contracts: $28,257.57 with Farmer Foodshare for the Double Bucks program (5-0) and $503,795.56 with the Interfaith Food Shuttle (4-0). Following a closed session on personnel matters, the Board voted 4-0 in open session to appoint Theresa Harrison as Interim Tax Administrator effective immediately.

agenda_items.title: Public Charge and Citizens' Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton read the public charge and opened 30 minutes of citizens' comments. James of Aura (Coalition for Affordable Housing and Transit) urged the Board to allocate $1.875 million in remaining ARPA funds for a $600-per-month rental assistance guaranteed income pilot for extremely low-income renters facing eviction. James Chavis criticized unreturned follow-up from July 2022, Bob Chapman updated the Board that City Council requested an item-by-item Planning Department analysis of SCAD text amendments ahead of a May 1 public hearing before coming to the BOCC, and a fourth speaker thanked the Board for supporting equity framework work, My Brother's Keeper, and Community Intervention and Support Services.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review (DSS Water Assistance, 500 E. Main Parking Deck, Jail Security, and 300 E. Main Childcare)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Dr. Kimberly Sowell introduced the 19-item consent agenda, including Item 23-0094 (23BCC0082 recognizing $473,659 in federal ARPA Low-Income Household Water Assistance funds for DSS), Item 23-0192 (23CPA0020 appropriating $875,000 in future taxable LOBs for the 500 East Main Street parking deck contingency with ZOM Living up to $32,701,100), Item 23-0193 ($145,520 Sheriff's Office contract with JNA Engineering LLC for detention center electric security replacement), and Item 23-0197 (23BCC0077 appropriating $300,800 for a contract with Child Care Services Association for the 300 East Main Street pre-K/childcare center). Commissioners Wendy Jacobs and Chair Brenda A. Howerton highlighted the county's second major downtown childcare investment, noting local childcare deserts and support for low-income downtown workers.

agenda_items.title: Item 23-0173: Criminal Justice Resource Center (CJRC) Detention Services Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CJRC staff and Kelly Aknazic briefed the Board on intake screening, substance use disorder medication verification, discharge planning, and mental health referrals inside the detention center, reporting that 47% of booked individuals were referred to mental health services last year. Staff also reviewed Medicaid sign-ups, MacArthur Foundation-supported risk assessment work, jail bed days saved, and daily jail operating costs rising from $98.73 to $199.50 in FY21. Commissioners asked about tracking mental-health-related recidivism and pursuing outside philanthropic grants such as MacKenzie Scott's open call.

agenda_items.title: Item 23-0225: Budget Ordinance Amendment 23BCC0083 (Farmer Foodshare Double Bucks Contract)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Food Security Coordinator Mary Oxendine and Cooperative Extension presented Budget Ordinance Amendment 23BCC0083 to appropriate $28,257.57 in general fund balance for a contract with Farmer Foodshare supporting the Durham County Double Bucks program. After brief commissioner questions, the Board voted 4-0 to suspend the rules and then voted 5-0 to approve the budget amendment and contract.

agenda_items.title: Item 23-0227: Budget Ordinance Amendment 23BCC0080 (Interfaith Food Shuttle Contract)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented Budget Ordinance Amendment 23BCC0080 to appropriate $503,795.56 in general fund balance and approve a contract with the Interfaith Food Shuttle to provide food to Durham County residents seeking food assistance. One commissioner remarked that it felt as though the Board was whittling down its fund balance, and staff assured the Board that the county remained in a solid fiscal position. The Board voted 4-0 to suspend the rules and 4-0 to approve the appropriation and contract.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Appointment of Interim Tax Administrator
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a commissioner request to introduce new County Manager team members at a future meeting, the Board voted to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) to consider personnel qualifications and appointment. Returning to open session at 06:27:27, the Board voted 4-0 to appoint Theresa Harrison as Interim Tax Administrator effective immediately.
