meetings.title: BOCC - March 27, 2023 - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the March 27, 2023 regular session, opening with her annual State of the County Address reviewing the $793.56 million FY2023 budget, unchanged $0.7222 tax rate, $177.15 million Durham Public Schools funding, Pre-K and Durham Tech investments, economic development such as Kempower's 360+ jobs, and the upcoming FY2024 budget calendar. Commissioners also reviewed a resolution supporting universal no-cost school meals in the state budget and unanimously approved five consent agenda items (5-0 for the main consent slate and 5-0 for the pulled Environmental Affairs Board report, Item 23-0195, after public comment). During boards and commissions appointments, Commissioner Nida Allam moved to extend the application period for the Raleigh-Durham (RDU) Airport Authority Board unless candidates achieved majority support on the ballot, which passed 4-1; one RDU vacancy was filled by ballot while the second seat was held open for re-advertisement. After a closed session on personnel and litigation, the Board returned to open session and voted 5-0 to approve a $170,000 starting salary for new DSS Director Maggie Cveticanin.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Public Charge, and Pledge of Allegiance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton called the March 27, 2023 Board of County Commissioners regular session to order and read the public charge. She asked Commissioner Nida Allam to lead the Pledge of Allegiance.

agenda_items.title: Item 23-0210: 2023 State of the County Address
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton delivered the 2023 State of the County Address, recognizing fellow commissioners, retired department heads Ben Rose and Willie Darby, late County Attorney Lowell Siler, and award-winning departments including Budget, Elections, Public Health, EMS, and Social Services. She highlighted the Hayti Reborn interlocal agreement, maternal health initiatives, Kempower's 360+ new jobs, and the $793,563,860 FY2023 budget ($0.7222 tax rate, $177.15 million for DPS, $6.4 million for Pre-K, and $9.74 million for Durham Tech). Chair Howerton closed by noting that the Manager's recommended FY2024 budget would be presented on May 8 with a public hearing on May 22.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Supporting Universal No-Cost School Meals in the State Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed a March 27 resolution urging the North Carolina General Assembly to fund universal free breakfast and lunch for all public school students in the state budget. Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs and commissioners supported sharing the signed resolution with the local legislative delegation and the Durham Public Schools Board of Education, and Clerk Monica Wallace confirmed it would be circulated for signatures and emailed out the next morning.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / No vote (formal vote truncated in digest)

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda and Item 23-0195 (Environmental Affairs Board Report)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Because one resident signed up to speak on Item 23-0195 (Environmental Affairs Board report), the Board voted 5-0 to approve the remaining four consent agenda items first. Resident Gwen Silver then offered public comments on Item 23-0195, after which the Board voted 5-0 to approve the EAB report with a commitment to relay her input to the EAB chair.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments and RDU Airport Authority Application Extension
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Before ballot results were announced, Commissioner Nida Allam moved (seconded) to extend the application period for the two Raleigh-Durham (RDU) Airport Authority vacancies to encourage more applicants, barring any candidate who received a majority on the current ballot; following procedural clarification from the clerk, the motion passed 4-1. The attorney then read the ballot results appointing Harold Hubbard (Boxing and Wrestling Commission), Sabrina Delaney (City-County Appearance Commission), Missina Redish (Women's Commission), Jonathan Leech (Memorial Stadium Authority), and Yesenia Polanco-Gautam to one RDU Airport Authority seat, while holding open and re-advertising the second RDU seat because the remaining candidates received two votes and one vote.
agenda_items.vote_summary: RDU extension motion passed 4-1; ballot appointments announced

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Appointment/Salary Approval for New DSS Director
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted to enter closed session pursuant to G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) (personnel) and G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with legal counsel regarding Hermana Miles Bumpass, Administratrix, and Jerry Jerome Bumpass, Jr. v. Clarence F. Birkhead. Returning to open session at 02:35:05, the Board voted 5-0 to approve a $170,000 starting salary for new Department of Social Services Director Maggie Cveticanin.

votes.item_title: Item 23-0195: Environmental Affairs Board (EAB) Report
votes.discussion_detail: Following public comment from Gwen Silver on Item 23-0195, a commissioner moved to approve the EAB report with the understanding that she would relay the speaker's request to the EAB chair for input. After a second, the motion passed 5-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Motion to Extend Application Period for RDU Airport Authority Board Vacancies (Barring Majority Ballot Winners)
votes.notes: Chair announced 4-1 by voice vote; the single dissenting commissioner was not identified by name on the record.
votes.discussion_detail: Commissioner Nida Allam moved to extend the application period for the two RDU Airport Authority Board vacancies to encourage more applicants, unless a candidate received majority support on the current ballot. After clarifying that balloting had occurred but results had not yet been announced, the Board voted 4-1 to approve the extension; as a result, one majority candidate was appointed and the second seat was re-advertised.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (Personnel and Litigation: Bumpass v. Birkhead)
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Brenda A. Howerton read the statutory citations under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) for personnel and G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) for attorney-client consultation in Bumpass v. Birkhead. The motion was seconded and passed by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of $170,000 Starting Salary for New DSS Director Maggie Cveticanin
votes.notes: Surname transcribed phonetically in ASR as 'side feed, Ted casting / Saviticin'.
votes.discussion_detail: Upon returning from closed session, the Board considered a motion to approve a starting salary of $170,000 for new Department of Social Services Director Maggie Cveticanin. The motion was moved, seconded, and passed 5-0 by voice vote.

disagreements.issue: Extending Application Period for RDU Airport Authority Board Appointments
disagreements.summary: Commissioners split 4-1 on Commissioner Nida Allam's motion to reopen and extend the application window for any RDU Airport Authority Board vacancy that did not receive majority support on the night's ballot, following procedural clarification over acting after ballots were cast.
disagreements.side_a_position: Extend the application period for any RDU Airport Authority seat without a majority ballot winner to broaden the applicant pool.
side_a_arguments: Encourages more applicants to seek appointment to the RDU Airport Authority Board.
Still allows a candidate who wins a majority of Board votes on the current ballot to be appointed immediately while extending only the unfilled seat.
disagreements.side_b_position: Opposed extending the application window (one dissenting vote; procedural concern raised about intervening before ballot results were read).
side_b_arguments: Procedural clarification noted that commissioners had already submitted ballots and were awaiting the clerk's announcement of the results.
disagreements.resolution: Motion passed 4-1; Yesenia Polanco-Gautam was appointed to the first vacancy by majority ballot vote, and the second vacancy was held open for re-advertisement.

meetings.title: BOCC - March 13, 2023 - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the March 13, 2023 regular session, which approved the February 27, 2023 regular session minutes and presented ceremonial recognitions for Year of the Trail, Women's History Month, and retiring 4th District U.S. Congressman David E. Price. Following a public hearing discussion on a general rezoning along Falls/Jordan from Residential Rural to Commercial General—where one commissioner voiced reservations about the breadth of the Commercial General district under state general-rezoning rules—the Board voted to adopt the rezoning ordinance and passed the statutory consistency statement 5-0. Under Item 23-0198, the Board held a public hearing with no speakers and voted 5-0 to adopt the final approving resolution for up to $235 million in Limited Obligation Bonds (Series 2023A and 2023B) to convert prior short-term draw financing into long-term fixed-rate debt. The meeting concluded with Item 23-0143, an informational Department of Social Services briefing on updated placement protocols for medically complex children aimed at avoiding needless institutionalization.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, Pledge, Announcements, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton called the meeting to order, read the public charge, and asked for the Pledge of Allegiance. Clerk Monica Wallace read community announcements covering walk-in COVID-19 vaccination hours, Durham Pre-K enrollment events, a March 20 public input session on Durham County's $11.6 million in National Opioid Settlement funds over 18 years, the Emily K Center College Expo, and AARP Tax-Aide. The Board then voted to approve the February 27, 2023 regular session minutes.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: Year of the Trail, Resolution Honoring Congressman David E. Price, and Women's History Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board presented Item 23-0183 proclaiming Year of the Trail and promoting local Creek Week and trail events, followed by Item 23-0189 honoring the retirement of U.S. Representative David E. Price for his decades of service in Congress, appropriations leadership, and advocacy for RTP and Durham's life sciences sector. Congressman Price and commissioners exchanged remarks reflecting on his constituent engagement, and the Board later read a Women's History Month recognition.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: General Rezoning on Falls/Jordan (Residential Rural to Commercial General)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: During public hearing deliberation on a general rezoning on Falls/Jordan from Residential Rural to Commercial General, staff clarified that state statute prohibits attaching use conditions to a general rezoning and explained that unlike a City annexation (which triggers City Code cost-benefit and service-operation analyses), a county general rezoning only changes the zoning district. A commissioner expressed unease over how broad the Commercial General district is while still indicating support. The Board adopted the rezoning ordinance and passed the N.C.G.S. 160D-605 consistency statement 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 23-0198: Public Hearing and Final Resolution for Not-to-Exceed $235 Million Limited Obligation Bonds (Series 2023A and 2023B)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance staff presented the final resolution for up to $235 million in Limited Obligation Bonds (Series 2023A and 2023B), continuing the financing calendar initiated on February 27 to convert draw-program debt into long-term fixed-rate financing via a supplemental installment contract amendment. After voting to open and close the public hearing with no speakers signed up, the Board voted 5-0 to adopt the final approving resolution.

agenda_items.title: Item 23-0143: Department of Social Services Update on Placement Protocols for Medically Complex Children
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DSS staff presented updated placement protocols and guidelines intended to ensure children with medically complex needs are cared for in home settings rather than needlessly institutionalized. A resident noted submitting a public records request regarding a connected lawsuit settlement agreement and questioned why litigation was not noted on the agenda. Commissioners discussed state DHHS policy constraints, Alliance Health coordination for therapeutic needs, hospital referral workflows, and DSS staff sacrifices during COVID-19.

meetings.title: BOCC - Work Session for March 6, 2023
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the March 6, 2023 Board of County Commissioners work session, enforcing strict time limits to move through a packed agenda. After hearing citizen comment from Sharon Hunter regarding a court restitution refund, the Board reviewed consent agenda items covering Public Health grants, a $250,000 general fund balance appropriation for out-of-county Youth Home placements, a $141,462 Sheriff's Office detention center body scanner, IT contracts, Criminal Justice Resource Center (CJRC) local reentry grants, and Phase 2 of the Alston Glenn farm conservation easement. Later in the session, commissioners questioned City Transportation and GoDurham staff on transit corridor budgets, bus stop maintenance accountability, fare-free transit continuity, and integrating affordable housing at Durham Station. The meeting concluded with discussions on a proposed $10 million County ARPA contribution toward four joint affordable housing projects, a Permanent Supportive Housing campus concept, and a request for an emergency management briefing on freight rail safety.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, and Citizens' Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton opened the work session, read the public charge, and asked commissioners and presenters to adhere to a strict three-minute question limit due to the packed agenda. Resident Sharon Hunter spoke during public comment regarding dismissed 2020 criminal charges involving her son's mental health status and difficulties obtaining a court restitution refund from bookkeeping.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review (Public Health, Youth Home, Sheriff's Office, IT, CJRC, and Farmland Preservation)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Dr. Kimberly Sowell walked through consent agenda items including five Public Health budget amendments (23-0044, 23-0045, 23-0046, 23-0048, and 23-0144), a $250,000 appropriation for Durham Youth Home out-of-county placements (23-0098), a $141,462 detention center body scanner contract with Tech 84 Inc., a $300,000 roofing project reduction (23-0109), the 2022 BPAC annual report (23-0113), IT contracts (Westaff, Info-Tech, Carahsoft, and SHI Microsoft licensing), CJRC Local Reentry Council grants (23-0148 and 23-0151, part of a $600,000+ City-County ARPA reentry housing collaboration), and a $142,500 transfer for Phase 2 of the Alston Glenn farm conservation easement (23-0156). Commissioners asked follow-up questions on communicable disease reporting, the mobile unit plan, Youth Home placement frustration, and quarterly CJRC data reports.

agenda_items.title: City Transportation and GoDurham Transit Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Transportation and GoDurham transit staff answered commissioner questions regarding budgets for the Fayetteville and Holloway transit corridors, the absence of a standalone city transit plan equivalent to the County Transit Plan (relying instead on the CIP, Bike+Walk plan, and GoTriangle's Short-Range Transit Plan update), and why affordable housing was not included in the current Durham Station renovation design. Staff also explained new operator contract tiers for bus stop trash and shelter maintenance, noted City Council commitment to fare-free bus service pending the City Manager's budget, and discussed tracking legacy versus transit-tax expansion metrics.

agenda_items.title: Joint City-County Affordable Housing ARPA Investment, Permanent Supportive Housing Campus, and Freight Rail Safety Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reviewed county housing partnerships, emergency rental assistance, and a proposal for the County to contribute $10 million in federal/ARPA funds alongside the City so four affordable housing projects could move forward without funding shortfalls. Gudrun Parmer also previewed a Permanent Supportive Housing campus concept modeled on Wake County and Charlotte (noting Charlotte data showing average emergency room bills dropping from $40,000 to $12,000 for housed residents) to gauge Board interest ahead of late March or April. Before concluding, a commissioner requested a future emergency management briefing on Durham's safety plan for freight rail traffic following a second Norfolk Southern accident.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners - Annual Budget Retreat Day 2 - March 1, 2023
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton opened Day 2 of the Board of County Commissioners Annual Budget Retreat on March 1, 2023, with Commissioner Nida Allam participating remotely via Zoom. HR and Budget staff reviewed the county's living wage policy and recommended a 9% increase from $16.90 to $18.40 per hour while warning against jumping to $23–$24 per hour or immediately extending the floor to all Durham Public Schools (DPS) employees due to salary compression and property tax pressures alongside the recently passed school bond. DSS staff then presented a SWOT analysis and FY23 utilization review of the Longtime Homeowners Relief Fund—projecting roughly $330,000 in spending out of its $1.25 million budget and floating a right-sized FY24 split—before commissioners closed the retreat by outlining FY24 budget priorities including DPS pay parity, a Durham Tech workforce pipeline, City-County housing and service-overlap coordination, reproductive care, immigrant services, Hayti Reborn, transit tax needs, and Veteran Services outreach.

agenda_items.title: Day 2 Opening and Agenda Overview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton welcomed commissioners to Day 2 of the budget retreat and acknowledged Commissioner Nida Allam joining via Zoom. County Manager Dr. Kimberly Sowell outlined the half-day agenda covering living wage options, the Longtime Homeowners Relief Fund, a Board of Elections space update, and Board budget priority discussions.

agenda_items.title: Living Wage Policy Update and DPS Employee Compensation Tradeoffs
agenda_items.discussion_summary: HR and Budget staff presented on the county's living wage policy (currently 7.5% above federal poverty guidelines, or $32,250 annually) and recommended raising the hourly floor by 9% from $16.90 to $18.40 without requesting a formal vote at the retreat. Staff cautioned that $23–$24 per hour proposals or extending the county wage floor to all DPS employees would impose exorbitant costs and pay compression alongside DPS's $10.8 million request and upcoming debt service from the historic school bond (potentially up to a 2.5-cent tax impact). Commissioners asked about mandatory overtime in vacant departments and total compensation equity including childcare and education benefits.

agenda_items.title: Longtime Homeowners Relief Fund (LTHP) Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DSS staff presented a SWOT analysis identifying foreclosure and gentrification as key threats and reported FY23 spending of approximately $302,000 (projected ~$330,000 with 20–25 pending applications) out of the $1.25 million joint budget ($750,000 County and $500,000 City via ILA), which also funded three administrative support positions. Staff noted discussions with the DSS board about potentially right-sizing the FY24 budget (such as halving allocations to $325,000 County and $250,000 City) while preserving room for program growth.

agenda_items.title: Commissioner FY24 Budget Priorities and Veteran Services Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners articulated individual budget priorities, including support for the Coalition for Affordable Housing and Transit's rental assistance proposal, a farm/supportive housing campus, and maximizing fund balance and grants. Commissioner Nida Allam advocated for extending the $18.40 wage increase to DPS staff, creating a Durham Tech workforce pipeline for EMS/public health/fire marshal vacancies, funding City-managed joint housing projects, studying City-County service overlap, creating a reproductive care fund, reviewing immigrant/refugee Welcome Center needs, and praising the new grant coordinator role. Other commissioners lifted up Hayti Reborn, mental health, the 2050 transportation plan's 1.5-cent transit sales tax, and Veteran Services Director Lois urged the Board to fund staffing and a $35,000 outreach vehicle.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners - Annual Budget Retreat Day 1 - February 28, 2023
meetings.executive_summary: On Day 1 of the Board of County Commissioners Annual Budget Retreat on February 28, 2023, County Manager Dr. Kimberly Sowell framed the FY23–24 budget development process and asked commissioners to narrow their November policy retreat priorities to their top three goals. Finance and Budget staff briefed the Board on the county's interest rate swap (maturing March 1, 2031, retained per financial advisor analysis to help offset over $60 million in annual debt service), 13 consecutive years of exceeding 100% of budgeted revenues, and peer-county financial comparisons against Mecklenburg, Wake, Guilford, Forsyth, and Orange counties. The Board also reviewed Public Health and maternal health funding distinctions between one-time ARPA items and recurring costs—with a request for inclusive outreach language and follow-up on a United Way-facilitated doula consortium—before holding an extensive briefing on the new Youth Home and Juvenile Assessment Center. Youth Home leadership presented a three-tier phased bed opening plan (16–36 beds) and warned of a 52% to 57% staffing vacancy rate, calling for a $50,000–$52,000 starting salary and overtime reforms ahead of opening.

agenda_items.title: Budget Retreat Day 1 Framing and Priority Narrowing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Dr. Kimberly Sowell outlined the two-day retreat agenda, noting Day 1 financial updates, ARPA reviews, and a Youth Home briefing, followed by Day 2 discussions on living wage ($23–$24/hour proposals alongside compensation study work), the Longtime Homeowners Relief Fund, and relocating the Board of Elections to the former Shops at Hope Valley. She asked commissioners to narrow their November policy retreat list down to three top priorities to guide FY24 budget drafting.

agenda_items.title: Financial Highlights, Interest Rate Swap Analysis, and Peer County Comparisons
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance staff reported that despite Federal Reserve interest rate volatility, financial advisors determined Durham County should remain in its interest rate swap through its March 1, 2031 maturity, using swap fund balance to help cover over $60 million in annual debt service and stabilize the property tax rate. Staff also noted 13 straight years of collecting over 100% of budgeted revenues (109.8% revenues vs. 92.86% expenditures in FY21) and compared Durham's budget execution and fund balance growth against peer North Carolina counties, with a commissioner requesting bond-rating columns be added.

agenda_items.title: Public Health, ARPA Eligibility, and Maternal Health Outreach
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff discussed aligning one-time Public Health items with ARPA eligibility while evaluating recurring costs through the regular budget process. Commissioners inquired about a follow-up from community doula organizations and a United Way-facilitated doula consortium, and requested that county maternal health materials use inclusive language recognizing non-binary and trans birthing people.

agenda_items.title: Youth Home and Juvenile Assessment Center Phased Budget and Staffing Crisis
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Angela Nunn and Gudrun Parmer presented a phased operating model for the new Youth Home and Juvenile Assessment Center—designed to divert at-risk and court-involved youth—beginning with Priority 1 (16–24 beds plus 3 FTEs for the assessment center and 4.3 administrative FTEs) and scaling to 36 beds at Priority 3 with roughly $720,000 in conservative projected revenues. Discussion centered on acute recruitment challenges, with Nunn reporting a 52% vacancy rate updated during the session to 57%, prompting calls for a $50,000–$52,000 starting salary, pay compression relief, and overtime-rule adjustments before opening.

agenda_items.title: Day 1 Wrap-Up and Day 2 Schedule Confirmation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Manager Sowell and commissioners confirmed Day 2 topics, encouraged commissioners to email budget questions overnight to Budget Director Keith Lane, and agreed to reserve Board priority discussion time at the end of Day 2 (9:00 AM–12:00 PM with box lunches available if extended).

meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the February 27, 2023 regular session, beginning with an hour-long closed session regarding confidential records and Case No. 23-CVS-664 (Fulton and General Woods v. Sarah Bradshaw) before returning with no action. Darby. In legislative action, the Board unanimously adopted Unified Development Ordinance amendments (Articles 12 and 15) strengthening sedimentation and erosion control protections and enforcement for Southeast Durham's Triassic soils along with the statutory consistency statement, and passed an amended motion under Item 23-0119 authorizing the County Manager to execute a $290,000 performance agreement with Kempower. Finally, the Board voted 5-0 on Item 23-0117 to adopt the initial resolution for up to $235 million in Limited Obligation Bonds (Series 2023A and 2023B) and call a March 13 public hearing, and announced ballot appointments to six county boards and commissions.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Confidential Records and Case No. 23-CVS-664)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(1) (Chapter 132 confidential records) and G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with legal counsel regarding Case No. 23-CVS-664 (Fulton and General Woods v. Sarah Bradshaw). Upon returning to open session at 01:01:40, Chair Howerton stated no action was needed.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (Voice vote; no action upon return)

agenda_items.title: Public Charge, Pledge, Announcements, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton read the public charge, Commissioner Heidi Carter led the Pledge of Allegiance, and Clerk Monica Wallace announced the 2023–24 Durham Youth Leadership Fund grants ($500–$8,000). The Board then voted 5-0 to approve the minutes of the January 3, 2023 and February 6, 2023 meetings.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: Black History Month Youth, Layne Riggs, Women's History Month, and Willie S. Darby
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board hosted Black History Month youth poetry readings, read a proclamation honoring Bahama/Durham County native Layne Riggs for winning the 2022 NASCAR Advance Auto Parts Weekly Series national championship at age 20, and proclaimed Women's History Month 2023. Commissioner Nimasheena Burns then read a resolution honoring retiring former Acting County Attorney Willie S. Darby for 14 years of service across two tenures, followed by remarks from Darby and his family.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendments (Articles 12 and 15 — Sedimentation and Erosion Control)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A resident spoke in support of proposed Unified Development Ordinance amendments protecting Southeast Durham's Triassic soils and strengthening enforcement, thanking Ryan Eaves and Sara Young while raising concerns about developments annexed into the city within the Falls Lake watershed. After closing the public hearing, the Board unanimously adopted the ordinance revising Article 12 (Infrastructure and Public Improvements) and Article 15 (Enforcement) and adopted the N.C.G.S. 160D-605 consistency statement.

agenda_items.title: Item 23-0119: Amended Motion for Kempower Performance Agreement ($290,000)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Nimasheena Burns noted that in an earlier motion on Item 23-0119 she had said 'the county' instead of authorizing the County Manager, and conferred with the clerk to correct the record. Her amended motion authorizing the County Manager to negotiate and execute a $290,000 performance agreement with Kempower passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Item 23-0117: Initial Resolution for Not-to-Exceed $235 Million Limited Obligation Bonds (Series 2023A and 2023B)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance Director Susan Tezai presented the initial resolution authorizing negotiation of an installment financing contract amendment for up to $235 million in Limited Obligation Bonds (converting the 2020/2021 draw program to long-term fixed-rate financing) and setting a March 13, 2023 public hearing. Commissioner Heidi Carter asked whether the action increased obligated debt, which Tezai confirmed reflected long-term issuance of debt obligated under the April 2021 draw program. The Board approved the resolution 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Ballot Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Attorney announced ballot appointment results for six advisory bodies: Takeeba Call (Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee), Darryl Glover (Board of Health optometrist seat), Jeffrey Backelchuk, Deborah Green and Michael Vanpran (Historic Preservation Commission), Libria Stevenson (Juvenile Crime Prevention Council), and Carl Newman (Library Board of Trustees).

votes.discussion_detail: Chair Brenda A. Howerton read the statutory grounds under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(1) and (a)(3) regarding Case No. 23-CVS-664 (Fulton and General Woods v. Sarah Bradshaw). The motion was seconded and approved by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of January 3, 2023 and February 6, 2023 Meeting Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: A commissioner moved to approve the January 3, 2023 and February 6, 2023 work session/regular session minutes as noted; after a second, the motion passed 5-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Ordinance Amending UDO Article 12 (Infrastructure and Public Improvements) and Article 15 (Enforcement)
votes.discussion_detail: After closing the public hearing on UDO sedimentation and erosion control revisions, a commissioner moved to adopt the ordinance amending Articles 12 and 15 of the Unified Development Ordinance. The motion was seconded and passed unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Statement of Consistency Pursuant to N.C.G.S. 160D-605 (UDO Articles 12 and 15)
votes.notes: Confirmed as already voted on by Commissioner Nimasheena Burns at 03:23:25.
votes.discussion_detail: A commissioner moved to adopt the appropriate statement of consistency pursuant to N.C.G.S. 160D-605 for the UDO Articles 12 and 15 amendments; Commissioner Heidi Carter seconded, and the Board approved it by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Item 23-0119: Amended Motion Authorizing County Manager to Execute $290,000 Kempower Performance Agreement
votes.discussion_detail: Commissioner Nimasheena Burns moved to amend the prior motion on Item 23-0119 so that the Board authorized the County Manager to negotiate and execute a $290,000 performance agreement with Kempower (replacing the earlier phrasing). Seconded and approved unanimously by voice vote, superseding the first motion.

votes.item_title: Item 23-0117: Initial Resolution for Not-to-Exceed $235M Limited Obligation Bonds (Series 2023A/2023B) and Call for March 13 Public Hearing
votes.discussion_detail: A commissioner moved to adopt the initial resolution for the not-to-exceed $235 million Limited Obligation Bonds Series 2023A and 2023B, approve the identified financing team, and call a public hearing for March 13, 2023. Seconded and passed 5-0 by voice vote.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners Work Session for Feb. 6, 2023
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the February 6, 2023 work session, opening with acknowledgments of Black History Month, condolences over a recent young man's death, and a ceremonial recognition of Soil and Water Conservation District Supervisor David Harris as statewide Supervisor of the Year. Commissioners reviewed 19 consent agenda items—including DPS lottery capital reallocations, excise tax refund delegation, detention center padded-cell protocols, sewer maintenance contracts, IT renewals, and stormwater/erosion inspector staffing for 280 active sites. After suspending the rules for time-sensitive items, the Board approved a Sheriff's Office IIR grant extension through the end of February (rules suspended 3-0) and Item 23-0077, a letter of support for a General Services EPA grant application. On Item 23-0107, the Board suspended the rules, voted to rescind its January 23 vote on Item 23-0063 (a PERK local-match ILA with the City), and approved a $2 million contract through June 30, 2024 with the National Institute of Minority Economic Development to serve as fiscal agent for the Hayti Reborn Justice Movement.

agenda_items.title: Public Charge, Opening Remarks, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton read the public charge and confirmed no citizens were signed up to speak in person or online. She acknowledged Black History Month and lifted up condolences regarding the recent killing of a young man on his way home, and Clerk Monica Wallace announced that 2023 DCo Cares nonprofit recipient applications were open through February 10.

agenda_items.title: Item 23-0059: Ceremonial Recognition of David Harris (Soil and Water Supervisor of the Year)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Soil and Water staff and Brian Evans, Executive Director of the North Carolina Association of Soil and Water Conservation Districts, recognized David Harris for receiving the statewide 2023 Supervisor of the Year award on January 19, 2023. Commissioners thanked Harris for his leadership on soil health, water quality, education, and farmland preservation.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review (19 Items: DPS Capital, Detention Padded Cells, Utilities, IT, and Erosion Inspection)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Dr. Kimberly Sowell walked through the 19-item consent agenda, including Item 23-0001 (CPA 23PA0012 reallocating Public School Building Capital Fund lottery funds for DPS), Item 23-0029 (excise tax refund delegation), Item 23-0041 ($160,077 Cornerstone Detention Products amendment up to $168,080), Items 23-0047 and 23-0050 (utility/sewer amendments), Item 23-0055 (NCDEQ access at 721 Foster Street), and IT renewals with NWN and SAP. Commissioners asked the Sheriff's Office about monitoring policies for detainees undergoing withdrawal or mental health crisis in padded cells (staff stated policies were being developed) and questioned erosion/sedimentation staff on staffing capacity, learning that three inspectors and one supervisor were covering roughly 280 active sites.

agenda_items.title: Sheriff's Office IIR Grant Extension Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff clarified that the Sheriff's Office had already been awarded a grant extension by IIR running only through the end of February, requiring the Board to suspend the rules at the work session to authorize the County Manager to sign before the late-February regular meeting. The Board voted 3-0 to suspend the rules and approved the extension by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Item 23-0077: Letter of Support for General Services EPA Grant Application
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Services requested a letter of support for an Environmental Protection Agency grant application covering roughly 25 assisted agreements nationwide (at least one per EPA region). The Board moved to suspend the rules and approved the letter of support by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Item 23-0107: Rescission of Item 23-0063 and $2 Million Contract with National Institute of Minority Economic Development (Hayti Reborn)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff requested that the Board first suspend the rules and rescind its January 23, 2023 vote on Item 23-0063 (which authorized a PERK local-match ILA with the City of Durham) in order to change fiscal agents. After rescinding Item 23-0063, the Board discussed quarterly reporting and administrative fee parity with United Way and voted to approve a $2 million contract through June 30, 2024 with the National Institute of Minority Economic Development to serve as fiscal agent for the Hayti Reborn Justice Movement.

agenda_items.title: Item 23-0102: Commissioner Comments (Boards & Commissions Parity, Housing, and Tracker Updates)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed standardizing stipends, gifts, and budget support across joint city-county boards and commissions in advance of the upcoming budget season, reflected on collaborations with housing providers, and reviewed pending items on the Board's follow-up tracker including scheduling recognitions for former County Attorney Willie Darby and former Congressman David Price.

votes.item_title: Motion to Suspend the Rules for Sheriff's Office IIR Grant Extension
votes.notes: Chair announced 3-0; two commissioners were away from the dais at the time of the vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Because the IIR grant extension ran only through the end of February and could not wait until the late-February regular meeting, a commissioner moved to suspend the rules. Seconded and passed 3-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of Sheriff's Office IIR Grant Extension Through February
votes.notes: Exact tally not announced aloud on the main motion.
votes.discussion_detail: Following suspension of the rules, the Board moved, seconded, and approved the Sheriff's Office IIR grant extension and authorized the County Manager to sign it.

votes.item_title: Item 23-0077: Suspend Rules and Approve Letter of Support for General Services EPA Grant Application
votes.discussion_detail: A commissioner moved to suspend the rules and support General Services' EPA grant application; after brief clarification on the regional award structure and a second, the motion passed by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Motion to Suspend the Rules for Rescission of Item 23-0063
votes.discussion_detail: A commissioner moved to suspend the rules in order to vote on rescinding the January 23, 2023 approval of Item 23-0063. Seconded and passed by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Motion to Rescind January 23, 2023 Vote on Item 23-0063 (PERK ILA with City of Durham)
votes.discussion_detail: A commissioner moved to rescind the Board's January 23, 2023 vote on Agenda Item 23-0063 (entering an ILA with the City of Durham as local match for the PERK program benefiting the Hayti Reborn movement) so the county could instead contract directly with a new fiscal agent. Passed by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Item 23-0107: $2 Million Contract with National Institute of Minority Economic Development (Hayti Reborn Justice Movement Fiscal Agent)
votes.discussion_detail: Following discussion confirming quarterly reporting requirements, matching United Way administrative fees, and a contract end date of June 30, 2024, the Board voted by voice vote to approve the $2 million contract with the National Institute of Minority Economic Development as fiscal agent for the Hayti Reborn Justice Movement.

meetings.title: BOCC - January 23, 2023 - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners reconvened from closed session with no action taken, approved the January 9, 2023 regular session minutes (5-0), and issued ceremonial proclamations honoring the North Carolina Central University 2022 Cricket Celebration Bowl championship football team and recognizing January 2023 as National Mentoring Month. Following a COVID-19 public health update noting 31% bivalent booster uptake locally, the Board unanimously approved (5-0) Item 23-0060, an interlocal agreement with the City of Durham and Budget Amendment 23BCC0057 appropriating $2,000,000 in General Fund fund balance for the Partnership for Equitable and Resilient Communities grant match after discussing the City-County funding split. The Board also received an informational presentation on the FY 2022 Annual Financial Audit and Annual Comprehensive Financial Report with no audit disagreements noted, and voted 5-0 to grant excused absences to Commissioners Nida Allam and Nimasheena Burns for the February 6 work session.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Report, Public Charge, Pledge of Allegiance, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton reconvened the meeting from closed session, reporting that the Board provided direction to staff with no action taken, and read the public charge while Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs led the Pledge of Allegiance. Clerk Monica Wallace read announcements covering COVID-19 vaccination clinic hours, the January 31 deadline for the $11.6 million National Opioid Settlement funding survey, the Durham Low Income Home Owner Relief Program, and Sheriff Clarence Birkhead's 'State of Urgency' youth gun violence play series with Durham Public Schools.

agenda_items.title: Approval of January 9, 2023 Regular Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Howerton presented the January 9, 2023 regular session minutes for review and asked for any edits or a motion to approve. A motion and second were made with no revisions requested.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation Honoring North Carolina Central University 2022 Football Champions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board presented a resolution honoring the North Carolina Central University football team, Coach Trei Oliver, coaching and support staff, and student-athletes for winning the December 17, 2022 Cricket Celebration Bowl (41-34 in overtime over Jackson State University) and the 2022 HBCU national championship. University and team representatives thanked the Board for the recognition.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation Declaring January 2023 as National Mentoring Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Wendy Jacobs read a proclamation declaring January 2023 as National Mentoring Month in Durham County, highlighting the role of mentoring in academic engagement and youth development. Community mentoring leaders, including representatives from Sidekicks Academy and the Thomas Mentor Leadership Academy, spoke about supporting Durham Public Schools students and addressing youth violence.

agenda_items.title: COVID-19 and Public Health Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health staff reported on COVID-19 metrics, noting 645,354 total vaccine doses administered in Durham County but only 31% updated bivalent booster uptake among eligible residents (compared to 20% statewide) ahead of emerging variants such as XBB.1.5. Discussion also addressed ongoing wastewater screening and cumulative county case counts exceeding 100,000.

meetings.executive_summary: With Chair Brenda A. Howerton and Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs absent on county business with excused absences, Acting Chair Heidi Carter presided over a three-member quorum alongside Commissioners Nida Allam and Nimasheena Burns. The Board unanimously approved (3-0) the December 12, 2022 regular session minutes and the consent agenda. Following a presentation from General Manager Jay Gibson and Duke State Relations Assistant Director Katie Light, as well as a public hearing with no speakers and recorded supportive remarks from Chair Howerton and Vice Chair Jacobs, the Board voted 3-0 to adopt a resolution requesting that NCDOT honorarily designate a portion of NC Highway 751 and Cameron Boulevard from Kerley Road to Duke University Road as Coach K Highway.

agenda_items.title: Opening Remarks, Quorum Note, Public Charge, and Announcements

Howerton and Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs were out of town on county business with excused absences, and confirmed a three-commissioner quorum with Manager Sowell and new County Attorney Alan Andrews present. Clerk Monica Wallace read announcements including COVID-19 vaccination clinic hours, the National Opioid Settlement survey, and a Thursday Lunch and Learn series.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Acting Chair Carter presented the December 12, 2022 regular session minutes for comments or revisions. With none offered, Commissioner Nida Allam moved approval and Commissioner Nimasheena Burns seconded.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Acting Chair Carter opened the consent agenda, noting the items had been thoroughly reviewed at the prior work session. Commissioner Burns raised brief comments and questions, after which she moved approval and Commissioner Allam seconded.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Resolution Requesting NCDOT Honorarily Designate NC Highway 751 / Cameron Boulevard as Coach K Highway

Commissioner Allam read the resolution, and a friendly amendment was discussed subject to NCDOT's 400-word limit. meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners Work Session for January 3, 2023
meetings.executive_summary: At its January 3, 2023 work session, the Board swore in new County Attorney Alan Andrews, heard Chair Brenda A. Howerton's remarks expressing concern over community gun violence, and reviewed nine consent agenda items including $5,693,238 in General Fund balance for the Emergency Rental Assistance Program (ERAP 2.0), a $349,810 Hub RTP sewer/water project amendment, a $225,000 Neal Middle School bioretention grant, and a Transit Plan Governance Study interlocal agreement amendment. The Board also received Made in Durham's annual report covering BULLS Academy and a new Durham Tech MOA, discussed a proposed $150,000 Boys and Girls Club after-school pilot, and reviewed commissioner conference updates and board directives. At the close of the session under Item 23-0021, the Board took four unanimous 5-0 roll-call votes to suspend the rules, appoint Commissioner Heidi Carter as temporary chair for the January 9 meeting, suspend rules for absences, and grant excused absences for Chair Howerton and Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs on January 9.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Remarks on Gun Violence, Swearing-In of County Attorney Alan Andrews, and Citizen Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton opened the first meeting of 2023, led the public charge and Pledge of Allegiance (with Commissioner Nida Allam), and spoke out against recent community shootings and gun violence. The Board held the swearing-in ceremony for new County Attorney Alan Andrews, followed by citizen comments where no speakers signed up in person, online, or by email.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review (9 Items)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Manager walked the Board through nine upcoming consent agenda items: 22-0688 ($12,500 tobacco prevention grant), 22-0735 ($42,000 Durham Congregations in Action food security micro-grants), 22-0737 ($349,810 Hub RTP sanitary sewer and reclaimed water project SE058 amendment and change order), 23-000x ($5,693,238 General Fund balance appropriation for DSS Emergency Rental Assistance Program ERAP 2.0), 23-0005 ($225,000 Neal Middle School bioretention grant), 23-0006 (Transit Plan Governance Study cost-sharing interlocal amendment with Durham and Orange County), 23-0007 (restaurant lease amendment), 23-0008 (2022 Edward Byrne Justice Assistance Grant interlocal agreement), and a Utilities Division contract amendment with Gans/Gaines Oil Company. Commissioners asked clarifying questions on the Hub RTP infrastructure pipeline and ERAP 2.0 rental assistance.

agenda_items.title: Made in Durham Annual Report and Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Made in Durham presenters delivered their annual report covering the BULLS Academy life sciences pathway, the Opportunity Youth Collaborative, and NCIP. Presenters highlighted efforts to connect young Durham residents to 4,500 regional life science careers and noted a newly executed MOA with Durham Technical Community College to share real-time data tracking student progression.

agenda_items.title: Boys and Girls Club After-School Pilot Partnership Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed a pilot expansion partnership with the Boys and Girls Club (where Durham Public Schools already drops off buses) requesting $150,000 for expanded staffing and services, alongside library ARPA programming funds and student meal support. Speakers emphasized removing financial barriers for families and expanding trained after-school capacity.

agenda_items.title: Commissioner Comments and Board Directives
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners shared updates on recognizing Coach K, local museum exhibits, coordinating services for individuals cycling between jail, emergency departments, and homelessness, the Triangle's 2027 World University Games bid, and takeaways from the NACo conference in Chicago (including Bull City United parallels and $50,000 in LATCF funding eligibility). Staff also briefly reviewed the status of pending Board directives.

agenda_items.title: Item 23-0021: Temporary Chair Appointment and Excused Absences for January 9, 2023 Regular Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Because Chair Howerton and Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs would both be out of town January 9–11, 2023, County Attorney Alan Andrews advised that a three-member quorum could meet on January 9 if rules were suspended to appoint a temporary chair, though items requiring a supermajority would need to be rescheduled. The Board took four unanimous 5-0 roll-call votes to suspend rules, appoint Commissioner Heidi Carter as temporary chair for January 9, suspend rules for absences, and approve excused absences for Chair Howerton and Vice Chair Jacobs.

meetings.title: BOCC - December 12, 2022 - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the December 12, 2022 regular session of the Durham Board of County Commissioners, with all five seated commissioners participating. The board unanimously approved prior meeting minutes, 23 consent agenda items, and pulled item 22-0726 accepting an Emergency Services grant with Duke Energy. Following a public hearing, the board voted 5-0 to adopt a final assessment resolution and $200,000 budget amendment for Little Acres Drive road repairs. Commissioners also unanimously approved $10,383,139 in American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) community grant awards before adjourning into closed session for economic development incentive negotiations.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Commissioner Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton called the meeting to order and read the public charge, followed by the Pledge of Allegiance led by Commissioner Nimasheena Burns. The clerk read public health and community announcements including COVID-19 and flu vaccination hours, the NC Homeowner Assistance Fund, Durham Food Security Network openings, Solarize the Triangle, and Low Income Energy Assistance Program (LIEAP) dates. Commissioners also offered holiday remarks and discussed honoring retiring County Attorney Lowell Siler/Darby in the new year.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (November 7, November 28, and December 5, 2022)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board considered minutes from the November 7 and December 5 work sessions and the November 28 regular session. No edits or corrections were offered by commissioners.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 22-0635 through 22-0734, excluding 22-0726)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Howerton pulled item 22-0726 for separate presentation at the end of the consent agenda and highlighted support for Durham Tech early childhood initiatives, suggesting a future board update. Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs noted two items of importance without pulling them. The remaining consent items were approved together.

agenda_items.title: Item 22-0726: Emergency Services Grant with Duke Energy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Emergency Services Director Jim Groves introduced Chief Emergency Manager Elizabeth Schroeder to present the grant item involving Duke Energy. Commissioners welcomed the grant funding without objection and approved the item unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing 22-0701: Little Acres Drive Repairs Final Assessment Resolution and Budget Ordinance Amendment No. 23BCC00052
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Transportation Manager Ellen Beckman and Jay Gibson presented the final assessment resolution and general fund appropriation for repairs to Little Acres Drive. Resident Laura Wheeler spoke in support of the neighborhood petition, explaining that the original developer had passed away and neighbors had faced prohibitive private estimates for years. Commissioners praised staff for working through statutory and procedural hurdles to create a model for future private road repair petitions and approved the combined resolution and $200,000 budget amendment.

agenda_items.title: Item 22-0718: American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) Update and Community Grant Awards ($10,383,139)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Manager Claudia Hager and staff presented an update on the county's ARPA portfolio, noting broadband RFP activity, infrastructure investments, and community grant recommendations totaling $10,383,139 across early childhood, maternal health, youth enrichment, and crime intervention initiatives. Commissioners asked clarifying questions about applicant eligibility for organizations with regional footprints and commended staff and review committees for an equitable evaluation process.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Economic Development Incentives)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted to enter closed session pursuant to G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) to discuss the location or expansion of industries or businesses and tentative economic development incentives. Upon returning to open session at 02:58:37, the chair reported direction was given to staff with no formal decisions made.

meetings.title: BOCC Work Session for December 5, 2022
meetings.executive_summary: During the December 5, 2022 work session, Senior Assistant County Attorney Larissa Williamson initially presided to conduct the annual board leadership elections, resulting in the unanimous re-election of Chair Brenda A. Howerton and Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs. The board suspended the rules and unanimously approved public official bonds (item 22-0690) and the 2023 BOCC meeting calendar. Commissioners then previewed 16 consent agenda items—including a $1.5 million Pay-Go addition for the 300 East Main Street affordable housing redevelopment and a Greater Triangle Commuter Rail MOU extension—heard from the Sheriff and staff on gun violence prevention and the new Community Intervention and Support Services department, and reviewed $10.38 million in ARPA community grant recommendations ahead of the December 12 vote.

agenda_items.title: Annual Election of Chair and Vice Chair
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Assistant County Attorney Larissa Williamson opened the work session, read the public charge, and presided over the election of the board chair. Brenda A. Howerton was nominated and re-elected chair, after which she took the gavel and read a statement highlighting the county's $794 million budget with no property tax increase, school and pre-K investments, maternal health nurses, and ARPA deployment. Wendy Jacobs was then nominated and unanimously re-elected vice chair.

agenda_items.title: Item 22-0690: Approval of Public Official Bonds
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board was requested to suspend its rules and approve official bonds for Sheriff Clarence Birkhead, Register of Deeds Sharon Davis, Tax Administrator Dwayne Bronson, and Chief Financial Officer Susan Tezai. Commissioners unanimously voted to suspend the rules and then unanimously approved the bonds.

agenda_items.title: Approval of 2023 BOCC Meeting Schedule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners considered the 2023 Board of County Commissioners meeting calendar. The board voted unanimously to suspend the rules and subsequently voted unanimously to adopt the 2023 meeting schedule.

agenda_items.title: Review of Consent Agenda Items (Including 300 E. Main St. Affordable Housing and Commuter Rail MOU)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy Manager Claudia Hager walked commissioners through 16 consent items, including the McKee family cemetery relocation (22-0635), AV support (22-0656), a Westaff IT staffing amendment (22-0660), a $1.3 million three-year Microsoft enterprise agreement (22-0661), a Greater Triangle Commuter Rail study MOU extension (22-0674), a $2,422 TB screening amendment (22-0675), an Innovative Interfaces amendment (22-0678), and item 22-0697 adding $1.5 million in Pay-Go funding and Loan No. 3 for the 300 East Main Street affordable housing redevelopment. Commissioners commended the board and developer partner for covering construction and supply-chain cost gaps to keep the affordable housing project moving forward.

agenda_items.title: Gun Safety, Sheriff Permit Administration, and Community Intervention and Support Services (CISS)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Sheriff Clarence Birkhead and staff discussed firearm safety, background checks, pistol permits, and guns stolen from unlocked vehicles, noting local registration would be a board policy decision while expressing support for responsible gun legislation. Commissioners highlighted the county's new Community Intervention and Support Services (CISS) department—consolidating My Brother's Keeper, Project BUILD, and Bull City United—alongside Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) and an upcoming February Public Health presentation by Donna Rosser treating gun violence as a public health issue.

agenda_items.title: American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) Community Grants Preview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Manager Claudia Hager and staff presented recommended ARPA nonprofit allocations across early childhood capacity building ($1.6M), affordable childcare scholarships ($12M), child and youth social-emotional enrichment ($1.5M), culturally affirming maternal health support, and four Crime Intervention Initiative recipients (Durham Crisis Response Center, Communities In Partnership, Triangle Literacy Council, and Durham County Teen Court and Restitution). Staff noted local funds were planned for the Hayti project and that remaining housing, food security, and library/Cooperative Extension allocations would be refined ahead of the December 31, 2024 federal obligation deadline, with a formal vote scheduled for December 12.

votes.item_title: Election of Brenda A. Howerton as Chair
votes.notes: Nominee Brenda A. Howerton did not cast a roll-call vote on her own nomination.
votes.discussion_detail: Presiding County Attorney Larissa Williamson called for nominations for Chair; Brenda A. Howerton was nominated with no other nominations offered and approved by roll call.

votes.item_title: Election of Wendy Jacobs as Vice Chair
votes.notes: Nominee Wendy Jacobs was not called in the four-name roll call.
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Howerton called for Vice Chair nominations; Wendy Jacobs was nominated with no competing nominations and approved unanimously by the four voting members.

votes.item_title: Suspend Rules for Item 22-0690 (Public Official Bonds)
votes.discussion_detail: Board voted to suspend rules at the work session to take formal action on public official bonds.

votes.item_title: Item 22-0690: Approval of Public Official Bonds
votes.discussion_detail: Approved bonds for Sheriff Clarence Birkhead, Register of Deeds Sharon Davis, Tax Administrator Dwayne Bronson, and CFO Susan Tezai.

votes.item_title: Suspend Rules for 2023 BOCC Meeting Schedule
votes.discussion_detail: Board suspended work session rules to act on the 2023 BOCC meeting calendar.

votes.item_title: Approval of 2023 BOCC Meeting Calendar

meetings.title: BOCC - November 28, 2022 - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its November 28, 2022 regular session, the Durham Board of County Commissioners opened by unanimously approving a contract hiring Allen A. Andrews as Durham County Attorney effective January 3, 2023. The board approved the November 14 minutes, the full consent agenda (items 22-0673 through 22-0705), and item 22-0715 certifying the voter-approved 2022 General Obligation Bond referendum results alongside presentations from Durham Public Schools, Durham Tech, and the Museum of Life and Science. After a presentation on the 2022 White House Conference on Hunger, Nutrition, and Health, commissioners concluded a lengthy quasi-judicial hearing for the Mason Farms conservation subdivision, voting 4-0 to approve both Major Special Use Permit M2200001 (community wastewater system) and Major Site Plan B2100325.

agenda_items.title: Contract Approval Hiring Allen A. Andrews as Durham County Attorney
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a pre-meeting closed session, Chair Howerton called the regular meeting to order and sought a motion to hire Allen A. Andrews as Durham County Attorney starting January 3, 2023. Commissioners unanimously authorized signing the contract, and Andrews briefly addressed the board expressing enthusiasm for serving Durham County.

agenda_items.title: Item 22-0707: Approval of November 14, 2022 Regular Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After the public charge, Pledge of Allegiance, and clerk announcements (including delinquent tax advertising and LIEAP dates), the board considered the November 14 regular session minutes with no edits requested.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 22-0673 through 22-0705)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: No commissioners requested to pull any consent items from 22-0673 through 22-0705, and the package was approved unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Item 22-0715: Certification of 2022 General Obligation Bond Referendum Results
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The county manager and commissioners recognized county staff (Claudia Hager, Deborah Craig-Ray, David Ades, and Susan Tezai), Durham Public Schools, Durham Technical Community College (highlighting a 35,000-square-foot life sciences training facility), the Museum of Life and Science, and Blue Ribbon Committee volunteers for the successful bond campaign. Commissioners praised voters for overwhelmingly passing the historic referendum and unanimously certified the statement of results for publication.

agenda_items.title: Item 22-0644: Learnings from the 2022 White House Conference on Hunger, Nutrition, and Health
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Food Security Coordinator Mary Oxendine presented takeaways from attending the September 27 White House Conference on Hunger, Nutrition, and Health, beginning with a Durham land acknowledgment.

agenda_items.title: Quasi-Judicial Hearing: Mason Farms Major Special Use Permit (M2200001) and Major Site Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: During the continued quasi-judicial hearing, the board heard technical testimony from Gary McConnell of McConnell and Associates regarding community wells, drawdown tests, and groundwater impacts, as well as an evidentiary objection regarding witness standing at 05:02:26. At 05:04:13, the board voted 5-0 to extend the meeting until 11:30 PM. Commissioner Heidi Carter questioned planning staff on UDO conservation subdivision purpose statements, the 80% primary conservation open-space requirement, and resident appeal rights to the Board of Adjustment, while County Attorney Massey clarified the substantial, material, and competent evidence standard before the board voted 4-0 to approve both the special use permit and the major site plan.

votes.item_title: Authorization of Employment Contract with Allen A. Andrews as Durham County Attorney
votes.notes: Chair stated 2022 by slip of tongue; Andrews confirmed 2023 start.
votes.discussion_detail: Following closed session, the board voted unanimously to authorize signing the contract hiring Allen A. Andrews as County Attorney effective January 3, 2023.

votes.item_title: Item 22-0707: Approval of November 14, 2022 Regular Session Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Approved without edits.

votes.item_title: Item 22-0715: Certification and Publication of 2022 General Obligation Bond Referendum Results
votes.discussion_detail: Board adopted the resolution accepting and certifying the 2022 general obligation bond referendum results and authorizing publication of the statement of results.

votes.item_title: Extend Meeting Past 11:00 PM Until 11:30 PM
votes.discussion_detail: At 10:40 PM during the Mason Farms quasi-judicial hearing, Chair Howerton requested a motion to extend the session past 11:00 PM to 11:30 PM.

votes.item_title: Case M2200001: Mason Farms Major Special Use Permit (Community Wastewater System)
votes.notes: Commissioner Nimasheena Burns was not called / did not vote during the roll call on this item.
votes.discussion_detail: Following testimony on community wells and runoff, legal guidance on quasi-judicial standards, and staff's approval recommendation, the board approved Major Special Use Permit M2200001 consistent with the submitted plans and staff conditions.

votes.item_title: Major Site Plan Approval: Mason Farms Conservation Subdivision
votes.notes: Case number transcribed as P2100325/B2100325. Commissioner Nimasheena Burns did not vote during the roll call.
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately after approving the special use permit, the board approved the accompanying Mason Farms major site plan.

meetings.title: BOCC Work Session for November 7, 2022
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 7, 2022 work session, the Board of County Commissioners heard public comments calling for a 'Family First County' DSS child welfare resolution and urgent mass grading, clear-cutting, and blasting protections in Southeast Durham. Commissioners reviewed upcoming consent agenda items, including grants for EMS community paramedicine and MAT partnership with Lincoln Community Health Center ($73,660), Youth Home nutrition ($5,239), Social Services Duke Energy rate settlement funds ($38,000), Public Health ($8,000), State Library assistance ($153,182), Detention Center fan replacements, and an $18,000 Burt's Bees Foundation grant to update the county's 35-year-old rare plant inventory. Planning and environmental staff also briefed the board on state-reviewed sedimentation and erosion control amendments—including flocculant mandates and stop-work order authority—as well as Triassic Basin well vulnerability and legal limits on local blasting regulation. No formal votes were recorded in the work session digest.

agenda_items.title: Citizens' Comments: DSS Family First Reform and Southeast Durham Grading/Blasting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A public speaker urged commissioners to adopt a 'Family First County' resolution incorporating Emancipate NC's recommendations during DSS leadership transition to keep children safely with their families and prioritize prompt reunification. Resident Pam Andrews thanked Vice Chair Jacobs and Chair Howerton for visiting Bahama, thanked Fire Marshals for responsiveness on blasting loopholes, and urged immediate completion of mass grading and clear-cutting amendments as annexations impact Southeast Durham creeks.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review: Budget Amendments, Detention Center HVAC, and Rare Plant Inventory
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff walked through consent budget ordinance amendments including item 22-0568 ($73,660 NCDHHS grant to EMS for MAT coordination with Lincoln Community Health Center), item 22-0594 ($5,239 NCDPI Youth Home nutrition grant), item 22-0595 ($38,000 Duke Energy settlement funds for DSS), item 22-0605 ($8,000 Public Health outdoor learning grant), item 22-0616 ($153,182 State Library operating grant), item 22-0627 (Detention Center roof exhaust and axial fan replacement), and item 22-0628 ($18,000 Burt's Bees Foundation grant for a rare plant community biological inventory). Vice Chair Jacobs praised the Burt's Bees grant—updating data last collected 35 years ago—and asked how planning staff would integrate it into rezoning and site plan open-space reviews.

agenda_items.title: Sedimentation, Erosion Control, Mass Grading, Blasting, and Groundwater Well Protection Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff briefed commissioners on proposed sedimentation and erosion control ordinance amendments scheduled for the November 15 NC Sedimentation Control Commission meeting, including making Durham the first NC jurisdiction to require flocculants, adding stop-work order authority, and closing agricultural dumping loopholes alongside separate fast-tracked mass grading/tree preservation amendments. Onsite Water Protection Supervisor Patrick Eaton explained that Triassic Basin wells are typically deep and low-yield, making borehole collapse or sedimentation difficult to repair. Commissioner Heidi Carter asked whether the Comprehensive Plan over-concentrated development in Southeast Durham and pressed staff to explore rezoning proffers for affordable housing and a developer-funded well testing and repair fund for blasting impacts.

meetings.title: BOCC - October 24, 2022 - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: With Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs absent, the remaining four commissioners convened the October 24, 2022 regular session under Chair Brenda A. Howerton. The board voted 4-0 to approve an excused absence for Commissioner Nimasheena Burns on November 14, adopted the September 28 and October 3 minutes, recognized PEACH for community health worker training and lead abatement alongside the inaugural winner of the Kids I Voted Sticker Contest, and passed a four-item consent agenda. Commissioners also voted to advance recommendations expanding Durham County's family-friendly workplace policies—including paid family medical leave, paid 'safe/wellness days' for domestic violence or sexual assault survivors, and codified pregnancy accommodations—received a COVID-19 and respiratory illness update, and met in closed session on attorney-client matters.

agenda_items.title: Announcements and Excused Absence Request for November 14, 2022
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk Monica Wallace read community announcements including COVID-19 vaccination clinics, the Durham Cultural Roadmap, and the November 10 Veterans Day celebration. Commissioner Nimasheena Burns requested an excused absence for the November 14 meeting, which the board approved 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (September 28 Regular Session and October 3 Work Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed the September 28 regular session and October 3 work session minutes with no edits requested.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: PEACH Recognition and Kids I Voted Sticker Contest Winner
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board recognized PEACH for its COVID-19 outreach, lead abatement work, and training of community health workers, with Commissioners Carter and Burns praising the organization's family health impact. Under item 22-07XX, commissioners also honored the inaugural winner of the Board of Elections' Kids I Voted Sticker Contest.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (4 Items)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: No items were pulled from the four-item consent agenda previously reviewed at work session, and the board approved it unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Other Business: Expansion of Durham County Family-Friendly Workplace Policies
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Advocates and County Manager Kimberly Sowell presented proposals building on Durham County's 2016 adoption of 12 weeks paid parental leave to add five weeks of paid family medical leave covering broader FMLA qualifying events, allow existing paid sick leave to be used as 'safe days' or 'wellness days' for domestic violence, sexual assault, or stalking without stigma, and formally codify reasonable pregnancy accommodations. Commissioner Burns emphasized the life-saving importance of stigma-free wellness/safe days for domestic violence survivors. The board voted to advance the recommendations so staff could draft policy language and cost estimates for final adoption.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (Roll call truncated after initial Aye)

agenda_items.title: Public Health Update on COVID-19 and Non-COVID Respiratory Illnesses
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health reported that Durham's COVID-19 lab positivity rate fell from 8.6% to 6.9% over three weeks, while noting hospital strain from non-COVID respiratory viruses and encouraging masking in crowded spaces especially for children.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Attorney-Client Privilege)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 4-0 to enter closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with legal counsel. Upon returning at 02:20:11, Chair Howerton reported direction was given to staff and no action was needed.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners - Special Session (Opioid Discussion with AG Josh Stein) - 10.14.22
meetings.executive_summary: All five county commissioners convened in a special session on October 14, 2022 with North Carolina Attorney General Josh Stein, Sheriff Clarence Birkhead, County Manager Kim Sowell, and public health and criminal justice leadership to strategize on deploying opioid settlement funds. Attorney General Stein reviewed fatal overdose trends—citing 108,000 U.S. deaths in 2021, over 3,500 in North Carolina, and 71 in Durham County in 2020—and explained that 85% of North Carolina's $750 million share of the $26 billion national settlement flows directly to local governments. County staff and commissioners outlined an upcoming community-wide survey and town hall, emphasized intensive case management and supportive housing, and discussed building a local peer support specialist pipeline and advocating to repeal the federal Medicaid Inmate Exclusion Policy. As an informational special session, no votes were taken.

agenda_items.title: Welcome, Introductions, and Remarks by NC Attorney General Josh Stein on Opioid Settlements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton welcomed Attorney General Josh Stein, acknowledging a quorum of all five commissioners alongside Sheriff Birkhead, County Manager Sowell, General Manager Joanne Pierce, CJRC Director Gudrun Parmer, and Public Health leadership. Attorney General Stein expressed condolences following the prior night's shooting in Raleigh, detailed rising fentanyl-driven overdose deaths nationally and locally, and explained why North Carolina structured its settlement agreement to direct 85% of the state's $750 million share to counties and municipalities.

agenda_items.title: Durham County Strategic Planning, Peer Support Workforce, Supportive Housing, and Medicaid Advocacy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County staff explained plans to launch a community survey and host a town hall to identify treatment and recovery service gaps before investing settlement dollars. Commissioners and staff discussed expanding outpatient treatment, supportive housing, case management, and peer support specialist pipelines—including justice-involved training, preventing provider burnout, and potentially using ARPA funds or hosting a statewide peer support conference in Durham—as well as joint advocacy with the Attorney General to end the federal Medicaid Inmate Exclusion Policy for individuals leaving jail.

meetings.executive_summary: At the October 10, 2022 regular session presided over by Chair Brenda A. Howerton, all five commissioners heard public comment from bond campaign co-chairs thanking the board for placing the $550 million general obligation bond referendum on the November 8 ballot. The board unanimously passed the consent agenda—with Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs praising EMS for winning a grant to expand community paramedicine—and voted 5-0 following a public hearing to permanently close a 970-linear-foot section of Akzo Boulevard (item 22-0604 / SC190001). Commissioners also voted 5-0 after a public hearing under item 22-0618 to rescind their September 12, 2022 approval of the Mason Farms Major Special Use Permit and schedule a new quasi-judicial hearing for November 14 to receive additional evidence, before holding a closed session on property acquisition and employment contract terms.
