meetings.title: BOCC - September 9, 2021 Regular Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the September 9, 2021 work session of the Durham Board of County Commissioners, starting at 10:36 AM following a Durham Tech dedication event, with all five commissioners participating. The board heard citizen comment on an eviction emergency, previewed 14 consent items—including utility repairs, a $50,000 Greater Durham Black Chamber of Commerce contract, $1.65M in mental health carryover, and a $2.4M co-located Fire/EMS Station 18 ILA—and voted 5-0 after suspending the rules to approve the Bahama Fire Station rezoning (Case Z2000046) and its consistency statement. Commissioners also heard an Animal Welfare Advisory Committee (AWAC) presentation supporting Trap-Neuter-Vaccinate-Return (TNVR) ordinance changes, reviewed 2050 Metropolitan Transportation Plan scenarios with DCHC MPO, examined a $21M–$31M Board of Elections space-needs assessment, previewed ARPA engagement and rubric plans, and voted 5-0 to suspend the rules and make a Dangerous Dog Appeal Board reappointment.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Citizen Comments on Eviction Crisis
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton opened the work session at 10:36 AM following a Durham Tech dedication event and read the public charge. Clerk Monica Toomer read a citizen comment from Larissa Sidel warning of an acute eviction emergency (citing 82 eviction hearings the previous Friday) and urging the county to distribute ERAP funds directly to tenants or through nonprofits such as Legal Aid when landlords refuse to participate.

agenda_items.title: Review of Consent Agenda Items (14 Items Including Station 18 ILA and Mental Health Carryover)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim Manager Claudia Hager walked through 14 consent items for the September 13 agenda, including the Building Bridges jail opioid-treatment grant (21-0522), McFarland Farm conservation easement (21-0526), Triangle Wastewater Treatment Plant and collection system repair amendments (21-0530, 21-0533, 21-0534, 21-0539, 21-0542), a $20 million Chinn Road pump station grant application (21-0540), Durham Pre-K funding (21-0536), a $50,000 Greater Durham Black Chamber of Commerce contract (21-0537), Alliance Behavioral Health $1.65M carryover funding including $650,000 for MOORS youth mobile crisis care, a $318,750 Governor's Highway Safety grant (21-0550), and a late-added $2.4M co-located Fire/EMS Station 18 ILA on Herndon Road. Commissioner Burns sought measurable deliverables by January for the Black Chamber contract, and Vice Chair Jacobs requested data on residents served by MOORS and tying utility capacity costs to developers.

agenda_items.title: Discussion Item 21-0561: Zoning Map Change for Bahama Fire Station (Case Z2000046)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following the August 23 public hearing and 24-hour comment window, Clerk Toomer reported no additional public comments received. The board closed the public hearing, voted 5-0 to suspend the rules, voted 5-0 to adopt the ordinance rezoning 1426 Bahama Road from CN and RS-20/MLR-A to Commercial Neighborhood with a Text-Only Development Plan (CN(D)/MLR-A) prohibiting on-site alcohol uses, and voted 5-0 to adopt the NCGS 160D-605 statement of consistency.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 5-0 (suspend rules, rezoning, and consistency statement)

agenda_items.title: Discussion Item 21-0521: Animal Welfare Advisory Committee (AWAC) Community Cat Management / TNVR Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: AWAC spokesperson Jan Paul presented an 18-month study of Durham County's estimated 30,000 feral cats, concluding that current trap-and-euthanize policies fail to reduce populations, strain APS and Animal Services budgets and staff, and lag behind 64 NC counties using Trap-Neuter-Vaccinate-Return (TNVR), while noting state wildlife experts found no threatened bird species endangered by cats in Durham. Commissioners Jacobs, Burns, and Carter strongly endorsed directing the County Attorney's Office to draft ordinance amendments permitting TNVR; Chair Howerton declined to entertain a motion due to severe time pressure and directed legal staff and management to follow up with ordinance proposals.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / No vote (staff directed to draft ordinance)

agenda_items.title: Discussion Item 21-0538: DCHC MPO 2050 Metropolitan Transportation Plan (MTP) Alternatives Analysis
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation Manager Ellen Beckman and DCHC MPO Senior Planner Andy Henry reviewed 2050 regional growth forecasts (52% Durham population growth and 85% employment growth) and compared Plans & Trends, Shared Leadership, and Altogether scenarios—with Altogether extending commuter rail to Mebane, adding BRT corridors, converting downtown NC 147 to a four-lane boulevard, and shifting funding from highway widening to transit and complete streets. Because state highway-centric funding (90% to roads) left carbon emissions rising +16% overall, Henry noted the MPO board directed staff to prepare two competing October drafts (a traditional highway-weighted option and a transit/equity/climate-weighted option). Commissioners urged prioritizing transit-dependent riders, Treyburn/RTP job access, bus shelter upgrades, and bus driver pay/childcare.

agenda_items.title: Discussion Item 21-0518: Board of Elections Space Needs & Programming Assessment Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant General Manager Perry Manns, Elections Director Derek Bowens, and RND Architects principal Charles Nicholson detailed severe operational, security, and fire-code deficiencies across the Board of Elections' split Judicial Annex (4,281 sq. ft.) and leased South Austin Avenue warehouse (10,400 net sq. ft. lacking climate control, adequate exits, and observer visibility), documenting a 13,000 net sq. ft. deficit against a 43,000 gross sq. ft. need. They presented three preliminary options—a $31M new build by 2025, a $21M+ leased flex space fit-up by August 2023, or a phased lease/renovation—for CIP evaluation, and Vice Chair Jacobs asked staff to also consider purchasing and retrofitting an existing building.

agenda_items.title: Discussion Item 21-0546: American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim Manager Claudia Hager, Jodi Miller, and Deborah Craig-Ray reviewed Durham County's $62.4 million ARPA allocation ($5.1M earmarked for FY22 COVID costs), 300+ survey responses and 80 community proposals from summer city-county engagement, upcoming Phase 2 outreach to unincorporated areas starting September 30, and an 8-category draft evaluation rubric ahead of a deeper review on September 27. Commissioners clarified future county RFP submission pathways and agreed to email rubric feedback.

agenda_items.title: Item 21-059X: Dangerous Dog Appeal Board Appointment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At the close of the work session, the board voted 5-0 to suspend its rules and voted 5-0 to appoint a member (referred to in audio as 'Mo' / 'Motriro') to an additional three-year term on the Dangerous Dog Appeal Board. Staff also noted commissioners could review directives online and agreed to confirm whether Acting County Attorney Willie Darby had sufficient guidance on drafting the TNVR ordinance prior to adjournment.

meetings.title: BOCC Regular Session for Aug. 23 (full audio)
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the August 23, 2021 regular session of the Durham Board of County Commissioners (full audio recording), with all five commissioners present. The board unanimously approved July 12 minutes and 11 consent agenda items, proclaimed September 2021 as National Recovery Month, and recognized three National Association of Counties (NACo) Achievement Awards won by the Board of Elections, Public Health/OES, and Tax Administration. Commissioners held a public hearing on rezoning the old Bahama Fire Station at 1426 Bahama Road (Case Z2000046) and kept it open 24 hours, voted 5-0 to approve a $125,000 economic development incentive for Smart Wires Inc., heard a Delta-variant COVID-19 briefing from Public Health Director Rodney Jenkins and interim manager Claudia Hager's employee vaccine incentive rollout, announced board appointments, and met in closed session before adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Commissioner Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton opened the August 23, 2021 regular session at 7:00 PM, read the public charge, and Commissioner Allam led the Pledge of Allegiance. Clerk Monica Toomer read community announcements including an August 31 MWBE outreach session for 300 East Main Street, Durham Center for Senior Life dementia care management, NCDOT fall litter sweep, the bilingual Nurturing Durham website, Durham Youth Ambassadors, and municipal primary early voting starting September 16. Commissioners Allam and Jacobs highlighted a state court ruling restoring voting rights to over 50,000 North Carolinians on felony probation/parole and urged community donations and volunteers for up to 90 Afghan refugees arriving in Durham in September.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (July 12, 2021 Regular Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board considered the July 12, 2021 regular session minutes with no edits or corrections. Vice Chair Jacobs moved and Commissioner Burns seconded approval, passing 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Item 21-0459: Proclamation for National Recovery Month (September 2021)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Howerton read the proclamation declaring September 2021 as National Recovery Month under the theme 'Recovery is for Everyone,' highlighting national mental health and substance-use treatment gaps. Dr. Lonnie Hall accepted the proclamation on behalf of the Recovery Community of Durham, and Vice Chair Jacobs and Chair Howerton emphasized reducing stigma and expanding support amid rising pandemic overdoses.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Item 21-0520: Recognition of Three NACo Achievement Awards
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim Manager Claudia Hager introduced three NACo Achievement Award-winning initiatives achieved amid both COVID-19 and a malware attack: the Board of Elections polling wait-time/operations app, Public Health and OES's COVID-19 Vaccine Distribution Dashboard, and Tax Administration's Jabber remote call center, 99.9%-satisfaction live chat, and long-term tax deferral program. Public Health Director Rodney Jenkins, Tax Administrator Dwayne Brinson, CIO Greg Morrow, and OES's Ari Shine accepted recognition and thanked cross-departmental teams.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (11 Items)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no items requested to be pulled and at Vice Chair Jacobs's suggestion to spare Interim Manager Hager's voice, the board waived reading the 11 consent agenda items and approved them unanimously 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing Item 21-0505: Zoning Map Change for Bahama Fire Station (Case Z2000046)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Manager Michael Stock presented the Bahama Volunteer Fire Rescue Company's request to rezone two parcels totaling 0.76 acres at 1426 Bahama Road from CN and RS-20/MLR-A to Commercial Neighborhood with a text-only development plan (CN(D)/MLR-A) barring bars, nightclubs, or on-site alcohol consumption (Planning Commission recommended 10-0). Stock explained to Chair Howerton that combining the parcels reduces non-conformity, and Fire Chief Len Needham testified the department seeks to sell the old station to help buy a fire truck without debt while protecting the surrounding village. The public hearing was kept open 24 hours until August 24, with a vote scheduled for the September 9 work session.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Held open 24 hours / Vote deferred to Sept. 9

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing Item 21-0511: Economic Development Incentive Allocation for Smart Wires Inc. ($125,000)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following the August 9 public hearing and 24-hour comment window, Clerk Toomer reported no comments received. Commissioner Carter moved and Commissioner Allam seconded allocating $125,000 to Smart Wires Inc. and authorizing Interim Manager Hager to execute the agreement incorporating the job-creation and investment conditions in the briefing sheet (as confirmed by Vice Chair Jacobs), passing 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Other Business: Durham County Public Health COVID-19 Response Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health Director Rodney Jenkins reported a surging Delta wave (118 seven-day moving average, 8.1% lab positivity, 793 active cases, and African Americans accounting for 47.83% of August cases), highlighted over 25,000 vaccine incentive gift cards ($100 first dose / $25 driver) driving a 37% vaccination increase, announced a September 1 pause on broad outreach to rest staff and launch third-dose boosters for immunocompromised residents, and noted unvaccinated residents faced six times the attack rate (1,580 vs. 251 per 100,000). Commissioners urged clear public criteria on immunocompromised eligibility, welcomed Interim Manager Hager's county employee policy ($250 and two bonus days off if vaccinated by October 4, or weekly testing), and inquired about pediatric clusters (<5).

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Acting County Attorney Willie Darby announced appointments to the Dangerous Dog Appeal Board (Brian Mulligan, corrected from 'Miriam' by Vice Chair Jacobs), Durham County Convention Center Authority (Miriam De La Hunt Andrews), Juvenile Crime Prevention Council (LaKeisha Blake, Joseph Jackson III, Brandon Morsey), and TJCOG Water Resource Collaborative (Michael Koenig).

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5), (a)(6)) and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) and (a)(6) regarding property acquisition/contract negotiations, employment contract terms, and individual personnel matters, after Chair Howerton reminded the public that the September work session would be held Thursday, September 9 at 9:00 AM due to Labor Day and Rosh Hashanah. Returning to open session at 02:18:19, the board reported giving direction to staff and adjourned 5-0.

votes.item_title: Approval of Minutes (July 12, 2021 Regular Session)

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Regular Session Meeting- August 23, 2021
meetings.executive_summary: This YouTube broadcast recording of the August 23, 2021 regular session (beginning mid-proclamation at 00:38:58 under Chair Brenda A. Howerton, with all five commissioners present) captures the board's recognition of National Recovery Month and three NACo Achievement Awards for Elections, Public Health/OES, and Tax Administration. Commissioners unanimously approved the 11-item consent agenda, conducted a public hearing on the Bahama Fire Station rezoning (Case Z2000046) before leaving the comment window open 24 hours, and voted 5-0 to approve a $125,000 economic development incentive for Smart Wires Inc. The board also received a Delta-variant COVID-19 briefing from Public Health Director Rodney Jenkins (including county employee vaccine incentives), announced boards and commissions appointments, and convened in closed session before adjourning 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Item 21-0459: Proclamation for National Recovery Month (September 2021)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton completed reading the proclamation designating September 2021 as National Recovery Month ('Recovery is for Everyone'). Dr. Lonnie Hall accepted on behalf of the Recovery Community of Durham, and Vice Chair Jacobs and Chair Howerton spoke on rising pandemic isolation and overdose rates.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Item 21-0520: Recognition of Three NACo Achievement Awards
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim Manager Claudia Hager recognized three NACo Achievement Awards earned despite COVID-19 and a malware attack: Board of Elections (election-day tracking app), Public Health and OES (COVID-19 Vaccine Distribution Dashboard), and Tax Administration (Jabber remote call center, 99.9%-satisfaction live chat, and tax deferral program), with remarks from Rodney Jenkins, Dwayne Brinson, CIO Greg Morrow, and OES's Ari Shine.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (11 Items)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no items pulled and at Vice Chair Jacobs's suggestion to save Interim Manager Hager's voice, the board waived reading the 11 consent agenda items and approved them 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing Item 21-0505: Zoning Map Change for Bahama Fire Station (Case Z2000046)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Manager Michael Stock presented the Bahama Volunteer Fire Rescue Company's request to rezone 0.76 acres at 1426 Bahama Road from CN and RS-20/MLR-A to Commercial Neighborhood with a text-only development plan prohibiting on-site alcohol sales (Planning Commission recommended 10-0). Stock explained combining the parcels reduces non-conformity, Fire Chief Len Needham testified the sale will help purchase a fire truck without debt while protecting community character, and the hearing was left open 24 hours ahead of a September 9 vote.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Held open 24 hours / Vote deferred to Sept. 9

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing Item 21-0511: Economic Development Incentive Allocation for Smart Wires Inc. ($125,000)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk Toomer reported no public comments were received during the 24-hour comment period after the August 9 hearing. Commissioner Carter moved and Commissioner Allam seconded allocating $125,000 to Smart Wires Inc. subject to the briefing sheet's performance terms, passing 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Other Business: Durham County Public Health COVID-19 Response Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health Director Rodney Jenkins reported a surging Delta wave (118 seven-day moving average, 8.1% positivity, 793 active cases, and 47.83% of August cases among African American residents), highlighted 25,000+ vaccine incentive cards ($100 first dose / $25 driver), and announced third-dose boosters for immunocompromised residents and a September 1 pause on broad outreach. Commissioners asked for clear public eligibility criteria for boosters, praised Interim Manager Hager's county employee program ($250 and two bonus days off by October 4, or weekly testing), and asked about pediatric clusters (<5).

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Acting County Attorney Willie Darby announced appointments to the Dangerous Dog Appeal Board (Brian Mulligan, corrected from 'Miriam' by Vice Chair Jacobs), Convention Center Authority (Miriam De La Hunt Andrews), Juvenile Crime Prevention Council (LaKeisha Blake, Joseph Jackson III, Brandon Morsey), and TJCOG Water Resource Collaborative (Michael Koenig).

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5), (a)(6)) and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) and (a)(6) for property/employment contract negotiations and personnel matters, after Chair Howerton announced the September work session would be held Thursday, September 9 at 9:00 AM due to Labor Day and Rosh Hashanah. meetings.title: Durham County BOCC Meeting Aug 9, 2021
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the August 9, 2021 regular session of the Durham Board of County Commissioners, with all five commissioners present. The board unanimously approved five sets of prior minutes and 21 consent items, while pulling Item 21-0491 to read and adopt the Durham County Language Equity Policy Resolution by a separate 5-0 vote. Ceremonial items recognized Register of Deeds Sharon Davis's international leadership, the Sheriff's Office National Sheriffs' Association Triple Crown accreditation (21-0451), and the Durham Digital Equity Plan (21-0484). Commissioners also held a public hearing on a $125,000 economic development incentive for Smart Wires Inc. (leaving comments open 24 hours), received a COVID-19 briefing on the county's newly enacted 5:00 PM indoor mask mandate and fourth-wave Delta surge, agreed to issue a support letter for adding Camp Butner to the NC Sentinel Landscape Partnership, and met in closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Commissioner Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton opened the meeting, read the public charge, and led the Pledge of Allegiance. Vice Chair Jacobs asked to ensure Item 21-0491 (Language Equity Policy Resolution) would be read aloud, and Chair Howerton agreed to pull it from consent. Clerk Monica Toomer read announcements on the August 20 Back to School Bash, vaccine clinic hours, 2021 property tax billing with partial payments, Durham Pre-K, P-EBT expansion, Register of Deeds vital-record appointments, 911 hiring, convenience site hours, and the newly reopened Main Library, while Vice Chair Jacobs highlighted $3.31 million in ERAP rent relief disbursed since June 1 and two DSS social workers stationed at the courthouse.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (May 18, May 27, June 3, June 7, and June 28, 2021)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board considered five sets of minutes (May 18, May 27, June 3 budget meeting, June 7 work session, and June 28 regular session) with no edits offered. All five sets were approved together by a 5-0 roll-call vote.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: Register of Deeds Recognition, Sheriff's Triple Crown Award (21-0451), and Digital Equity Plan Resolution (21-0484)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Howerton recognized Register of Deeds Sharon Davis for her international leadership role. Chief Deputy Whited, Lt. Hartigan, and Sgt. Kusher accepted recognition for the Sheriff's Office becoming 1 of 49 agencies nationally (and 2nd in NC) to earn the Triple Crown accreditation (CALEA, NCCHC, and ACA), and Chair Howerton read Resolution 21-0484 adopting the Durham Digital Equity Plan, joined by Library Director Tammy Baggett, Digital Durham founder Laura Fogle, and Claudia Tooms (noting the Stanford L. Warren digital navigator grant, Item 21-0453).

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (21 Items, Excluding Item 21-0491)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Item 21-0491 (Language Equity Resolution) was pulled for reading, and Vice Chair Jacobs requested that quarterly performance reports under grant Item 21-0474 be shared with the board via the County Manager. Commissioner Burns moved and Commissioner Carter seconded approval of the 21 remaining consent items, passing 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 21-0491: Durham County Language Equity Policy Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Jacobs read the resolution enacting the Durham County Language Access Policy to remove communication barriers through expanded translations (beginning with Spanish) and closed captioning. General Manager Deborah Craig-Ray thanked the board for supporting the initiative, and commissioners unanimously approved the resolution 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing Item 21-0499: Economic Development Incentive Allocation for Smart Wires Inc. ($125,000)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic Development Officer Andy Miracle presented a $125,000 performance-based grant for Smart Wires Inc. to relocate its corporate headquarters from San Francisco to Durham, creating 250 jobs and $23.5 million in investment alongside a state JDIG award and partnerships with DPS CTE, Durham Tech, and the Research Triangle Cleantech Cluster. Chief People Officer Shannon Ross affirmed local hiring and clean-grid commitments, Commissioner Burns criticized state press releases for omitting county officials and staff, and the public hearing was left open 24 hours through August 10 ahead of an August 23 vote.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Held open 24 hours / Vote deferred to Aug. 23

agenda_items.title: Other Business Item 21-0492: Public Health COVID-19 Update and Indoor Mask Mandate
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy Health Directors Liz Stevens and Kristen Patterson detailed the county's new State of Emergency indoor mask mandate effective at 5:00 PM for ages 5+, reporting a Delta-driven fourth wave (70 cases/day 7-day average, 4.6% positivity, 54.1% total / 62.9% 12+ fully vaccinated per CDC, 20% July breakthrough cases, and 23% July cases under age 18) and the new $100 first-dose/$25 driver cash card incentive. Commissioners requested 12–18 vaccination rates, urged expanding incentives to minors ages 12–17, called for clearer online testing site listings, and heard Stevens explain that BinaxNOW rapid antigen tests have roughly 40% sensitivity compared to PCR tests.

agenda_items.title: Other Business Item 21-0493: North Carolina Sentinel Landscape Partnership Support Letter
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Manager Deborah Craig-Ray introduced Dr. Mary Lou Addor of NC State University, who presented the 33-county Eastern NC Sentinel Landscape Partnership coordinating military readiness, farmland and forest conservation easements, flood catchments, and carbon sequestration. She requested a county support letter by August 26 to add Camp Butner (Durham and Granville counties) and MOTSU to the federal designation; Commissioners Burns and Jacobs endorsed the effort and Chair Howerton instructed staff to prepare the letter for signature.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / No vote (consensus to issue support letter)

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Economic Development Incentives — G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4)) and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to adjourn into closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) to discuss industrial/business location or expansion and tentative economic development incentives. Returning to open session at 02:51:20, Chair Howerton announced direction was given to staff and the board voted 5-0 to adjourn.

meetings.title: BOCC - August 2, 2021 Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the August 2, 2021 virtual work session with all five commissioners, Interim County Manager Claudia Hager, and Acting County Attorney Willie Darby present. During citizen comments and consent agenda review, the board heard an emailed comment opposing COVID-19 restrictions and reviewed multiple of the 20 consent items, including HVAC procurement evaluation and MWBE participation, a Library Digital Navigators grant, a $3.3 million NCDHHS public health grant, a $75,000 immunization grant, and Board of Elections and EMS billing contract amendments. After suspending the rules (5-0), the board voted 5-0 to appoint Chair Howerton as voting delegate and Commissioner Nida Allam as alternate to the NCACC 114th Annual Conference. Commissioners also discussed NACo conference takeaways on ARPA processes, food security cold-storage grants, the Delta variant, and the expiration of the federal eviction moratorium before entering and returning from a closed session under attorney-client privilege.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Citizen Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton called the work session to order, read the public charge, and noted a 3:30 p.m. call scheduled with the Mayor and Public Health Director. Clerk Monica Wallace read one emailed citizen comment from Kimberly Israel opposing the reinstatement of COVID-19 masking and distancing restrictions.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review (Items 21-0449, 22-BC-007, 21-0454, and Related Contracts)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim County Manager Claudia Hager walked through items from the 20-item consent agenda ahead of the upcoming regular session. Commissioners questioned why the top-ranked vendor was not selected and why MWBE goals were not met on HVAC RFP 21-0449, heard library staff describe the Digital Navigators pilot (22-BC-007) at Stanford L. Warren with Digital Durham, reviewed a $3.3 million NCDHHS epidemiology/communicable disease grant (21-0454) and a $75,000 immunization grant, and clarified Board of Elections, DPS shelter MOA, Evergreen Services, and EMS billing fee amendments (21-0462).

agenda_items.title: Appointment of NCACC 114th Annual Conference Voting Delegate and Alternate
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle digest omission, the board took up appointing a voting delegate and alternate for the August 12–14 NCACC annual conference. Because Commissioner Heidi Carter switched to virtual attendance, Commissioner Nida Allam replaced Carter as alternate; Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs briefly asked about rotating the voting delegate role to newer commissioners, and the board agreed to continue rotating at future conferences. The board voted 5-0 to suspend the rules and 5-0 to appoint Chair Howerton as voting delegate and Commissioner Allam as alternate.

agenda_items.title: Commissioner Comments and Review of Directives
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Nida Allam yielded her comment time to Commissioner Nimasheena Burns, who reported on the NACo conference and praised Durham's ARPA planning relative to counties using full participatory budgeting. Commissioners also discussed a USDA cold-storage feasibility grant for food security, the Delta variant, and urging landlords to participate in rental assistance following expiration of the federal eviction moratorium, followed by a brief directives tracker check-in from Drew Cummings.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Attorney-Client Privilege)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 by roll call to enter closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with the county attorney and preserve attorney-client privilege. Upon returning at 05:59:32, Chair Howerton reported that the board met in closed session and gave direction to staff before adjourning 5-0.

meetings.title: Durham Board of County Commissioners Virtual Regular Session for July 12, 2021
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the July 12, 2021 virtual regular session of the Durham Board of County Commissioners (joining from the NACo annual conference alongside Commissioner Nimasheena Burns), with all five commissioners present. During public comments, the Durham County Racial Equity Core Team (GARE) submitted a letter criticizing the sudden removal of former County Manager Wendell Davis and requesting board racial equity training, mediation, equity tools, and an open town hall. The board unanimously approved June 14 minutes, welcomed new Chief Fire Marshal Jason B. Shepherd (21-0403), passed 13 consent items—including a 3% COLA pay band alignment (21-0439), the National Institute of Economic Development FY22 contract (21-0443), and a resolution authorizing up to $50 million in Series 2021 GO Bonds (21-0448)—announced board appointments, and returned from closed session to vote 5-0 approving an extended contract with up to an 11% salary increase for Clerk Monica Toomer.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, NACo Recognition, and GARE Citizen Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton called the virtual meeting to order (while attending NACo with Commissioner Burns), read the public charge, and Commissioner Allam led the Pledge of Allegiance. Clerk Monica Toomer read announcements on Main Library reopening July 20, 300 E. Main public art, a July 13 job fair, Triangle Bikeway, and the 2020 Community Health Assessment, while Burns and Howerton celebrated Board of Elections NACo awards and NACo DEI participation. Clerk Toomer then read a letter from the Durham County Racial Equity Core Team (GARE) questioning the sudden removal of former County Manager Wendell Davis and calling for board racial equity training/mediation per the Coleman report, improved interpersonal relations, equity tools across the strategic plan, and a public town hall, prompting Commissioner Burns to note employees are feeling strain nationwide.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (June 14, 2021 Regular Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed the June 14, 2021 regular session minutes with no edits or corrections. Vice Chair Jacobs moved and Commissioner Allam seconded approval, passing 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Item 21-0403: Introduction of Chief Fire Marshal Jason B. Shepherd
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Emergency Services Director Jim Groves introduced Jason B. Shepherd, formerly Orange County's Fire Marshal, who joined Durham County on June 21 as the new Chief Fire Marshal in the OES Fire Marshal Division. Commissioners Jacobs and Burns and Chair Howerton welcomed Shepherd and highlighted his state-level leadership.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (13 Items Including 3% COLA Pay Band Alignment, Institute Contract, and $50M GO Bond Series 2021)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim Manager Claudia Hager read 13 consent items including contracts with the Animal Protection Society (21-0420), food security contracts ($296,220 with BU Cafe/Eat NC and Farmer Foodshare, 21-0432), collection system capital reserves ($750,000, 21-0436), Durham Tech GO bond transfers ($580,339.98, 21-0438), a 3% COLA pay band adjustment (21-0439), the FY22 National Institute of Economic Development contract (21-0443), and a resolution authorizing up to $50 million in General Obligation Bonds Series 2021 (21-0448). Commissioner Burns praised Interim Manager Hager and Griffin & Strong for expanding MWBE/HUB support under Item 21-0443 without pulling the item, and the board approved all 13 items 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Acting County Attorney Willie Darby announced appointments to the ABC Board (Gail Adlin/Audlin, Ryan Hugohart), Dangerous Dog Committee (Mimi Davis, Michelle Diggs/Dixby), Durham County Women's Commission (Sherelle Thomas), and Juvenile Crime Prevention Council (John Morris).

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4), (a)(6)) and County Clerk Extended Contract Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) and (a)(6) for industrial/business incentive negotiations and personnel evaluation/contract matters. Returning to open session at 00:59:42, the board voted 5-0 to approve an extended contract for Clerk Monica Toomer effective July 1, 2021 with an up to 11% salary increase before adjourning 5-0 at 8:00 PM.

meetings.title: BOCC - June 28, 2021 Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton reconvened the June 28, 2021 regular session at 7:00 PM following closed session, with Interim County Manager Hager, Acting County Attorney Willie Darby, and all five commissioners participating (with Commissioner Nida Allam joining shortly after the opening). The board voted 5-0 to approve the May 24, 2021 minutes after Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs thanked residents for 133 written budget comments on school funding, mental health, and non-law enforcement crisis response, and introduced a 22-item consent agenda alongside a ceremonial Pride Proclamation. In subsequent portions captured in the digest, commissioners discussed broadband access pilot options and federal funding timing before announcing appointments across 14 boards and commissions. The board then voted 5-0 to enter closed session for property/contract negotiations, security/privileged information, and personnel matters, returning at 03:18:38 to report direction given to staff and adjourn.

agenda_items.title: Reconvening, Pledge of Allegiance, and Community Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton reconvened the June 28, 2021 regular session at 7:00 PM following closed session, noting the public charge had already been read and leading the Pledge of Allegiance; Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs noted Commissioner Nida Allam was running late. Clerk Monica read announcements covering the Triangle Bikeway Study, Durham Gang Reduction Strategy survey, Durham County Public Health COVID-19 vaccine walk-in hours, a Vets to Vets no-cost veterinary clinic, and July events at Durham County Stadium.

agenda_items.title: Approval of May 24, 2021 Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs thanked residents who submitted 31 pages (133 written comments) during the budget hearing addressing school funding, mental health services, and non-law enforcement crisis response services. Moved by Vice Chair Jacobs and seconded by Commissioner Nida Allam, the May 24, 2021 minutes were approved 5-0 by roll call.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (22 Items) and Ceremonial Pride Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Howerton introduced the 22-item consent agenda and a ceremonial Pride Proclamation, clarifying that a version oversight regarding the proclamation was hers rather than the clerk's. Subsequent consent agenda discussion and action occurred within the truncated middle portion of the transcript digest.

agenda_items.title: Broadband Access Gap and Federal Funding Timing Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed closing the county's broadband gap with staff member Greg, including pilot options, timelines, and recurring quarterly resident inquiries. Staff highlighted that waiting carefully over the next few months avoids prematurely spending roughly $3 million before federal broadband funding programs are announced.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Acting County Attorney Willie Darby reported the board's selections across 14 different boards and commissions, including William Bruce (education/communications), Sherry Taylor (public health), Wilson Sows (air quality/air resource), and Tonette Amos (jury commission). Chair Howerton thanked citizens for participating on county boards and commissions.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Property/Contracts, Privileged/Security Information, and Personnel)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Howerton and Clerk Monica read three statutory closed session bases: G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) for real property acquisition and employment contract negotiation terms, G.S. 143-318.11(a)(1) and G.S. 132-1.7(b) for privileged/confidential information and security/emergency procedures, and G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) for personnel matters. Moved by Commissioner Nimasheena Burns and seconded by Commissioner Nida Allam, the board voted 5-0 to enter closed session, reconvening at 03:18:38 after giving directions to staff and adjourning 5-0.

meetings.title: BOCC - June 28, 2021 Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton called the meeting to order at 7:00 PM (referencing July 12, 2021 in spoken remarks, though archived under the June 28, 2021 metadata record) with all five commissioners, Interim County Manager Hager, and Acting County Attorney Willie Darby present. Following community announcements, recognitions for the Board of Elections and NACo leadership, and the start of a public comment from the Durham County Racial Equity Core Team (GARE), the board voted 5-0 to approve the consent agenda, including a 3% COLA pay band adjustment, a $41,900 ClearPoint software contract renewal, the FY 2022 National Institute of Economic Development contract, and a not-to-exceed $50 million General Obligation Bond Series 2021 resolution. After announcing board and commission appointments and meeting in closed session on economic development incentives and personnel, the board voted 5-0 to approve a contract for the Clerk to the Board effective July 1, 2021 with an up-to-11% salary increase.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Community Announcements, and Board Recognitions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton opened the session (stating July 12, 2021 in spoken remarks) and read the public charge, with Commissioner Nida Allam leading the Pledge of Allegiance. Clerk Monica read announcements covering a public art survey for the East Main Street parking deck, a Discover Durham/American Tobacco Campus job fair, the Triangle Bikeway Study survey, and the final 2020 Community Health Assessment. Commissioners also recognized the Durham County Board of Elections (including Nikita Reese) for recent awards and noted NACo election leadership.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment: Durham County Racial Equity Core Team (GARE)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk Monica began reading a submitted public comment letter from the Durham County Racial Equity Core Team / Government Alliance on Race and Equity (GARE). The remainder of the public comment was omitted in the middle truncation of the transcript digest.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 21-0439, 21-0442, 21-043, 21-048, and Newton Building Transfers)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim County Manager Hager read consent items including Newton Building project transfers, item 21-0439 aligning salary pay bands with the 3% COLA in the adopted budget, item 21-0442 renewing Ascendant Strategy's ClearPoint software contract ($41,900), item 21-043 approving the FY 2022 National Institute of Economic Development contract, and item 21-048 authorizing up to $50 million in General Obligation Bonds, Series 2021. Commissioner Nimasheena Burns offered brief remarks without pulling item 21-043, highlighting HUB visibility and opportunities for women-owned, small, and minority-owned businesses. The consent agenda passed 5-0 by roll call.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Acting County Attorney Willie Darby reported the board's appointments across four bodies: Gail Audlin/Atlan and Ryan Eugerhart (ABC Board), Mimi Davis and Michelle Dixby (Dangerous Dog Committee), Sherelle Thomas (Durham County Women's Commission), and John Morris (Juvenile Crime Prevention Council). Chair Howerton congratulated the appointees and thanked them for their service.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Economic Development Incentives and Personnel)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board was requested to enter closed session to discuss economic development incentives offered in negotiations and personnel matters under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6). Moved by Commissioner Heidi Carter and seconded by Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs, the motion passed 5-0 by roll call.

agenda_items.title: Post-Closed Session Action: Clerk Contract with Up to 11% Salary Increase
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Returning from closed session, the board considered entering into a contract for the Clerk to the Board effective July 1, 2021 with an increase of up to 11% of her current salary. Moved by Commissioner Nida Allam and seconded by Commissioner Heidi Carter, the contract passed 5-0 by roll call before the board adjourned at 8:00 PM.

meetings.title: BOCC - June 14, 2021 Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the June 14, 2021 regular session, which opened with community announcements, recognition of the county's upcoming Juneteenth holiday on June 18, unanimous 5-0 approval of the May 10 regular session minutes, and a ceremonial proclamation marking the 12th Anniversary of World Sickle Cell Awareness Day (21-0396). Interim County Manager Claudia Hager pulled item 21-0339 for a contract modification and read five newly added consent items covering an NCDOT road maintenance abandonment (21-0387), senior meal delivery (21-0388), Lincoln Community Health Center ARPA-funded renovations (21-0397), temporary COVID-19 screening staffing (21-0400), and Durham Housing Authority summer learning camps (21-0380 / 21-BCC-0115). Following a middle digest gap, the board heard a joint presentation from Discover Durham, the Durham Convention Center, Durham Arts Council, and Zweli's Restaurant and voted 5-0 to approve Budget Ordinance Amendment 21-BCC-0116 allocating $239,700 toward hospitality workforce recovery, expanded leisure marketing, and a convention center campus initiative, before holding a closed session on personnel matters with no action taken.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Juneteenth Recognition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton called the meeting to order, read the public charge, and led the Pledge of Allegiance. Clerk Monica Wallace read announcements covering Library Summer of Learning and DPS summer meals, the Emergency Rental Assistance Program, DCHC MPO transportation feedback, Community Health Coalition utility assistance, and a public health blood drive, and Chair Howerton recognized the upcoming June 18 county closure for Juneteenth.

agenda_items.title: Approval of May 10, 2021 Regular Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Howerton presented the May 10, 2021 regular session minutes for approval with no edits offered. The board approved the minutes 5-0 by roll call.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Item 21-0396: 12th Anniversary of World Sickle Cell Awareness Day
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board presented proclamation 21-0396 recognizing the 12th Anniversary of World Sickle Cell Awareness Day and highlighting collaborative clinical, educational, and community support efforts for individuals living with sickle cell disease.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review (Including Items 21-0387, 21-0388, 21-0397, 21-0400, and 21-0380)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim County Manager Claudia Hager pulled item 21-0339 (Southern Repair Services COVID homeless housing contract) to return June 28 after modification, and read five new consent items: NCDOT abandonment of 0.91 mile of SR 1680 / Mickey Dam Road (21-0387), a $243,720 food-delivery contract (21-0388), consent for ARPA-funded HVAC and parking renovations under $500,000 at Lincoln Community Health Center (21-0397), $121,580 for temporary COVID-19 screening staff (21-0400), and Budget Ordinance Amendment 21-BCC-0115 appropriating $270,101 of general fund balance for DHA summer learning camps (21-0380). Commissioners praised the nonprofit partnerships; subsequent consent and budget actions fell inside the omitted middle digest segment.

agenda_items.title: Discover Durham Funding Request and Budget Ordinance Amendment 21-BCC-0116 ($239,700)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Discover Durham CEO Susan Amey, Durham Convention Center GM Rebecca Bolton, Durham Arts Council ED Sherry DeVries, and Zweli's Restaurant owner Leonardo Williams presented three pandemic-recovery proposals split 50/50 with the City of Durham: hospitality workforce job fairs and training ($33,500 total), expanded leisure-travel marketing ($250,000 total), and a downtown convention center campus activation linking the Convention Center, Armory, Marriott, Arts Council, and Carolina Theatre. Commissioner Nimasheena Burns requested clearer program timetables while praising the four-corners arts campus concept, Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs praised the campus approach and workforce focus, and the board approved the $239,700 allocation 5-0 by roll call.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Personnel Qualifications and Performance)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 by roll call to enter closed session pursuant to G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) regarding personnel qualifications, competence, performance, or employment conditions. Upon reconvening at 02:43:17, the board reported no action was taken in closed session and voted 5-0 to adjourn.

meetings.title: BOCC - June 7, 2021 Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the June 7, 2021 work session, Chair Brenda A. Howerton and the board heard numerous emailed citizen comments ahead of budget adoption, reflecting competing community views on Sheriff's Office funding versus redirecting public safety dollars to community health, alongside requests for Route 9 transit justice infrastructure, Black maternal health doula partnerships, and My Brother's Keeper ARPA funding. After reviewing the 37-item consent agenda and receiving a Comprehensive Plan update focused on resident-centered planning, the board voted 5-0 to suspend the rules and 5-0 to approve a $1,000,000 economic development allocation to Carcigen Therapeutics (21-0375). The board also received a directives review and board appointment results, then met in closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) and (a)(6). Returning to open session, commissioners voted unanimously 5-0 on three administrative actions: accepting Interim County Manager Claudia Hager's contract, issuing a training RFP, and approving a 20% salary increase for Acting County Attorney Willie Darby retroactive to March 25, 2021.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Emailed Citizen Comments on Budget Priorities
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton called the meeting to order and Clerk Monica Wallace read emailed public comments covering Route 9 transit justice (Stella Adams), former manager/school budget transparency (Sheila Huggins, Angelique Stallings), Black maternal health and doula inclusion (Joy Foster), and the My Brother's Keeper $5 million ARPA request. Competing public safety comments included Jeremy Roth backing the People's Alliance proposal to redirect law enforcement funds to community health and seven commenters opposing a 10% Sheriff's Office cut while urging full funding for vehicles, a 3% COLA, and CIT training support.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review (37 Items)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim County Manager Claudia Hager began walking commissioners through the 37-item consent agenda, starting with item 21-0262 (a Memorandum of Agreement with Triangle J Council of Governments for regional planning and technical assistance). Remaining consent review occurred in the middle digest omission.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan and Resident-Focused Planning Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff addressed commissioner questions regarding concerns with the 2005 tier system and described a departmental commitment to shift away from developer-focused processes toward a resident-focused, resident-serving Comprehensive Plan that expands resident voice in land-use decisions.

agenda_items.title: Item 21-0375: Public Hearing Closing and $1,000,000 Economic Development Allocation to Carcigen Therapeutics
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Howerton closed the public hearing first opened on May 25 regarding a $1,000,000 economic development allocation to Carcigen Therapeutics, with Clerk Monica Wallace confirming no public comments were received. The board voted 5-0 by roll call to suspend the rules and 5-0 by roll call to approve the $1,000,000 allocation and authorize the Interim County Manager to enter preliminary negotiations and execute an agreement.

agenda_items.title: Review of Commissioner Directives and Board/Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Drew Cummings presented the commissioner directives tracking document, and Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs inquired about timing for a follow-up on the February 21 tax rebound directive. Senior Assistant/Acting County Attorney Willie Darby then announced results from the May 24 board and commission ballots, including the Durham County Hospital Corporation Board physician representative (Bryson) and Shannon Casey to the Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Post-Closed-Session Actions (Interim Manager Contract, Training RFP, Acting County Attorney Pay)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) (economic development incentives) and (a)(6) (public officer/employee qualifications and performance). After reconvening at 06:45:31, the board voted 5-0 on three separate motions: accepting the offered contract for Interim County Manager Claudia Hager, issuing an RFP for training, and increasing Acting County Attorney Willie Darby's salary by 20% effective March 25, 2021 while he serves in the acting role.

meetings.title: BOCC - Budget Work Session: Day 4
meetings.executive_summary: During Day 4 of the FY2021-22 budget work sessions (addressed by Chair Brenda A. Howerton on June 3, 2021 and published June 4, 2021), commissioners reviewed Durham County's behavioral health infrastructure and the budget add/delete list with no formal votes taken. Criminal Justice Resource Center Director Gudrun Parmer and Behavioral Health stakeholders reviewed the Stepping Up Initiative, sequential intercept mapping, mental health court, and diversion gaps. A policy disagreement emerged when an unidentified commissioner suggested freezing unfilled Sheriff's Office positions to fund unarmed behavioral health crisis responders, which the Durham County Sheriff strongly opposed amid high gun-violence rates and staffing vacancies, advocating instead for federal ARPA/CARES funding and a law-enforcement-centered co-responder model. Later in the session, commissioners and staff discussed base budget revenue growth, the Master Aging Plan placeholder, deliverables for the Black Chamber of Commerce request, shifting resources from the underutilized tax deferral program to the tax grant program, and late fund-balance adjustments for RTP tax valuations and Risk Management insurance premiums before canceling the June 9 session.

agenda_items.title: Item 20-3078: Behavioral Health Infrastructure and Crisis Response Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Gudrun Parmer and behavioral health partners reviewed the 2015 Stepping Up Initiative resolution, sequential intercept mapping, de-escalation training, mental health court, and LME/MCO coordination with Alliance. Debate arose over crisis response staffing: an unidentified commissioner proposed testing an unarmed behavioral health/paramedicine response by freezing unfilled law enforcement positions, while the Sheriff opposed any position freezes or 10% budget cut given nearly 1,000 shootings and existing vacancies, urging ARPA/CARES funding and law enforcement participation in co-responder design.

agenda_items.title: Budget Add/Delete List, Tax Relief Programs, and Late Fund Adjustments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle digest omission, Interim Manager Claudia Hager and budget staff reviewed the add/delete list and base budget philosophy that tax increases should be an absolute last choice. Commissioner Heidi Carter and another commissioner questioned deliverables on the Black Chamber of Commerce proposal; Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs asked whether staffing from the tax deferral program (which had only one applicant) could shift toward the tax grant program; and David Ades presented fund-balance-covered adjustments for the RTP special district valuation and a Risk Management insurance premium increase, before the board agreed to drop the June 9 work session and adjourn ahead of June 14 budget adoption.

disagreements.issue: Freezing Unfilled Law Enforcement Positions to Fund Unarmed Behavioral Health Crisis Responders
disagreements.summary: During the behavioral health infrastructure presentation, an unidentified commissioner and the Durham County Sheriff disagreed over whether unfilled Sheriff's Office positions should be frozen to fund behavioral health crisis response specialists versus using federal ARPA/CARES funds while keeping law enforcement centered in co-responder models.
disagreements.side_a_position: Freeze unfilled law enforcement positions and reallocate duties to behavioral health specialists for non-armed crisis response.
side_a_arguments: Communities are asking to decriminalize behavioral health challenges, poverty, and homelessness and reduce racial bias in crisis response.
Reorganizing unfilled positions rather than cutting filled roles avoids punitive action against officers while scaling non-armed response such as paramedicine.
disagreements.side_b_position: Do not freeze Sheriff's Office positions or cut 10% of the Sheriff's budget; fund behavioral health response with ARPA/CARES dollars and include law enforcement at the center of co-responder models.
side_b_arguments: The Sheriff's Office is already short-staffed amid nearly 1,000 shootings and over 129 shooting victims in Durham's Black and brown communities.
Ample federal CARES and American Rescue Plan funds are available for behavioral health initiatives, and established models like CAHOOTS operate in coordination with law enforcement.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken during the work session; both sides agreed on continuing collaboration around crisis response models.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2021-06-03 1:30 PM - Budget Work Session - Day 4
meetings.executive_summary: At the June 3, 2021 Budget Work Session (Day 4) presided over by Chair Brenda A. Howerton with all five commissioners present, the Board reviewed Item 20-0378 on Durham County's behavioral health infrastructure and the Stepping Up Initiative alongside Interim County Manager Claudia Hager, LME/MCO mental health leadership, and the Durham County Sheriff. A sharp policy disagreement emerged over how to fund an alternative crisis response model: the Sheriff opposed freezing vacant law enforcement positions or shifting 10% of the Sheriff's Office budget—urging federal CARES/Recovery Act funding instead and criticizing law enforcement's exclusion from the Community Safety and Wellness Task Force—while a commissioner argued that reorganizing unfilled law enforcement positions into behavioral health specialists would reduce harmful armed encounters and free deputies to fight violent crime. Later in the session, commissioners reviewed the budget add/delete list, with Commissioner Heidi Carter and another member questioning deliverables in the Black Chamber of Commerce proposal and Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs inquiring whether three tax-deferral positions (with only one applicant) could shift savings toward the joint City-County tax grant program. Finance staff also briefed the Board on RTP district fund-balance adjustments, a $700,000 Risk Management insurance premium increase covered from fund balance, deferring an ARPA broadband update to June 24, and cancelling the June 9 work session ahead of June 14 budget adoption; no formal votes were taken.

agenda_items.title: Item 20-0378: Behavioral Health Infrastructure, Stepping Up Initiative, and Alternative Crisis Response Debate
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim County Manager Claudia Hager introduced Item 20-0378 reviewing Durham County's Stepping Up Initiative (established by BOCC resolution on June 8, 2015), CIT/de-escalation training, 911 call routing, uninsured resident access, and LME/MCO outreach gaps. Commissioners and the Durham County Sheriff debated alternative crisis response funding: the Sheriff strongly opposed freezing unfilled deputy positions or cutting 10% of his budget amid nearly 1,000 shootings and advocated using federal CARES or Recovery Act funds, while a commissioner defended reorganizing vacant positions into behavioral health specialists to decriminalize mental health, poverty, and homelessness and free armed officers for crime fighting.

agenda_items.title: Budget Add/Delete List, Master Aging Plan, Black Chamber Deliverables, and Tax Grant Staffing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and commissioners discussed keeping tax increases as a last resort, placing a placeholder for the late Master Aging Plan request awaiting City budget coordination, and evaluating summer youth programming capacity. Commissioner Heidi Carter and a colleague questioned deliverables in the Black Chamber of Commerce proposal and asked to follow up with staff, while Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs asked whether savings from three staff positions originally budgeted for the tax deferral program (which drew only one applicant) could help fund the joint City-County low-income homeowner tax grant program.

agenda_items.title: RTP District & Risk Management Fund Adjustments and Budget Calendar Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget staff member David Aves reported two late adjustments outside the general fund: using RTP special district fund balance to offset updated tax valuations, and using Risk Management fund balance to cover a $700,000 spike in insurance premiums for the coming year (flagging future general fund pressure). Staff and commissioners agreed to move an ARPA-funded broadband discussion to June 24 and cancel the June 9 work session ahead of the June 14 budget adoption.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners on 2021-06-03 1:30 PM - Budget Work Session - Day 4
disagreements.issue: Behavioral Health Crisis Response Funding: Freezing Sheriff's Office Positions vs. Federal Relief Funds
disagreements.summary: During the behavioral health infrastructure work session, the Durham County Sheriff and a County Commissioner disagreed over whether to reorganize unfilled law enforcement positions into behavioral health crisis response roles or rely strictly on state/federal relief funds while keeping law enforcement centered in co-responder models.
disagreements.side_a_position: Do not freeze law enforcement positions or shift 10% of the Sheriff's budget; fund behavioral health crisis response with federal CARES/Recovery Act or state funds and include law enforcement centrally.
side_a_arguments: The Sheriff's Office is already short-staffed while Durham experienced nearly 1,000 shootings and over 129 shooting victims in the prior year.
Federal CARES Act and Recovery Act funds are available for behavioral health infrastructure without cutting public safety staffing.
Excluding law enforcement from Community Safety and Wellness Task Force discussions is a mistake because 911 data and co-responder models such as CAHOOTS rely on law enforcement partnership.
disagreements.side_b_position: Reorganize unfilled law enforcement positions into behavioral health specialists to reduce armed police responses to mental health, poverty, and homelessness calls.
side_b_arguments: Black and brown communities experience disproportionate harm from armed law enforcement encounters in behavioral health crises.
Freezing an unfilled position and shifting duties to a behavioral health specialist is a reorganization rather than a punitive budget cut, freeing armed deputies to focus on violent crime.
The County should collaborate with Stepping Up Initiative stakeholders and the Community Safety and Wellness Task Force to pilot a new crisis response model.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken during the work session; the Sheriff's Office position was voiced by the Durham County Sheriff (non-voting county official) and the counter-position by an unidentified Commissioner in the transcript, with discussion continuing toward the Stepping Up Initiative and Community Safety and Wellness Task Force.

meetings.title: BOCC - Budget Work Session: Day 3
meetings.executive_summary: At Day 3 of the FY2021-22 budget work sessions on June 1, 2021, Chair Brenda A. Howerton and commissioners reviewed workforce development, employee compensation, and community violence intervention proposals with no formal votes taken. Durham Technical Community College President JB Buxton presented the $500,000 manager-recommended request and potential ARPA expansion for the 'Back to Work' short-term training program and the 'BULLS' life sciences pipeline for young adults of color, including wraparound stipends for childcare and transportation. Commissioners and HR/budget staff then examined county salary competitiveness, lagging 2017 pay bands, longevity pay, and the balance between rising personnel costs (~85% of the county budget) and lifting wages for the 47% of county workers earning $49,000 or less. Finally, General Manager Joanne Pierce outlined plans to consolidate Bull City United, My Brother's Keeper, and Project BUILD into a new department expanding from 16 to 36 staff in partnership with Cure Violence Global before the board adjourned.

agenda_items.title: Item 21-0364: Durham Technical Community College Budget Request (Back to Work & BULLS)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham Tech President JB Buxton presented the college's workforce recovery budget request centered on two initiatives: 'Back to Work' (short-term 6–8 week courses under $1,000 with $500 scholarships and wraparound stipends for childcare, transportation, and books) and 'BULLS' (biowork and life sciences training, coaching, and job placement for 18–24-year-old students of color and opportunity youth). Buxton detailed how the $500,000 in the manager's recommended budget plus potential one-time federal ARPA dollars could fund facility renovations, campus planning, direct student stipends, and specialized corporate and financial aid staffing.

agenda_items.title: County Employee Compensation, Market Bands, and Workforce Retention
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle digest omission, HR and budget staff reviewed how county pay bands based on 2017 data continued to lag peer jurisdictions even after a 3% band adjustment, alongside prior hazard/risk adjustments for public safety, DSS, and EMS and the potential return of longevity pay. Commissioners noted that personnel accounts for roughly 85% of the county budget—requiring careful sustainability planning for new positions—while emphasizing that 47% of employees earn $49,000 or less annually and must be prioritized to reduce turnover.

agenda_items.title: New Departmental Structure for Bull City United, My Brother's Keeper, and Project BUILD
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Manager Joanne Pierce presented the organizational plan to unify Bull City United, My Brother's Keeper, and Project BUILD into a single new department following City Council (March) and BOCC (April) interlocal funding approvals. Working with Cure Violence Global, the expansion increases total staffing from 16 to 36 positions, adding a department administrator and a data analyst to manage grant compliance and public reporting, with the next quarterly report due July 31.

agenda_items.title: Schedule Preview, Research Triangle Foundation Tour, and Closing Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim County Manager Claudia Hager previewed upcoming work sessions on June 3 and June 9 (including a possible ARPA broadband update) and staff noted a future tour opportunity at Research Triangle Foundation's Boxyard project. Commissioner Nida Allam wished LGBTQIA residents and staff a Happy Pride, Chair Howerton acknowledged Memorial Day, and the meeting adjourned without a vote.

meetings.title: BOCC - May 27, 2021 - Budget Work Session Day 2
meetings.executive_summary: During Day 2 of the FY2021-22 budget work sessions on May 27, 2021, Interim County Manager Claudia Hager and early childhood staff briefed the board on American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funding rules and early childhood pandemic impacts, with no formal votes taken. Hager outlined Durham County's $62.4 million ARPA allocation, federal obligation (December 31, 2024) and expenditure (2026) deadlines, GFOA guidance prioritizing FEMA reimbursements and one-time or transitional investments, and ~$2.9 million in initial FY22 ARPA allocations alongside candidate priorities such as $750,000 in homeowner tax relief, housing, behavioral health, Durham Tech workforce programs, food security, and Pre-K/K-12. Early childhood presenter Kate then detailed pandemic childcare closures, a 200% spike in diaper need, and early brain-development impacts, prompting Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs and Budget Director Keith Lane to verify funding for Reach Out and Read ($50,000), Wash and Learn, and Article 46 Pre-K revenue before previewing the June 3 behavioral health work session.

agenda_items.title: American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) Allocation Framework and FY22 Priorities
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim County Manager Claudia Hager briefed the board on Durham County's $62.4 million ARPA allocation (half expected in June 2021 and half in 2022), eligible spending categories, U.S. Treasury reporting timelines, and GFOA best practices such as maximizing FEMA reimbursements, focusing on one-time or phased investments, centering equity and MWBE support, and coordinating community engagement with the City and Durham Public Schools. She reviewed ~$2.9 million already identified in the FY22 budget for COVID cleaning, screening security, and revenue losses ($48,000 and $265,000 court facility fees) plus candidate uses including $750,000 for DSS long-term homeowner relief (<=30% AMI), non-congregate housing, vaccine equity, behavioral health, workforce development, business support, food insecurity, and Pre-K/K-12.

agenda_items.title: COVID-19 Impacts on Early Childhood Systems and ARPA Opportunities
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle digest omission, early childhood lead Kate presented pandemic impacts on Durham's early childhood sector, including permanent childcare closures, lower enrollment, staff burnout, a greater than 200% surge in diaper need, and housing/food instability affecting ages 0–5. Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs asked for budget clarity on Reach Out and Read and Wash and Learn, highlighted Cooperative Extension's Welcome Baby and diaper demand, and noted Article 46 sales tax generated ~$75,000 for Pre-K, while Commissioners Nimasheena Burns and Chair Howerton emphasized aligning federal/state grants for early childhood.

agenda_items.title: June 3 Behavioral Health Session Preview and Budget Schedule Confirmation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff member Jody previewed the June 3 behavioral health work session involving Gudrun Parmer (Stepping Up Initiative), DSS, Public Health, CJRC, the Sheriff's Office, and Alliance. Budget Director Keith Lane confirmed $50,000 was budgeted for Reach Out and Read and committed to confirming Wash and Learn via email, and Interim Manager Hager announced the June 1 and June 3 budget session times before the board adjourned.

meetings.executive_summary: In this second stream recording of the May 24, 2021 regular session, Chair Brenda A. Howerton opened the meeting at 00:12:52 with the public charge, Pledge of Allegiance, and community announcements, followed by the minutes motion (whose roll call was truncated in the digest) and the introduction of Food Security Coordinator Mary Oxendine. The board unanimously approved the five-item consent agenda (5-0)—including $100,000 for GRAIL, $3.21 million for Snow Hill Pump Station, NC Farm School funding, April tax releases, and the Vines Architecture contract—and approved street-renaming item 21-0311 (Palmer Way to Alexandria Way) by a 5-0 roll-call vote before introducing UDO text amendment 21-0312 prior to a middle digest truncation. Later segments captured the COVID-19 Public Health Focus update (21-0318, reporting 142,841 fully vaccinated or 44.4% of Durham residents), the Board of Elections facility needs presentation, deferral of board appointment ballot results to June 7, and a unanimous 5-0 vote to enter closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) before reconvening and adjourning.

meetings.title: BOCC Budget Work Session - Day 1
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over Day 1 of the Board of County Commissioners' FY2021-22 budget work session, held with all five seated commissioners and newly appointed Interim County Manager Claudia Hager following an earlier joint morning session with the Durham Public Schools (DPS) Board of Education. Budget Director Keith Lane and Hager reviewed the $18 million DPS request—of which the recommended budget funded roughly $8.2 million in new current expense and capital dollars—and led extensive discussion on DPS's late request for 20 additional school nurses and social workers, with commissioners favoring housing school nurses in the County Public Health Department on a phased hiring timeline to avoid the roughly 28% charter school per-pupil surcharge. Commissioners also debated community safety and mental health funding ahead of upcoming work sessions, with Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs proposing a crisis-response gaps analysis while Chair Howerton and Commissioner Nimasheena Burns urged consulting the new Community Safety and Wellness Task Force co-chairs and recognizing existing county mental health spending before shifting Sheriff's Office funds. Additional commissioner priorities flagged for subsequent May and June work sessions included Durham Pre-K, the Early Childhood Action Plan, Master Aging Plan staffing, northern Durham broadband via ARPA funds, coordinator role consolidation, and a shared county-city TV studio upgrade. No formal votes were taken during this informational work session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Budget Work Session Schedule Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton called the Day 1 budget work session to order (noting it followed the morning joint session with the Durham Public Schools Board of Education). Interim County Manager Claudia Hager and Budget Director Keith Lane outlined the tentative work session calendar: May 24 budget public hearing, May 27 ARPA next-steps framework, vaccine equity proposal, DSS Medicaid support, and low-income homeowner tax subsidy (<=30% AMI), June 1 economic development, Durham Tech, Office of Sheriff peer comparisons, and maternal health infrastructure, plus a June 3 placeholder.

agenda_items.title: Durham Public Schools (DPS) Budget Request, School Nurses, and Federal ARPA Strategy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Keith Lane explained that of DPS's $18 million funding request, the recommended budget included $7 million in general current expense plus $1.9 million for $15/hour wages and $1.13 million in additional current capital (bringing current capital to $4.5 million toward a $6 million request). Staff and commissioners discussed DPS's late request for 20 additional school nurses and social workers (roughly 18 nurses and 2–3 social workers), agreeing in principle to explore hiring nurses through the County Public Health Department on a phased schedule to avoid the 28% charter school pass-through surcharge and navigate regional nursing shortages. Interim Manager Hager also noted using one-time ARPA funds (~$1.2M for custodial cleaning) to avoid ongoing tax shocks, while Commissioners Carter, Jacobs, and Allam requested follow-up on English language learners, students with disabilities, IT refresh needs, and per-square-foot capital expenditure comparisons.

agenda_items.title: Community Safety and Wellness Task Force, Crisis Response Gaps Analysis, and Sheriff's Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter asked staff to consider packaging existing upstream safety and wellness programs across departments so the board and community—including advocates from Durham Beyond Policing and Durham For All—could assess current resources before shifting positions away from the Office of the Sheriff. Commissioner Nimasheena Burns cited CJRC Director Gudrun Parmer's preliminary mapping, legal mandates governing law enforcement calls, and roughly $30–40 million in existing county mental health spending (including jail clinical staff), urging concrete staffing plans rather than cutting the Sheriff's budget in a vacuum. Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs suggested funding a comprehensive gaps analysis of the crisis response system in the upcoming budget, and Chair Howerton asked Interim Manager Hager to consult the task force co-chairs.

agenda_items.title: Additional Commissioner Budget Priorities, Coordinator Review, and TV Studio Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners Carter and Jacobs highlighted early childhood priorities (Durham Pre-K, Reach Out and Read, Early Childhood Action Plan), the sustainability plan, Master Aging Plan staffing, language equity, and broadband expansion. Chair Howerton emphasized northern Durham broadband, climate, maternal health, and reviewing whether separate coordinator positions across county programs could be consolidated after budget season. General Manager Deborah Craig-Ray and Perry Mann also updated the board on using leftover Admin II capital funds to upgrade the county TV studio in a no-money broadcast-swap partnership with the City of Durham.

Regarding a late DPS request for roughly 20 school nurses and social workers, the Manager recommended hiring any added school nurses through the County rather than DPS current expense to avoid an automatic 20% charter school pass-through cost, while cautioning against using one-time fund balance or federal funds for ongoing school operating expenses.
