meetings.title: BOCC - Special Session - May 13, 2021
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the contentious May 13, 2021 special session with all five commissioners, Acting County Attorney Willie Darby, and outside counsel Denise Smith Klein present. After voting 5-0 to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3), the board returned to open session and passed three deeply divided 3-2 votes initiated by Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs: (1) not renewing County Manager Wendell Davis's contract, terminating it effective June 29, 2021 (Ayes: Nida Allam, Heidi Carter, Wendy Jacobs; Nays: Nimasheena Burns, Brenda A. Howerton); (2) relieving Davis of his duties effective immediately pending appointment of an interim manager (Ayes: Nida Allam, Heidi Carter, Wendy Jacobs; Nays: Nimasheena Burns, Brenda A. Howerton); and (3) extending outside attorney Denise Smith Klein's contract to execute the board's decisions (Ayes: Nida Allam, Heidi Carter, Wendy Jacobs; Nays: Nimasheena Burns, Brenda A. Howerton). During debate, Chair Howerton and Commissioner Burns sharply condemned the non-renewal as retaliatory, racially motivated, and lacking merit or a formal performance appraisal, while also objecting that the outside counsel extension lacked a confirmed total cost. A final motion to adjourn was also contested on roll call, passing with Nida Allam, Heidi Carter, and Wendy Jacobs voting Aye, Nimasheena Burns voting No, and Chair Howerton declaring the motion carried and adjourning the meeting.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton called the May 13, 2021 special session to order, read the public charge, and cited N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with legal counsel (Acting County Attorney Willie Darby and outside attorney Denise Smith Klein). On a motion by Commissioner Heidi Carter seconded by Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs, the board entered closed session 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Non-Renewal of County Manager Wendell Davis's Employment Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Upon returning to open session, Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs moved under Section 4 of the County Manager's contract not to renew the agreement, terminating it on June 29, 2021 while complying with all contractual obligations. Chair Brenda A. Howerton stated the decision was made without discussion with Black board members and praised Davis's seven-year record on finances and schools, while Commissioner Nimasheena Burns read a prepared statement condemning the motion as racially motivated retaliation following Davis's 2020 racial bias complaint and citing the Coleman Report and lack of a performance appraisal. The motion passed 3-2 on roll call.

agenda_items.title: Immediate Relief of County Manager Duties
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs moved to relieve County Manager Wendell Davis of his duties effective immediately and proceed to appoint an interim county manager. Following a second, the board approved the motion 3-2 on a roll-call vote with Nida Allam, Heidi Carter, and Wendy Jacobs in favor and Nimasheena Burns and Brenda A. Howerton opposed.

agenda_items.title: Extension of Outside Counsel Denise Smith Klein's Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs moved to extend outside attorney Denise Smith Klein's existing contract to assist with executing the board's decisions and obligations, clarified as an extension at her existing hourly rate after Acting Attorney Willie Darby advised an RFP was not required to extend an existing contract. Chair Howerton and Commissioner Burns objected that no price cap or confirmed rate for expanded services had been provided and warned of wasted funds and litigation risk, while Commissioner Carter affirmed her readiness and seconded the motion. The motion passed 3-2.

agenda_items.title: Contested Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After Acting Attorney Darby noted Klein could decline the extension terms if she wished (requiring renegotiation), a motion to adjourn was made and seconded. On roll call, Commissioners Allam, Carter, and Jacobs voted Aye, Commissioner Burns voted No, and Chair Howerton declared the vote carried and adjourned the meeting.

disagreements.issue: Non-Renewal and Immediate Relief of County Manager Wendell Davis
disagreements.summary: The board split 3-2 over Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs's motions to not renew County Manager Wendell Davis's contract (terminating June 29, 2021) and to relieve him of his duties immediately.
disagreements.side_a_position: Exercise Section 4 of the County Manager's contract to not renew his agreement and relieve him of duties immediately pending an interim appointment.
side_a_arguments: Board has contractual authority under Section 4 to decide on non-renewal and comply with all contract obligations.
Board needed an immediate transition to an interim county manager.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose non-renewal and immediate removal as unwarranted, racially motivated, and procedurally unfair.
side_b_arguments: Decision was made without consulting Black board members and without completing a formal performance appraisal or board training.
Wendell Davis maintained seven straight years of strong county financial standing and school-building progress.
Action constituted retaliation for Davis and county staff raising racial bias concerns, while failing to implement Coleman Report and Racial Equity Task Force recommendations.
disagreements.resolution: Both motions passed 3-2 on roll-call votes (Ayes: Allam, Carter, Jacobs; Nays: Burns, Howerton).

disagreements.issue: Extension of Outside Attorney Denise Smith Klein's Contract Without Confirmed Total Cost
disagreements.summary: Commissioners split 3-2 over extending outside counsel Denise Smith Klein's contract to assist with executing the manager contract termination and related obligations.
disagreements.side_a_position: Extend Klein's existing contract at her existing hourly rate to assist with executing all obligations flowing from the board's decisions.
side_a_arguments: Acting County Attorney Willie Darby advised that extending an existing contract did not require a new RFP.
An existing hourly rate was already set in Klein's current engagement, making the motion sufficiently definite.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose extending the contract without a confirmed cost ceiling, RFP, or Klein's confirmation of rates for expanded scope.
side_b_arguments: Klein's prior contract covered only document review, whereas execution work could entail different costs.
Voting on a contract without a defined price or prior board discussion of cost violates sound fiscal stewardship and risks litigation.
disagreements.resolution: Motion passed 3-2 (Ayes: Allam, Carter, Jacobs; Nays: Burns, Howerton), with Acting Attorney Darby noting Klein could decline the extension terms.

meetings.title: BOCC May10 2021  Durham County
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the May 10, 2021 regular session of the Durham Board of County Commissioners (captured in this recording starting mid-announcements), with all five commissioners present. The board unanimously approved prior minutes (5-0), issued four ceremonial proclamations (Children's Mental Health Awareness Month, Cooperative Extension Week, Older Americans Month, and National Foster Care Month), recognized the Board of Elections for winning a U.S. Election Assistance Commission 2020 Clearinghouse Award, and approved all 14 consent agenda items 5-0, including $12.438 million for IS&T capital modernization and $92.785 million in limited obligation bonds for Northern High School. Public Health Director Rod Jenkins reported declining COVID-19 case trends alongside FDA emergency use authorization for Pfizer vaccinations for ages 12 and older, and County Manager Wendell Davis presented the proposed ~$730 million FY2021-22 recommended budget featuring a 1-cent general fund property tax increase, 3% employee COLA plus merit pay reinstatement, $163.3 million for Durham Public Schools, and $750,000 for a long-time homeowner tax relief grant program. The board also received annual reports from the Appearance Commission and Open Space and Trails Commission and held public hearings on Palmer Way renaming and UDO Omnibus Text Amendment TC2100001, leaving both open for 24-hour comment ahead of May 24 votes.

agenda_items.title: Announcements and Commissioner Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: This recording begins mid-announcements as Clerk Monica Toomer read notices on Food for Durham, Real ID enforcement updates, DCHC MPO long-range transportation plan comments, and a workaround link after a technical glitch delayed the Durham Emergency Rental Assistance Program (ERAP) launch. Commissioners thanked nurses for National Nurses Week, praised DSS Director Ben Rose and staff member Janine Gordon for ERAP rollout efforts, and Commissioner Nida Allam shared mutual-aid resources for COVID-19 relief in India.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (April 5 Work Session and April 12 Regular Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board considered the minutes of the April 5, 2021 work session and April 12, 2021 regular session without edits. Commissioner Heidi Carter moved approval, seconded by Commissioner Nida Allam, and the minutes passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations (Mental Health, Cooperative Extension, Older Americans, Foster Care) and Board of Elections Award
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners read four proclamations: Children's Mental Health Awareness Month (21-0237, accepted by Tika Dobson and Alliance Health CEO Rob Robinson, who discussed a forthcoming 16-bed regional child crisis facility), Cooperative Extension Week (accepted by Donna Rewalt and Chrystal Gibson), Older Americans Month (accepted by DSS Director Ben Rose and Janine Gordon), and National Foster Care Month (21-0283, accepted by Ben Rose and Jovetta Whitfield, noting 306 children in Durham foster care). At [00:58:19], the board also recognized Board of Elections Chair Phil Lehman and Director Derek Bowens (Item 21-0304) for winning a 2020 U.S. Election Assistance Commission Clearinghouse Award for their early voting wait-time tracking tool.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (14 Items)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Wendell Davis reviewed all 14 consent items, including Item 205 ($12,438,000 IS&T capital project amendment), Item 248 (City-County sodium chloride storage ILA), Item 255 ($130,412 sewer utility capital transfer), Item 260 ($60,000 Convention Center roof fireproofing), Item 261 ($1,034 CJRC donation), Items 263 and 273 (David Young Utilities contracts), Item 267 (FY22 Transit Work Program and material change), Item 274 (NCDOT Riddle Road widening support resolution), Item 282 ($325,428.60 Sheriff Office 365 migration), Item 284 (janitorial services RFP), Item 292 ($92,785,075 LOBs capital amendment for Northern High School), Item 293 (JCPC multi-year funding), and Item 306 (NIED DPS MWBE contract amendment). Vice Chair Jacobs highlighted full funding for Northern High School and Commissioner Burns commended JCPC multi-year funding before the board approved the consent agenda 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 21-0270: Public Health COVID-19 Focus Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health Director Rod Jenkins reported 25 active COVID-19 cases, 227 cumulative deaths, and 25,409 total cases, with 41.6% of Durham's total population and 80.1% of seniors vaccinated and community transmission dropping from high to substantial. He highlighted persistent overrepresentation of Black residents in new cases (60.78%), expanding Latinx vaccine turnout (28% partial, 20% full), walk-in hours, community paramedic outreach to unhoused residents, and preparations to vaccinate ages 12 and up following FDA emergency use authorization for Pfizer.

agenda_items.title: FY2021-22 County Manager's Recommended Budget Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Wendell Davis presented the proposed FY2021-22 budget totaling nearly $730 million across all funds (and nearly $500 million General Fund, up 6.89%), recommending a 1-cent general fund property tax rate increase ($4.58M) plus a 1-cent Durham County Fire & Rescue Service District increase and 0.75-cent Lebanon Fire District increase. Key investments included $163.3 million for Durham Public Schools (+$10.1M total), $500,000 for Durham Tech workforce/BULLS pipelines, a 3% employee COLA plus 2%–3% merit pay reinstatement, $750,000 plus 3 FTEs for a Long-Time Homeowner Tax Relief Grant Program (<=30% AMI), Bull City United expansion into a standalone department, 10 DSS Medicaid quality assurance FTEs, 39 Sheriff vehicles, Justice Center court parking validation, a $1M public safety storage lease, 4.76% sewer rate increase, 2 racial equity FTEs, and ~$2.9M in ARPA offsets. Chair Howerton noted discussion would begin in work sessions rather than that evening.

agenda_items.title: Items 21-0285 & 21-0286: City-County Appearance Commission and Open Space & Trails (DOST) 2020 Annual Reports
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Planner Kayla Seibel presented the Appearance Commission 2020 Annual Report, prompting Commissioner Burns to ask about addressing members with 20–30% attendance rates despite excused absences. Senior Planner Carl Kolosna presented the DOST 2020 Annual Report noting four matching grants totaling over $77,000 against $190,000 in requests, and Vice Chair Jacobs urged restoring the DOST matching grant budget from $77,175 back to its pre-2008 level of $100,000.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing Item 21-0288: Palmer Way Street Renaming to Alexandria Way
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Cole Renigar and Planning Director Sara Young presented an applicant-initiated request to rename Palmer Way (between T.W. Alexander Drive and Ellis Road) to Alexandria Way, noting adjacent parcels are owned by the applicant and reviewing agencies had no objections. No callers or speakers signed up; Chair Howerton opened the 24-hour comment window closing May 11 and deferred the vote to May 24.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Public hearing held / Vote deferred to May 24

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing Item 21-0289: UDO Text Amendment Omnibus Changes 16 (TC2100001)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Planner Michael Stock and Planning Director Sara Young presented UDO Text Amendment TC2100001 (recommended 11-1 by the Planning Commission and approved May 3 by City Council), covering technical revisions, co-living parking parity (removing the term 'co-housing'), Commercial General height consistency (50 to 55 feet), and maximum driveway width expansion from 25 to 30 feet. Staff clarified to Commissioner Carter that Northgate Mall is zoned CC and unaffected by the CG height change and that watershed impervious limits still govern driveways, while Vice Chair Jacobs welcomed the co-living correction. With no public speakers, the hearing remained open 24 hours with a vote scheduled for May 24.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Public hearing held / Vote deferred to May 24

meetings.title: BOCC - May 3, 2021 Work Session Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the six-hour May 3, 2021 work session of the Durham Board of County Commissioners with all five commissioners present. After hearing citizens' comments on the County Manager's 2016 contract, DPS school nurses/social workers, and transit equity, the board reviewed 12 consent agenda items and received extensive briefings on the Community Child Protection/Child Fatality Prevention Teams' 10 recommendations, DFI's market analysis for redeveloping the former DSS Main Street building into affordable Class B/C small-business office and retail space, the Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) refresh timeline ahead of a planned 2022 bond referendum, the Triangle's 2027 World University Games bid, and updates on the Durham County Transit Plan scenarios and Triangle Commuter Rail feasibility study. On the sole substantive action item, commissioners voted 5-0 to suspend the rules and 5-0 to approve the City-County Planning Department's FY22 Work Plan (Item 21-0266). During Commissioner Directives and Comments, Chair Howerton and Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs clashed over Jacobs's late-night request to add an ARPA funding discussion to the May 10 agenda without agenda-prep review or final U.S. Treasury guidance, before the board voted 5-0 to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and adjourned.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Citizens' Comments, and Consent Agenda Review (12 Items)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton opened the work session and read the public charge. Clerk Monica Toomer read emailed comments from Barbara Jacobs urging fiscal restraint on the County Manager's contract and Nicholas Graber-Grace advocating 50 DPS school nurse and social work positions (800+ DAE petition signatures), while Bike Durham's Eric Landfried presented a transit equity rider video. County Manager Wendell Davis then reviewed 12 consent items for the May 10 agenda (including $12.4M IS&T capital modernization, $92.785M Northern High School amendment, FY22 Transit Work Program, and JCPC funding), with Commissioner Nida Allam requesting email follow-up on IT equipment recycling and the northern Durham broadband study.

agenda_items.title: Item 21-0232: Community Child Protection Team and Child Fatality Prevention Team Annual Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Kristi Mallett, coordinator Cheryl Scott, DSS Director Ben Rose, Jovetta Whitfield, and Public Health Director Rod Jenkins presented 10 system recommendations: Medicaid expansion (citing maternal/infant mortality and child poverty reductions), universal high-speed broadband (noting gaps in Rougemont), county health coverage for undocumented foster children, implicit bias training, countywide non-Spanish language line access, services for youth with autism and intellectual disabilities, a safe sleep awareness campaign, House Bill 630 / Families First preventive child welfare reform, the Early Childhood Action Plan, and child abuse reporting outreach. Vice Chair Jacobs requested Ms. Scott's Medicaid expansion brief for NCACC advocacy.

agenda_items.title: DFI Update #2: Former DSS Main Street Facility Market Analysis
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy Director Perry Mann and UNC School of Government DFI Project Manager Sarah Odio presented a market analysis for redeveloping the former DSS Main Street site at East Main and South Roxboro. DFI found roughly 35% of Durham small businesses had closed through February 2021 and downtown Class B/C affordable office space was rapidly disappearing as renovated Class B buildings approached Class A rents (~$38.50/sq ft), while ground-floor retail recovery remained tied to return-to-office trends and 1,500 new downtown households. Next steps include engaging an architect to test Class B/C small-office, retail, artist, lab, and community meeting spaces ahead of August public outreach.

agenda_items.title: Item 21-0281: Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) Refresh Process Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Manager Claudia Hager and financial advisor Doug Carter (DEC Associates) outlined Durham County's ~$600 million existing debt, $225 million upcoming LOBs draw, and >$1 billion 10-year CIP (including >$275 million for DPS), proposing a CIP refresh schedule running from August 2021 facility assessments through February–June 2022 adoption. Vice Chair Jacobs pressed staff to integrate the 2022 GO bond referendum timeline and DPS master facility coordination directly into the schedule, while County Manager Davis and Doug Carter discussed roughly $40 million in remaining 2016 bond funds and Local Government Commission draw-down compliance.

agenda_items.title: Update on Triangle Bid for 2027 World University Games
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic Development Officer Andrew Miracle and North Carolina Bid Committee Chair Hill Carrow briefed the board on the Triangle's selection as U.S. candidate city for the 2027 Summer World University Games (FISU), competing internationally ahead of a spring 2022 host decision. Carrow outlined potential Durham venues (Durham County Stadium, Duke, NCCU, Durham Tech), a projected $99 million budget funded largely via national sponsorships, broadcast rights, and state/federal support, and an estimated $150 million regional economic impact.

agenda_items.title: Item 21-0266: City-County Planning Department FY22 Work Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Sara Young presented the FY22 Work Plan allocating 46 FTEs across mandated development review and the in-house Comprehensive Plan (including Southeast Durham and Braggtown focus areas), plus minor engineering assistance inspecting GoTriangle bus shelters. Following Vice Chair Jacobs's questions on open space plans, the city's bilingual language access plan, and the new real-time development mapping tool, commissioners voted 5-0 to suspend the rules and 5-0 to adopt the FY22 Work Plan.

agenda_items.title: Durham County Transit Planning Update and Triangle Commuter Rail Feasibility Study
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation Manager Ellen Beckman and DCHC MPO's Aaron Cain presented three fiscally constrained 20-year transit scenarios ($475M–$500M available beyond committed bus and micro-transit projects): Scenario A (expanded bus frequency, later hours, sidewalks, paratransit), Scenario B (Bus Rapid Transit and dedicated roadway infrastructure), and Scenario C (Commuter Rail to Wake County around 2029). GoTriangle's Jay Heikes then reviewed the Commuter Rail Feasibility Study ($1.8B Durham-to-Garner capital cost, $29M annual operating, five Durham stops, and TJCOG affordable housing and job-access equity analyses). Informational only.

agenda_items.title: Commissioner Directives, ARPA/Agenda Process Dispute, Board Training, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff liaison Drew Cummings reported directives were current. Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs pushed to add a 15-minute ARPA funding process discussion and the Mayor's vaccine equity proposal to the May 10 agenda, prompting Chair Brenda A. Howerton to rebuke Jacobs for late-night/same-day emails and refuse to add ARPA before agenda-prep review and pending U.S. Treasury guidance (with GM Hager confirming Treasury rules were still awaited). Commissioner Nida Allam proposed initiating board relationship/Coleman Report training below the RFP threshold, and the board voted 5-0 to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) before returning to report staff direction and adjourning.

votes.item_title: Suspend the Rules to Vote on Item 21-0266 (City-County Planning Department FY22 Work Plan)
votes.discussion_detail: Board suspended its work-session rules to take immediate action on the Planning Department's FY22 Work Plan.

votes.item_title: Approve City-County Planning Department FY22 Work Plan (Item 21-0266)
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the 46-FTE FY22 Planning Department Work Plan prioritizing the Comprehensive Plan and adding minor GoTriangle bus shelter inspection support.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3))
votes.discussion_detail: Board entered closed session under attorney-client privilege; upon returning at [06:09:16], Chair Howerton reported direction was given to staff.

disagreements.issue: Process and Timing for Placing ARPA Funding Discussion on the BOCC Agenda
disagreements.summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton and Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs clashed over Jacobs's request to schedule a 15-minute ARPA funding discussion during the May 10 regular session.
disagreements.side_a_position: Place a 15-minute high-level ARPA process discussion on the May 10 regular session agenda (or use commissioner comments time) pursuant to the board's March 22 directive.
side_a_arguments: The March 22 minutes reflected a board directive for Claudia Hager to bring ARPA back at the April/May sessions.
Any three commissioners can request an agenda item, and a 15-minute high-level process discussion required no staff preparation.
disagreements.side_b_position: Defer ARPA agenda placement to the Chair/Vice Chair agenda-prep meeting until staff prepares materials and U.S. Treasury guidelines are released.
side_b_arguments: Sending emails late Sunday night and mid-day Monday bypassed established agenda-prep procedures and left board members and staff unprepared.
General Manager Claudia Hager advised that the School of Government and State Treasury urged local governments to wait for official U.S. Treasury ARPA guidance before formal discussions.
disagreements.resolution: Chair Howerton declined to place the item on that day's or May 10's agenda without agenda-prep review and moved forward with the agenda.

meetings.title: DCo BOCC April 26 2021
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the April 26, 2021 regular session of the Durham Board of County Commissioners (this stream is offset by approximately 39 minutes at the start compared to the alternate broadcast), with all five commissioners present. The board approved March 8 and March 22 minutes 5-0, jointly read a Bird-Friendly Durham resolution and National Volunteer Week proclamation, passed a four-item consent agenda 5-0, reviewed COVID-19 and vaccine equity data with Public Health Director Rod Jenkins, and announced appointments to the Safety and Wellness Task Force and Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee. After entering closed session 5-0 under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) and (a)(3), the board returned to approve a $19,622.25 pre-litigation settlement with Neighbors Eatery Restaurant 5-0 and passed a 3-2 vote authorizing outside counsel Denise Smith Klein to review the County Manager's contract—with Nida Allam, Heidi Carter, and Wendy Jacobs voting Aye and Nimasheena Burns and Brenda A. Howerton voting No on the grounds that in-house county attorneys should handle contract review.

agenda_items.title: Announcements on ARPA Funding and Approval of March Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs and Commissioner Nimasheena Burns reported on DDI Summit and NCACC discussions regarding equitable deployment of federal American Rescue Plan (ARP) tranches across the county, city, and school system. At [00:41:49], the board approved the March 8 and March 22, 2021 regular session minutes 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Item 21-0192: Bird-Friendly Durham Resolution and National Volunteer Week Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: All five commissioners took turns reading Resolution 21-0192 endorsing New Hope Audubon Society's Plan and Best Practices for a Bird-Friendly Durham, with New Hope Audubon President Barbara Driscoll thanking the board. At [00:53:23], Chair Howerton read a proclamation declaring April 18–24, 2021 as National Volunteer Week, recognizing 300+ volunteers serving on 40+ boards and commissions.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (4 Items)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Wendell Davis reviewed four consent items: Morrisville review officer designation (239), March property tax release/refund report (244), Harrell Salil LLC public art agreement for 318 East Main Street parking deck (254), and NCDOT secondary road addition for Sunstone Drive (257). The board approved the consent agenda 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Health COVID-19 and Vaccine Equity Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health Director Rod Jenkins reported 131 active COVID-19 cases, 223 deaths, and 24,943 cumulative cases, alongside 43.5% adult and 73.2% senior vaccination rates and newly launched walk-in clinic hours. Commissioners discussed J&J vaccine pause lifting, multilingual clinic support, racial vaccination disparities (44% white vs 22% Black and 16% Latinx fully vaccinated), and protecting community health workers from contractor nonpayment.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Acting County Attorney Willie Darby announced the appointments of Andrea Hudson to the Durham County Safety and Wellness Task Force and Lashelle Welby Jr. to the Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee. At [01:40:54], the board voted 5-0 to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) and (a)(3).

agenda_items.title: Post-Closed Session Actions: Neighbors Eatery Settlement and Outside Counsel Engagement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Returning to open session, the board approved a $19,622.25 pre-litigation lease-termination settlement with Neighbors Eatery Restaurant (5-0). The board then voted 3-2 to authorize Acting Attorney Willie Darby to finalize a letter of engagement with outside attorney Denise Smith Klein to review the County Manager's contract and consult individually with each commissioner, over objections from Chair Howerton and Commissioner Burns.

disagreements.issue: Hiring Outside Attorney Denise Smith Klein to Review the County Manager's Contract
disagreements.summary: After closed session, commissioners split 3-2 on authorizing Acting County Attorney Willie Darby to finalize an engagement letter with outside attorney Denise Smith Klein to review the County Manager's contract.
disagreements.side_a_position: Retain outside counsel Denise Smith Klein to review the County Manager's contract and hold separate consultations with each commissioner.
side_a_arguments: Secures independent outside legal review and individual commissioner consultations regarding the County Manager's contract.
disagreements.side_b_position: Rely on in-house county attorneys for contract interpretation without spending extra taxpayer money.
side_b_arguments: County attorneys on staff are competent to interpret contracts as a normal function.
Using taxpayer funds for an outside attorney on a task staff can perform is wasteful and unfair.
disagreements.resolution: Motion carried 3-2 (Ayes: Allam, Carter, Jacobs; Nays: Burns, Howerton).

meetings.title: BOCC- Regular Session 04-12-21
meetings.executive_summary: At its April 12, 2021 Regular Session, the Durham Board of County Commissioners opened with a moment of silence for victims of community violence, approved prior work session minutes 5-0, and recognized a resolution on the Black Maternal Health Crisis proclaiming April 11-17 as Black Maternal Health Awareness Week. Commissioners also discussed a resolution supporting a local non-discrimination ordinance and state hate crime prevention legislation including the Equality for All Act. The board unanimously approved the consent agenda (Items 180-38, including Bull City United) 5-0 and received a COVID-19 public health and vaccination update from Public Health Director Rod Jenkins. The board concluded by voting 5-0 to enter closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) regarding real property acquisition and employment contract terms, returning with no action taken before adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Moment of Silence, Announcements, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton led the Pledge of Allegiance (with Commissioner Nida Allam reading) and observed a moment of silence for victims of violence across the community and nation. After an announcement regarding Durham-Orange FY22 annual work programs, the board took up the first work session minutes for approval.

agenda_items.title: Resolution on Black Maternal Health Crisis and Black Maternal Health Awareness Week
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Nimasheena Burns read a resolution developed with the Durham County Women's Commission, Mayor's Council for Women, Equity Before Birth, and MAAME highlighting that Black women accounted for 32.9% of Durham County births in 2018 while Black infants die at more than three times the rate of white infants. Speakers Vivian Slede and Joyce Spencer urged the county to examine its healthcare budget, expand access to midwives, doulas, and prenatal/postpartum care, and build a diverse birth-worker pipeline. Commissioners expressed unanimous support for exploring current county partnerships such as Lincoln Community Health Center and proclaimed April 11-17, 2021 as Black Maternal Health Awareness Week.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Supporting Non-Discrimination Ordinance and Hate Crime Prevention Bills
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners spoke in support of a county resolution backing state hate crime prevention legislation, the Equality for All Act, and protections for transgender youth and marginalized residents, while advancing toward a local non-discrimination ordinance. Commissioner Heidi Carter expressed interest in extending explicit non-discrimination protections into Durham County contracts, and Chair Brenda A. Howerton credited County Attorney Curtis Massey and staff for carefully drafting the legal language.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 180 through 38)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Manager presented consent agenda items 180 through 38 following prior work session review. Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs briefly highlighted and celebrated the Bull City United violence-interruption item without pulling it from consent, and the manager noted a future community presentation on the initiative.

agenda_items.title: Community Recognitions and COVID-19 Public Health & Vaccination Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Nimasheena Burns recognized recent community passings, centenarian birthdays, and Judge Jim Hardin's retirement after 25 years on the bench. Public Health Director Rod Jenkins then reported 406 active COVID-19 cases and 23,711 cumulative cases, warning against a fourth wave and detailing outreach via UNC mobile clinics, Durham Tech campus vaccinations, geomapping, and community health workers.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Real Property Acquisition and Employment Contract Terms)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted to enter closed session pursuant to G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) to instruct negotiating agents regarding the price and material terms of real property acquisition and employment contract compensation/terms. Upon returning to open session at 02:54:20, the board reported no actions were taken and adjourned.

meetings.title: BOCC Work Session - April 5, 2021
meetings.executive_summary: During its April 5, 2021 Work Session, the Durham Board of County Commissioners heard emailed citizen comments defending the County Manager's fiscal record and criticizing board tensions, and reviewed 14 consent items including the U.S. Marshals Service detention intergovernmental agreement and a $1.1 million-plus capital amendment for Sheriff's Office body-worn cameras. Commissioners also discussed micro-transit needs for Treyburn, upcoming American Rescue Plan priorities, and a potential animal welfare feral cat ordinance. Procedural disagreements surfaced over the use of open-ended commissioner comments as unscheduled agenda items and over whether board training consultant selection belonged in open or closed session before commissioners reached informal consensus to submit scope-of-work feedback to the attorney by Friday. The board voted 4-0 (with Commissioner Nimasheena Burns temporarily disconnected from the call) to enter closed session on economic development, real property, personnel/contract matters, and attorney-client privilege, returning nearly three hours later to direct staff and adjourn without taking formal action.

agenda_items.title: Public Charge and Emailed Citizen Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk Monica Toomer read two citizen comments received prior to the deadline (noting one late submission). Larry Crane praised Durham's AAA bond rating and urged renewing the County Manager's contract, while Anthony Jones submitted a letter from the Durham Committee on the Affairs of Black People criticizing board dysfunction and alleged disrespect toward the county attorney and a potential consultant at the March 8 meeting.

agenda_items.title: Consent Item 180: U.S. Marshals Service and Sheriff's Office Detention Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs questioned a cost study by Mike Murphy suggesting $99.55 per day might go uncovered for federal detainees. Sheriff Clarence Birkhead and finance staff explained the facility is a public county jail unaffected by President Biden's private-prison ban, operates under a detainee cap, and remains fiscally positive; Commissioner Nimasheena Burns praised keeping detainees closer to their families during COVID-19.

agenda_items.title: Consent Item 191: Sheriff's Office Body-Worn Camera Capital Project Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Manager presented a capital project amendment appropriating over $1 million from debt service fund balance (pay-go) plus $124,460 from the general fund to fund the first two years of the Sheriff's Office body-worn camera project. Sheriff Birkhead told Vice Chair Jacobs that this initial allocation covers primary patrol/field needs with plans to later expand to court and detention personnel.

agenda_items.title: Past Directives, Micro-Transit, American Rescue Plan, and Commissioner Business
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a review of past board directives with Clerk Monica Toomer, commissioners discussed the need for micro-transit to Treyburn, mobile outreach, and ensuring full board input into American Rescue Plan recovery funding for affordable housing infrastructure, school nurses, mental health counselors, and small business/rental/mortgage assistance. Commissioner Heidi Carter objected to the open-ended 'other business' item feeling like an unscheduled agenda placeholder and flagged an upcoming feral cat ordinance from the Animal Welfare Committee.

agenda_items.title: Board Training Consultants and RFP Scope-of-Work Process
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton reported that the UNC School of Government had declined to work with the board and reviewed section 5 of the county RFP policy, highlighting the Center for Creative Leadership alongside Commissioner Nida Allam's recommendation of the Redwood Group. Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs twice suggested the matter belonged in closed session, which Howerton noted lacked a statutory exception for training, while Commissioners Heidi Carter and Nimasheena Burns urged defining a scope of work for the attorney by Friday to issue an RFP.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Economic Development, Real Property, Personnel, and Attorney-Client Privilege)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 4-0 (with Commissioner Nimasheena Burns temporarily disconnected from the call) to enter closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3), (a)(4), (a)(5), and (a)(6) covering industrial incentives, real property acquisition, employment contract terms/personnel complaints, and attorney-client privilege. Returning at 07:47:16 with all five commissioners present, the board noted it had given staff and the attorney directions (awaiting legal feedback and pricing) and adjourned.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3), (4), (5), (6))
votes.notes: During the 04:46:55 roll call, Commissioner Nimasheena Burns did not respond and was noted as having dropped off ('I think she jumped').
votes.discussion_detail: Board entered closed session on economic development incentives, real property negotiations, personnel/employment contract matters, and attorney-client consultation; returned at 07:47:16 with directions to staff and attorney.

disagreements.issue: Board Training Consultant Selection Process and Open vs. Closed Session Venue
disagreements.summary: Commissioners disagreed over whether discussions of board training consultants and prior RFP policy handling should occur in open or closed session, as well as the propriety of using open-ended commissioner comments for unscheduled policy topics.
disagreements.side_a_position: Discuss RFP policy context and consultant options openly in public session since no statutory closed-session exception applies to board training, and use commissioner comments to inform the public.
side_a_arguments: County legal guidance indicated there is no North Carolina statutory exception allowing closed session for board training.
Publicly clarifying section 5 of the RFP policy prevents half-truths about prior consultant outreach.
disagreements.side_b_position: Keep sensitive personnel/consultant commentary in closed session where appropriate, avoid using open-ended comments as unscheduled agenda items, and establish a formal scope of work for an attorney-led RFP.
side_b_arguments: Open-ended commissioner comment placeholders risk turning unscheduled remarks into de facto agenda items.
Consultant and legal discussions tied to agenda items are more appropriately handled in closed session or through a formal scope-of-work RFP process.
disagreements.resolution: Commissioners agreed by informal consensus at 04:43:50 to submit scope-of-work input for board training to Attorney Darby by Friday so an RFP could be issued.

meetings.title: BOCC Regular Session - March 22, 2021
meetings.executive_summary: At its March 22, 2021 Regular Session, the Durham Board of County Commissioners opened with a Girl Scouts Pledge of Allegiance, added an end-of-agenda discussion on the Community Safety and Wellness Task Force, read a board statement condemning anti-minority and anti-Asian hate killings, and approved February 22 minutes 5-0. Commissioners unanimously approved a nine-item consent agenda (5-0) covering a $753,843 state vaccination grant, a $376,350 food-insecurity meal contract extension with Food Insight Group, and $2.96 million in East Main Street capital reallocations, and held a public hearing on up to $226 million in Series 2021A/B Limited Obligation Bonds (including ~$113 million for schools). Following departmental testimony on pandemic frontline operations, the board voted 5-0 to approve 10% COVID-19 differential/hazard pay totaling $1.9 million-plus for eligible classifications eligible for FEMA reimbursement. Commissioners concluded by requesting an April work session briefing on American Rescue Plan funding and briefly discussing lived-experience criteria for the Community Safety and Wellness Task Force before adjourning 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Agenda Adjustment, Announcements, and Statement Condemning Hate
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a virtual Pledge of Allegiance by the Girl Scouts of North Carolina Coastal Pines, Chair Brenda A. Howerton added a discussion of Community Safety and Wellness Task Force member selection to the end of the agenda. Clerk Monica Toomer read announcements on Group 4 COVID-19 vaccine scheduling, small business loans, veteran services, and a virtual job fair, and Chair Howerton read a board statement condemning recent anti-Asian/minority killings and calling for community unity.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Regular Meeting Minutes (February 22, 2021)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board considered and unanimously approved the February 22, 2021 regular session minutes without edits.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 177, 181, 184, 185, 186, 188, 190, 198, 210)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs commended the food security team and Food Insight Group before the County Manager summarized nine consent items: a $201,048 transportation/human services budget reclassification, a $753,843 NCDHHS vaccination grant, Youth Home parcel recombination, Wiley Jacobs May family cemetery relocation, a $2,959,120 capital amendment shifting funding to the 300 block of East Main Street redevelopment, the February property tax relief report, a $376,350 food-insecurity meal contract extension, and appointments to the Criminal Justice Advisory Committee and Crime Prevention Council.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Up to $226 Million Limited Obligation Bonds (Series 2021A & 2021B)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief Financial Officer Susan Tezai presented the proposed issuance of approximately $225-$226 million in Limited Obligation Bonds scheduled for April, including roughly $113 million for Durham Public Schools (new Northern High School, a new elementary school, and existing school improvements) alongside county capital projects. Under virtual meeting rules, the public hearing remained open for 24 hours with final board resolution approval scheduled for April 12.

agenda_items.title: COVID-19 10% Employee Differential Pay ($1.9M+, FEMA-Reimbursable)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Department heads and commissioners reviewed the pandemic demands on frontline staff—including Public Health, EMS, wastewater operators, and library workers—and discussed pairing FEMA-reimbursable hazard/differential pay with across-the-board employee raises in the upcoming FY22 budget. Commissioner Nimasheena Burns moved, seconded by Commissioner Nida Allam, to approve 10% differential pay for eligible job classifications at $1.9 million-plus eligible for FEMA reimbursement.

agenda_items.title: American Rescue Plan Outlook & Community Safety and Wellness Task Force
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Nimasheena Burns and Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs asked staff to schedule a high-level April work session briefing on incoming federal American Rescue Plan recovery dollars ahead of budget deliberations. Commissioners also briefly discussed prioritizing lived experience when selecting members for the Community Safety and Wellness Task Force.

votes.notes: ASR transcribed Nida Allam as 'Commissioner Obama' when seconding and 'Commissioner alone' during roll call.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved unanimously with no corrections.

votes.item_title: Approval of 10% COVID-19 Differential Pay for Eligible Job Classifications ($1.9M+)
votes.discussion_detail: Approved 10% differential pay for qualifying frontline classifications totaling $1.9M+, structured to qualify for federal FEMA reimbursement while noting broader across-the-board raises would be considered in the FY22 budget.

meetings.title: BOCC Regular Session - March 8, 2021
meetings.executive_summary: At its March 8, 2021 Regular Session, the Durham Board of County Commissioners approved February minutes with corrections 5-0 and issued ceremonial proclamations for Meals on Wheels Month, National Social Work Month, and Women's History Month. Later, sharp board divisions emerged on two governance votes: first, the board voted 4-1 (Ayes: Nida Allam, Nimasheena Burns, Heidi Carter, Wendy Jacobs; Nay: Brenda A. Howerton) to pursue board training on rules of engagement and managing dissent while directing the County Attorney to bring back two additional consultant proposals alongside the existing 'Bob' group proposal. After a 5-0 vote into closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and (a)(6), the board returned to open session where Chair Howerton moved—and Commissioner Burns seconded—that Commissioner Carter recuse herself from involvement in the County Manager's contract. Carter refused to recuse herself, and the recusal motion failed 2-3 (Ayes: Brenda A. Howerton, Nimasheena Burns; Nays: Nida Allam, Heidi Carter, Wendy Jacobs) before the board adjourned.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Announcements, and Approval of Minutes with Corrections
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton read the public charge and led the Pledge of Allegiance, and Clerk Monica Toomer read announcements for Teen Book Fest and a 4-H Youth Entrepreneurship Workshop. Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs requested two corrections to the February 1 minutes (correcting Karen Haldeman's name and clarifying that DPS would be involved in appointing members to the Racial Equity Commission), and the board approved the minutes 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations: Meals on Wheels, Social Work Month, and Women's History Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter read the 19th Annual March for Meals Month proclamation accepted by Meals on Wheels' Jason Peacock, who noted a 40% pandemic surge in meal deliveries. Commissioner Nimasheena Burns read the National Social Work Month proclamation accepted by DSS Director Ben Rose, and the board also recognized Women's History Month and discussed workplace equity and paid leave.

agenda_items.title: Board Training Consultant Proposal and Request for Two Additional Proposals
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following presentations/comments involving consultant 'Mr. Bob,' Ms. Axam, Ms. Nesk, and facilitator Martha Marshall, Commissioner Heidi Carter moved (seconded by Commissioner Nida Allam) that the board commit to training on rules of engagement, group norms, and managing dissent while directing County Attorney Siler to return with two additional consultant proposals alongside the Bob group's proposal. Chair Brenda A. Howerton expressed disappointment that board concerns were not resolved beforehand and voted no, with the motion passing 4-1.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Personnel and Attorney-Client Privilege)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session pursuant to G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) and (a)(3) regarding public officer/employee qualifications, performance, or complaints and attorney-client privilege. Upon returning to open session at 04:02:19, the chair reported the board gave directions to staff with no formal action taken.

agenda_items.title: Motion to Require Commissioner Heidi Carter to Recuse from Manager's Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Immediately after reporting out of closed session, Chair Brenda A. Howerton moved—and Commissioner Nimasheena Burns seconded—that Commissioner Heidi Carter recuse herself from comments and involvement in the County Manager's contract based on prior meeting precedent. Commissioner Carter stated she would not recuse herself regardless of the vote, and the motion failed 2-3 on a roll-call vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of February 1 Work Session and February 8 Regular Session Minutes with Corrections
votes.notes: ASR transcribed Nida Allam as 'Commissioner Wong'/'alone' and Heidi Carter as 'Commissioner Connor'.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved with Vice Chair Jacobs's two corrections to page 5 of the February 1 work session minutes.

votes.item_title: Pursue Board Training and Direct Attorney to Bring Back Two Additional Consultant Proposals
votes.notes: Clerk recorded Heidi Carter as mover and Nida Allam as first seconder (Burns also offered a second); ASR transcribed 'four to one' as 'for the board one'.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion committed the board to training on rules of engagement, group norms, and constructively managing dissent, and directed Attorney Siler to bring back two additional consultant bids/options (ideally via RFP) alongside the existing Bob group proposal. Chair Howerton voiced disappointment that objections were raised at the dais rather than beforehand and voted no.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and (a)(6))
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session for personnel/officer matters and attorney-client consultation; returned at 04:00:41 with directions given to staff.

votes.item_title: Motion to Require Commissioner Heidi Carter to Recuse Herself from the County Manager's Contract
votes.notes: Initial voice vote failed before a roll-call vote was requested and recorded at 2-3.
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Howerton moved that Carter recuse herself from comments and involvement in the County Manager's contract citing prior meeting precedent; Burns seconded while noting she had been unaware of the motion. Carter stated she would not recuse herself regardless of the vote, Allam cited legal advice/communications received, and the motion failed 2-3.

disagreements.issue: Board Training Consultant Selection and Solicitation of Additional Proposals
disagreements.summary: Commissioners split 4-1 over whether to accept or solicit two competing consultant bids alongside the existing 'Bob' group proposal for board governance and dissent-management training.
disagreements.side_a_position: Commit to board training on group norms, rules of engagement, and managing dissent, and instruct the County Attorney to bring back two additional consultant options/bids before selecting a vendor.
side_a_arguments: Having two additional options alongside the Bob group proposal ensures a sound, competitive selection process.
The board should collaboratively define its training topics and scope of work.
disagreements.side_b_position: Proceed without delaying or subjecting the current MWBE-linked consultant team to additional late objections that should have been sent to the attorney beforehand.
side_b_arguments: Commissioners had prior opportunities to submit questions and concerns in advance rather than objecting publicly with consultants on the line.
Delaying an already-presented customized proposal undermines good-faith outreach to the invited consultants.
disagreements.resolution: Motion passed 4-1 directing Attorney Siler to return with two additional consultant options.

disagreements.issue: Motion to Compel Commissioner Heidi Carter's Recusal from the County Manager's Contract
disagreements.summary: Following closed session, Chair Brenda A. Howerton moved (seconded by Nimasheena Burns) to require Commissioner Heidi Carter to recuse herself from commenting on or participating in the County Manager's contract, which failed 2-3.
disagreements.side_a_position: Require Commissioner Carter to recuse herself from comments and involvement in the County Manager's contract based on precedent from prior meetings.
side_a_arguments: Precedent from prior meetings warranted Carter's recusal from discussions and decisions on the manager's contract.
disagreements.side_b_position: Reject forced recusal and allow Commissioner Carter to participate in deliberations on the County Manager's contract.
side_b_arguments: Commissioner Carter stated unequivocally that she would not recuse herself regardless of the vote.
Commissioner Nida Allam cited legal advice/communications previously received by the board in voting no.
disagreements.resolution: Motion failed 2-3 on roll call; Commissioner Carter remained seated on the matter.

meetings.title: BOCC - Work Session Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At its March 1, 2021 Work Session, the Durham Board of County Commissioners reviewed a 16-item consent agenda—including $194,208 for courthouse/detention x-ray machines, $300,000 for 500 East Main Street parking deck architecture, $731,683 for COVID-19 janitorial/facility expenses, and $465,920 for non-congregate homeless housing at Carolina Duke Inn—and voted 5-0 twice to suspend the rules and approve Item 171 (ReCity/Kate's Corner learning centers at three Durham Housing Authority sites). Commissioners received a presentation on the Durham County Early Childhood Action Plan (21 recommendations) and discussed federal stimulus inequities and commuter rail updates. Sharp disagreement surfaced during commissioner comments over a board training consultant proposal's scope, cost, and lack of broad board input, as well as limited registration slots for Racial Equity Institute training. The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and (a)(6), returning to instruct members to send training feedback to the County Attorney within the week before adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Public Charge, Citizen Comment, and Consent Agenda Review (16 Items)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After Clerk Monica Toomer noted one emailed citizen comment and Chair Brenda A. Howerton urged strict timekeeping for a packed agenda, the County Manager reviewed 16 consent items. Key items included detention/courthouse x-ray machines ($194,207.63 with Point Security, distinct from GTL), a $300,000 legacy claim transfer, $188,000 City sustainability grant, $37,200 in Youth Home amendments, $300,000 East Main Street 500-block parking deck design with Little Diversified Associates, $731,683 for COVID-19 facility costs, and $465,920 with Reinvestment Partners for non-congregate homeless housing at Carolina Duke Inn.

agenda_items.title: Consent Item 171: Suspension of Rules and Approval of Kate's Corner Learning Centers Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: To resolve vendor cash-flow issues immediately, the board voted 5-0 to suspend its rules and then voted 5-0 to approve the contract with ReCity as fiscal agent for Kate's Corner learning centers at three Durham Housing Authority communities.

agenda_items.title: Item 0074: Durham County Early Childhood Action Plan (ECAP) Funding Recommendations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the comprehensive Durham County Early Childhood Action Plan developed with more than 100 organizations, 1,000 community responses, and 60+ meeting hours, outlining 21 broad recommendations alongside a narrower set of initial county funding options.

agenda_items.title: Federal Relief Formula, Commuter Rail, Board Training Consultants, and Racial Equity Training
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed advisory board stipend requests (such as BPAC), federal COVID relief formulas disadvantaging counties under 500,000 population, and commuter rail studies. A contentious debate followed regarding a board training consultant proposal's cost, scope of work, and whether all commissioners had input, alongside concerns from Commissioners Nida Allam and Wendy Jacobs that only three commissioners could initially register for a Racial Equity Institute session.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Personnel and Attorney-Client Privilege)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) and (a)(3) regarding public officer/employee qualifications, performance, or complaints and attorney-client privilege. Returning at 06:20:12 with directions given to staff and no formal action taken, Chair Howerton asked commissioners to submit training questions/decisions to the attorney within the week so consultants would not be left waiting, and the board adjourned.

votes.item_title: Suspend the Rules to Act Immediately on Consent Item 171 (Kate's Corner Learning Centers)
votes.notes: Mover and seconder were not identified by name in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Board suspended work-session rules to enable immediate action on the ReCity/Kate's Corner learning centers contract.

votes.item_title: Approve Consent Item 171: ReCity / Kate's Corner Learning Centers at Three DHA Sites
votes.discussion_detail: Approved contract with ReCity as fiscal agent for Kate's Corner learning centers at three Durham Housing Authority communities to resolve vendor cash-flow issues.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and (a)(6))
votes.notes: ASR transcribed Nida Allam as 'Commissioner Lom'.
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session for personnel/officer matters and attorney-client consultation; returned at 06:20:12 with staff directions and no formal action.

disagreements.issue: Board Training Consultant Proposal Scope, Cost, and Board Involvement
disagreements.summary: Commissioners debated the scope, cost, timeframe, and fairness of the board training consultant proposal process, as well as limited initial slots for Racial Equity Institute training.
disagreements.side_a_position: Question the consultant proposal's cost, timeframe, and scope of work, ensure all five board members have direct input, and explore less expensive public/nonprofit alternatives such as UNC School of Government or Racial Equity Institute.
side_a_arguments: All five commissioners should help define the training scope of work rather than relying on a process where only two commissioners were initially involved.
Public or nonprofit providers may offer lower-cost options, and all commissioners should have access to racial equity training slots.
disagreements.side_b_position: Defend the timeline and clerk's recordkeeping on prior discussions and training registration, and move expeditiously so consultants are not left waiting.
side_b_arguments: The clerk maintained attendance records of prior conversations and registered commissioners for racial equity training in the order responses arrived.
The newly sworn-in board had discussed spring training since February and owed the consultants timely clarity.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken; after closed session, Chair Howerton directed commissioners to email questions, concerns, or decisions to the County Attorney within the week.

meetings.title: BOCC Budget Retreat - Day 2
meetings.executive_summary: On Day 2 of the Durham Board of County Commissioners FY21-22 Budget Retreat on February 25, 2021, County Manager Wendell Davis and facilitator Martha Marshall opened with a review of Day 1's economic outlook and budget guiding principles. North Carolina Medicaid Chief Administration Officer Melanie Bush briefed the board on Medicaid Transformation to managed care starting July 1, 2021, including Prepaid Health Plans, care management for high-risk pregnancies and children, and non-emergency medical transportation impacts on county DSS staffing. Commissioners then reviewed 52 compiled budget priorities, raising caution over vetting eviction-diversion legal providers ahead of incoming federal stimulus funds, refining priority language (such as Commissioner Nida Allam's tax welfare program correction), and emphasizing small business and entrepreneurship support alongside corporate recruitment. No formal votes were taken during the planning retreat, which concluded with staff preparing for April budget deliberations.

agenda_items.title: Retreat Day 2 Opening and Guiding Principles Framing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Wendell Davis and facilitator Martha Marshall recapped Day 1's economic outlook and financial solvency overview and outlined Day 2's agenda covering Medicaid transformation, budget policy/tax review, and revisiting compiled commissioner priorities.

agenda_items.title: North Carolina Medicaid Transformation Briefing and Local County Impact
agenda_items.discussion_summary: NC Medicaid Chief Administration Officer Melanie Bush presented the transition of 1.6 million of North Carolina's 2.5 million Medicaid beneficiaries into Prepaid Health Plans (PHPs) on July 1, 2021 under capitated payments. Commissioners Heidi Carter and Nimasheena Burns questioned local county budget, staffing, and non-emergency medical transportation impacts (~15% shifting to PHPs) as well as excluded populations, while DSS staff outlined unbiased virtual outreach plans with the state enrollment broker.

agenda_items.title: Compiled Board Budget Priorities, Eviction Diversion Caution, and Economic Strategy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Reviewing 52 compiled commissioner priority submissions, speakers cautioned against awarding millions in incoming federal eviction-diversion funding to attorneys lacking proven eviction-defense track records and confirmed existing county funding supports both emergency rental/utility staff and direct aid. Following Chair Brenda A. Howerton's departure, the remaining four commissioners offered final adjustments—including Commissioner Nida Allam clarifying 'tax welfare program'—and discussed balancing major corporate recruitment with local entrepreneurship before closing the retreat.

meetings.title: BOCC Budget Retreat - Day 1
meetings.executive_summary: On Day 1 of the Durham Board of County Commissioners FY21-22 Budget Retreat on February 23, 2021, County Manager Wendell Davis and facilitator Martha Marshall led the board through financial oversight, tax relief status, economic forecasting, and preliminary priority-setting. Financial officers Susan Tezai and Doug Carter presented five-year revenue-to-budget trends, peer comparisons with North Carolina's Big 10 counties and Orange County, and swap revenues trending favorably above $915,000. Commissioners also discussed improving small nonprofit grant-writing capacity, workforce pipelines such as the $75,000 Bulls Initiative, upcoming $150 million school bond financing, and operating cost pressures including $2 million-plus for the schools' $15/hour wage plan and $800,000 in employee health insurance increases. Commissioner Nimasheena Burns cautioned that low-income property tax relief proposals must avoid legally tying tax increases on some residents to paying taxes for others, and no formal votes were taken ahead of Day 2.

agenda_items.title: Retreat Opening, Agenda Framework, and Ground Rules
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Wendell Davis introduced facilitator Martha Marshall and previewed Day 1 topics including financial overview, property tax relief (with Tax Administrator Duwain), major county needs, economic outlook from Dr. Michael Walden, and commissioner priority identification.

agenda_items.title: Fiscal Overview, Swap Performance, and Peer County Comparison
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Claudia Hager, CFO Susan Tezai, and Doug Carter presented the county's fiscal position, highlighting over $915,000 received on the first interest-rate swap payment of the fiscal year (trending upward), five-year actual-vs-budget performance, and FY20 collection and expenditure comparisons against peer Big 10 NC counties and Orange County.

agenda_items.title: Nonprofit Capacity, Capital Bond Financing, Operating Pressures, and Tax Relief Legality
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members discussed holding grant-writing workshops for small nonprofits ahead of the next 18-month grant cycle and expanding workforce partnerships like the $75,000 Bulls Initiative. Manager Wendell Davis outlined the upcoming $150 million tranche of school bond financing, noted a potential 2022 school bond referendum could use just-in-time financing without an immediate FY22 tax hike, and flagged operating increases ($2M+ for schools' $15/hour plan and $800,000 for employee insurance), while Commissioner Nimasheena Burns warned that property tax relief programs cannot legally tie a tax increase on one group to paying another's taxes.

meetings.title: BOCC Meeting - February 22, 2021
meetings.executive_summary: At its February 22, 2021 Regular Session (stream G8cW5GSAEnU), the Durham Board of County Commissioners approved January 2 work session minutes 5-0 and adopted ceremonial recognitions honoring Deah Barakat, Yusor Abu-Salha, and Razan Abu-Salha—read by Deah's brother Farris Barakat to condemn Islamophobic hate crimes—and proclaiming February 22-26, 2021 as Black Entrepreneurship Week alongside Carolina Small Business Development Fund CEO Kevin Dick. Budget Director Claudia Hager later presented unbudgeted COVID-19 needs and employee compensation options (differential/hazard pay vs. 5% pay vs. three weeks of non-expiring leave), prompting sharp criticism from Commissioner Nimasheena Burns over repeated delays in compensating frontline workers while other initiatives received prompt funding. Commissioners also selected appointees to the Board of Health (Mary Braithwaite and Jean Rhea) and Memorial Stadium Authority (Ebon Coleman) before voting 5-0 to enter closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and (a)(6).

agenda_items.title: Public Charge, Announcements, and Approval of January 2 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following the public charge, Pledge of Allegiance, and Clerk Monica Toomer's announcements (including a Feb 23 trilingual COVID-19 vaccine town hall), the board unanimously approved the January 2 work session minutes 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Honoring Deah Barakat, Yusor Abu-Salha, and Razan Abu-Salha
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Introduced by Commissioner Nida Allam and read by Farris Barakat, the resolution honored the 2015 Chapel Hill shooting victims killed in an Islamophobic hate crime, condemned implicit bias and anti-Muslim hate, and recognized the victims' local humanitarian service.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: Black Entrepreneurship Week (February 22-26, 2021) & Small Business Relief
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board proclaimed February 22-26, 2021 as Black Entrepreneurship Week in partnership with Carolina Small Business Development Fund and Shaw University. CSBDF representative Kevin Dick addressed Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs's questions on grant demand vs. loans, commending the City-County 3%, 10-year small business loan product with no personal guarantee or collateral and highlighting state RetoolNC grants.

agenda_items.title: COVID-19 Financial Update, Community Needs, and Employee Hazard/Differential Pay Debate
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Claudia Hager updated the board on unbudgeted COVID-19 expenses, food security and rental/housing needs (which Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs noted could require $16-$40 million per DSS estimates), and compensation options held since July—comparing FEMA-reimbursable differential pay, a non-reimbursable 5% option, and three weeks of non-expiring leave. Commissioner Nimasheena Burns strongly criticized ongoing delays in compensating frontline employees compared to projects like the $75,000 task force or TIF funding, while other commissioners opted to carry detailed budget questions into the February 23-24 retreat.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The clerk announced ballot appointment results selecting Mary Braithwaite (physician) and Jean Rhea (pharmacist) to the Board of Health and Ebon Coleman to the Memorial Stadium Authority.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Personnel and Attorney-Client Privilege)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After adding an additional statutory item texted to the chair, the board voted 5-0 to enter closed session pursuant to G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) and (a)(3) for personnel/officer matters and attorney-client privilege.

votes.discussion_detail: Minutes approved unanimously without edits; Vice Chair Jacobs praised the clerk's detailed minutes.

disagreements.issue: Delays and Equity in Approving COVID-19 Employee Compensation / Differential Pay
disagreements.summary: Commissioner Nimasheena Burns sharply criticized repeated board delays and questioning over compensating frontline county staff during the pandemic, contrasting that scrutiny with quick approvals for other projects, while colleagues sought FEMA-reimbursement clarity and deferred action to the budget retreat.
disagreements.side_a_position: Move decisively to compensate frontline employees who worked long hours without raises during COVID-19 rather than repeatedly delaying while other projects receive unquestioned funding.
side_a_arguments: Frontline staff worked 12- to 20-hour days without raises for over a year while board members continually asked for more analysis.
Certain county initiatives such as TIF projects and task forces receive funding with minimal scrutiny, making employee compensation an issue of labor equity.
Targeting FEMA 75% reimbursable differential pay rather than the non-reimbursable 5% option is fiscally responsible.
disagreements.side_b_position: Review financial options carefully—including FEMA reimbursement eligibility, liability-free leave alternatives, and broad staff vs. AMI criteria—and defer detailed deliberation to the February 23-24 Budget Retreat.
side_b_arguments: Understanding the difference between differential pay, non-expiring leave liability, and COLA impacts is necessary before adopting a policy.
The board was scheduled to begin a day-and-a-half budget retreat the following morning where full budget trade-offs would be examined.
disagreements.resolution: No vote was taken on February 22; commissioners agreed to carry detailed questions into the February 23-25 Budget Retreat (and subsequently approved 10% FEMA-reimbursable differential pay on March 22).

meetings.title: Joint BOCC and BOE Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 16, 2021 Joint Board of County Commissioners and Durham Public Schools Board of Education (BOE) meeting presided over by Chair Brenda A. Howerton, members approved the November 11, 2020 joint minutes by voice vote after Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs requested removing an erroneous 'Doctor' title from Commissioner Heidi Carter's name. Racial Equity Commission co-chairs Judge Elaine O'Neal and Dr. Kern Holoman discussed draft bylaws emphasizing youth representation across DPS, charter, private, and disconnected youth, while Chair Howerton and Vice Chair Jacobs urged rapid alignment across the City, County, and BOE ahead of budget season. DPS administrators presented updates on virtual learning, state summer-learning mandates relative to federal relief funds, Commissioner Nida Allam's inquiry on demographic breakdowns of return-to-school surveys, Northern High School construction progress, MWBE/HUB outreach, HB 90 K–3 class-size rules, deferred capital/IT refresh needs, and COVID-era Pre-K expansion. At the close of the meeting, Commissioner Nimasheena Burns and Chair Howerton admonished DPS officials for bypassing the BOCC Chair and newer commissioners on late budget requests, urging transparent partnership ahead of the May 18 joint meeting.

agenda_items.title: Approval of November 11, 2020 Joint Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs requested a correction near the end of the November 11, 2020 minutes to remove the title 'Doctor' erroneously attached to Commissioner Heidi Carter's name. Following a motion and second, the joint boards approved the corrected minutes by unanimous voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Durham City-County Racial Equity Commission Bylaws Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Co-chairs Judge Elaine O'Neal and Dr. Kern Holoman presented on the Racial Equity Commission's draft bylaws, stressing broad youth participation including DPS, private, charter, and disconnected youth. Chair Howerton urged swift action on any stipends or funding so items could be included in upcoming budget retreats, and Vice Chair Jacobs referenced the three-board process agreed upon at the joint City-County meeting to finalize the bylaws.

agenda_items.title: DPS Virtual Learning and Summer Programs Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy Superintendent Dr. Nakia Hardy, Nelson, and Online Learning Director Matthew Hickson presented on virtual learning and summer programs. Vice Chair Jacobs asked whether federal and state funding would cover summer learning, prompting DPS staff to flag concerns that a newly filed General Assembly bill mandated six weeks of summer learning using federal dollars rather than the state's $4 billion reserve, while Commissioner Nida Allam asked about survey demographics on families preferring virtual versus in-person instruction.

agenda_items.title: DPS Capital Projects (Northern High School) and MWBE/HUB Participation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS staff showcased construction progress at Northern High School, detailing foundation work for the arts and cafeteria wing, wet-weather mitigation, and collaborative circulation design. Speakers also emphasized strengthening MWBE/HUB participation in school repairs and construction, noting a planned March session with Tammy Hall on the HUB process.

agenda_items.title: DPS Budget Priorities, Pre-K Expansion, and Inter-Board Communication
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS presented budget pressures including HB 90 K–3 class-size mandates, prior county funding (including $3.8 million toward the $15/hour minimum wage), $6 million in annual maintenance needs, and a $15 million technology refresh, followed by Dr. Suzanne Cotterman and Dr. Debbie Pittman on Pre-K expansion, rising disability identifications, and Head Start's January in-person reopening. At the end, Commissioner Nimasheena Burns and Chair Howerton criticized late budget outreach that bypassed the Chair and new commissioners, urging DPS to respect board protocol and provide a consolidated request list.

meetings.title: BOCC Virtual Regular Session - Feb. 8, 2021
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the February 8, 2021 virtual regular session with all five commissioners participating (with Commissioner Nida Allam dialed in off-camera due to a concussion). Following a Black History Month poetry recitation by Mr. McDuffie and community announcements, the board voted 5-0 by roll call to approve the January 25 and January 27, 2021 regular session minutes and read a proclamation establishing Juneteenth as an official paid county holiday commencing June 19, 2021. Later in the session, County Manager Wendell Davis and commissioners discussed upcoming budget retreat priorities and maintaining a 10% hazard pay differential for frontline employees, with Commissioner Nimasheena Burns strongly defending hazard pay against potential cuts.
