meetings.title: BOCC Work Session - February 1, 2021
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the February 1, 2021 work session with all five commissioners, the county manager, and the county attorney attending. During public comments, the Transit Equity Campaign urged measurable job-access objectives for BIPOC and low-wage riders in the Durham County Transit Plan update, and World Relief Durham requested multi-year county investment to expand bilingual tutoring and mental health services for refugee and immigrant youth. Commissioners then began reviewing the 17-item consent agenda (including a $221,243 WK Dickson stormwater nutrient management contract) and later received ETC Institute's 2020 resident survey showing sharp satisfaction gains in education transparency and strong public support for increased funding in schools (69%) and affordable housing (58%). Following updates on state/federal rental assistance and upcoming Racial Equity Institute and UNC School of Government board trainings, the board voted 5-0 by roll call to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) for attorney-client consultation and adjourned 4-0 after returning with Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs absent.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Public Comments (Transit Equity Campaign and World Relief Durham)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk Monica Toomer read an email from Eric Landfried of the Transit Equity Campaign calling on the Durham County Transit Plan update to prioritize BIPOC and low-wage transit riders, set measurable job-access goals (noting a 1-hour transit trip from Oxford Manor to Duke/VA hospitals versus 15 minutes by car), and assume a one-third local county match for commuter rail. Adam Clark of World Relief Durham presented a three-slide funding proposal to close service gaps for refugee and immigrant students beyond the 25% currently served, which Chair Howerton referred to staff.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review (Items 21-0018 and 21-0028)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Wendell Davis began walking the board through the 17-item consent agenda, including item 21-0018 ($8,540 state DHHS budget amendment) and item 21-0028 ($221,243 contract with WK Dickson for stormwater nutrient management strategy implementation). Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs and Commissioner Heidi Carter asked questions regarding neighborhood stakeholder engagement on stormwater projects before the middle portion of the digest truncated.

agenda_items.title: 2020 Durham County Resident Survey Results (ETC Institute)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jason Morado of ETC Institute presented findings from the 2020 Durham County resident survey disaggregated across unincorporated county areas, PAC areas 2–4, and race/ethnicity. Results showed steady overall satisfaction, a steep rise in satisfaction with education-related decision-making transparency (from 23% the prior year), high satisfaction with sheriff protection and public health, and top resident funding priorities in schools (69%) and affordable housing (58%).

agenda_items.title: COVID-19 Rental Assistance Updates and Board Governance/Equity Training
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners and staff discussed ongoing federal/state rental assistance distributions (noting roughly $548 million remaining at the state level and newly opened DOT COVID transportation grants) alongside plans for board training. Staff reported ongoing coordination with the Racial Equity Institute (REI) in Greensboro and the UNC School of Government for governance and manager-board alignment sessions for the newly constituted all-female board.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Attorney-Client Privilege under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3)) and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Howerton read the statutory basis under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with county attorneys under attorney-client privilege. Following a 5-0 roll call vote at 04:32:11 (coupled with a short lunch break until 1:40 PM), the board met in closed session, reconvened at 06:25:33 with Vice Chair Jacobs absent, reported giving direction to staff, and adjourned 4-0.

meetings.title: BOCC Regular Session - January 25, 2021
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the January 25, 2021 regular session with all five commissioners present, opening with a moment of silence for COVID-19 losses and the ceremonial introduction of new EMS Chief Paramedic Mark Lockhart. The board voted 5-0 to approve the January 11, 2021 minutes as corrected and voted 5-0 to adopt the consent agenda, highlighted by Item 21-0071 appropriating $950,000 from general fund balance to fund a $15-per-hour minimum wage for Durham Public Schools classified employees. Public Health Director Rod Jenkins reported declining active COVID-19 cases (1,255) and emphasized vaccine supply bottlenecks rather than local delivery capacity, while Planning staff introduced UDO text amendments under N.C.G.S. Chapter 160D (Item 20-043). Later in the meeting, Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs questioned funding ongoing 10% hazard pay via lapsed-salary strategies amid potential department budget cuts affecting DSS rental and food assistance, whereas County Manager Wendell Davis and Chair Howerton maintained that $8.9 million in fund balance growth and expected federal reimbursements covered hazard pay without cutting DSS services, before the board entered closed session 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Community Announcements, and Introduction of EMS Chief Mark Lockhart
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Howerton called the meeting to order, Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs led the Pledge of Allegiance, and the board observed a moment of silence for families lost to COVID-19. Clerk Monica Toomer read announcements on the Southern High School remote vaccination site, Comprehensive Plan objectives feedback, Innovate Durham 2021, and energy assistance, and Emergency Services introduced newly hired EMS Chief Paramedic Mark Lockhart from Wisconsin.

agenda_items.title: Approval of January 11, 2021 Regular Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Howerton requested a correction to reflect that she (rather than Vice Chair Jacobs) read the Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. resolution. Moved by Commissioner Nimasheena Burns and seconded by Commissioner Nida Allam, the minutes were approved 5-0 by roll call.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 0005, 0022, 0036, 0037, 0040, 0048, 0068, and 0071)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Wendell Davis summarized the consent agenda, including Landscape Manual revisions (0005), economic development allocation (0022), Special Board of Equalization and Review appointments (0036), business personal property tax extension (0037), Hope Learning Centers funding (0040), December 2020 tax release/refund report (0048), JCPC appointment (0068), and Item 0071 appropriating $950,000 of general fund balance for $15/hour pay for DPS classified employees. Moved by Commissioner Nida Allam and seconded by Commissioner Nimasheena Burns, the consent agenda passed 5-0 by roll call.

agenda_items.title: Durham County Public Health COVID-19 Crisis Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health Director Rod Jenkins reported 1,255 active COVID-19 cases (trending downward) and 17,331 inactive cases, highlighting simultaneous testing, surveillance, and vaccination operations at the Health and Human Services building and upcoming OptumServe support. Jenkins and commissioners underscored that state vaccine allocation—not county service delivery capacity—was the limiting factor and discussed engaging retired nurses and doctors.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Item 20-043 UDO Text Amendments (N.C.G.S. Chapter 160D, TC2000004)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Planner Michael Stock introduced text amendment TC2000004 revising the Unified Development Ordinance to comply with new state enabling legislation under N.C.G.S. Chapter 160D, consolidating city (160A) and county (153A) statutes along with technical reorganizations and policy updates. The remainder of the hearing fell within the truncated middle portion of the digest.

agenda_items.title: Reflections on $15/Hour DPS Classified Pay and 10% Hazard Pay Financial Debate
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners celebrated unanimous approval of the $15/hour minimum wage for DPS classified employees (bus drivers, cafeteria workers, instructional assistants) and emphasized truth and accountability in public life. County Manager Wendell Davis and staff then defended continuing 10% hazard pay using $8.9 million in FY 2020 fund balance growth and expected federal reimbursements, while Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs pressed for hazard-pay cost figures and cautioned against department budget cuts that could threaten DSS rental, food, and emergency assistance.

disagreements.issue: Funding 10% Employee Hazard Pay and Potential Department Budget Cuts (DSS Impact)
disagreements.summary: Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs questioned the fiscal sustainability of funding ongoing 10% hazard pay through lapsed-salary reserves while departments were asked to model budget cuts that could affect DSS assistance, whereas County Manager Wendell Davis and Chair Brenda A. Howerton maintained that hazard pay was covered without threatening DSS funds.
disagreements.side_a_position: Question reliance on April 2020 lapsed-salary strategies for unbudgeted hazard pay until full costs and downstream impacts on mandated DSS programs are clear.
side_a_arguments: Hazard pay was not included in the original April 2020 budget-management blueprint.
Departments are simultaneously being asked to examine conservative budget cuts, which in DSS could threaten mandated rental, emergency, and food assistance.
Commissioners need complete hazard-pay cost totals before making fully informed spending choices.
disagreements.side_b_position: Continue 10% hazard pay using FY 2020 fund balance savings, departmental cash-flow management, and federal reimbursements, with no cuts to DSS assistance.
side_b_arguments: Expenditure mitigation strategies produced $8.9 million in FY 2020 fund balance growth without spending budgeted reserves.
In 30 years of disaster management, federal emergency reimbursements have consistently covered eligible response costs; pressures are isolated to public safety cash-flow timing.
Chair Howerton urged staff to clarify publicly that funding hazard pay will not eliminate any DSS assistance funds.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote taken; County Manager Wendell Davis committed to returning with detailed hazard-pay cost figures and budget clarification.

meetings.title: BOCC Work Session - January 4, 2021
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton opened the January 4, 2021 work session with all five commissioners present, noting over 400 community emails received regarding the RDU Airport Authority fence application. Commissioners began reviewing the consent agenda—covering a $6.7 million encumbrance rollover (Item 684), the City-County Gang Reduction Strategy Committee assessment and Project BUILD interlocal agreement (Item 685), a sole-source wastewater lift station purchase (Item 686), $124,000 for Hope Learning Centers (Item 003), and a sales tax interlocal extension (Item 006)—before later suspending the rules (5-0) to vote 5-0 approving a $243,960 contract with Gene IQ for employee COVID-19 testing (Budget Amendment 21BCC0063). During commissioner directives, members and staff debated the timing and retroactivity of appropriating $950,000 for DPS classified staff $15-per-hour pay ahead of upcoming bond-rating agency calls, converging on taking partial retroactive action to January 2021 on January 11 while revisiting July/August 2020 retroactivity later in the month. The board then voted 5-0 to enter closed session for economic development incentives and attorney-client consultation and adjourned 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Public Comment Acknowledgment (RDU Airport Fence Application)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Howerton opened the first work session of 2021 at 9:00 AM with all five commissioners, the county attorney, and the county manager present, offering condolences to residents who lost loved ones to COVID-19. Clerk Monica Toomer reported that over 400 community emails regarding the RDU Airport Authority fence application were received over the weekend and distributed to commissioners, the manager, the attorney, and senior staff.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review (Items 684, 685, 686, 003, and 006)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Wendell Davis reviewed consent items ahead of the next regular session: Item 684 ($6.7M encumbrance rollover, where Vice Chair Jacobs flagged missing column headers), Item 685 (City-County Gang Reduction Strategy interlocal agreement and 7-year assessment/Project BUILD evaluation discussed by Commissioner Carter and Jim Stuit regarding the 1/3 City bilingual worker share), Item 686 (sole-source Muffin Monster wastewater equipment for Stirrup Iron Creek), Item 003 ($124,000 for Hope Learning Centers), and Item 006 (sales tax interlocal extension through June 2022). The remainder of the agenda fell within the truncated middle portion of the digest.

agenda_items.title: Gene IQ Employee COVID-19 Testing Contract and Budget Amendment 21BCC0063 ($243,960)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to suspend its rules in order to take immediate action during the work session. On a restated motion, the board voted 5-0 by roll call to authorize the county manager to execute a contract with Gene IQ for employee COVID-19 testing and approve Budget Ordinance Amendment 21BCC0063 transferring $243,960 from the general fund to the risk management fund.

agenda_items.title: Commissioner Directives and Debate on $950,000 Retroactive DPS Classified Staff Pay Timing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief of Staff Drew Cummings opened review of commissioner directives, leading into a debate over when to appropriate the remaining $950,000 for DPS classified employees' $15/hour pay raise. Finance staff cautioned that accurate year-end projections were needed within three weeks for bond-rating agency calls, while Commissioner Heidi Carter and Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs emphasized elected officials' policy authority and risk tolerance; commissioners agreed to advance pay retroactive to January 2021 at the January 11 meeting and revisit August 2020 retroactivity later in the month.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Economic Development Incentives and Attorney-Client Privilege) and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Howerton read two statutory closed session bases: N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) for economic development incentive negotiations and N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) for attorney-client privilege. Moved and seconded by Commissioner Nimasheena Burns, the board voted 5-0 to enter closed session, reconvened at 07:06:04 after giving staff direction, and adjourned 5-0.

disagreements.issue: Timing and Retroactivity of $950,000 DPS Classified Staff $15/Hour Pay Funding Ahead of Bond Rating Calls
disagreements.summary: Commissioners and county staff differed over whether to appropriate the full $950,000 for retroactive $15/hour DPS classified employee pay immediately on January 11 or defer action until late January so staff could finalize year-end projections for bond rating agencies.
disagreements.side_a_position: Willingness to take a calculated fiscal risk to act sooner on DPS classified pay and exercise elected policy authority even when differing from cautious staff recommendations.
side_a_arguments: Commissioner Heidi Carter argued the disagreement reflected differing 'risk budgets' and supported taking full action on January 11 rather than delaying.

Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs emphasized that elected officials must make decisions aligned with community priorities and values even when differing from staff recommendations, and sought clarity on July 1 versus August 2020 retroactivity.
disagreements.side_b_position: Avoid rushing financial commitments before delivering accurate year-end fiscal projections to bond rating agencies within three weeks.
side_b_arguments: County staff noted that rating agency calls require accurate, non-speculative year-end outlooks for the current and prior fiscal years.
Deferring the full remaining $950,000 review until January 24/25 allows finance staff to complete projections without rushing rating-agency prep.
disagreements.resolution: Compromise direction reached without a formal vote: move forward at the January 11 meeting with pay retroactive to January 2021 and return later in the month to consider the remaining $950,000 retroactive to August 2020 (subsequently approved on January 25, 2021).

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2020-12-16 9:00 AM - Reconvene - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 16, 2020 reconvened regular session, Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over closing public hearings and final votes on three items following the mandatory 24-hour public comment period that expired December 15, 2020. With Clerk Monica confirming no additional public comments were received on any item, the four initially connected commissioners (Nida Allam, Heidi Carter, Wendy Jacobs, and Chair Howerton) voted 4-0 to approve a $50,000 economic development incentive for The Clorox Company (150 new jobs and $7.5 million investment) and 4-0 to approve a $395,000 economic development incentive for BioAgilytix Labs LLC (878 jobs and $61.5 million investment). The board also voted 4-0 to adopt a General Obligation Refunding Bond Order and accompanying resolution authorizing the issuance of $70 million in Series 2021 General Obligation Refunding Bonds. Commissioner Nimasheena Burns joined via phone at adjournment after resolving technical issues, and the board adjourned 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Economic Development Incentive for The Clorox Company
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and Chair Brenda A. Howerton reconvened the public hearing on Item 20-060 regarding $50,000 in economic development funds for The Clorox Company, which planned to create 150 new jobs and invest $7.5 million in Durham. Clerk Monica confirmed no additional public comments were received after the 24-hour comment period expired on December 15, 2020, and Chair Howerton formally closed the public hearing after confirming with legal counsel that closing a hearing is a chair action. Commissioners noted the increased tax revenue would be at least four times the incentive and approved the allocation and county manager contract authorization 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Economic Development Incentive for BioAgilytix Labs LLC
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Howerton reopened Item 20-061 to consider allocating $395,000 in economic development funds to BioAgilytix Labs LLC (transcribed variously in ASR as Biogenetic/Biogenics), a life sciences testing company creating 878 jobs and investing $61.5 million in Durham County. Clerk Monica reported no additional public comments after the December 15 expiration of the 24-hour comment window, and Chair Howerton closed the public hearing. The board approved the $395,000 incentive and authorized the county manager to negotiate and execute the agreement by a 4-0 voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and $70 Million General Obligation Refunding Bonds, Series 2021
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following the December 14 public hearing and expiration of the 24-hour comment period on December 15, 2020, Chair Howerton closed the public hearing on Item 20-067 regarding the General Obligation Refunding Bond Order introduced on November 23. Commissioners considered both the refunding bond order and the bond resolution authorizing the issuance of $70 million in General Obligation Refunding Bonds, Series 2021. Both measures were adopted together by a 4-0 voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Approval of December 7, 2020 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Howerton held the November 23 regular session minutes for clerk follow-up and called for a motion on the December 7 work session minutes. The board approved the December 7 minutes 5-0 by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Citizens Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk Monica Toomer read one public comment raising concerns over whether CARES Act spending authorized by County Manager Davis in March was fully federally reimbursed and questioning why it was not presented in the budget.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Resolution Supporting NCACC Food System Resiliency Initiative
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Howerton read a resolution prepared with Deborah Craig-Ray endorsing the NCACC presidential initiative and task force on food system resiliency. All five commissioners were to sign the resolution for forwarding to the association.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Overview and Pull of Item 650
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Manager summarized consent items including utility contracts, a $1,178,584.02 Microsoft Enterprise Agreement, Snow Hill lift station testing, and 300 East Main Street contracts and $20.8 million limited obligation bond funding (Item 653). Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs asked to pull Item 650 (300 East Main Street Master Development Plan/Agreement) to the end of the agenda for review, leading to a brief exchange over whether her concerns could still be voted on that night to meet project deadlines.

agenda_items.title: Hope Learning Centers Continuation Funding ($124,000)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following presentations from three learning center providers, Commissioner Nimasheena Burns moved—and amended with Vice Chair Jacobs and finance staff input—to approve $124,000 in continuation funding through the end of January for Hope Learning Centers from the $819,000 remaining balance in the BOCC COVID Relief Fund. Commissioner Heidi Carter emphasized the urgency of supporting students struggling with remote learning while deferring broader fall funding questions to the January work session.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Lowell Siler began the boards and commissions appointment results, starting with one vacant seat on the Durham Open Space and Trails Commission.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Items 0650 and 0663 (300 East Main Street Affordability & Shelter Funding)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Jacobs questioned how the 300 East Main Street Master Development Agreement secures affordability in perpetuity and reflects the specific 30% and 50% AMI unit mix rather than only an 80% AMI cap. Staff explained ground lease renegotiation and reversion protections as well as Urban Ministries / Marriott shelter funding from the $1.01 million July allocation before the board approved Items 0663 and 0650 unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Post-Closed Session Real Estate Actions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session on economic development incentives, real property acquisition, and employment contract terms. Returning to open session at 03:51:07, the board reported giving staff economic development direction and voted 5-0 to purchase three vacant parcels (PINs 171556, 171557, and 171558) for $50,000 and 5-0 to approve a 10-year restaurant lease in Suite 150 at 201 East Main Street.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2020-12-14 7:00 PM - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 14, 2020 regular session, newly elected Chair Brenda A. Howerton thanked Commissioners Wendy Jacobs, Heidi Carter, Nida Allam, and Nimasheena Burns before leading the board through consent items, housing contracts, public hearings, and post-closed-session property actions. The board unanimously approved the December 7 work session minutes (pulling the November 23 minutes for clerk review), adopted a resolution supporting the NCACC Food System Resiliency Initiative, opened the 24-hour public hearing on $70 million in Series 2021 General Obligation Refunding Bonds (Item 674), and passed the consent agenda 5-0 except for pulled items 650 and 663. Later in the meeting, the board voted 5-0 to allocate $124,000 from the remaining $819,000 BOCC COVID Relief Fund to extend Hope Learning Centers through January, and voted 5-0 to approve pulled Items 650 (300 East Main Street affordable housing master development agreement) and 663 ($400,000 Reinvestment Partners homeless housing contract amendment) after questioning affordability perpetuity, AMI/bedroom breakdowns, and COVID-positive housing metrics. Following closed session, commissioners voted 5-0 to purchase vacant property from April Permann for $50,000 and 5-0 to approve a 10-year restaurant lease in County Administration Building II.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Chair Remarks, Announcements, and Minutes Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton called the meeting to order, read the public charge, and thanked her fellow commissioners for electing her Chair for the year. She pulled the November 23, 2020 regular session minutes for clerk review ahead of January and called a vote on the December 7, 2020 work session minutes, which passed 5-0. Clerk Monica also read a citizen comment from Dr. Lavonia Allison questioning unbudgeted March spending and federal reimbursement certainty.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Resolution Supporting NCACC Food System Resiliency Initiative
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Howerton presented a resolution supporting the North Carolina Association of County Commissioners (NCACC) Presidential Initiative promoting food system resiliency, citing Feeding America projections that North Carolina county food insecurity could rise from 14% to 19.3% due to the COVID-19 pandemic. All commissioners agreed to sign the resolution committing to examine and strengthen Durham County's local food system.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review and Approval (Items 603–680, excluding 650 and 663)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Manager reviewed consent items including utility division contract amendments (Items 603, 604, 634, 637), a $1,178,584.02 Microsoft Enterprise Agreement (Item 633), construction materials testing for the 300 East Main Street parking deck (Item 651), $20.8 million in limited obligation bonds for 300 East Main (Item 653), citizen board removals for poor attendance (Items 661 and 662), and a $250,000 CARES Small Business Grant ILA with the City of Durham (Item 665). Commissioners pulled Items 650 and 663 for end-of-agenda discussion and directed staff to provide the list of Item 665 grant recipients. The remaining consent agenda passed 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: $70 Million General Obligation Refunding Bonds (Item 674)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presenter Susan explained that Item 674 initiates the second tranche of the $170 million 2016 bond referendum by issuing $70 million in GO refunding bonds to pay off a bank bond anticipation note (BAN) within the three-year window while taking advantage of favorable interest rates. Because the meeting was virtual, the board opened the public hearing and left it open for a 24-hour comment period ahead of reconvening on December 16, 2020.

agenda_items.title: Hope Learning Centers Continuation Funding from BOCC COVID Relief Fund
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners considered continuation funding for Hope Learning Centers through the end of January 2021 while vetting longer-term funding sources. Following finance staff input and a suggested friendly amendment from Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs, Commissioner Nimasheena Burns amended her motion to allocate $124,000 from the remaining $819,000 balance in the BOCC COVID Relief Fund. The motion passed 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Siler announced the results of board ballot voting for advisory bodies, including selecting Zia Ming-Haoi to fill a vacancy on the Durham Open Space and Trails Commission (DOST) and appointments to the Environmental Affairs Board.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Items: 300 East Main Master Development Agreement (650) and Reinvestment Partners Homeless Housing Amendment (663)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners questioned how Item 650 ensures affordable units at 300 East Main Street remain affordable in perpetuity rather than reverting to market rate, why the contract referenced 80% AMI instead of the full 30%/50%/80% AMI and bedroom mix, and plans for green parking deck certification. On Item 663 ($400,000 amendment to Reinvestment Partners' homeless housing contract), staff confirmed they were exploring hotels, apartments, and a COVID-positive housing RFP. Because NC Housing Finance Agency deadlines required December action on Item 650, the board approved both items 5-0 with follow-up scheduled for the January 4 work session.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Post-Closed-Session Property Acquisition and Lease
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) and (a)(5) regarding economic development incentives, real property acquisition, and contracts. Upon returning at 03:59:02, Chair Howerton reported staff received direction on economic development, and the board voted 5-0 to purchase vacant property from April Permann for $50,000 and 5-0 to approve a 10-year restaurant lease in County Administration Building II (201 East Main Street, Suite 150).

votes.item_title: Approve December 7, 2020 Work Session Minutes (pulling November 23 minutes for clerk review)
votes.discussion_detail: November 23, 2020 minutes were pulled for clerk review of questions ahead of January.

votes.item_title: Approve Consent Agenda (excluding pulled Items 650 and 663)
votes.discussion_detail: Approved utility, IT, construction testing, $20.8M 300 East Main LOBs, and $250,000 CARES small business grant items while pulling Items 650 and 663 for discussion.

votes.item_title: Approve $124,000 continuation funding through end of January for Hope Learning Centers from remaining $819,000 BOCC COVID Relief Fund
votes.discussion_detail: Amended by mover Nimasheena Burns per Wendy Jacobs's suggestion to specify the $819,000 BOCC COVID Relief Fund balance as the funding source while vetting future funding.

votes.item_title: Approve pulled Consent Agenda Items 650 (300 East Main master development agreement) and 663 ($400,000 Reinvestment Partners homeless housing contract amendment)
votes.discussion_detail: Approved after staff clarified NC Housing Finance Agency deadlines and committed to reviewing affordability perpetuity and unit-mix details at the January 4 work session.

votes.item_title: Adjourn to Closed Session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) and 143-318.11(a)(5)
votes.discussion_detail: Closed session to discuss economic development incentives, real property acquisition, and employment contract terms.

votes.item_title: Approve purchase of vacant real property owned by April Permann (PIN 17156 / 17157 / 17584) for $50,000 and authorize county manager execution
votes.discussion_detail: Action taken after returning from closed session; voted individually per procedural requirement.

votes.discussion_detail: Lease covers 3,057 sq ft at $20/sq ft/year increasing 3% annually plus annual common area maintenance fees.

meetings.title: BOCC Work Session - December 7, 2020
meetings.executive_summary: This recording of the December 7, 2020 BOCC organizational work session begins with Board of Elections Chair Phil Lehman certifying the election of Nida Allam, Nimasheena Burns, Heidi Carter, Brenda A. Howerton, and Wendy Jacobs amid historic 74% turnout (~180,000 voters). The board unanimously elected Brenda A. Howerton as Chair (5-0), then split on two Vice Chair ballots: Chair Howerton's nomination of Nimasheena Burns failed 2-3 (Ayes: Nimasheena Burns, Brenda A. Howerton; Nays: Heidi Carter, Nida Allam, Wendy Jacobs), after which Wendy Jacobs was elected Vice Chair 3-2 (Nida Allam and Wendy Jacobs recorded Aye, Brenda A. Howerton recorded Nay, with Carter and Burns splitting the remaining two votes in the preceding omitted segment). Chair Howerton also called for January manager-commissioner relations and Racial Equity Institute trainings, and the board voted 5-0 to suspend the rules, approve the public officials bond (5-0), and adopt the 2021 meeting schedule excluding a September 7 Rosh Hashanah conflict (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Certification of 2020 BOCC Election Results by Board of Elections Chair Phil Lehman
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board of Elections Chair Phil Lehman formally certified the election of Nida Allam, Nimasheena Burns, Heidi Carter, Brenda A. Howerton, and Wendy Jacobs to four-year terms. Lehman reported ~180,000 total votes (118,000 early voting, 47,000 mail, 14,000 Election Day) and 74% turnout, thanking Director Derek Bowens, staff, and volunteers.

agenda_items.title: Election of Board Chair (Brenda A. Howerton)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presided over by County Attorney Lowell Siler, the board unanimously elected Brenda A. Howerton as Chair by roll-call voice vote (5-0). Chair Howerton thanked colleagues and emphasized unity, pandemic safety, and fiscal stewardship.

agenda_items.title: Election of Vice Chair (Split Votes: Burns Failed 2-3; Jacobs Elected 3-2)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Howerton nominated Commissioner Nimasheena Burns for Vice Chair citing community calls for racial equity, which failed 2-3 with Burns and Howerton voting Aye and Carter, Allam, and Jacobs voting No. On the subsequent Vice Chair vote, Wendy Jacobs was elected Vice Chair 3-2, with Nida Allam and Wendy Jacobs heard voting Aye and Chair Howerton voting Nay.

agenda_items.title: Chair Directives on Board-Manager Relations and Racial Equity Institute Training
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following Vice Chair Jacobs's third-term remarks, Chair Howerton requested that the County Manager and County Attorney schedule manager-commissioner relations training and Racial Equity Institute (REI) training for January to address concerns stemming from an investigation involving former commissioners.

agenda_items.title: Suspension of Rules and Approval of Public Officials Bond
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter moved to suspend the rules to enable formal voting at the work session (5-0), followed by a 5-0 voice vote approving the public officials bond.

agenda_items.title: Approval of 2021 BOCC Meeting Schedule (Amended)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Jacobs flagged that rescheduling the September 2021 work session to Tuesday, September 7 because of Labor Day conflicted with Rosh Hashanah. The board approved the 2021 meeting schedule as amended excluding the September work session date (5-0) before adjourning.

votes.item_title: Election of Brenda A. Howerton as Chair of the Board of County Commissioners
votes.notes: No other nominations were made.
votes.discussion_detail: County Attorney Lowell Siler called each commissioner by name for the unanimous election of Chair Howerton.

votes.item_title: Election of Vice Chair — Nomination of Nimasheena Burns
votes.notes: Carter, Allam ('No, no, no'), and Jacobs voted No; Burns and Howerton voted Yes.
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Howerton nominated Commissioner Burns for Vice Chair; the nomination failed to achieve the required three votes.

votes.item_title: Election of Vice Chair — Election of Wendy Jacobs
votes.notes: At 00:20:20 after an omitted gap, Nida Allam ('Commissioner Long') and Wendy Jacobs are recorded voting Yes and Chair Howerton states 'and mine is no' ('minus no' in ASR) before announcing 3-2; Heidi Carter and Nimasheena Burns's individual calls occurred in the omitted gap prior to 00:20:20.
votes.discussion_detail: Following the failed nomination of Burns, the board voted 3-2 to elect Wendy Jacobs as Vice Chair.

votes.item_title: Motion to Suspend the Rules to Vote During Work Session
votes.notes: Voice vote unanimous.
votes.discussion_detail: Suspended work session rules to permit formal votes on organizational items.

votes.item_title: Approval of Public Officials Bond
votes.notes: Voice vote unanimous.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the public officials bond after suspending the rules.

votes.item_title: Approval of 2021 BOCC Meeting Schedule (Amended to Exclude September 7)
votes.notes: Mover and seconder were not named in transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the 2021 meeting calendar with the September 7 work session date removed for revision due to Rosh Hashanah.

disagreements.issue: Selection of BOCC Vice Chair (Nimasheena Burns Nomination vs. Wendy Jacobs Election)
disagreements.summary: The newly seated board divided 2-3 against Chair Brenda A. Howerton's nomination of Nimasheena Burns for Vice Chair and then elected Wendy Jacobs 3-2.
disagreements.side_a_position: Elect newly seated Commissioner Nimasheena Burns as Vice Chair to reflect racial equity and community advocacy for Black and brown women's leadership.
side_a_arguments: Chair Howerton cited extensive community emails and racial equity considerations in nominating Burns.
disagreements.side_b_position: Reject Burns's nomination and elect veteran Commissioner Wendy Jacobs as Vice Chair.
side_b_arguments: Heidi Carter, Nida Allam, and Wendy Jacobs voted No on Burns's nomination; Allam and Jacobs are recorded voting Aye on the 3-2 ballot electing Jacobs (with Howerton voting Nay and Carter/Burns split in the unrecorded gap).
disagreements.resolution: Wendy Jacobs was elected Vice Chair on a 3-2 vote.
